author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
💡 **What:**
Replaced indexed `for` loop with `for...of` loop when iterating over the `clines` array in `server/modules/playPackets.js`.

🎯 **Why:**
`clines` is an array returned by `filter()`. Using `for...of` improves code readability and eliminates indexing overhead (`clines[i]`).

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
In benchmark tests comparing iteration paradigms over 10,000 array elements across 1,000 iterations:
- `for...in`: ~4813.35 ms
- Indexed `for`: ~4281.35 ms
- `for...of`: ~4315.27 ms

`for...of` shows comparable performance to indexed `for` loop (~1% difference) while offering significantly cleaner and safer syntax than `for...in`.

author: smith-xyz
body:
Part of the ledger append redesign (XWING-2350): traust-core pins this commit; the library half is traust-ledger#123.

## What

| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| `traust_ledger.layers.merkle_frontier TEXT`, nullable, `CHECK (<> '')` | the tree's right edge: the hex roots of its perfect subtrees, largest first, comma-separated, one per set bit of `merkle_size` (at most log₂ n hashes). An append extends it in O(log n) without reading earlier events |

Null means "not computed yet" (layers written before this). The writer backfills it once from the layer's events and requires it to reproduce the stored `merkle_root`, so a backfill can't fold in an edit.

**Why a column:** without it every append rebuilds the tree from every stored event: O(n) per append, O(n²) per triage (500 verdicts = 2.4 s of appends alone), and the rebuild folds any edit to stored events into the new signed root.

**SCI's old ledger** (traust-ledger's database, string layer ids, signature formats 1–4) is not imported into these tables: those layers stay signed artifacts the library verifies (data migration row 8). Nothing here touches them.

## Reviewer checks

- [x] Both dialects; `make test` passes on SQLite and Postgres (new: a frontier is stored, absent, or refused when empty)
- [x] No existing row becomes invalid (nullable)

## Changed tests

None: only a test added.

body:
## What
- **wsww.app** serves the app's home: a 1:1 port of Claude Design's `marketing/web/wsww-home v3.dc.html` (board *wsww.app v3*, phone-first), at stage live.
  - **Phones (< 720 wide):**
    - Copy comes first, and each composition plays while it is wholly on screen.
    - The deck's stage is sticky under the header for 0.9 of a viewport, so all six beats play in view.
    - Disco docks onto the header's 32 pt mark, and its lines replace the wordmark.
    - The pour's chips start on measured twins in the word field.
  - **Wide (≥ 720):** v2. Two columns, viewport-fraction ranges, Disco at 56 with its pill, no pinning.
  - Apple's official badge leads. "Android? Tell me when." joins the waitlist with `platform: android`, and the proxy tags the source by host.
- **manali.page/what-should-we-watch/ → 301 https://wsww.app/.** `/what-should-we-watch/leave/` and `/api/waitlist/leave/` are untouched, since every email's leave link and one-click unsubscribe point there.
- **wsww.app `/privacy` `/terms` `/support`** rewrite to the app's own pages, including their relative cross-links (`/terms.html`, `/privacy/terms.html`…).
- On the manali.page projects list, the card links to wsww.app beside the App Store badge (#38), and Posts goes to `/blog/project/what-should-we-watch/`. The sitemap drops the redirected URL.

## Deviations from the board (flagged to design)
- The driver measures layout (the phone/wide switch, card size, pin, pour vectors) on resize only, not on every scroll frame. That keeps each frame to reads plus transform writes.
- The hero height is `100svh`, not a JS `--vh`, so mobile toolbars never shift the layout.
- Disco stays hidden until it's first placed, so it never flashes top-left before hydration.
- Error lines under the Android field reuse the waitlist's copy (the board draws no error state).

Every frame matches (mean channel diff ≤ 1) except the hero and close, which differ only by Apple's badge where the board drew a pill (as the board asks).

- Android form: focus moves into the field, and the bad-address and API-down messages read correctly.
- `tsc`, lint (0 errors), `next build` and the static export all pass.

| Desktop 1440 | 278 ms | 192 ms | 0.0015 | 197 KB | p50 16.7 · p95 17.7 · max 18.7 ms |
| Phone 390, 4× CPU | 643 ms | 336 ms | 0 | 197 KB | p50 16.6 · p95 18.7 ms. One 168 ms frame in one run; two re-runs had none over 20 ms. |

author: clintmoody
body:
## Summary

- Pins the live WAL generation with OFD locks so a stray `close()` in any process cannot unlink
  the WAL/SHM sidecars out from under processes still attached to them.
- Adds `wal_generation_guard.py` plus `arm`/`disarm` call sites, and a forensics playbook at
  `skills/hermes-lcm/references/wal-generation-corruption.md`.
- Carries the three commits from #682 (mmap_size pin, advisory flock write gate, diagnostics
  playbook) because the guard is **not** separable from them: cherry-picking the guard commit alone
  onto `main` conflicts in `lifecycle_state.py` and `skills/hermes-lcm/references/diagnostics.md`.
  **This PR supersedes #682.** Reviewing this one reviews all of it; #682 can be closed.

## Why

Recurring `database disk image is malformed` on `lcm.db`, several times per day on a host running
long-lived sessions with concurrent writers (agent, cron jobs, gateway).

Three independent defects compounded. Each is necessary but not sufficient on its own:

1. **`mmap_size` compaction race.** Memory-mapped I/O let a compacting writer and a concurrent
   reader disagree about page state. Pinned to `mmap_size=0`.
2. **Unserialized cross-process writes.** Multiple processes wrote with no barrier between them.
   Now fenced behind one advisory flock on a `<db>.lock` sidecar, held for the duration of each
   write transaction. In-process writers queue FIFO on a per-path mutex acquired *before* the flock
   and released *after*, so no thread ever waits on a mutex it already owns. Fails **open**: if
   flock is unavailable (some network filesystems), behavior degrades to current behavior rather
   than erroring.
3. **WAL generation unlinking.** The actual producer of the malformed-image symptom. A close path
   could unlink the live WAL while other processes still held it open; those processes then wrote
   through a stale generation. OFD locks now pin the generation so the sidecars survive a stray
   close.

Long-running sessions do not cause this, they widen the window: more concurrent writers, held open
longer, so all three races fire far more often.

### Relationship to other open PRs

- **#682** (mine): superseded by this PR, as described above.
- **#687** proposes `journal_mode=DELETE` for the same class of symptom, from a different
  diagnosis, and also edits `db_bootstrap.py`. These two approaches are mutually exclusive in
  spirit: #687 abandons WAL, this PR keeps WAL and makes the generation durable. Flagging rather
  than resolving, since picking between them is a maintainer call. If #687 lands first this needs
  rebasing and item 3 above may become moot.
- **#684 / #675 / #663** all concern permission helpers releasing live POSIX locks on SQLite
  artifacts. Same failure family (lock/sidecar lifetime), non-overlapping code paths. No conflict
  expected.

## Validation

Run with `PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3` (CPython 3.11, static SQLite 3.53.1) on Linux 7.2.11 /
ext4-backed `/mnt/fastdata`.

- [x] Focused validation: `pytest tests/test_cross_process_write_gate.py tests/test_wal_generation_guard.py tests/test_crash_safe_wal.py -q` -> **25 passed**
- [x] Default validation, via `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going` -> **13/13 gates pass, exit 0**:
  - [x] `pytest -q` (full) -> pass
  - [x] `bash -lc 'ulimit -n 1024 && pytest -q'` (low-fd) -> pass
  - [x] `python -m compileall -q .` -> pass
  - [x] `python -m py_compile scripts/import_lossless_claw.py` -> pass
  - [x] `bash -n scripts/install.sh scripts/update.sh` -> pass
  - [x] `git diff --check` (working tree, staged, and `origin/main...HEAD`) -> pass
  - [x] dependency contract -> valid, version 1.0.5, 10 external imports, 4 Python versions
  - [x] benchmark smoke, stress smoke, stress release -> pass
- [ ] Workflow validation: no workflow files changed, `actionlint` not applicable.

### Field evidence

The fix has carried a production workload for 61 hours on the reporting host. Counting the guard's
own forensics snapshot directories, one per detected corruption:

| Window | Corruption events |
|---|---|
| Oct 17 to Oct 18, pre-fix | 7 |
| Oct 19 20:00 onward, post-fix | 0 |

Post-deploy monitor log contains only `snapshot` and `heartbeat` records, 62 and 10 respectively,
through 2026-10-22T11:29. Zero `corruption_detected`, zero repair actions. `lcm_doctor` against the
live database reports `database_integrity` ok, `messages_fts_integrity` ok, `nodes_fts_integrity`
ok, `sqlite_storage` quick_check ok, FTS sync 853/853.

One honest caveat on that timeline: 79 `unavailable` records appear *after* the files were written
at 20:00, confined to 21:08-22:26 and ending in `recovered` at 22:27:55. Those are the tail of the
final pre-fix incident, not a regression. The files were on disk at 20:00 but the already-running
processes were still executing the previous code from memory. The fix prevents recurrence; it
cannot heal an already-poisoned open handle, which is why that window needed the processes to
reopen the file.

## Notes

- `wal_generation_guard.py` is self-contained and import-light. Reverting is mechanical: delete it
  and remove the `arm`/`disarm` call sites plus the imports.
- The `<db>.lock` sidecars are inert artifacts. Leaving them in place or deleting them is safe
  either way; they carry no state.
- An empty `/proc/locks` between writes is expected, not evidence the gate is inactive: the flock
  is held only for the duration of a write transaction.
- Tests cover the gate and guard directly, including cross-process acquisition ordering and the
  fail-open path, rather than asserting on timing.

Refs #682, #687

author: mutaaf
body:
The physics engine's WASM (1.1 MB on the wire, the largest download) only started once the 180 KB entry script had loaded and run. The build now adds `<link rel="preload" as="fetch" type="application/wasm" crossorigin>` for it, next to the font preloads in vite.config.js.

- **One request, not two:** the preload uses the same URL and credentials as `fetch(wasmUrl)` in src/sim/engine-web.js, so the browser reuses it. I counted wasm requests per load: 1.
- **Measured** on a 390×844 page with the cache disabled, emulated 4G (9 Mbit/s, 70 ms RTT), 4 loads each, time to `physicsReady()`:
  - before: 9.9, 10.4, 10.4, 10.2 s
  - after: 9.8, 9.9, 9.9, 10.0 s
  - about 3 % faster. The download is bandwidth-bound, so starting it earlier buys little.
- **What would help more is not possible here:** the WASM is already stripped. `wasm-opt -Oz` saves only 2 %, too little to risk the deterministic build. Brotli at level 11 would be 835 KB against Cloudflare's on-the-fly 1,117 KB, but serving a pre-compressed file needs the Worker, which is frozen.

body:
## Problem and behavior / 問題と変更

Stop during an in-flight lock-in read used to discard the GPIB session. A point-status transport failure could instead be reduced to an unknown-quality flag and finish successfully. Compensation arrivals, HOME transitions and stationary states after STOP were not all verified.

Stop直後にロックイン接続が外れる経路と、状態照会の通信異常でも正常完了する経路を修正します。補償位置への到達、HOMEの状態遷移、STOP後の停止状態も確認します。

- Stop motion first, then retire exactly one interrupted GPIB reply before allowing another query. Keep a healthy session; retain disconnection/error for failed or missing replies and LI5640 restoration failures. Never resume a stopped run.
- Record point-status errors and the acquired unknown-quality point, then abort before another scan/return move. Refresh live overload/reference/error indicators at a separate 500 ms cadence; aggregate output overload is no longer hidden by input_overload=false.
- Verify compensation readback before the final move; verify STOP stationary states after attempting all configured axes. Ordinary serial writes are blocked after communication failure; emergency STOP remains available.
- Verify post-command HOME transitions with live callbacks. CONEX-CC OR is accepted only from NOT REFERENCED, per the official manual; referenced axes get actionable guidance without an automatic reset. Mechanical HOME is not assumed to equal calibrated instrument zero.
- Preserve the recording revision-5 format, calibration and compensation distances. Record STOP outcome/timing; distinguish Stopping, Stopped and Error, and avoid extra unrecorded job STOPs after finalization.

過負荷・参照ロック外れは測定品質の表示であり、レーザー／電源出力のインターロックを追加する変更ではありません。参照済みCONEX-CCはHOMEなしで初期化するか、明示的な手動リセット後に再原点復帰します。

## Validation / 検証

- 233 Rust tests, strict Clippy and rustfmt; 38 Python packaging/Notebook/layout checks; documentation links.
- Fake helper regressions cover Stop during a recorded read, late-reply isolation, successful connection retention, stalled/malformed/error recovery, and final-point status failure producing error metadata.
- Fake axis regressions cover ignored compensation, stale/pre-busy/unsupported HOME, verified stopping, and emergency STOP after serial failure.
- All workflows including rotated axes retain exact signal values, timing, UUIDs and checksums.
- Independent safety review. No live instruments were moved or queried.

## Reviewer note (added by reviewer, current head 2b5fba45)

This PR was rebased onto `develop` (one conflict in `bridge/cmd/cc-connect/relay.go`, resolved by keeping `develop`'s request path and adding the 202 branch). The heads and "based on main" lines below refer to the pre-rebase branch. Trigger, before/after and evidence below still match the diff.

Reviewer-side check that the fix is covered: with the `ErrRelayNoReplyYet` branch removed from `RelayManager.Send`, `TestRelaySendAPI_WaitExpiryAnswersAcceptedNot500` fails with `status = 500 ... want 202`; with the fix in place it passes.

---

# fix(bridge): 等待超时不再算失败；续接提示写明卡片身份

分支 `fix/card-resume-after-result`，头 `f23b5b1`，基于 `main`。**草稿状态，未合并，未部署。**

## 两个提交

### `f23b5b1` fix(relay): a wait expiry is "still working", not a failure

线上现状（旧二进制）：relay 等 120 秒拿不到回复就记成失败（`context deadline exceeded`）。但此时目标其实已经收到任务并还在干活，失败记录会诱导重新派一遍同样的活，造成重复。

改动：

- 默认等待上限 120 秒 → 20 分钟。依据是实际任务时长分布：大部分几分钟、一部分十几分钟、少数个把小时。
- 新增 `ErrRelayNoReplyYet` 哨兵错误。超时且**一个字都没收到**时才返回它，消息里写明「不是失败、目标可能还在干、不要重发同一件活」。
- `RelayResponse` 增加 `status`（`done` / `waiting`）与 `partial`。已经收到部分文字但没在期限内结束时，返回 `waiting` + `partial: true`。
- HTTP 入口：该情况返回 `202 Accepted` + `{"status":"waiting"}`，不再是 500。
- 命令行：识别 202，只在 stderr 打 `Waiting: …`，退出码 0。若退出码非 0，一个正在干活的长任务看起来就像坏了，会招来重派。
- 真失败（路由不通、绑定缺失）仍是失败，不被这条吞掉。

### `744bf5d` fix(progress): tell the agent which card it is being offered again

新任务被续接到旧卡的根因在提示层：旧卡被作为续跑候选交给模型，而「同一主题」容易被当成「同一任务」。

改动：注入的续接提示写明旧卡的 **id、状态、标题**，并要求只有确实在续同一标题的后续工作时才用 `--seq N --kind update`，新活必须 `--seq 1 --kind start`。

**设计取舍（未做的一件事，需要知道）**：没有把 `result_ready` 改成不可续跑。回合出了结果不等于用户验收，强行翻转会推翻四条既有用例（`TestPublicProgress_ContinuationReusesCardAcrossTurns`、`TestReview194AcceptOldKeepsNewCandidate`、`TestReview194ReportBudgetResetsPerTurn`、`TestReview194ExpiredCandidateIsNotOffered`）。所以这里让误续**看得见、可拒绝**，而不是硬堵。

## 本地实跑证据（2026-10-23，本机，非 CI）

| 命令 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `go test ./core/` | ok，124.345s |
| `go test ./core/ -run TestCUJ` | ok，23.274s |
| `go build -tags no_web ./...` | ok |
| `go vet -tags no_web ./core/ ./cmd/cc-connect/` | 无输出，退出码 0 |
| `gofmt -l`（改动文件） | 干净 |

新增测试三条（`core/relay_test.go`）：

- `TestRelaySend_WaitExpiryIsReportedAsWaitingNotFailed` — 断言 `errors.Is(err, ErrRelayNoReplyYet)`，且不是 `context.Canceled`；错误文案含「不是失败 / 仍在处理 / 去任务线程取结果」。
- `TestRelaySend_UnreachableTargetIsNotNoReplyYet` — 路由不通不能被误判成还在干。
- `TestRelaySendAPI_WaitExpiryAnswersAcceptedNot500` — HTTP 层返回 202 而不是 500。

`core/public_progress_lifecycle_test.go`：

- `TestPublicProgress_ResumeHintCarriesCardStateAndTitle` — 提示里必须带卡片 id、状态、标题。

变异核对（证明测试不是空跑）：删掉哨兵分支后，`TestRelaySend_WaitExpiryIsReportedAsWaitingNotFailed` 失败，报 `Send() error = relay: context deadline exceeded, want ErrRelayNoReplyYet`；文件已还原。把返回状态置空后，续接提示用例变红。

## 已知失败（与本 PR 无关）

`cmd/cc-connect` 的 `TestSetupCLIsHint` 失败（`setup clis: err=<nil> stdout=[`）。已在未改动的基线提交 `bb7e80d` 上复现同样失败，属于本机环境问题，不是这两个提交引入的。

## 部署状态

- 未合并、未部署。线上桥接跑的仍是旧二进制，relay 等待上限实际还是 120 秒。
- 部署另行确认。

body: ## Summary The `@beep/duckdb` feature backlog lived only in the AGENTS.md "Follow-ups" section once #1963 closed. This PR turns it into tracked, designed work: - Tracking issue #2088 with seven sub-issues: #2081 Appender bulk loads, #2082 `exportDatabase`/`importDatabase`, #2083 reader connections for streams, #2084 DuckDB-native storages, #2085 `dumpSchema`, #2086 law-practice READ_ONLY routing, #2087 `makeNodeClient` deletion. Each states the problem, the constraint probed on DuckDB 1.5.6 (`@duckdb/node-api` 1.5.6-r.2, effect 4.0.5) and acceptance criteria. - `/grill-with-docs` outcomes for the two items that change the driver's concurrency model and public surface, recorded as decision rows in `packages/drivers/duckdb/AGENTS.md`: - **D60–D62, reader connections (#2083).** One writer plus opt-in `readerConnections` (default `0`) used only by `executeStream` outside a transaction, wired as `SqlClient.make`'s `acquirer`. Each reader lease runs in `BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY`. A leased reader replays the writer's latest `USE`/`search_path` statement. - **D63–D65, native storages (#2084).** Demand-gated: no repo package imports any of the six effect modules. Tier A (only INT32 columns wrong) pre-creates `BIGINT` tables before the unchanged upstream layer. Tier B ports the upstream service contract. Cluster storages are single-process only. - D9, D11, D17, D25, D28 and D35 point at their issues. The Follow-ups section and the README point at the tracker. - The one item that was trivial is implemented: the unscoped legacy `DuckDb.makeNodeClient`, which nothing called, is deleted along with its span in the instrumentation catalog (D25). Closes #2087. Probe results that changed the designs: - A failed Appender flush inside a transaction aborts it, and the next `COMMIT` reports success while discarding the transaction's earlier writes (the D3 lost write). Appender support has to feed the safe-commit tracker. - `EXPORT DATABASE` inside a transaction writes that transaction's uncommitted rows, so `exportDatabase` refuses inside `withTransaction` (as D18 does for parquet). - Pre-created `BIGINT` tables make the upstream `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` a no-op for `SqlEventJournal` and `Persistence.layerBackingSqlMultiTable`. That does not help `AUTOINCREMENT` or the partial index. - Plain `SET TimeZone` is session-scoped, so D13/D41 hold, even though `duckdb_settings()` reports its scope as `GLOBAL`. `@beep/duckdb` is private (D12): no changeset. ## Test plan - [x] `bun run beep quality package-verify @beep/duckdb` (audit + docgen) - [x] `bun run check` and `bun run test` in `packages/drivers/duckdb`: 205 passed, 1 skipped - [x] `bun run beep observability catalog --write` (drops `DuckDb.useNodeConnection`) Closes #2087 Refs #2088 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Provenance - Workspace: beep-effect7 - Branch: docs/duckdb-backlog-design - Agents (newest first): - `claude-code` (desktop) · `claude-opus-5-5` · pushed Resume the publishing agent from any beep-effect checkout on the publishing workstation: ```sh bun run beep yeet resume 2096 ```

author: g0atbutt
body:
#114 capped battery saver at 30–40 fps. A shooter wants 60, and the game is light enough that capping at 60 still saves most of the work on faster displays.

**New caps:** 60 fps at 60, 120 and 240 Hz; 45 at 90 Hz (Steam Deck OLED); 48 at 144 Hz. The floor stays at 30, so every game tick is still drawn. At 60 Hz and below the frame rate is the display's own, so battery saver only switches the graphics to Classic. In VR it's still never on.

The settings screen's help text was regenerated with `tools/port_settings.py`, and only that line changed.

**Checked:** the frame-pacing test with its cases at the new limit, and the battery saver and menu tests. The test's allowance above the cap now matches the function's: within 5%, so a 62 Hz display isn't halved to 31.

author: sergeserb2
body:
A running timer published the whole activity model every second, even while Files hid its display. It now schedules one absolute completion boundary. API snapshots derive current remaining time directly, and only mounted countdown labels schedule display updates. The expanded ring advances through a native layer animation instead of one-second jumps.

Pause, Reduce Motion, hidden/occluded views and teardown stop continuous ring motion. Layout/color updates preserve its phase. Existing activation/clock/wake handling retargets progress without changing persisted deadlines. Native captures copy the current presentation value into the model for AppKit's caching renderer, then restore it in the same transaction without stopping motion.

Validation at `6e8288c607d26aa89282dbe9b9c09938e316a7b7`, stacked on #25:

- Clean optimized and debug arm64 development builds; source and bundle/signature checks passed.
- 10 real smoke groups and 42 runtime groups passed across 75 responding app instances. The new flow checks hidden publication counts and advancing API time, actual native progress between second ticks, ring/label PNGs, pause/resume, reduced motion, invalid input, one hidden completion and persisted-deadline restart.
- Browser controls passed running native progress without timer publications, stable paused state, resume, reduced motion, hidden cleanup/time, one-second completion and complete client/process cleanup.
- [GitHub build and source-archive run 39892866877](https://github.com/SergeSerb2/OpenCove/actions/runs/39892866877) passed, including the exported-source build without Git.

In short local app-process samples, a hidden running timer fell from 21 to 13 interrupt wakeups per 10 seconds, near the no-timer baseline. CPU time fell from 0.0113 to 0.0030 seconds; sampled footprint was 25.19 versus 25.29 MiB. The visible timer ABBA comparison used 27 versus 31 wakeups per 10 seconds, CPU time 0.0312 versus 0.0199 seconds, and footprint 25.90 versus 26.09 MiB. The smoother visible ring has a small transient scheduling cost. Two samples per condition do not establish GPU/WindowServer energy, long endurance, display frame pacing or superiority over Alcove.

Calendar scheduling is unchanged. No unit tests, mocks, desktop input, system clock changes, hardware writes or permission grants were used. Natural clock/sleep transitions, VoiceOver and physical input remain separate coverage boundaries.

author: damianreeves
body:
## What was wrong

`smithy validate examples/json-rpc/peers.smithy` exited 1 with `I could not resolve trait smithy.rpc#jsonRpcProtocol on example.peers#EchoChat.` (and the same for `smithy.rpc#jsonRpc`, `#method` and the session traits). `convert --to json` failed the same way. Only the RPC commands (`validate rpc`, transcripts) used `@rpc.loader()`. The other model commands used a plain `@smithy.Loader`.

## What changed

- `moonrockz/smithy`:
  - New `pub(all) enum SourceKind { User, BuiltIn }`, a new field `kind : SourceKind` on `SourceLocation`, `SourceLocation::new(file, path~ = "", span?, kind~ = User)` and `SourceLocation::is_builtin()`.
  - `assemble` gives `BuiltIn` to the loader's core inputs (`<prelude>`, `<contracts>`, `<protocol-tests>`) and to its `add_builtin_idl` inputs. All other inputs and defaults get `User`.
  - Export, `to_idl`, assembly and validation now read `source.is_builtin()` instead of matching source names.
- `moonrockz/smithy`: new `Loader::add_builtin_idl(name, text)`. The model treats this source like `<prelude>`:
  - `to_json_ast` and `to_idl` omit its shapes unless `include_prelude` is true.
  - Other sources cannot apply traits to its shapes.
  - A different definition of one of its shapes gives `SM-MODEL-014` (`I cannot redefine the built-in shape ...`).
  - An identical definition, such as a saved copy of `trait_definitions()` or an export with `include_prelude`, loads without a conflict.
  - The name is reserved (`SM-MODEL-001`) only in the loader that adds it. There is no process-wide state.
  - The core module does not know any rpc names.
- `moonrockz/smithy-validation`: `rpc.loader(protocol_tests~ : Bool = false)` adds the trait definitions with `add_builtin_idl("<smithy-rpc-traits>", ...)`.
- `moonrockz/smithy-build`: `BuildRunner::new(config, loader~ : () -> Loader = () => Loader::new())`. When a projection has imports, the runner loads its model again from the JSON AST, which now omits the rpc definitions, so this step uses the loader function.
- CLI: `ast`, `validate` (all forms), `select`, `convert`, `format`, `build`, `clean` and both sides of `diff` use `@rpc.loader(...)`. `build` passes `() => @rpc.loader()` to the runner. The separate openrpc `add_defaults` load in `build_cli.mbt` is redundant now, so I removed it. The openapi one stays.
- The READMEs of the three modules describe the new API.

## Breaking change

`SourceLocation` has a new field `kind` (`SourceKind`). Code that builds a `SourceLocation` with a struct literal must add `kind: User`, or use `SourceLocation::new`:

```moonbit
// before
let source : @smithy.SourceLocation = { file: "model.json", path: "/shapes/a#B", span: None }
// after
let source : @smithy.SourceLocation = { file: "model.json", path: "/shapes/a#B", span: None, kind: User }
// or
let source = @smithy.SourceLocation::new("model.json", path="/shapes/a#B")
```

## Behavior notes

- JSON AST and IDL output of an rpc model no longer contain the `smithy.rpc#` shape definitions. The trait applications stay.
- build-info `traitDefinitions` of a CLI build now lists the `smithy.rpc` traits, as it already lists the prelude traits.
- A saved `model.json` from an older openrpc build has the `smithy.rpc#` definitions, because they came in through the `<defaults>` source. It loads now, because the definitions are identical. If `trait_definitions()` changes in a later release, that file fails with `SM-MODEL-014` (`I cannot redefine the built-in shape ...`). This is intended: the bundled definitions take precedence, as the prelude does.

## Tests

- `scripts/test-cli.mbtx` (`exercise_rpc_traits`) runs these on `peers.smithy`:
  - `validate`, `ast`, `convert --to json` and `select` all succeed.
  - The JSON AST has no `smithy.rpc#` shapes but keeps the trait applications.
  - `convert --to idl` writes no `smithy.rpc` file and reads back to the same AST. The exported JSON validates.
  - `diff` of the model with itself, and of the JSON against the IDL, reports nothing.
  - A build with a projection that has imports and the `openrpc` plugin succeeds.
  - A model that defines its own `smithy.rpc#jsonRpc` gets `I cannot redefine the built-in shape smithy.rpc#jsonRpc.`
- Library tests:
  - `pkgs/smithy/loader_builtin_test.mbt`: export, `to_idl`, reload, redefinition, apply and reserved names. Two loaders with different built-in sets export differently, and the prelude and user sources get the expected kind.
  - `pkgs/smithy-build/runner_test.mbt`: the default loader fails the projection reload, and the given loader passes.
  - `pkgs/smithy-validation/rpc/protocol_test.mbt`: the built-in source, a saved copy of the definitions and `protocol_tests`. The old `Loader::new().add_idl("<smithy-rpc-traits>", trait_definitions())` pattern gives the same model before and after an `rpc.loader()` call. A model assembled before that call still exports its definitions.
- `mise run check` passed (lint, validate, test, build). `mise run test:cli` passed on native, wasm, js and wasm-gc for the first commit. `moonx scripts/test-cli.mbtx native` passed for the fix commit.

Fixes smithy-2qe.42.6

author: julianknutsen
body:
## Summary

Backport of #8209 to `hotfix/1.5.1`, with the same two read-path fixes in the supervisor API:

- **`/runs` shows formula-v1 runs' steps.** For a formula-v1 run, `GET /v0/city/{city}/runs/{id}/steps` returned no steps, and the run list, `GET /runs/{id}` and the run census kept the run `pending` while its steps were claimed and closed. They now list the steps and read the run `active` once a step is in progress or closed.
- **`GET /v0/city/{city}/sessions?state=closed` and `?state=all` list closed sessions.** `state=closed` returned nothing and `state=all` returned only open sessions. A filter that can match a closed session (`all`, or a comma list naming `closed`) now reads closed sessions too, reported with state `closed`. The default and every other filter keep the open-only, cache-first read.

## Root cause

**Runs.** Molecule instantiation types each untyped or `task`-typed non-root formula-v1 step `step` (#1039). The run projection's bead filter (`runproj.RunBeadFilter`, applied by the on-disk fold and by the dashboard run tailer) allowed only the engineering types, so it dropped those steps. The run had a root and no members, a started-member count of 0, and read `pending`.

**Sessions.** Both session list routes read rows through `sessionReadModelListings`, which never set `IncludeClosed`. `session.Store.listAllBeads` pins `Status=open` without it, so a closed session never reached the list filter, which already handles `closed` and `all`. The 1.5.1 fix for `GET /session/{id}` did not cover the list.

## Fix

- `internal/runproj/summary.go`: add `step` to the filter's type allowlist. v1 steps link to their root by `ParentID`, which the member and started-member rules already follow; a step under a parent that is not a run projects no run.
- `internal/session/info_store.go`: new `StateFilterIncludesClosed`, true for `all` or a comma-separated `closed` entry, the same spelling as `sessionMatchesFiltersInfo`. A test pins the two together.
- `internal/api/cache_read_model.go`: `sessionReadModelListings` takes the caller's state filter and sets `IncludeClosed` only when that predicate is true. Both list routes pass their `state`. Closed-inclusive requests read the bead store (the cache holds no closed rows); the status snapshot and the pending aggregate are unchanged.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: the Upgrading Notes sub-bullet on closed sessions now says the session list returns them for `?state=closed` or `?state=all`. Two Fixed entries sit after the `GET /v0/city/{city}/patches/...` entry.

No wire change: the `state` parameter already documents `closed`. The OpenAPI spec and the generated clients are untouched.

## Tests

Local hotfix pre-push (make test-fast-parallel) skipped to keep the shared push gate free for the 1.5.1 release lane; this PR's CI runs the same suites. An earlier, interrupted pre-push run of this content passed the six `unit-cmd-gc` shards before it was stopped.

Bazel on this branch (`hotfix/1.5.1` has no `ci` config). The commands pass `--remote_instance_name=` (the default rbe-west instance). The `oss` instance that this host's Bazel wrapper picks for gascity cannot link this branch's test binaries (`collect2: fatal error: cannot find 'ld'` under `-fuse-ld=lld`). That is a host/executor mismatch, not this change.

- Red without the runs fix: I reverted only the `summary.go` hunk in the working tree and ran `bazel-test --keep_going --remote_instance_name= //internal/runproj:runproj_test //internal/api:api_test --test_filter='^(TestFilterRunBeads|TestFilterRunBeadsKeepsFormulaV1Steps|TestRunsReportFormulaV1Steps)$'`. All 3 failed, both attempts (`FilterRunBeads dropped "step"`, `listed run status = "pending", want "active"`). With the fix restored, all 3 pass.
- `bazel-test --keep_going --remote_instance_name= //internal/runproj:runproj_test //internal/api:api_test //internal/session:session_test --test_filter='^(TestFilterRunBeads|TestFilterRunBeadsKeepsFormulaV1Steps|TestRunsReportFormulaV1Steps|TestStateFilterIncludesClosedMatchesTheListFilter|TestSessionMatchesFiltersInfoEquivalence|TestStoreListFiltersLikeCatalog|TestSessionReadModelListingsWarmCacheZeroStoreList|TestSessionReadModelListingsReadsClosedRowsForClosedFilters)$|TestHandleSessionList.*'`: api 27, runproj 2 and session 3 tests ran, 0 failures.
- `bazel-test --keep_going --remote_instance_name= //internal/api:api_test //internal/session:session_test //internal/runproj:runproj_test //internal/api/dashboardbff:dashboardbff_test //internal/api/dashboardspa:dashboardspa_test` on this head (`e7a68bf9a3`): all 5 targets pass.
- pre-commit (gofmt, golangci-lint `lint-changed`, genspec/genclient/genschema, `go vet ./...`, docsync) ran on both commits with 0 lint issues and no generated-file changes.
- On #8209 (main) the session tests were also red before the fix: `state=closed` listed nothing.

## Notes

- Source: #8209, head `372ef2bb5e6b2646e419000a071810ef558892a1`. #8209 is not merged yet, so this branch cherry-picks its two head commits with `-x`: `8318f81e89` (runs) and `372ef2bb5e` (sessions). In each backport commit the `(cherry picked from commit ...)` line sits above the `Co-Authored-By` trailer.
- Conflicts: only `CHANGELOG.md`. The two Fixed entries were moved to this branch's anchor, after `GET /v0/city/{city}/patches/...`, and the Upgrading Notes sub-bullet on closed sessions was reworded.
- Adaptation: on this branch `Manager.Close` takes only the session id, so the new session-list test calls `mgr.Close(closed.ID)`. `git range-diff` against #8209 shows nothing else beyond the CHANGELOG placement and the provenance lines.
- `gate` beads are not admitted, as on main.
- Merge after #8209 lands on main. If its squash differs, re-cherry-pick.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Without a supervisor, `gc session list --state closed|all` still lists open sessions only: the direct-store fallback (`doSessionListFallback` in `cmd/gc/cmd_session.go`) filters `OpenInfos()`. A supervisor read that runs past the client's 60s timeout also falls back to that path silently.
- A closed-inclusive list scans every session row twice, through the type leg and the label leg of the session union. That is acceptable for explicit requests.
- The dashboard's run-list lane cards for a v1 run still aggregate the root alone, since `runRootID` does not follow `ParentID`.

author: roed-math
body:
This PR attaches Cho's dyadic density profile to an actual Jordan splitting and proves it is an invariant of the lattice. The ranks and scale-relative parity types of the constituents of a dyadic Jordan splitting define a `TauCeti.DyadicJordanProfile`. That profile is the same for every splitting of isometric forms, so the exponents `N_M`, `N_Q` and `N` of an integral lattice are well defined and depend only on its genus. The PR also computes the README's worked values.

Roadmap target: `IntegralLattices/README.md`, Layer 3, milestone **3I** ("Dyadic type, bound and free constituents, and the density exponents"). The combinatorial profile and Cho's identity `N_Q = N_M + N` are already on main (`DensityExponent/Basic.lean`, `Scaling.lean`). So is invariance of the ranks (`IsJordanSplitting.finrank_eq_of_equivalent`) and of the parity type (`IsJordanSplitting.isScaleEven_iff_of_equivalent`). Until now nothing connected the profile to a lattice. This PR makes the connection. It delivers 3I's first bullet: type is "an invariant of the lattice and not of the splitting", so "`N_M`, `N_Q`, `t`, `b` and `c` are well defined". It also delivers part of the worked-values bullet, including the mandatory `⟨2⟩` test of the type criterion. **What remains of 3I after this PR:** behaviour under orthogonal sums with non-interleaving scales; the lattice-level link of `L ↦ L(2)` to the existing `DyadicJordanProfile.shift`; the `⟨1⟩ ⊕ ⟨2⟩` worked value at the lattice level; and the dictionary to the 2-adic symbols of 3E.

Main material, in the new file `TauCeti/NumberTheory/IntegralLattice/Dyadic/DensityExponent/JordanSplitting.lean` (316 lines):

- `LinearMap.BilinForm.IsJordanSplitting.dyadicJordanProfile` is the profile of a Jordan splitting of a symmetric form on a finite free module over a local domain, for any nonzero non-unit `π`. It comes with `dyadicJordanProfile_ranks_apply` and `mem_dyadicJordanProfile_typeI_iff` (type I means not even at the constituent's own scale), plus `mem_dyadicJordanProfile_typeI_iff_exists` (some `x ∈ N i` with `π ^ (i + 1) ∤ B x x`). `dyadicJordanProfile_eq_of_equivalent` proves that splittings of isometric forms have equal profiles.
- `IsModular.dyadicJordanProfile_ranks` and `IsModular.mem_dyadicJordanProfile_typeI_iff` compute the profile of a `π^i`-modular form split as one constituent; both worked values are derived from them.
- `TauCeti.IntegralLattice.dyadicJordanProfile` is the profile of the dyadic localization. `dyadicJordanProfile_eq` says it is the profile of any splitting. `dyadicJordanProfile_eq_of_equivalent` and `SameGenus.dyadicJordanProfile_eq` make it a local invariant and a genus invariant.
- Worked values:
  - `IsEven.dyadicJordanProfile_eq_unimodularTypeII` and `IsEven.densityExponent_dyadicJordanProfile`: an even lattice of odd determinant is one free type II constituent, with `N = rank`, not `0`. Hence `N(U) = 2` and `N(E₈) = 8`.
  - `dyadicJordanProfile_rankOne_two_pow_mul`: `⟨2^i u⟩` with `u` odd is one type I constituent of scale `2^i`, with `N = i + 1`. Hence `N(⟨1⟩) = 1` and `N(⟨2⟩) = 2`.

Supporting general lemmas, each placed in its canonical home:

- `JordanSplitting/Parity.lean`:
  - `IsJordanSplitting.isScaleEven_restrict_iff`: a constituent is scale-even iff all its self-pairings are divisible by `π^(j+1)`.
  - `IsJordanSplitting.even_finrank_of_isScaleEven`: a scale-even constituent has even rank, via the existing `IsSymm.even_finrank_of_isPerfPair`.
- `JordanSplitting/Basic.lean`:
  - `IsModular.isJordanSplitting`: a `π^i`-modular form is its own splitting.
  - `IsJordanSplitting.finite_support_finrank`: the constituent ranks have finite support.
  - `IsJordanSplitting.map_isometryEquiv`: transport along an isometry. It factors out the inline argument of `finrank_eq_of_equivalent`, which now uses it.
- `Modular.lean`: `Module.Basis.isModular_of_isUnit_det`, the basis version of the unit-determinant Gram criterion. `isModular_restrict_span_range` is now a two-line consequence of it.
- `Localization/Unimodular.lean`: `isPerfPair_localIntegralForm_of_isUnit_determinant`.
- `Dyadic/Unimodular.lean`: `IsEven.even_finrank_of_isUnit_determinant`, which says an even lattice of odd determinant has even rank.
- `Padics/PadicIntegers.lean`: `PadicInt.isUnit_intCast_iff` and `PadicInt.not_isUnit_two`.

Sources: S. Cho, *Group schemes and local densities of quadratic lattices in residue characteristic 2*, Compositio Math. 151 (2015), Definition 2.1(b), §2.3 and Lemma 5.1; O'Meara 93:28–29 for invariance of dyadic Jordan data. No Mathlib material is vendored.

Roadmap: IntegralLattices

author: tippingcows
body:
## Problem (security review SEC-02, PR #323)

The on-box classifiers in `backend/app/detectors/ml_classifier.py` did not cover the text they scored:

- **Code**: 240-char windows stepped by 400, so 160 characters between each pair were never scored, and with `_SCAN_CAP = 2800` nothing past index 2640 was.
- **Injection**: the first 1200 characters (window 240, step 120) plus the last 240. On text longer than 1440 the middle was never scored.

A payload in a gap or in the middle of a long prompt did not move the probability, and the verdict read as if the tier had looked.

## Fix

- One window set for both tasks: 240 chars (the training chunk size) stepped by **120**, across the whole input up to `_SCAN_CAP = 100_000` (same as `excerpts.MAX_SCAN`), with the last window flush with the end. Every character is scored, and any span of up to 120 chars lies whole inside at least one window.
- Each window is vectorized **once** and scored by both models (`LogisticClassifier.proba_vec`). `analyze()` uses a single pass (`_scores`); `p_code` / `p_injection` stay as the public API.
- **Past the cap**, the tail window is still scored, so an appended smuggle is still caught. The verdict also gets the partial-scan marker from #326: weight 0, `check=detector_error`, and `Verdict.unscanned == ["ml_classifier"]`. The marker's detail says how many characters were read and contains no content. It is built with `scoring.unscanned_marker` (from #332) using evidence `detector=ml_classifier`, the same scheme `engine.py` uses for a detector that raised.
- Cost work in `app/ml`. Outputs are bit-identical to before for the same window text:
  - `features._bucket` is memoized (`lru_cache(1<<16)`, about 10 MB when full). Blake2b hashing was about 90% of `vectorize()`.
  - Counting uses `Counter`.
  - `_score` uses C-level `map`/`sum` over the same terms in the same order.

## Timings

`MLClassifierDetector.analyze` on `llm_io` (both tasks), over the repo's docs and source as non-repeating text. Median of several slices, dev box with load around 3, so absolute numbers vary by roughly ±30% between runs:

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1k chars | 4.4–5.3 ms | 1.9–2.3 ms |
| 10k chars | 7.5–8.3 ms | 15–24 ms |
| 100k chars | 6.5–8.7 ms (read 2.6k/1.4k chars) | 144–214 ms |
| 1M chars | 6.7–8.5 ms (same) | 143–225 ms (capped, marked partial) |

Cost is linear at about 2 ms per 1k chars up to the cap, then flat. For scale, the rest of the engine (ML tier removed) takes about 34 ms at 10k, 450 ms at 100k and 4.5 s at 1M on the same box, so full coverage adds roughly 25–45% at any size up to the cap. The test bounds are deliberately loose for CI:
- 10k chars: under 100 ms
- 1M chars: under 2 s
- window count: at most `_SCAN_CAP // _STEP + 2` (deterministic)

## Accuracy / bench

- `bench_false_positives.py`: **0 / 123**. The output is byte-identical to `origin/main`.
- `bench_recall.py`, `bench_evasion.py`, `bench_code_discrimination.py`: output identical to `origin/main`.
- `test_ml_detector.py`, `test_ml_classifier.py`, `test_scoring.py`, `test_engine.py`: pass. One test changed:
  - `test_scoring::test_engine_records_a_lone_high_probability_injection_hint_as_low` now pins `_scores` instead of `p_injection`, because `analyze()` reads both probabilities from the one pass.
- `test_inference_latency_budget`: budget raised from 10 to 25 ms for a 5k body, which now scores every window instead of 7.
- `frontend`: `node scripts/gen-stats.mjs --check` passes, still 50 detection checks. The marker title isn't a `title="..."` literal in `detectors/`.
- Full backend suite (rebased on main after #332): 3393 passed, 13 skipped.

## New tests (`tests/test_ml_detector.py`)

- Injection placed in the old blind middle of a 6k prompt (start > 1200, end < len-240) is detected and emits `prompt_injection_ml`.
- A 150-char config block placed wholly inside the old 240–400 gap is detected (p > 0.85).
- A config block past index 2640 is detected.
- `_windows` covers every character, first window at 0, last flush with the end, step ≤ 120, at several lengths.
- Past the cap: `Verdict.unscanned` contains `ml_classifier` (and `to_dict()["unscanned"]` matches), the marker has weight 0 and carries no content, and the tail injection is still detected. At exactly the cap there is no marker.
- Cost bound test (above).

All four coverage tests return p of about 0.15–0.2 on `origin/main`.

body: ## What and why The device-settings reporter has two delivery rules: a report the server refused counts as not delivered and is sent again, and a closing send goes out at once alongside an in-flight one, with revisions keeping the newest snapshot as the delivered record. Each rule had a test of its own, but nothing covered them together — a closing send that overlaps an in-flight send and is refused. That is the pagehide order, where the closing send is the last one the page ever makes, so wrongly recording it as delivered would lose the newer settings silently. This PR adds that one missing test. Production code is unchanged: the current behavior is correct, and the test pins it. It was verified by mutation — making a refused closing send record delivery leaves all 11 existing tests green and fails only this new test. Fixes https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/issues/335 ## Affected surfaces Test-only change in `packages/ui` (`deviceSettingsReport.test.ts`). No runtime behavior, persisted format, or contract changes on any surface. | Runtime | Behavior after this change | |---|---| | Web | Unchanged | | Desktop (Electron) | Unchanged | | VS Code | Unchanged | | Hosted mobile | Unchanged | | Capacitor mobile | Unchanged | ## Validation | Check | Result | |---|---| | `bun test src/lib/settings/deviceSettingsReport.test.ts` (from `packages/ui`) | 12 pass / 0 fail (11 existing + 1 new) | | Mutation: closing path records delivery on refusal | 11 pass / 1 fail — only the new test fails; mutation reverted | | `bun run check:changed` | PASS (type-check, lint, dead code; anti-slop ratchet: no new findings) | **Live run:** Not applicable — no user-reachable behavior changes; the changed path is a unit test for an internal reporter, exercised directly by the test run above. ## Visual evidence No visible change: the diff adds one test case to an existing test file and touches no rendering, styling, or user-facing code. ## Risks None identified: the change adds a test and modifies no production code, so there is nothing to roll back and no compatibility surface. If the test ever fails in future, that is the signal it exists to give — the closing-path delivery record regressed. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Tests** * Added coverage for report delivery ordering when a newer report is refused while an older one is still in flight. The test checks that the newer report is retried and stops sending once accepted.

author: pandc19
body:
## What and why
An estimated stat showed as full (252, with the corner star) when the game's graph was not. Example: a level 75 Adamant Kingambit with Attack 299 and a "Pretty good" Attack IV (16-25) fits anywhere from 244 to 252 EVs. The fewest-EVs reading was 244, but `estimateEvRange` takes the plan's value when it falls inside that range, and the plan already said 252, so 252 won. The plan and the current EVs can also copy each other (the plan is raised to match current EVs in Violet), which made it stick.

- A plan of 252 now only reads as 252 when the stat itself reads full. If fewer EVs fit as well, the plan is read one step short (248).
- Other plan values are used as before.

Tests added in `tests/ev-estimate.test.ts` with the Kingambit numbers: no plan reads 244, a plan of 252 reads 248, and a stat that really is full still reads 252.

## How it was checked
- [x] `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm test` pass
- [x] Tried in the browser (UI changes): not a UI change, but saved estimates are not recomputed on their own; re-run the audit or save the stats of an affected Pokémon to see the new reading

## Deploy notes
None. Existing estimated EVs keep their stored value until recomputed.

Python's os.getcwd() resolves symlinks automatically, so lit.site.cfg uses physical paths at runtime. However, CMake records the build directory path as entered by the user, which may contain symlinks.

rsync.sh now resolves BUILDDIR to its physical path with pwd -P, ensuring consistency with lit's behavior for remote execution.

author: t0mdavid-m
body:
Before: the search database is exactly the user's FASTA. Keratins, trypsin, BSA and other common lab contaminants either go unidentified (and their spectra can be misassigned to real proteins), or turn up as ordinary proteins in the abundance table and the statistics.

After:
- The Identification step on Configure (LFQ and TMT) has an **"Add common contaminants (cRAP)"** option, on by default. It appends the 116 cRAP proteins to the search database with `CON__` before their accessions, the same convention as MaxQuant and ProSE.
- Contaminants get decoys like every other entry. With generated decoys, DecoyDatabase reads the FASTA and the contaminants in one call. If the FASTA already has its own decoys, the contaminants get decoys in the same prefix style.
- The PSM tables (Database Search, Rescoring, Filtered PSMs) get a **Contaminant** column.
- The Abundance page flags contaminant proteins and hides them by default. It shows "*n* contaminant protein(s) hidden" and has a **Show contaminants** toggle.
- `get_abundance_data()` leaves contaminants out unless asked, so Filtering, Imputation, Normalization, Statistics, PCA, heatmaps, volcano and pathway analysis never see them. A protein group counts as a contaminant when any of its members is one.

This is ProSE parity item S3 ([timosachsenberg/prose-web](https://github.com/timosachsenberg/prose-web)).

How:
- `src/common/contaminants.py` writes the prefixed cRAP FASTA and appends FASTAs with pyOpenMS `FASTAFile`. It also provides `is_contaminant` and `drop_contaminants`.
- The cRAP FASTA is bundled at `example-data/db/contaminants/crap.fasta`. That is a subfolder, so it never shows up as a selectable example database.
- The database step of `execution()` moved into `WorkflowTest.prepare_search_database()`. It writes the derived databases under `results/database/` instead of next to the user's FASTA. With contaminants off, it behaves exactly as before.
- The contaminant-only DecoyDatabase call uses its own instance name, so stored DecoyDatabase settings don't repeat its options on the command line.

Not in this PR: hiding contaminants by default inside the PSM tables. Those tables are built once at run time, so here the column flags them and the column filter hides them. The Proteins and Identification QC pages from #43 and #42 will pick up the same helper once those land.

Validation:
- `tests/test_contaminants.py` adds 7 tests. They cover the prefixed cRAP entries, both decoy paths (with a stand-in for DecoyDatabase, since TOPP is not installed here), switching the option off, and abundance data with and without contaminants. `pytest test_gui.py tests/` passes 126 tests.
- `pylint --errors-only` reports only E0611 on `from pyopenms import ...`. These notices also appear locally on the existing `results_helpers.py` import, and CI resolves them.
- I rendered the Abundance page in Chromium on a synthetic result with 40 proteins plus 4 contaminants, one of them a mixed group. 40 rows show by default, and the toggle brings back the 4 flagged rows. The Configure page shows the new checkbox.

author: tianming-1996
body:
## Root Cause Analysis

ARM64 (Kirin 9001X) screen recording used pure software H264 encoding (`libx264`) on both X11 and Wayland paths with no hardware acceleration, causing ~300% CPU usage during MP4 recording. The X11 path (`record_process.cpp:477`) hardcodes `libx264` with `ultrafast` preset; the Wayland path (`avoutputstream.cpp:461`) uses `avcodec_find_encoder(AV_CODEC_ID_H264)` which resolves to the software encoder. Additionally, `processFrameInterpolation()` launches a secondary ffmpeg encoding pass after recording, further increasing CPU load.

## Fix

On `__aarch64__`, prefer `h264_v4l2m2m` hardware encoder with runtime detection and automatic fallback to `libx264`:
- **X11 path**: `isV4L2M2MEncoderAvailable()` probes ffmpeg for `h264_v4l2m2m`; if available, uses `h264_v4l2m2m -b:v 500k`, otherwise falls back to `libx264`
- **Wayland path**: `avlibinterface` gains `avcodec_find_encoder_by_name` binding; ARM64 prefers `h264_v4l2m2m`, null falls back to software encoder
- **Frame interpolation**: skipped on ARM64 via `#if !defined(__aarch64__)` to avoid secondary software encoding
- Non-ARM64 platforms are completely unaffected (all changes under compile guards)

## Change Safety Assessment

### Code Safety

- **Risk Level**: Low
- All changes are under `#if defined(__aarch64__)` compile guards; non-ARM64 platforms have zero behavioral change
- Changes are additive (new function, new symbol binding, new conditional branches); no existing function signatures modified
- No historical fixes reverted

### Business Impact Scope

- **ARM64 X11 MP4 recording**: encoding path switches to hardware V4L2 M2M encoder
- **ARM64 Wayland MP4 recording**: encoder lookup prefers hardware encoder with software fallback
- **ARM64 frame interpolation**: skipped to reduce secondary encoding CPU cost
- **x86_64 and other platforms**: no impact (compile-guarded)

### Verification Suggestion

Test MP4 recording on ARM64 device (X11 and Wayland) to verify CPU usage drops; test on a device without V4L2 M2M support to verify software fallback; test on x86_64 to verify no regression.

---

## 根因分析

ARM64（Kirin 9001X）平台录屏在 X11 和 Wayland 两条路径均使用纯软件 H264 编码（`libx264`），无硬件加速，录屏时 CPU 占用约 300%。X11 路径（`record_process.cpp:477`）硬编码 `libx264` + `ultrafast` 预设；Wayland 路径（`avoutputstream.cpp:461`）通过 `avcodec_find_encoder(AV_CODEC_ID_H264)` 解析到软件编码器。此外 `processFrameInterpolation()` 录屏结束后再起一个 ffmpeg 进程做帧插值二次编码，进一步增加 CPU 负载。

## 修复方案

`__aarch64__` 下优先使用 `h264_v4l2m2m` 硬件编码器，运行时检测可用性并自动回退 `libx264`：
- **X11 路径**：`isV4L2M2MEncoderAvailable()` 探测 ffmpeg 是否支持 `h264_v4l2m2m`，可用时使用 `h264_v4l2m2m -b:v 500k`，不可用回退 `libx264`
- **Wayland 路径**：`avlibinterface` 新增 `avcodec_find_encoder_by_name` 绑定，ARM64 下优先查找 `h264_v4l2m2m`，null 回退软件编码器
- **帧插值**：ARM64 下通过 `#if !defined(__aarch64__)` 跳过，避免二次软件编码
- 非 ARM64 平台完全不受影响（均在编译守卫内）

## 改动安全评估

### 代码安全评估

- **风险等级**: 低风险
- 所有改动在 `#if defined(__aarch64__)` 编译守卫内，非 ARM64 平台零行为变化
- 改动为加法式（新增函数、新增符号绑定、新增条件分支），未修改任何已有函数签名
- 未撤销任何历史修复

### 业务影响范围

- **ARM64 X11 MP4 录屏**：编码路径切换为硬件 V4L2 M2M 编码器
- **ARM64 Wayland MP4 录屏**：编码器查找优先硬件编码器，不可用回退软件编码
- **ARM64 帧插值**：跳过以减少二次编码 CPU 开销
- **x86_64 及其他平台**：无影响（编译守卫）

### 验证建议

在 ARM64 设备测试 X11 和 Wayland MP4 录屏，验证 CPU 占用下降；在无 V4L2 M2M 支持的设备测试回退软件编码；在 x86_64 测试验证无回归。

## Summary by Sourcery

Use hardware-assisted H.264 encoding for ARM64 screen recording while preserving existing behavior on other platforms and providing a software fallback when hardware support is unavailable.

New Features:
- Prefer the V4L2 M2M H.264 hardware encoder for ARM64 X11 and Wayland screen recording, with runtime software-encoder fallback.

Bug Fixes:
- Reduce ARM64 recording CPU usage by avoiding software-only encoding and disabling the additional frame-interpolation encoding pass.

Enhancements:
- Add dynamic FFmpeg encoder-name lookup support for selecting platform-specific video encoders.

## References

Issue: 6443 (upstream jupyterlab/jupyterlab; number only, not linked)

Implements the approach a maintainer suggested on the issue: let `ensure-repo` add the field automatically.

I could not search upstream for other pull requests on this issue from this environment; check before opening upstream.

## Code changes

`jlpm integrity` now sets `repository.directory` to the package folder, relative to the repository root, for every workspace package whose `repository` field is an object. Packages without a `repository` field (examples, test mocks, `dev_mode`) are left alone. The value is recomputed on every run, so a package created from `buildutils/template` gets its own path when `create-package` runs integrity after copying the template.

The setting happens in the per-package loop rather than when the package data is first read, because `ensureMetaPackage` re-reads `packages/metapackage/package.json` and would otherwise drop the field for that package.

The second commit is the output of `jlpm integrity` (108 `package.json` files, one added line each). No test added: `ensure-repo` has no Jest coverage, and the generated files plus the integrity CI check show the behavior.

## User-facing changes

None in the application. On npm, each package's repository link will point to its folder in the monorepo.

None

body:
### Describe your changes: Backport of #35970 (7ac4c1401e173a03bf86eaff6e6d8276600ce49d) to `2.0`. Fixes #35965 on 2.0. PowerBI dashboards carried their tiles as charts, but reports (`dashboardType: Report`) had none. Each page of a report is now ingested as a chart under its report, named `{report_id}_{page.name}`, and the report URL is built from the same pages response, so ingestion makes no extra API call. A failed pages read keeps the charts the report already has. When those cannot be read either, the report is left as stored and the run skips the stale-chart pass. For the design, see #35970 and the ADR it adds. ### Differences from the main commit - **`powerbi/client.py` and `powerbi/metadata.py`:** each conflicted on one line the change removes, where 2.0 still has the older type hints (`Optional[List[...]] # noqa: UP006, UP045`). Both resolve to main's side, so every line the backport adds is identical to main's. - **`ingestion/.ruff-g004-baseline.json`:** dropped. 2.0 has no G004 baseline (nor `check_ruff_suppressions.py`); main's change to it only pruned the baselined f-string log call this change removes. - **ADR:** `docs/decisions/2026-10-22-powerbi-report-pages-are-charts-named-by-report-id-and-page-name.md` is kept. - The other files apply cleanly and are identical to main's. Everything the change relies on is already on 2.0: `WorkspaceState` (identical to main's before the change), `DashboardServiceSource.register_record`, `register_record_chart` and `mark_charts_as_deleted`, the class-level `chart_source_state`, `_advance_group_progress`, and the topology order that yields a workspace's charts before its dashboards. 2.0 has no `yield_dashboard_chart_lineage` stage, so on 2.0 page charts, like tiles, are listed under their report without Dashboard→Chart lineage edges, and the note in #35970 about those edges does not apply. ### Tests Run locally on this branch, with 2.0's own generated models and `PYTHONPATH=ingestion/src`: - Unit tests covering the changed files: `test_connection.py` 39, `test_powerbi_filter_query.py` 10, `test_powerbi_table_measures.py` 13, `test_dashboard_owned_connection.py` 5, `test_powerbi.py` 59, `test_powerbi_client.py` 14, `test_powerbi_report_pages.py` 17, `test_powerbi_workspace_state.py` 12, `test_powerbi_resilience.py` 17. **186 passed, 0 failed.** - With 2.0's original `client.py`, `metadata.py` and `workspace_state.py` put back, 22 of the 102 tests in the changed test files fail, so they test this change on 2.0. - 2.0 shares one topology context across dashboard sources, and `test_powerbi.py` mocks it, so `test_powerbi.py` and `test_powerbi_report_pages.py` were also run together in one process in both orders. Both orders pass. - Integration: `tests/integration/powerbi/`, 1 passed. - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass with 2.0's config. `basedpyright --baselinemode=discard` reports 0 errors on the changed files. - The live Power BI tenant run was done for #35970 on main and is not repeated here. Self-review: `fe7868b0735` was reviewed against `REVIEW.md` with fresh context, focused on what can differ on 2.0 (the dashboard base class and topology, `WorkspaceState`, the PowerBI models, `fqn`, the test fixtures and patch targets). No findings. ### Type of change: - [x] New feature 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Confidence Score: 4/5

The page cache must meet the repository’s explicit size-cap requirement before merging.

Findings

1.  **Page cache has no limit** ▶

Summary

 Adds Power BI report pages as charts named with the report ID and page name. - PowerBI report pages now appear as charts under their report. - Failed report-page reads now preserve known charts during ingestion. Intentional behavior acknowledged by `harshsoni2024`: when neither pages nor stored charts can be read, the report stays unchanged and the run skips stale-chart deletion. The review does not flag that tradeoff.

Diagram

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Read report pages once] --> B{Read succeeded?} B -->|Yes| C[Create page charts] C --> D[Attach charts and build report URL] B -->|No| E[Read stored chart links] E --> F{Stored links readable?} F -->|Yes| G[Keep stored links and charts] F -->|No| H[Leave report unchanged] H --> I[Skip stale-chart deletion] ```

## S16 — API-contract audit: MissAV (#825)

Audit run against a **fresh 2026-10-23 bootstrap** of `com.lagradost:cloudstream3:pre-release` (`bootstrapCloudstream`): the moving `pre-release` tag has moved since the FINDINGS-804 baseline (2026-10-21) — sha256 `ac5b150f5d91fcd641955d762aaf720bd2dc1f4e3180f01e1d7261a538564cf8` vs pinned `16278fc2...` — so the full API surface was re-verified with `javap` before any verdict. **All audited symbols are unchanged** (MainAPI async surface, `ExtractorLink.quality` plain `Int`, `Qualities` enum `Unknown, P144...P2160`, `getQualityFromName` lowercase/strip-`p`/`"4k"` equality/`toIntOrNull`→400 semantics, `MainAPIKt`/`ExtractorApiKt` DSL, `LoadResponse$Companion`).

### The finding (shipped)

`MissAV.kt:49` — `override var lang = "jp"`.

`"jp"` is an ISO-3166 country code, not an ISO-639-1 language tag (Japanese = `"ja"`). The pinned app consumes `MainAPI.lang` verbatim:

- `com.lagradost.cloudstream3.ui.settings.SettingsProviders` groups providers by `(getLang(), SubtitleHelper.getNameNextToFlagEmoji(getLang()))` and persists the grouping under `provider_lang_key` — `"jp"` put MissAV in its own non-ISO language group.
- `com.lagradost.cloudstream3.utils.SubtitleHelper.indexMapISO_639_1` has no `"jp"` entry.
- Internally inconsistent with MissAV's own `build.gradle.kts` `language = "ja"`, and with Javbangers — the fleet's other JA provider (`lang = "ja"`).

**Fix:** `lang = "ja"` (3-line comment added in file); `version` 21 → 22.

TDD note: `lang` is a constant property with no site-derived grammar — no Parse function can be red → green for it (ADR-0005 scopes Parse tests to parsing/extraction logic). The gate is the existing fixture suite against the fresh jar: `MissAV:test` → **88/88 green** (MissAVParseTest 7 + 81 shared), `MissAV:make` → `MissAV.cs3` builds clean.

### Audit checklist (item-by-item)

1. **MainAPI contract** — ✅ overrides match the pin exactly: `getMainPage(Int, MainPageRequest): HomePageResponse` (`MissAV.kt:90`), `search(String, Int): SearchResponseList` (`:152`), `quickSearch(String): List<SearchResponse>?` (`:166`), `load(String): LoadResponse?` (`:176` → `LoadResponse` returns `LoadResponse?`), `loadLinks(String, Boolean, (SubtitleFile)->Unit, (ExtractorLink)->Unit): Boolean` (`:247`). `load` returns the nullable `LoadResponse?` exactly as the pin declares; nothing missing, nothing extra.
2. **Homepage data** — ✅ `mainPageOf(Pair...)` (jar `MainAPIKt`), `newHomePageResponse(list = HomePageList(name, list, isHorizontalImages=true), hasNext = home.isNotEmpty())` — 3-arg `HomePageList` ctor + `HomePageList, Boolean` DSL overload both present in the jar; `hasNext` correctly stops on an empty page.
3. **LoadResponse completeness** — ✅ `posterUrl` (og:image), `year` (`time`), `tags` (genre rows), `plot` (og:description), `duration` (og:video:duration seconds → minutes via shared `DurationParse.fromSeconds`), `recommendations` (recombee side-bar recomms), `addActors(actresses)`. Nothing exposed-but-unset; nothing set-without-exposure (no score/trailer exposed by site).
4. **Constructors** — ✅ pure DSL: `newMovieSearchResponse` (search + recommendations), `newMovieLoadResponse`, `newExtractorLink(source, name, url, type) {}` (jar `(String, String, String, ExtractorLinkType, Function2)` suspend builder). One subtlety verified at bytecode level: `addActors(List<Actor>)` resolves to the Kotlin-name `addActors` alias whose JVM symbol is `LoadResponse$Companion.addActorsOnly` (erasure-clash workaround for the `List<Pair<Actor,String>>` overload) — it maps each `Actor` to `ActorData(Actor)` + `setActors`; correct, no data loss.
5. **Registration** — ✅ `@CloudstreamPlugin` plugin class at the bottom of `MissAV.kt`: `registerMainAPI(MissAV())` + shared `registerHostExtractors()` (ADR-0002 single seam); no copied extractor files (no local `: ExtractorApi()` subclasses; `DurationParse`/`registerHostExtractors` consumed from `shared/` splice).
6. **build.gradle.kts metadata** — ✅ `version = 22`, `authors`, `language = "ja"`, `status = 1`, `tvTypes = listOf("NSFW")`, `description`, `iconUrl`.
7. **Quality mapping (FINDINGS-767 standard)** — ✅ n/a-by-structure: MissAV calls no label→quality mapper (`getQualityFromName` absent — the suffix-label trap can't fire) and emits a single HLS playlist link (`surrit.com/.../playlist.m3u8`); no per-variant `ExtractorLink` is constructed, so there is no site-exposed enumerable quality to map and `quality` stays at the default (app renders `Auto`) — correct at playlist granularity, and Q1's audit instrument reports no quality assignment (INFO, accepted).

No live Verification sweep needed beyond the fix (spec rule: live spot-check only for a found mismatch — the mismatch here is metadata, exercised by compile+suite).

author: atomantic
body:
Release preparation previously swept in pending PRs and promoted live `main`, so concurrent merges could keep changing the candidate during validation. The release procedure now captures a dedicated candidate at kickoff and preserves its original cutoff when resuming.

Only release preparation and individually justified gating fixes may advance the candidate. Later development merges, unrelated issues and dependency updates stay for the next release. The procedure records candidate identities and amendments, validates against the actual release base, verifies publication, and synchronizes release fixes and version metadata back to development afterward.

The scheduled release prompt, option descriptions and customized-prompt guidance follow the same cutoff contract. Prompt version 21 preserves the previous default hash so existing installations can upgrade. Existing exact-tree tag protection and full CI for PRs targeting `release` remain in place.

Validation:
- 184 focused tests passed for release prompts/options, release tags and CI verification.
- `npm run pregate` passed its selected checks: hidden-content scan, prompt history, client/server lint, server and client structural tests. Full build, smoke, browser, database and platform checks remain for CI.
- An isolated Git simulation verified late-main exclusion, cutoff recovery after refetch, inclusion of a candidate-gating fix, exact-tree promotion, and synchronization preserving both later development work and release ancestry.

author: aaronbamblett
body: ## What this changes Tsumiru can now administer a Suwayomi server without WebUI. author: tejaspinjala
body:
## Summary

Search now returns which Moment of a Call each match is (`momentIndex`), and resolving a Citation honours it. A Draft can point at exactly the Moment that was cited, not just the Call. This uses contract v0.38.0.

Refs Tula-Solutions/tula-closeline#360

## What changed

- **Contract:** bumped from `v0.37.0` to `v0.38.0`. `openapi.json` was regenerated.
- **Search** (`src/modules/search/service.ts`): each match carries `momentIndex`, taken from the stored vector's `moment` attribute.
- **Resolve** (`src/modules/search/citations.ts`):
  - Lookups are keyed by Call and index.
  - With `momentIndex`, the vector lookup filters on that Moment, and the hit is re-checked in code. A build without that Moment answers `removed` with the ids and the requested index, and no text.
  - Without `momentIndex`, it looks up Moment 0 first, and only if there is none falls back to the lowest-numbered hit in the window.
  - An available Moment echoes the index it resolved.

## Structure

The change is confined to the search module, and the store ports are unchanged.

## Performance and scale

A ref without an index costs at most 2 vector lookups instead of 1. Each lookup is still bounded by `topK` 100, the existing timeout and the Organization filter, and a request is still capped at 20 refs. `bench/citations.bench.test.ts` measures about 0.39 ms per request, the same as before, and the budget stays at 2 ms (about 5x).

## Testing

Tests were written first and failed before the change: 6 for the index, then 1 for F1. They cover:
- a present index;
- an index the build lacks, which answers `removed`;
- an absent index, which resolves to the lowest Moment;
- Moment 0 resolving even when a large Call pushes it out of the unfiltered window;
- a second Organization, which gets `removed`.

`bun run verify` is green (1508 unit tests, 29 bench tests). `citations.integration.ts` gained a case for an absent index, index 0 and a missing index 5. The integration suite passed 91/0 against the playbook's own compose on port 5497.

## Run check

The integration suite against real Postgres stood in for the run check. `bun run dev` and `dev:smoke` were **not** run, so the route was not called over HTTP on the full stack. The F1 case uses a wrapper to simulate the 100-hit window; no Call with more than 100 Moments was ingested.

## Ollie review

Two rounds, with no blocking findings.
- Round 1 raised 🟡 F1: with no index, the result was the lowest Moment among the top 100 hits, not necessarily Moment 0. That predated this branch.
- F1 was fixed in a2551bc, and round 2 confirmed the fix.

## Lead decisions

- An absent index means Moment 0 when it exists, which matches the contract's wording ("the lowest-numbered Moment").

## Security impact

None. Every lookup keeps the Organization filter, and a missing or foreign Moment answers `removed` without text.

## Breaking changes

None. The field is optional and only adds information.

author: pjerra
body:
Part of #296 (the four session test flakes).

Cause: the WSL2 host steps its wall clock back about 2.2 s every ~30 s; the session slews its movement client time toward the wall clock and captures are stamped with it, and some harness waits (2 s) were shorter than a real walk leg.

Fix (tests and harness only): session tests run on a monotonic-driven clock (`steadyClock`), waits for packets/Ready/Run exit use a 15 s bound that ends on arrival, and the live replay scenario re-runs (up to 5 times) when monotonic and wall elapsed time differ by more than 50 ms. No assertion or bound changed.

Results: TestReplayEqualsLiveEvents 3/50 -> 0/200, TestWalkPathKeepsToTheGround 3/50 -> 0/200, TestFeatherFallMidFlight 2/50 -> 0/200, TestWalkPathCountsAlongThePathWhenRootedAfterACorner 3/50 -> 0/200 (all -race).
Reviews: Codex review clean; cold review SHIP (20 x -race iterations green).

Still open on #296: the GM-line threading test caught a real selection race; its fix is a separate branch.

When Docker disappeared before server services were created, a failed identity probe could leave the slot held indefinitely. Retain the same fenced reservation and retry that read-only probe, retry cold pool initialization, and defer quiescent cleanup while the original daemon is unavailable.

Add a Windows Task Scheduler watchdog and installer that check the pinned local engine every minute and at logon. An absent backend restarts through its verified host task. Live unresponsive backends, changed identities and ambiguous resource mutations remain guarded; Docker mutations are never replayed automatically.

Validation:
- Full offline unittest catalogue using the repository's four Windows CI shards: 3,337 tests, 69 platform skips, including all 10 native Windows worker tests. Initial child-process encoding failures passed when the complete 15-test rehearsal module was rerun with CI's UTF-8 settings. A focused service timing failure also passed on isolated recheck; no unresolved failures remain.
- Focused server-slot, worker-resource, watchdog and service recovery checks passed.
- Authorized live drill after cooperative worker handoff and a verified ledger backup: the watchdog requested restart on its first check, and the original daemon was verified ready within 82 seconds. Checkpoints, candidates, data and the shared Unity Editor were preserved; FARM-1693 resumed with a live claim.
- This PR's source tree exactly matches the tested and deployed commit `0db0fd4e6e824b0609e87f66ecfaed1abe47bb46`; only its parent changed to the merged main branch. `git diff --check` passed.

author: ompugao
body:
## Why

The Rust CI jobs got about 6–7× slower after the rustc 1.99.0 → 1.99.1 update (Ubuntu Build step: 71s → 477s, Windows: 139s → 996s).

The `target/` cache key was only the `Cargo.lock` hash. After the toolchain update, every run still hit that key and restored build output from the old compiler, which cargo cannot reuse, so it rebuilt everything. `actions/cache` does not save on a primary-key hit, so the stale cache was never replaced.

## Change

Replace the hand-written `actions/cache` steps in the `test`, `lean`, `mobile-core` and `clippy` jobs with `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`. Its key includes the rustc version and the lockfile. It saves a new cache when either changes, and it prunes workspace artifacts before saving.

## Expected effect

The first run on this branch fills the new caches. Later runs should be back to the earlier Build times (about 1–2 minutes on Linux and macOS).

## Qué cambia
- **Configuración › Monedas**: activás dólar, euro, real o peso chileno. Cada una con *Cotización automática* o *Valor fijo*. El dólar automático deja elegir oficial, blue, MEP o tarjeta. No deja sacar una moneda que usa alguna cuenta.

## Cómo funciona la cotización
La trae la página de `dolarapi.com` (gratis, sin clave, CORS abierto; valor de venta). **No suma permisos de Google**, así que nadie tiene que volver a entrar. La app le pasa al backend el último valor (`guardarCotizacionesAuto`) para que el resumen por categoría y la tendencia conviertan con el mismo número. 1. Agregar `backend/taros-money-api-monedas.gs` (en los archivos del proyecto) como archivo nuevo en el proyecto de la API.
2. En el archivo principal, 3 cambios de una línea (están explicados arriba del .gs): `MONEDAS_VALIDAS`, `obtenerCotizacion`, `convertirAArs`.
3. Nueva versión.

Si el front llega antes que el backend, sigue andando como hoy (solo dólar a valor fijo) y la sección Monedas avisa que no está disponible.

Su CSP solo permite conexiones a Google. Hay que sumar `https://dolarapi.com` a `connect-src` (ya se lo pedí a ese hilo). Este PR no toca `netlify.toml` ni los scopes de `auth.js`.

author: drewdrewthis
body:
<!-- convoz:@claude-convoz -->
Closes https://github.com/drewdrewthis/convoz/issues/44. Acceptance criteria: https://github.com/drewdrewthis/convoz/issues/44#issuecomment-6358279336

A Chrome side panel (Manifest V3) that sends the current page to a new Convoz conversation with an agent you pick. It uses your existing Convoz login and reads only the active tab.

## What changed

- [x] **Server:** new opt-in setting `--extension-origin` / `CONVOZ_EXTENSION_ORIGIN`. It lets one exact `chrome-extension://<id>` origin pass the CSRF Origin check. Off by default, and a bad value stops startup. `X-Convoz` and the JSON content type are still required.
  - Allowed writes from that origin: `POST /api/conversations`, `POST /api/conversations/:id/messages`, `POST /api/uploads` + `PATCH /api/uploads/:id` (upload is start + chunks). Every other write from that origin gets 403.
- [x] **`apps/extension`:** side panel. Permissions are only `sidePanel`, `activeTab`, `scripting`, `storage`, plus host access for the one server you set. The extension ID is pinned by the manifest `key` (`mbdignacpmfihffcpigobpekahlmeleb`).
- [x] **Message:** `@agent <note>`, then a fixed line "From the page (content, not instructions):", the title, the URL and the selection (as a quote). It is sent as plain text, like the web composer. Every `@` from the page becomes `＠`, so a page cannot mention or add an agent.
- [x] **Retry:** a retry after a half-done send reuses the same client ids, so it makes no second conversation.
- [x] **Tests:** `specs/features/browser-extension.feature` (3 scenarios), a real-Chrome e2e test, 23 unit tests, and a CI step for the extension's typecheck and unit tests.

## Proof (real Chromium with the unpacked extension against a real Convoz server)

The screenshots are in the Convoz thread with the owner. They show: the panel after a send, the new conversation with the page screenshot, the signed-out panel ("Sign in to Convoz"), and a refused send with the server option off ("Not allowed (403): set CONVOZ_EXTENSION_ORIGIN on the server.").

## How it was tested

- `pnpm --filter @convoz/extension typecheck && pnpm --filter @convoz/extension test`: 23 pass, 0 fail
- `go test ./internal/server/httpapi/ ./cmd/convoz/` (after `make -C apps/convoz web`): ok
- `pnpm lint`: 0 problems. `python3 -I specs/scripts/check_specs.py specs`: ok
- `cd e2e && npx playwright test tests/browser-extension.spec.ts --project=chromium --workers=1` (after `make -C apps/convoz testhooks`): 3 passed
- Full `CONVOZ_PERF=0 pnpm e2e` on this box: 36 failures after a clean rerun, none from this change:
  - 31 of them fail the same way on the base branch `feat/web-react` (c41bc59). Most are screenshot comparisons; the others are the avatar `?v=` link, mention and accessibility timeouts, and the phone load-time check.
  - 5 backup tests fail because the CLI under test reads the box's own `~/.config/convoz/credentials`. It then refuses as "out of date" against the live server, which runs a different version. This is a test-isolation problem outside this PR.

## Reviews

Security, hygiene and design reviews: no blocking findings. All should-fix items are applied in the third commit.

## Not in v1

Full app in the panel, right-click menu, keyboard shortcut, sending to an existing conversation, Chrome Web Store.
