author: aliromman
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Proves a necessary completion bound for a simple hypercube path and a functional that omits one coordinate. The bound counts unused matching edges and endpoint capacity, including the final edge to the start. It rejects prefixes that pass matching balance and return distance. This is an enabling proof with finite corroboration; there is no engine change, runtime claim or change to the complete kappa calculation (`60403/20000000`).

[Proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fe3226ea4e36469f43c6b116c5b98cc221a9b1af/research/f7-prefix-matching-capacity/README.md), [exact receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fe3226ea4e36469f43c6b116c5b98cc221a9b1af/research/f7-prefix-matching-capacity/RESULT.json), [verifier](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fe3226ea4e36469f43c6b116c5b98cc221a9b1af/research/f7-prefix-matching-capacity/verify.py), and [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fe3226ea4e36469f43c6b116c5b98cc221a9b1af/research/f7-prefix-matching-capacity/SOURCES.json).

The written condition covers `n >= 2`, even `4 <= L <= 2^n`, and simple prefixes with 2 through L vertices. Universality is not required. The returned splits are necessary conditions, not certificates that a completion exists.

## Task and overlap

Answers Open next question 2 of [PR #4907](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4907). The sharp cap in [PR #4992](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4992) is related context, not a dependency. Base: `bee95ce88f9f19802f0613f92838895cd0e14a1f`, priority revision 7. Main was unchanged at submission. The refreshed search covered 308 open PRs, 4,096 Discussion records and 65 of 6,690 local notes, followed by relevant direct reads. Sparse omissions, arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain outside that coverage.

## Validation

CPython 3.12, standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/f7-prefix-matching-capacity
```

Expected: `PASS_F7_PREFIX_MATCHING_CAPACITY` in both normal and optimized commands, then `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

Passed: 110,655 prefix/functional checks across four domains; exact descendant-split containment; 3,838 closed cycles; independent literal-word enumeration in two domains; 640 capacity cases; ten boundary controls. There are 704 strict rejections before the leaf relative to matching balance and return distance. Five actual code mutations fail with `false completion prune`, including omission of the closing edge or endpoint partners. Committed-byte checks, all four exact source pins and Git-free read-only optimized export replay pass.

The full-history wrapper was not run in the shallow checkout; the pinned base ancestry and all source blobs/SHA-256 values were checked directly. No seven-label census, maintained-engine comparison, selected cold replay, independent human review or formal proof-kernel check ran.

## Credit

Nick Petalas supplied matching balance in [PR #4894](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4894); Mihir Srivastava supplied the explicit handoff in [PR #4907](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4907). Their [retained proof notice](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bee95ce88f9f19802f0613f92838895cd0e14a1f/research/f7-five-label-pruning-proof/README.md) credits Ross Richardson's prefix model and Nicholas Stone's parity correction. No predecessor code is imported. Prepared for Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Measure an opt-in engine implementation against unchanged leaf receipts and runtime. The cost of this condition can exceed the work saved; integration and a performance gain remain unproved.

author: ianonjuguna
body:
Closes #198

## What changed

One section in `docs/operations.md`: §9, **the convert book is a measurement, not a constant**.

Settlement prices every swap against Tempo's stablecoin book, and the runbook said nothing about what happens when that book has no resting liquidity. On practice the answer is that nothing converts, silently: every pathUSD holding is skipped as `no-market`, so the settlement happy path cannot be run there at all.

Measured today, read-only, through the server's own pricing path (`quoteDexConvert`, the same call `classifySettle` uses), pathUSD to OUSD:

| Network | Result |
| --- | --- |
| mainnet (4217) | quotes at every size tried, 10 to 1,000,000 units; at 1,000,000 in, 999,922.37 out (about 0.008% impact) |
| practice (42431) | quotes nothing, down to 10 units; `quoteSwapExactAmountIn` reverts, selector `0xbb55fd27` |

Three consequences are written down: practice skips every pathUSD balance as `no-market` so settlement has to be exercised on mainnet or after seeding the practice book; a balance trimmed to fit a book is not evidence the book is still there; and **the "~2,388 units" an earlier scratch script recorded was a snapshot of that day**, not a rule and not a mainnet property. Mainnet has since quoted a million.

The section also states what the probe cannot answer: it reads the quoter, so an empty book and a pair whose tokens are not registered the way the DEX expects both arrive as a revert. If practice has to quote and does not, compare `backend/src/config/networks.ts` against the DEX's own listing before concluding the book is empty.

## How it was verified

The numbers are the verification, and the section says how they were taken so they can be retaken: a throwaway script importing `quoteDexConvert` and stepping sizes from 10 to 1,000,000 units against both networks. It was deleted after the run, so no probe is left in the tree.

`git diff` adds 34 lines to one markdown file and touches no code, no config and no check suite, so `npm run verify` is unaffected. This is the kind of change nothing compiles: the gate is reading it against the two RPCs, which is what the table is.

## Decisions and tradeoffs

**No constant, no threshold.** The tempting version of this section is "the book fills up to N"; that is exactly the mistake the old scratch script made. The section gives a dated measurement and names the date, so a reader knows how much to trust it.

**The caveat is in the document, not only in this PR.** A probe that reports what the quoter answers looks like a probe that reports why the market is missing, and the next operator will read it that way unless told not to.

**§9 rather than a renumber.** `deploy-oracle.md` cross-references `operations.md` §1, §4 and §7 by number, so inserting a section mid-document would have quietly broken three links.

## Risk and rollback

Docs only. The risk it removes is an operator trusting a dead book as if it were live, or inventing a limit from a snapshot. Rollback: revert the one commit.

## Screenshots

None: no surface.

author: zhangjlfdf
body:
## 根因

`ws_task_room` 把同一个 SQLAlchemy `Session` 复用在整条 WebSocket 连接上，welcome 快照只读 `users` / `task_comment_read` / `task_comment_read_record` 之后不提交。`autocommit=False` 下这就是一个 **idle-in-transaction**：事务期间取得的表级 MDL 一直挂到连接断开。

`users` 是 `companies` 的外键子表（`users_ibfk_2: company_id -> companies.id`），所以这个长事务连 `ALTER TABLE companies` 也能堵住。部署的 `schema_sync.py` 设了 `lock_wait_timeout = 15`，第一条补列就抛 `1205`，整次发版中止 —— 2026-10-23 两次 prod 部署（39905944436 / 39907977494）均因此失败，7 个新列一条都没落地。

现场证据（prod `helpdesk_724`，只读查询 `performance_schema.metadata_locks`）：服务重启 8 秒后就有 4 条 `Sleep` 连接分别持有 `users` / `task_comment_read` / `task_comment_read_record` 的 `SHARED_READ`（`lock_duration=TRANSACTION`），它们的最后一条语句正是 welcome 里的 `SELECT ... FROM users`，此后再无 `ROLLBACK`。

## 改动

**应用侧（根治，`backend/app/modules/tasks/api/ws.py`）**
- welcome 快照改走 `_welcome_snapshot()`：独立短会话，查完显式 `rollback()` 并关闭
- 已读上报改走 `_report_read_once()`：每次一个新会话，写完即关，事务不跨帧存活
- 移除常驻 `db` 与 `finally` 里的 `db.close()`（已无常驻会话）

**脚本侧（加固，`backend/scripts/schema_sync.py`）**
- `lock_wait_timeout` 15s → 45s，给应用侧短事务留收尾窗口
- DDL 遇 `1205/1213` 退避重试 3 次（间隔 5s）；**其他错误立即失败**，不掩盖真问题
- 重试期间打印当前持有表级 MDL 的会话（只读，绝不 KILL）
- 修正诊断查询列名：`metadata_locks` 实际列为 `OBJECT_NAME`（原写 `OBJECT_TABLE_NAME` 必报 1054 并被吞掉，提示永远打不出来），并限定 `OBJECT_TYPE='TABLE'`

## 验证

- 定向：`pytest tests/test_schema_sync.py tests/test_ws_session_lifetime.py` → **43 passed**
- 本地全量：`pytest --ignore=tests/tasks --continue-on-collection-errors` → **500 passed、1 failed、146 errors**；失败与错误全部是本机环境问题（缺 `aiosqlite`、`alembic` 版本不兼容报 `No module named 'alembic.migration'`、SQLite 方言编译 MySQL DDL 失败），与本次改动无关
- prod 真库实测：修正后的诊断 SQL 在 `helpdesk_724` 上执行返回正常（`[OK]` 10 行），确认列名正确
- 新增用例守住不变量：会重试锁冲突、重试耗尽必须抛出（不静默跳过缺列）、非锁错误不重试、诊断查询失败不影响补列、诊断 SQL 不得引用不存在的列；WS 侧守住「用完即结束事务」（含查询抛异常也要 rollback + 关闭）

## 上线注意（重要）

prod 部署取 **dev** 分支，且本次修复必须先到 prod 才生效；而只要旧代码还在跑、有人开着工单详情页，补列 DDL 仍会被堵。落地顺序：

1. PR 合入 `test`（需他人 approve）→ 再按常规把 `test` 合入 `dev`
2. 低峰期停后端：`supervisorctl stop openrobot`（125.122.97.107:8802，`usp-a` 在 supervisor 组，免 sudo）
3. 手动触发 Deploy workflow：`environment=prod`、`confirm=DEPLOY-PROD`、`git_ref` 留空（→ dev）
4. deploy 末尾自带 `supervisorctl restart openrobot`，服务自动拉起；此时无 WS 连接，7 条 `ADD COLUMN` 一次过

窗口想更短也可以：停服 → 手工执行那 7 条 `ADD COLUMN` → `supervisorctl start openrobot` → 再跑流水线。

临时规避只治标：`supervisorctl restart openrobot` 能清掉泄漏会话，但用户一刷新页面就会重新长出来。

## 上线后确认

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM performance_schema.metadata_locks
WHERE OBJECT_SCHEMA = 'helpdesk_724' AND OBJECT_TYPE = 'TABLE'
  AND LOCK_STATUS = 'GRANTED' AND LOCK_DURATION = 'TRANSACTION';
```

应为 0（或仅偶发的正在执行语句），不再出现长时间 `Sleep` 连接持 `users` 表锁。

body:
## Problem

`TestIntegrationStdioCallReturnsAtItsDeadlineWhenTheServerStopsReadingStdin` fails intermittently in the integration job:

```
--- FAIL: TestIntegrationStdioCallReturnsAtItsDeadlineWhenTheServerStopsReadingStdin (0.75s)
    stdio_integration_test.go:152: Call error = context deadline exceeded, want the interrupted write
```

Failed runs: [39885348171](https://github.com/mcpmini/mini/actions/runs/39885348171) (attempt 1), [39884659797](https://github.com/mcpmini/mini/actions/runs/39884659797), [39885347672](https://github.com/mcpmini/mini/actions/runs/39885347672).

The test gives `Call` a real 200ms deadline and expects the write of a 1MB payload to block on the full pipe and be interrupted. Under `-race` on a loaded runner, `json.Marshal` of that payload alone took 176–415ms, so the deadline passed before the write began. `writeJSONContext` then correctly returns the plain context error without writing anything (and keeps the connection). That is the "cancelled before the write" path, not the one this test covers. Timing from an instrumented stress run ([39895915603](https://github.com/mcpmini/mini/actions/runs/39895915603)):

```
Call error = DEBUG lockWrite marshal=404.749297ms total=404.759155ms deadlineLeftAtStart=159.665832ms: context deadline exceeded
Call error = DEBUG postlock marshal=202.212278ms total=213.300135ms deadlineLeftAtStart=175.190599ms: context deadline exceeded
```

Product behavior is correct. The test is racing its own deadline.

## Fix

The deadline runs on a fake clock (`clock.WithTimeout` + `clock.Fake`), and the test advances it only after `Call` starts writing to the child's real stdin pipe, which a thin wrapper signals. Everything else stays real: the subprocess, the OS pipe, and `SetWriteDeadline` interrupting the blocked write. With the interruption disabled, the test still fails at its 5s hang guard.

Alternatives considered: a longer real deadline (still races, only less often), and pre-encoding the payload (scheduling delay before the write can still use up the deadline).

## Stress (same workflow: full integration suite, `-race -parallel 16`, 20 shards × 8 rounds)

| Branch | Failed rounds | Run |
|---|---|---|
| main (e0c8b9bc) | 48 / 160, all this test | [39895926755](https://github.com/mcpmini/mini/actions/runs/39895926755) |
| this fix | 0 / 160 | [39896547215](https://github.com/mcpmini/mini/actions/runs/39896547215) |

`./check.sh` passes locally.

author: debayush1
body:
## User Story

As a user, I want a grocery list to be generated from my weekly meal plan so that I know which ingredients I need to buy.

## Acceptance Criteria Met

- [x] The grocery list includes ingredients from all recipes in the weekly meal plan.
- [x] Ingredients used across multiple planned recipes are aggregated into a single entry with combined quantities.
- [x] Exact ingredient quantities are displayed for essential items, including meat, eggs, produce, dairy, and grains.
- [x] Spices, seasonings, and garlic are categorized as pantry staples without displaying unnecessary micro-measurements.
- [x] The grocery list updates dynamically whenever the weekly meal plan changes.

## Key Changes

### Backend
- Added the `MealPlanItem` database model with cascading foreign key relationships.
- Implemented `/api/meal-plan` endpoints (`GET`, `POST`, and `DELETE`) for weekly meal plan persistence.
- Added the `/api/grocery-list` endpoint with aisle-based ingredient categorization:
  - Produce
  - Meat & Seafood
  - Dairy & Eggs
  - Bakery & Grains
  - Spices & Seasonings
- Integrated Groq AI using `openai/gpt-oss-20b` to automatically categorize new or unrecognized ingredients from future recipes.
- Added backend unit tests, with all 8 tests passing.

### Frontend
- Replaced the grocery list placeholder with an interactive, categorized grocery checklist.
- Added a one-click **"Check All Pantry Staples"** button.
- Connected the Weekly Planner to backend persistence.
- Added direct navigation links to the grocery list for a seamless user experience.

## Testing
- [x] All 8 backend unit tests pass.
- [x] Grocery ingredients are aggregated across planned recipes.
- [x] Grocery items are organized into appropriate categories.
- [x] Weekly meal plan changes are reflected in the grocery list.

## Summary

This PR connects the Weekly Planner with the Grocery List, enabling users to generate an organized shopping list directly from their planned meals. It also introduces AI-powered ingredient categorization and an interactive checklist to make grocery planning easier and more efficient.

author: klurvio
body:
ADR-0040 Tier2 (live) for the Go SDK — the parallel of the sdk-js and sdk-py live suites. Drives the real `sukko.Client` against the **latest released** platform (published GHCR images, verified by the committed prod-signed Community license, kafka backend), not a source build.

## Cells (`e2e/`, build-tagged `e2e`, env-driven)
- **round-trip** — REST publish **and** the fire-and-forget WebSocket `Publish` both deliver back; asserts the kafka `Pos` cursor. The WS leg exercises the client→gateway send path (would catch a transport sending client frames on the wrong opcode — the bug the Python SDK shipped; sdk-go writes `MessageText`, so it is clean).
- **api-key auth** — an `X-API-Key` client subscribes and receives; a JWT client publishes (API keys are read-only).
- **kafka gap→replay recovery** — the subscriber dials through an in-process TCP proxy that **holds** (not refuses) its reconnect while a direct publisher lands messages offline; on restore the SDK replays from its last position. Asserts seq 2+3 replayed and the anchor not re-delivered (exclusive cursor).
- **push VAPID** — skipped on Community (Pro-gated), recorded rather than omitted.

## Verification
- Full live suite green against the released Community+kafka stack: round-trip, api-key, recovery pass; push skips.
- Recovery proven **non-vacuous** by a both-sides mutation: with `WithReconnect(false)` the replay wait fails (30s timeout); with reconnect it passes.
- `-race` throughout. Normal `build`/`vet`/unit gate unchanged — the `e2e` dir is excluded without the tag.

## Harness / CI
- `e2e/run.sh` boots the released stack via the `sukko` CLI, provisions a demo-tenant fixture, exports `SUKKO_IT_*`, runs `go test -race -tags e2e`.
- `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` runs nightly + on a `run-e2e` label, never on every PR.

Test-only; no SDK release owed.

author: kare0638
singlebanana2632
body:
### Summary
Addresses connection failures and Bluetooth system bans (`APPLICATION_REGISTRATION_FAILED`, `HciStatus 257`) on Android 17 (API 37) caused by client registration quotas and timing changes during GATT parameter negotiation.

### The Problems
1. **GATT Client Leaks & System Bans (`status=257`):**
   Modern Android enforces a strict process-level quota on registered GATT clients. Previously, `BluetoothScannerManager`, `BleConnector`, and various scale adapters each initialized independent instances of `BluetoothCentralManager`. On Android 17, repeated discovery or reconnect loops quickly exhausted the system table, resulting in permanent `status=257` client registration failures until the Bluetooth stack was toggled.
2. **GATT Queue Stalls Post-Discovery:**
   Android 17 applies connection parameter updates (e.g., `interval=9`) immediately after service discovery. Initiating characteristic operations concurrently with this handshake can cause packet drops or timeouts on stricter BLE stacks.

### Key Changes
* **Singleton `BluetoothCentralManager` (`BluetoothFacade.kt`):**
  Instantiates a single, lazy application-scoped `BluetoothCentralManager` in `BluetoothFacade`. System BLE events are routed through a composite `internalCentralCallback` to `BleConnector` and `BluetoothScannerManager`.
* **Post-Scan Cooldown:**
  Added a 1500 ms cooldown after stopping scanning before initiating connection in `BluetoothFacade`, allowing the OS client registration table to clear.
* **Post-Discovery Delay (`ModernScaleAdapter.kt`):**
  Added `postDiscoverDelayMs` to `BleGattTuning` (100 ms for Balanced, 150 ms for Conservative) to allow the link to settle before starting GATT I/O.
* **Shared Instance Propagation:**
  Updated `ScaleFactory` and `BroadcastScaleAdapter` to accept the shared manager instead of creating per-instance clients.
* **Lifecycle Fix (`BluetoothViewModel.kt`):**
  Removed `bt.close()` from `onCleared()` with documentation explaining that `BluetoothFacade` is an application singleton managed by Hilt.
* **Permissions (`AndroidManifest.xml` & `BluetoothScreen.kt`):**
  Restricted `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` with `android:maxSdkVersion="30"` for backward compatibility without forcing location on API 31+. Re-checks actual granted state on callback.

### Verification
- [x] Verified on physical Google Pixel running Android 17 (API 37).
- [x] Verified that repeated scan/connect/disconnect loops no longer trip `APPLICATION_REGISTRATION_FAILED` or leak clients.
- [x] Verified existing unit tests pass (`ScaleFactoryDeveloperModeTest`).

## Summary

`Nightly` on `main` is red in the `security` job. `just audit` reports three advisories. certifi is fixed by #84. This PR fixes the other two.

- **virtualenv 21.14.5** (CVE-2026-113725, CVE-2026-113722). It is a dev dependency through `pre-commit`. `uv lock --upgrade-package virtualenv` in both locks moves it to 21.14.13. The root lock also moves `python-discovery` 1.6.0 → 1.6.4, because virtualenv 21.14.13 needs `>=1.6.1`.
- **opentelemetry-api 1.44.0** (CVE-2026-114603: unbounded parsing of inbound `tracestate` headers). Nightly never showed it, because the root audit fails first. The lock could not move past 1.44.0: from 1.45.0 the OTLP exporter needs `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-common`, which only ships beta versions. Under `prerelease = "explicit"` uv did not fail; it silently kept the whole OpenTelemetry set on 1.44.0. The fix adds that package to the template's `constraint-dependencies` (same pattern as the four existing entries) and corrects the comment that said this case always fails `uv lock`. Then `just regen`, and the example lock upgrades OpenTelemetry to 1.45.1 / 0.66b1.

No new kind of pre-release: the `0.66b1` versions are the instrumentation's permanent beta line, which the lock already used at `0.65b0`.

Nightly will still be red after this PR and #84 land. `just scan` has a separate Trivy finding in the `migrate` binary, which needs a human decision: #86.

author: gregpriday
body:
## Summary
- Plugin project-database creation, migration and writes now obey the remote drive lease, the same way `host.fs`, settings and process APIs already do.
- A view that only watches the project can no longer create or write a project database. `db.open`/`db.resolve` with a writable handle rejects `DRIVEN_ELSEWHERE` before the consent prompt, creates nothing, and is re-checked after consent.
- A handle opened before a takeover loses write authority, since every call on a writable handle re-checks the lease.

Resolves #14094

## Changes
- Writable handles re-check before every call: `run`/`exec`/`transaction`, plus `query`/`get`/`columns` because `RETURNING` can write.
- The checked path is the database's declared path plus the handle's resolved path, so nested projects and moved links are covered.
- Worker handles ask main through a new internal `db.authorizeWrite` host call, and only inside an invocation. Background work skips the round trip.
- A transaction's `tx` statements stop working once its callback settles.
- Readonly handles, local databases, background work and agent MCP tool calls stay unchecked. `docs/plugins/host-api.md` documents this and says it is not a sandbox.
- Backup destinations were already gated through the `host.fs` write approver.

Not changed, worth a follow-up:
- The dev-worker bridge treats an expired invocation id as background for every host call, db included.
- There are no per-statement checks inside a running transaction. It is checked at entry, like the other APIs.

## Testing
- New `electron/services/plugin/__tests__/pluginDriveLeaseDatabase.test.ts`. 4 of its 8 tests fail on unmodified code.
- Added coverage in `pluginDevWorkerHostProxy.test.ts` and `PluginDevWorkerMainBridge.test.ts`.

author: alexandersmyslowski
body:
Reopening a saved production case can still report an unavailable draft because its old handoff link refers to a replaced source revision. It also loses the main read action once the editing step is completed.

The panel now explains the applied successor and offers an explicit view switch only when a complete replacement chain leads to a server-confirmed apply of that exact revision. The original draft is never labeled as applied. Completed production cases with a persisted result keep the existing read action, named “Plan und Einkauf anzeigen”; archived cases and completed cases without a result stay terminal.

No API writes, approval changes, data changes or automatic navigation are introduced. Missing, unrelated, incomplete or ambiguous ancestry retains the cautious state.

Validation: reproduced both regressions; 26 draft-panel tests and 34 affected action/bar/flow/integration tests pass. TypeScript, Vite build and diff checks pass. Independent reviews accepted the two scoped deltas. A local synthetic 390px browser preview confirmed the existing read handler focuses and scrolls to the result; this is not a new Nürnberg acceptance. Not yet installed on Nürnberg.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-10-16

### Added

**Backend**
- FastAPI application with health check endpoint (`GET /api/health`)
- SQLite database via SQLAlchemy 2.0 with declarative models
  (`Profile`, `JobPosting`, `EvaluationResult`)
- Pydantic schemas for all request/response models
- ScoringEngine with 5-dimension weighted scoring:
  - Skills match (Jaccard similarity, weight 0.40)
  - Experience level (ordinal comparison, weight 0.20)
  - Location affinity (weight 0.15)
  - Role type (title keyword overlap, weight 0.15)
  - Dealbreakers (binary, weight 0.10)
- Text processing utilities: normalization, BOM stripping, skill extraction
  with word-boundary matching, experience-level detection, slug generation
  with Unicode transliteration
- REST API endpoints:
  - `PUT /api/v1/profiles/default` — upsert default profile
  - `GET /api/v1/profiles/default` — retrieve default profile
  - `POST /api/v1/jobs` — create job posting (auto-extracts skills)
  - `GET /api/v1/jobs` — list jobs
  - `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}` — get job by ID
  - `POST /api/v1/evaluations` — evaluate a job against profile
  - `GET /api/v1/evaluations` — list evaluations
  - `GET /api/v1/ranking` — rank evaluated jobs by score
- Pydantic-settings configuration with environment variable support
- COR

Validation: secret-scan, WIP: application QA not completed; no release-readiness claim; review deferred; hosted Actions disabled.

body:
Implemented 'The Halal Pharmacy' desktop POS webapp using Svelte 5, Tailwind CSS v4, and Dexie IndexedDB for 100% offline functionality.

Key features created:
1. Sale Page (POS): Search by generic name, brand, or strength, live cart calculations, anonymous checkout, invoice receipts, and Bill Hold functionality.
2. Dashboard: Revenue analytics, items sold, active inventory count, low stock (< 10 units) & expiry warnings, recent transactions, and top sellers.
3. Add Medicine: Auto Mode (search & auto-fill from MedEx catalog dataset) and Manual Mode (custom brand, generic, power, price, stock).
4. Records: Comprehensive transaction audit trail with date/payment filters, receipt modal, void/refund with automatic restocking, and CSV export.
5. Settings: Day/Night (Light/Dark) mode toggle, MedEx catalog quick refetch & 7-day auto-refetch schedule, sample data seeding & reset tools.
6. Documentation: Complete AGENTS.md and README.md detailing offline database architecture, features, and setup.

author: abasset1
body:
## Contexte

Le contrôle de la base bêta (22/10/2026) a relevé de nombreux doublons exacts : même source, même titre, même jour. Par exemple, l'agenda VélOOise publie 42 fois « Atelier d'aide à la réparation – Nogent-sur-Oise », avec 42 identifiants OpenAgenda différents mais les mêmes horaires et le même lieu.

Le détail (`doublons_detail.sql`) montre que ce n'est pas un réimport défaillant : les clés d'import sont toutes distinctes, ce sont des événements distincts côté source. Il y a deux cas :
- **de vraies copies**, avec les mêmes créneaux et le même lieu : VélOOise, et une partie de France Travail ;
- **des créneaux ou des lieux différents** publiés sous un même titre, par exemple « Atelier senior 360 » dans 13 villes le même jour. Ce ne sont pas des doublons.

## Changements

### Import (`ImportService`, nouvelle règle pure `SameSourceDuplicates`)
- Avant le traitement des éléments, ceux d'une même collecte sont regroupés par **signature** : titre normalisé (casse, espaces), **tous** les créneaux (début et fin) et lieu (position, adresse, commune). Un élément sans titre, sans créneau ou sans lieu n'est jamais rapproché.
- Un seul élément par groupe est importé : celui qui a l'**activité publiée la plus ancienne** (plus petit id), sinon la plus petite clé d'import. Le choix est stable d'un import à l'autre, et l'activité déjà visible le reste.
- Les autres sont comptés dans `ImportResult.duplicates`. Leur activité, si elle est publiée, est archivée, même inchangée : la règle passe avant l'import incrémental. Une activité dans un autre statut, par exemple annulée par un administrateur, n'est pas modifiée.
- Si l'élément conservé disparaît de la source, une copie restante devient la conservée et son activité est republiée au prochain import.
- Cet archivage ne passe pas par le garde-fou d'archivage massif : il ne dépend pas d'une disparition, puisque la source publie toujours l'événement.

### Scripts de contrôle (`infra/verification/`, lecture seule)
- `controle_beta.sql` :
  - une requête en erreur n'interrompt plus les suivantes (`ON_ERROR_ROLLBACK`) ;
  - un `lock_timeout` distingue une table verrouillée d'une requête lente ;
  - nouvelle section 0 : sessions et verrous en cours ;
  - la section 2a est réécrite : l'ancienne version relisait `activity` une fois par source et dépassait le délai avec 4 721 sources ;
  - les sections sur les sources sont résumées.
- `doublons_detail.sql` (nouveau) : nature des doublons exacts (clés d'import, horaires, lieux, URL et dates de création distincts).

### Documentation
- `docs/02_Architecture/COLLECTOR_OPERATIONS.md` : nouvelle section « Déduplication dans une même source ».
- `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Tests
- `SameSourceDuplicatesTest` (6 tests) : copies regroupées ; casse et espaces ignorés ; créneaux, lieux et heures de fin différents gardés distincts ; tous les créneaux comparés quel que soit leur ordre ; jamais de rapprochement sans créneau ni lieu ; même clé collectée deux fois non traitée comme un doublon.
- `ImportServiceTest` (5 nouveaux tests) : une seule copie créée ; la plus ancienne publiée conservée et l'autre archivée ; copie annulée laissée intacte ; republication quand la copie conservée quitte la source ; créneaux différents tous importés.
- `mvn verify` en local, comme la CI (PostgreSQL/PostGIS 16) : **BUILD SUCCESS, 1 489 tests, 0 échec**.
- Scripts SQL testés sur des bases locales migrées jusqu'à V62 et V74, y compris avec un verrou simulé.

## Effet attendu après déploiement
Au premier import horaire, les copies en trop déjà publiées sont archivées. Le chiffre de 2 911 est une borne haute : elle compte aussi des créneaux et lieux distincts, qui restent publiés. Vérification : compteur « doublons » dans les logs `Import planifie termine`, puis nouveau passage de `doublons_detail.sql`.

author: js10839
body:
### What is this PR?

- **변경 내용**: Flutter 앱의 기본 라우팅을 `go_router`로 전환하고, 홈·날짜 선택·기간 선택 화면에서 공유할 월 달력 컴포넌트를 추가합니다. 온보딩 섹션에서 사용할 Figma 원본 SVG도 함께 준비합니다.
- **배경**: 세 화면은 날짜를 월과 요일에 맞춰 배치하는 방식은 같지만, 날짜 칸에 표시할 정보와 선택 상태는 다릅니다. 공통 배치를 먼저 구현해 화면별 달력을 각각 만들지 않도록 했습니다.
- **동작 변화**: 앱의 진입 화면은 `MaterialApp.router`를 통해 `/` 경로에서 표시됩니다. 현재 `/`에는 기존 임시 홈이 연결되어 있습니다.

### Changes

#### 1. 기본 라우팅

`go_router` 의존성을 추가하고 경로 정의를 `app_router.dart`로 분리했습니다. 이후 화면 경로를 한곳에서 확장할 수 있도록 앱 진입점을 `MaterialApp.router`에 연결했습니다. 이번 변경에는 `/` 외의 화면 경로나 공유 딥링크 처리는 포함되지 않습니다.

#### 2. 공통 월 달력

`AppMonthCalendar`가 월의 시작 요일, 일수, 앞뒤의 빈 칸을 계산해 일요일부터 시작하는 7열 달력을 만듭니다. `firstDate`·`lastDate`로 선택 가능 범위를 제한하고, 선택된 날짜와 탭 결과를 화면에 전달합니다.

홈의 지출액·카드 표시, 단일 날짜 선택, 기간 강조는 서로 다른 표현이므로 `dayBuilder`로 날짜 칸을 구성하도록 했습니다. 마감일 설정 화면의 1~31일 선택은 월·요일에 따른 달력이 아니어서 이 컴포넌트에 포함하지 않았습니다.

#### 3. 온보딩 SVG

온보딩 소개와 이후 가입·설정 화면에서 참조하는 Figma 원본 SVG 22개를 `assets/onboarding/`에 추가했습니다. 기존 `back.svg`와 같은 아이콘이나 기기 상태 표시줄 그래픽은 중복 에셋으로 추가하지 않았습니다. `setup_loader.svg`는 현재 정적 원본이며, 로딩 애니메이션은 화면 구현 단계에서 다룰 예정입니다.

### Etc

- 검증: `flutter test` 8개 통과, `flutter analyze` 문제 없음. SVG 22개는 XML 형식 검사를 통과했습니다.
- 아직 각 화면은 연결되지 않았으며, SVG도 `pubspec.yaml`에 등록하거나 위젯에서 사용하지 않았습니다. 실제 화면 구현 시 필요한 에셋을 등록하고 Figma와 렌더링을 대조해야 합니다.

author: jnhu76
body:
## Summary

Port of the DP-0 study's DP-1 arm (research evidence: PR #570,
`docs/research/data-movement-dp0/dp1-publication.md`, verdict
ELIMINATED_CONFIRMED) to production. All four inline publication call sites
(`publish_zero_op_inline` / `publish_one` in `UringAsyncBackend` and
`ThreadPoolBackend`) materialized a 120-byte `PublicationPayload` whose only
consumed field was `.id` (24 B) — the request key the publisher already
holds. At `-O3` without LTO the compiler cannot remove it (cross-TU DSE
keeps every byte), so the payload init (`rep stos`, 15 qwords) and the
12-move fill executed per operation. The call sites now pass `nullptr` and
deliver with the in-scope key.

## Preserved invariants

- `begin_publication`'s `out != nullptr` snapshot form is retained (its
  conformance tests still exercise it; today no production consumer exists —
  field-liveness-matrix.md residual fact 2).
- The two-phase publication protocol (`begin_publication` /
  `publication_inflight` pin / `complete_publication`), observer
  claim/retirement, generation identity and slot reclaim pin are untouched.
- No publication phases merged, no RequestCore bypass, no ReadyEvent
  semantic change, no publication authority moved to the backend, no new
  persistent state.

## Compiler proof (WSL2 GCC 15.2.0, release -O3, no LTO)

Evidence under `docs/evidence/dp1-publication-payload-elimination/`:
- The 15-qword `rep stosq` payload initialization executes in all four base
  publish functions and is absent in all four candidate functions.
- `publish_one` stack frames shrink 232 B → 96 B; call sequences identical
  (context → begin → complete → claim → deliver → retire); no new
  allocation; no equally sized hidden temporary.

## Named negative oracles

- Skipping the publication grant → `complete_publication` returns
  `not_in_flight` → named fail-fast. Mutant
  `SLUICE_URING_MUTANT_PUBLICATION_BEGIN_SKIPPED` killed with rc=134.
- Delivering a foreign key → observer retirement never happens → settlement
  strands → bounded watchdog kill. Mutant
  `SLUICE_URING_MUTANT_PUBLISH_DELIVERS_FOREIGN_KEY` killed at test 9/9
  (rc=142, harness `alarm(120)`).
- Premature reclaim → owned by the existing `public_request_test`
  publication-epilogue pause-gate oracle (green, unmodified) and the

author: jdeun
body:
## Objective (stacked on #1717)
Actual fixed Qwen3-0.6B EN/KO/JA local-source attempt in #1717 succeeded operationally but **all non-FULL arms prematurely finalized without executing a native source**. The original 12-route FULL arm cannot be disclosed under the existing **K=5** host limit, so a full four-arm cost/quality claim is incomparable. Preserve these negative results and the 12-route scaling control unchanged.

## Implementation
- Preregister a distinct, genuinely **four-original-route** native registered source with exactly the same 2-hop CRM typed path plus **2 unrelated, read-only inventory routes**. FULL is now actually within K5. Do **not** split a 12-route FULL menu, relax disclosure cap, or use task gold in route selection.
- Same original four native registered ToolSpecs and scoped principal/source witness for FULL, lexical K5, typed G5 and model-chosen surgical G5, each using the original host executor. Collect actual Qwen model turns, token receipts, schema requests, native invocations and structural final success separately. All four arms' denominators are **one local synthetic task per language**, not independent E2.
- Keep the default `catalog_size=12` former E1 path and its explicitly incomparable null denominator; reject out-of-scope size/negative condition.
- Add EN/KO/JA scripted-agent regression that genuinely exercises original callbacks, strict K5, measured one-task denominators, and 12-route negative isolation.
- Upgrade dedicated pinned-Qwen public CPU workflow to **3 languages × {4,12} route cohorts**. Fail if actual model generation does not occur or synthetic evidence is mispromoted. Publish only bounded allowlisted numeric/category metrics.

## Qualification
**DRAFT** until exact-head six-job real-model matrix, regression, protected CI and CodeQL pass. The four-route cohort can measure actual model behavior and full prompt costs but cannot establish CodeGraph scale savings or independent publisher-authored E2. The earlier 12-route first-turn premature-final observations remain preserved and negative, not corrected. #1346 external E2 blocked and v0.18 #1356 HARD HOLD.

## Added preregistered pinned 1.7B candidate (separate model intervention)
The actual pinned 0.6B four-route matrix at [run 39922466111](https://github.com/JDeun/SchemaRouter/actions/runs/39922466111) generated real tokens in all EN/KO/JA four-arm branches but **prematurely finalized all 12/12 four-route attempts** with zero tool calls (all 0/1 per language/arm). No success or reduced total tokens in the 0.6B case.

This PR additionally reuses the repository's already-pinned **Qwen3-1.7B** `70d244cc86ccca08cf5af4e1e306ecf908b1ad5e` through its **existing inherited original generation implementation**, as a *new, separately labeled checkpoint-only candidate* in the same actual original four-route local source. Source/tool/authorization/scorer/K5 contract unchanged. New pinned-model independent EN/KO/JA CPU matrix validates weights' original HF revision, exact model receipts, model generations, one local task denominator per arm, original source calls, schema requests and sanitized token receipts. No provider HTTP, E2, or release claim. **Model size effect is not CodeGraph context effect.**

Keep this PR **Draft until both 0.6B and 1.7B new-head 3-language matrices and protected CI are terminal green**, and preserve the 12-route FULL-menu limitation.

## Verified actual-model results (2026-10-23; retained baseline; NOT E2)
- [Pinned Qwen3-0.6B, EN/KO/JA × {4,12}](https://github.com/JDeun/SchemaRouter/actions/runs/39922466111): all six actual-model jobs succeeded. In four-route K5-safe cohort every arm 0/1 per language (twelve of twelve failures), all returned premature final, no original calls or surgical schema requests. Twelve-route FULL remains genuinely blocked/incomparable.
- [Pinned Qwen3-1.7B, EN/KO/JA × 4](https://github.com/JDeun/SchemaRouter/actions/runs/39923618201): all three actual-model jobs succeeded. All four arms 0/1 per language (twelve of twelve failures). In KO, FULL/lexical each executed one original local callback then prematurely finalized; KO and JA surgical each requested one scoped schema, then a malformed follow-up call stopped before native execution. No full two-hop task completed.
- Every arm/model/language input+output token receipt and negative is preserved in [the new E1 research note](research/autoresearch/codegraph-real-qwen-fourarm-local-e1-20261023.md). Surgical total model tokens were larger than G5 on these failed trajectories; this proves **neither CodeGraph agent task success nor end-to-end cost savings**. Qwen3-1.7B changes model weights and is not a causal CodeGraph ablation.
- [#1723](https://github.com/JDeun/SchemaRouter/issues/1723) tracks fail-closed diagnosis of strict native tool-call grammar vs model output and genuine second-step continuation. This PR **remains Draft** and stacked on #1717 while its refreshed exact-head CI runs; preserve source/external E2/release holds.

author: oleross
body:
## Summary

v1 connections were Rx observables of a peer that could disconnect behind the app's back: GATT calls raced each other, a peer that stopped answering hung them, and connecting stopped the shared scan for good. This third PR of the v2 stack adds connections on both sides, on the driver layer from #159 and #160, built against the Mock backend.

A connection is an owned object that ends exactly once: `Disconnected` and every failing call report the same `DisconnectInfo`. Its requests run one at a time in call order through a per-connection queue, which also times out a peer that does not answer within 30 s (the ATT timeout). Read, write and notify come in the next PR; this one carries the MTU exchange and discovery.

## Changes

```csharp
// Central
await using ConnectedPeripheral connection = await adapter.Central.ConnectAsync(address, cancellationToken: ct);
RemoteGattService service = await connection.Gatt.DiscoverServiceAsync(0x180D, ct);   // GattException(NotFound) if missing
IReadOnlyList<RemoteGattCharacteristic> characteristics = await service.DiscoverCharacteristicsAsync(ct);
DisconnectInfo info = await connection.Disconnected;   // LocalRequest, RemoteRequest, ConnectionTimeout, AttTimeout, TransportLost

// Peripheral
var builder = new LocalGattServiceBuilder(0x180D);
builder.AddCharacteristic(0x2A37, GattProperty.Notify);
await adapter.Peripheral.Gatt.AddServiceAsync(builder, ct);
await using AdvertisingSet set = await adapter.Broadcaster.StartAdvertisingAsync(data, interval, autoRestart: true, cancellationToken: ct);
foreach (ConnectedCentral central in adapter.Peripheral.ConnectedCentrals) { /* Address, Disconnected, DisconnectAsync */ }
```

Review `BleCentral.cs`, `ConnectedPeripheral.cs`, `Connections/RequestQueue.cs` with `Backends/GattRequest.cs`, `BlePeripheral.cs`, `ConnectedCentral.cs`, `Gap/AdvertisingSet.cs`, `Scanning/ScanCoordinator.cs` and `src/Darp.Ble.Mock/`. The `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` changes follow the code.

- Request queue: cancelling a queued request drops it; cancelling after it was sent abandons it, and the next request waits for its answer. Each ATT transaction gets its own timeout on the manager's `TimeProvider`. Send order and the slot that waits for an answer are still one chain; they split when write without response arrives in the next PR.
- Scans: `ConnectAsync` pauses the adapter's radio scan until the link is up. Scans keep running, and a radio that cannot start again ends them with its error instead of failing the connect.
- Advertising: a connection stops the set it came through, as controllers do. Drivers report it through the new `IAdvertisingSetSink`, after the peripheral sink reported the central. Starting, stopping or disposing the set, and disposing the adapter, cancel a pending restart.
- Adapter disposal: ends connections and disconnects centrals, also ones that connect while it runs, and runs every step even if one fails.
- Examples: `connect.cs` and `host-service.cs`.

## Testing

- Added Mock tests for connecting, unreachable addresses, local and remote disconnects on both sides, adapter disposal, discovery of hosted services, `NotFound`, and `autoRestart` with and without a restart.
- Added tests at the driver boundary for request order, cancellation before and after sending, the per-transaction ATT timeout on a fake clock, a lost link failing running and queued requests with the first reason, ATT errors, and scans around a connect.
- Probed races between teardown and hand-off, late centrals, stop and restart, and admission closure with throwaway driver probes; the fixes are in the commits.
- Built every commit on its own and ran the examples.
- Not covered: the UTC rollback and late-central fixes only have the throwaway probes, no regression test.

## Impact

- Removed: `ConnectionTiming` (`BleConnectionParameters.ConnectionInterval` is a `TimeSpan`).
- `BleBroadcaster.StartAdvertisingAsync` takes `autoRestart` before the token; `IBroadcasterDriver.CreateAdvertisingSetAsync` takes an `IAdvertisingSetSink`; `IBleAdapterDriver` gains `Central` and `Peripheral`.
- `GattProtocolStatus` names the ATT errors.

## Checklist

- [x] Documentation (and changelog) is updated if needed
- [x] CI Pipeline is successful
- [ ] (Human) Self-review was done

author: lucasdicioccio
body:
projectz feature `76992361-e38e-4775-9805-1d3d57c28e39`

Automatic HTTPS with ACME (Let's Encrypt or any ACME server), TLS-ALPN-01 challenges answered by the HTTPS server itself, so no port 80. Built on acme-not-a-joke 0.2.0.0, acme-not-a-joke-wai 0.1.0.0 and acme-not-a-joke-warp 0.1.0.0 from Hackage.

## serve

```
kitchen-sink serve --srcDir site --servMode SERVE \
  --acmeDomain example.com --acmeContact certmaster@example.com \
  --acmeDirectory letsencrypt --acmeStateDir /var/lib/kitchen-sink/acme
```

- `--acmeDomain` (repeatable) turns ACME on. One certificate per name, and the first one is the default. HTTPS defaults to port 443 (the only port the ACME server connects to). It can't be combined with `--tlsCertFile`/`--tlsKeyFile`.
- `--acmeDirectory` is **required**: `letsencrypt`, `letsencrypt-staging` or a directory URL. I made it required on purpose so nobody gets untrusted staging certs or hits production rate limits by accident. If you'd rather have a default, it's a one-line change.
- `--acmeContact` (repeatable, `mailto:` is added to bare addresses) and `--acmeStateDir` (default `./acme-state`: `account.jwk`, `<domain>/key.pem`, `<domain>/certificate.pem`).
- Stored certificates are served right away and renewed when two thirds of their validity have elapsed. If getting a certificate fails, the failure is logged and retried with backoff, and the daemon keeps running.

## multisite

The same `--acmeContact/--acmeDirectory/--acmeStateDir` flags, plus a new certificate source in a TLS stanza:

```json
{ "sniDomains": ["example.com", "www.example.com"], "certificate": { "tag": "AcmeCertificate" } }
```

One certificate manager covers every ACME domain of the config, and one challenge store is keyed by SNI. In the SNI hook, the per-site file certificates come first, then ACME domains, then the `--tlsCertFile` fallback (or the first ACME domain when there are no fallback files). With ACME, multisite serves HTTPS even without fallback files.

## ⚠️ Dependency bound: needs an owner action before release

The acme packages need `tls >= 2.1.3` together with `crypton-x509` 1.8, which means tls 2.2. `prodapi-proxy-0.2.0.0` caps `tls < 2.1`. It builds unchanged against tls 2.2.2, so `hs/cabal.project` carries `allow-newer: prodapi-proxy:tls` for now. kitchen-sink's own bound becomes `tls >= 2.1.3 && < 2.5` (and `warp-tls >= 3.4.13`). **A Hackage metadata revision of prodapi-proxy-0.2.0.0 relaxing tls to `< 2.5`** (or a release) is needed before a kitchen-sink Hackage release resolves without the allow-newer. After that, the cabal.project stanza can be dropped.

## Checks

- `cabal build` (-Werror): clean.
- `bash scripts/smoke-test.sh`: all checks passed.
- `bash scripts/daemon-test.sh`: all checks passed, including the new ACME section. This section runs serve and multisite with ACME certificates "stored by a previous run" (private-CA certs placed in the state dir) and an ACME directory on a closed local port. It checks that:
  - the managed certs are served over HTTPS (serve, plus multisite mixing a file-cert site and an ACME site);
  - an `acme-tls/1` handshake with no pending challenge gets no certificate;
  - `--acmeDomain` without `--acmeDirectory` is refused;
  - an unreachable ACME server for a third domain is logged and retried while the other sites keep serving.

**Untested:** an actual ACME exchange. There is no pebble locally, and I didn't hit Let's Encrypt, staging included. That path is the library's `acmeTlsAlpn01Issuer` / `withTlsAlpn01`, covered by acme-not-a-joke's own test suites. A first real run against `letsencrypt-staging` on a public host is the remaining check.

author: nikneem
body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Manual testing required before merge**
>
> - [ ] **Round trip** (task 6.3): add a few medicines with schedules, stock batches and a mix of taken, skipped and missed doses. Settings → Export data → enter the passphrase twice → save the file. Then Reset app (or uninstall and reinstall) → Settings → Import data → pick the file → passphrase → tick → Replace data. **Expected:** medicines (active and inactive), schedules, stock batches with expiry dates, the "I ordered new" state and the full history match what was there before. Reminders fire for the imported schedules, and a paired watch shows the imported doses.
> - [ ] **Wrong passphrase** (6.4): import a valid file with the wrong passphrase. **Expected:** the dialog stays open with "This passphrase does not open the backup…", nothing changes, and the right passphrase then works without picking the file again.
> - [ ] **Damaged file** (6.4): change a byte in a `.pill` file (or pick any other file). **Expected:** "This file is not a Pillsner backup, or it is damaged. Nothing was changed." with no passphrase asked for in the non-backup case. Nothing on the phone changes.
> - [ ] **Cancelling each picker** (6.4): back out of the save picker during export and the open picker during import. **Expected:** "Export cancelled. No file was saved." / "Import cancelled. Nothing was changed." No file is created and no data changes.
> - [ ] **App lock across the picker**: turn the PIN lock on, then start an export and an import. Opening the system picker relocks Pillsner, so after picking you see the unlock screen. **Expected:** after unlocking, the export finishes (snackbar) and the import continues at the passphrase dialog. The picked file is not lost.
> - [ ] **Overwriting a backup**: export, choosing an existing `.pill` file to overwrite. **Expected:** it is replaced by the new backup. (A failed overwrite restoring the old file is covered by unit tests; it cannot be staged by hand.)
> - [ ] **Large font / TalkBack**: at 200 % font, the three dialogs scroll and nothing truncates. With TalkBack, the confirm checkbox row reads as one checkbox.

## What this does

Adds **Export data** and **Import data** to Settings, in a new *Your data* section directly above the danger zone (spec `data-backup-restore`).

- **Export:** passphrase entered twice, with a warning that it cannot be recovered → the SAF create-document picker → a single `.pill` file. The file holds every medication (active and inactive, with its low-stock acknowledgement), schedule, stock batch and dose, including the reminder bookkeeping, so restored history reads exactly as before. It never holds the app lock PIN or biometric setting, the accepted legal documents or any watch pairing state.
- **File format v1:** a plaintext header (`PILL` marker, format version, PBKDF2 iteration count, salt, nonce), then JSON → **GZIP** → **AES-256-GCM**, with the key from PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations. The salt and nonce are random per export, and the header bytes are GCM associated data, so changing any of them fails authentication. Everything is built in (`javax.crypto`, `java.util.zip`, `kotlinx.serialization`); no new dependency.
- **Import:** the SAF open-document picker → a header check that needs no passphrase (refuses non-backups, newer formats and iteration counts outside 100,000–2,000,000 before any key is derived) → passphrase (a wrong one keeps the dialog open to retry) → a confirmation built like the reset dialog (what is replaced, what stays, a tick, the red button) → replace.
- **All-or-nothing replace:** `RoomBackupDataStore` deletes and reinserts every table in one `withTransaction`, remapping export-local ids to new Room ids. A failure leaves the data exactly as it was. No schema change.
- **After import:** the same reconciliation a reset uses: notifications for the old data come down, the silently-missed record and queued stock warnings are forgotten, and a `MEDICATIONS_CHANGED` wake rebuilds every alarm and republishes to the watch.
- **No permissions:** the manifest is unchanged. SAF grants access to the one picked document only.
- Strings are in all six shipped languages (en, nl, de, fr, es, pt). Lint requires all five translations, not only Dutch as task 4.7 says. The README is updated.

## Decisions and corrections made during apply

These are recorded in `design.md` and the spec deltas of this change:

- **Stock batches are included.** The proposal predates `medicine-stock-tracking` and said there was no stock to export. Schema v6 has `stock_batches` and `low_stock_acknowledgement`, and clearing every table on import would have silently wiped them. Format v1 now carries both (confirmed with the requester).
- **GZIP before encryption** was added to format v1 (confirmed with the requester). The version number defines it, so there is no extra header flag.
- **The SAF launchers live at the root of `PillsnerApp`, above the lock gate,** and the view model is activity-scoped. The picker is another app, so opening it relocks Pillsner (app-lock spec) and takes Settings out of composition. A launcher registered in Settings would have lost the picked file.
- **The replace deletes table by table** instead of calling `clearAllTables()`, which can't run inside an outer transaction. As a side effect, autoincrement ids are not reused, so a leftover pre-import notification or alarm can never point at an imported dose.
- **Use cases follow the codebase's verb naming**: `ExportBackup` and `ImportBackup`, not the `…UseCase` names in tasks.md.

## Verification

- **Unit tests:** 773/773 pass, including 58 new ones (snapshot, export/import use cases, codec round trip, compression, wrong passphrase, altered ciphertext and header, truncation, newer version, out-of-range iterations without key derivation, and the full view model flow).
- **Lint:** 0 errors. No new warnings on files this change added. I fixed the one warning this change introduced (`ModifierParameter`).
- **Pillsner UI review** (`pillsner-ui-review`): compliant. Red is used only on the destructive confirm button and the validation error.
- **Instrumented tests** on an API 37 emulator: the full suite ran (442 tests). All new tests pass: `RoomBackupDataStoreTest` (round trip, replace, mid-transaction failure leaves data intact), `ImportBackupEffectsTest` (no old reminder or alarm survives, every imported dose is armed, the watch gets exactly the imported doses) and `BackupSettingsTest`. The reset and settings tests also pass.
  - `AboutSectionTest.aboutSectionComesAfterSecurity` broke because of this change. It assumed About could never scroll to the top of the list. I fixed it to check the order from both ends.
  - **Two failures that are not from this change:** `ReminderRecoveryTest.aStepThatThrows_isRetriedLikeATimeout` and `TrustedClockStoreTest.withNothingEverWrittenThereIsNoPriorSample` fail the same way on `development` (verified there on the same emulator). This change doesn't touch them.
- **Not verified:** everything in the manual-testing callout above.

## Review fixes (PR review)

- `29c3ae2`: a failed export never deletes a picked document that already held something (high).
- `e525554`: overwriting a picked backup is rolled back if the write fails. SAF truncates before writing and has no atomic replace, so the old contents are read first and written back on failure (high, second review).
- `29d7189`: a picked document is never deleted, not even an empty one, since the picker's fresh placeholder and an existing zero-byte file cannot be told apart. A failed export may leave an empty file the user named, and says it failed (high, third review).
- `5bdc549`: if the picked document's current contents can't be read, nothing is written at all; a truncating write it couldn't undo is never attempted (high, fourth review).
- `5ef0544`: a picked document waits until the app is unlocked again. Returning from the picker relocks the app, and the export or import used to run b

author: kolyshkin
body:
The new criu 4.3 package in the criu PPA is now split into multiple packages
(criu, libcriu2, libcriu-dev, python3-pycriu, libcompel1, libcompel-dev),
following the Debian and Ubuntu packaging, so the libcriu headers and
library are no longer shipped in the criu package.

As a result, crun is built without CRIU support in CI:

```
configure: CRIU headers not found, building without CRIU support
```

and the checkpoint/restore tests are either silently skipped or, in
the runc integration tests job, fail with `unknown command checkpoint`
(see e.g. #2404).

Install libcriu-dev (which also pulls in libcriu2) to fix this
(the first commit is also a part of #2259).

To not let this happen again:
 - make an explicit `configure --enable-criu` fail if libcriu is not
   found (without the option, CRIU support is still autodetected, and
   `--disable-criu` works as before);
 - use `--enable-criu` in CI builds.

author: piyushvijay
body:
## Problem
`scripts/dist-with-retry.test.mjs` timed out intermittently during a full local suite on macOS (`retries the detach flake on macOS …` at 5.3 s against the 5 s limit), and passed when run alone.

The script under test does no real waiting (`DIST_RETRY_DELAY=0`). The time went to `beforeEach`, which wrote fresh `npm` and `hdiutil` stubs for every test. macOS scans an executable the first time it runs: about 0.5 s per fresh file, at near-zero CPU, and the scans queue on a loaded machine. Measured directly, a fresh stub's first run took 0.56 s and its second 0.00 s. So each test paid one or two scans before doing any work (300–900 ms alone), and under a full suite's load the detach case went past the timeout.

## Change
The stubs are written once in `beforeAll` and each is run once there, so the scan happens before any test starts. `run()` already clears the files the stubs record into, so tests stay independent.

## Test
Per-test time is now 20–70 ms (was 300–900 ms). The full suite passed twice in a row locally on macOS with the change.

author: 1998x-stack
body:
## P0-C — Execution Arbitration & Shared Cell Reliability

### Implemented
- One immutable `CellOperation` record per (`notebook_id`, `operation_id`), with request digest, owner identity, expected document version, committed version and replay response.
- All five MCP Cell tools (`cell_add`, `cell_insert`, `cell_update`, `cell_move`, `cell_delete`) now call one server-side CAS endpoint. An Agent can supply `expected_version` + `operation_id`. No silent auto-rebasing on 409.
- Successful operations atomically commit the document, forkable NotebookRevision, operation result, audit and SSE `document.committed` event including action/operation ID.
- One SQLite primary-key `KernelGate` serializes direct browser/MCP Jupyter WebSocket `execute_request` and managed `run_submit`. Release requires observed matching Kernel idle. Transport break or API restart marks gate uncertain; a deliberate Runtime stop resets it, never a TTL.
- Updated MCP generated documentation, English/Chinese README, detailed architecture and local acceptance plan.

### Tests
- Backend unit tests: Cell add/update/move/delete, exactly-one retry result, conflict and unique key collision, cross-account viewer denial, cross-account same-ID replay denial, history+SSE provenance, concurrent 409, gate exclusivity, restart recovery, managed wait behind legacy, Runtime reset.
- Existing durable Run + event tests, frontend build, MCP unit tests and generated tool reference check.

### Boundaries
- Trusted **single-process** deployment only, not a cross-node dispatcher or exactly-once arbitrary Python external side effects.
- Kernel gate is intentionally conservative: a missing completion status may require stopping Runtime and losing Kernel RAM (persistent files and Notebook remain).
- Browser and MCP whole-document saves retain optimistic CAS; text-level CRDT automatic merge is out of scope.
- **Host acceptance still needed** before a public production tag: two Pi agents, browser Kernel WebSocket, real Docker CPU/GPU, disconnect/restart and stress testing.

See [docs/EXECUTION_ARBITRATION.md](docs/EXECUTION_ARBITRATION.md).

author: leow4u
body:
## O que muda

Parte 3.9a da Fase 3 (`docs/plataforma/fase-3-operacao.md`). A OS em execução agora conclui no backend e vai para Em revisão.

- **`completeServiceOrder`.** Entra pela linha `requireOperacaoCaller(..., { campo: true })`: atende owner, admin, interno e o campo escalado na OS.
- **Aceite com assinatura.** O responsável do cliente informa o nome, com cargo e documento quando houver. A imagem da assinatura sobe antes ao Storage, e a callable confere que o arquivo chegou e é uma imagem.
- **Sem aceite no local.** A OS conclui com o nome de quem recebeu. O aceite vem depois, pela validação do cliente no Comercial.
- **O que a conclusão pede.**
  - Ao menos uma foto do final, que são as fotos da etapa Fim.
  - O motivo de cada item feito a menos que o previsto. Um item sem feito conta zero.
  - Uma hora que não venha antes da última etapa.
  - No celular, só o líder conclui.
- **Motivo de item sem diferença.** Um item pode já ter o feito completo porque outro aparelho o registrou antes. O motivo dele fica de fora e não recusa a conclusão, para o responsável não precisar assinar de novo.
- **O que grava.** Grava `conclusao` na OS, registra a etapa Fim quando ela faltava e muda o status para Em revisão. Depois disso a OS não recebe mais andamento.
- **Eventos.** `os.completed` sai junto com `os.signed` ou `os.completed_without_acceptance`, e `os.step_recorded` sai para o Fim. Nenhum deles leva o nome, o documento ou os motivos.
- **Storage.** A nova regra cobre `os/{numero}/assinatura/as_<16 hex>.png`. Sobe quem coordena ou está escalado, só com a OS em execução, e nada se sobrescreve nem se apaga. O suporte também lê.

## Testes

- `conclusao.test.ts` (unitário): cobre o motivo obrigatório por item a menos, a foto do final, a assinatura no Storage, o líder no celular, a hora, o status e o schema sem valor.
- `conclusao.integration.test.ts` (emulador): a líder conclui com assinatura e a repetição não duplica. Também cobre "sem aceite" pelo escritório, e uma conclusão recusada que não grava nada.
- `operacao-fotos.rules.test.ts`: as regras da assinatura falham antes e passam depois.
- `callables.test.ts` e a lista de callables do app ganham `completeServiceOrder`.

body:
## Tóm tắt

Checkout mobile không gửi `deliveryMethod` → preview báo không phí ship còn server tính phí khi có địa chỉ (hầu như luôn có vì checkout tự chọn địa chỉ mặc định) → khách bị thu nhiều hơn tổng hiển thị. Ngoài ra chọn ZaloPay luôn lỗi 400 vì server không hỗ trợ.

- Checkout thêm lựa chọn **Nhận tại tiệm / Giao tận nơi** (mặc định nhận tại tiệm, giống web). Ô địa chỉ + địa chỉ đã lưu chỉ hiện khi giao tận nơi và bắt buộc nhập; đơn nhận tại tiệm không gửi địa chỉ.
- `deliveryMethod` (enum `DeliveryMethod`) đi qua VM → service → repository → API cho cả preview lẫn tạo đơn; `PreviewIncentiveResult.deliveryFee` parse từ preview.

Revisión completa de Ciegos con dos repasos de código y pruebas de estrés. Arreglos:

**Motor (`zt4k9m/ciegos.js`)**
- Vidas: al desatascar, alguien podía quedar metido dos veces en la misma ronda. Ahora se empieza en la ronda siguiente y los que faltan descansan.
- Vidas: no se puede corregir un resultado si alguno de los 4 está jugando un partido posterior.
- Monster/Suizo: si se va tanta gente que no da para un partido, el torneo se cierra con la clasificación (antes se quedaba atascado).
- Quien se va no sube al podio ni cobra; en la tabla sale «🚪 se fue».
- Corregir una semifinal con el mismo ganador ya no vuelve a sortear la final.
- Con el partido siguiente en mesa no se tocan los anteriores, y el aviso dice qué hacer.

**Panel (`r5c2w8/`) y `store.js`**
- Sin red: nunca se sube una copia vieja encima de cambios más nuevos de otro móvil; se pregunta cuál quedarse. Tampoco se pregunta en falso si el guardado propio sí llegó.
- Tras un error de verdad (contraseña, servidor) se avisa una vez y se reintenta cada minuto; tocar el estado reintenta.
- Cada llamada al servidor se corta a los 15 s y cuenta como «sin red».
- El repaso de fondo ya no pisa un cambio recién hecho.
- Deshacer quita la acción entera de un toque.
- Si al irse alguien empieza la final o se acaba el torneo, sale el sorteo o los campeones.
- Service worker: cada versión de la página usa sus propios scripts (`?v=`), así no se mezclan versiones con mala cobertura.

author: arcanumruna
body:
Fixes #565
Part of #276
Part of #273

## Root causes
- **#565:** `GroupCoordinationService` never cleared `coordinators_` when the node lost the coordinator role, and the per-group loop in `doWork` had no `isLocalCoordinator()` guard. An ex-coordinator kept ageing its stale groups: members expired, generations went up, and it sent revoke and empty Assign frames to clients that were already heartbeating to the new coordinator. Session revoke, eviction and topic-drop paths also called `leave` on these stale groups.
  - **Fix:** a Kafka-style unload. When `doWork` finds it is not the coordinator, `unloadGroups_()` ends each bound session's group push subscriptions (no Assign frame is sent), then clears `memberSessionMap_`, the per-group lineage state and `coordinators_`. Group membership is never persisted, so a node that regains the role rebuilds each group as members re-join. Parked commits, transactional offsets in flight and the offsets store are left as they are.
  - **Handler audit:** every group handler answers NotCoordinator before it looks up or creates a group, so no handler needed a change.
- **#276 / #273:** test gaps. I checked the existing coverage first and wrote only the tests that were missing.

## Tests
**#565** (`GroupJoinAdversarial` in `broker/libs/node/tests/node/GroupCoordinationServiceTest.cpp`). All four failed before the fix:
- `AStaleGroupOnAnExCoordinatorNeverRebalancesRegression`
- `AnExCoordinatorSendsNoAssignOnUnloadButEndsPushSubscriptionsRegression`
- `ASessionRevokeOnAnExCoordinatorTouchesNoGroupRegression`
- `ALeadershipFlapRebuildsTheGroupByRejoinRegression`
- I also adapted `ALateTopicOnANodeNoLongerCoordinatorNeverRebalancesAdversarialRegression`, which held a group reference across the role flip.

**#276** (`AuthEnforcementTest.cpp`). Each test turns red when its deny branch is removed:
- `SyncGroupIsDeniedWithoutGroupReadRegression`
- `AClientControlBatchIsRefusedForAnAuthorizedWriterRegression`

**#273:**
- `ShardRevokeOkMeansTheWorkerAlreadyRefusesRegression` now also runs 100 rounds without the lifecycle hold.
- New: `GetTopicSchemaAnswersPerTheObjectsOwnKindAcrossTopicKindsRegression` covers data topics, views and system topics. It turns red when the own-kind branch of `authorizeTopicOrViewName` is removed.

**Runs:**
- `rune_group_coordination_service_tests`: 102/102.
- `rune_auth_enforcement_tests`: all passed.
- `rune_auth_matrix_tests`: all passed.
- The new tests passed with `--gtest_repeat=20`.

## Residuals (left open on the issues)
- **#276:** the matrix still has no `OwnedByOther` column. A new Timing changes the 720-cell table that the stress test, the 3-node slice and the docker e2e all share.
- **#273:**
  - an MDC fallback test;

  - a 45 on a follower that has not applied the change yet (needs a multi-node auth rig);
  - a shard column in the matrix;
  - a session-spoof test over the wire on the shard worker ingress (today it is covered only at unit level).

The build dependencies came from a local prebuilt set outside the repo. None of them are committed.

## Summary

## Parent

[[spec] Effect の書き方の規約・検査ゲート・既存コードの移行](https://github.com/daiki-beppu/nyaucast/issues/814)

経路: **feature**（takt）。期間: v0.1。

## What to build

`test/effect-migration.test.ts` を削除する。構造の規則がテストの中に残っていない状態にし、テストが失敗したら振る舞いの退行だけを意味するようにする（決定: [#780](https://github.com/daiki-beppu/nyaucast/issues/780) 決定 2）。

### 決定

先行の issue（lint への移し替え、構造の検査スクリプト 3 本、規約の文書の `throw` の検査の削除）が、移せる検査はすべて移して消している。この issue では、残った検査を移さずに捨て、ファイルを削除する。捨てる理由は、別の検査がすでに覆っているか、移行の時点の確認でしかないことにある。

| 捨てる検査（`it` の名前） | 捨ててよい理由 |
|---|---|
| drops zod, Drizzle and the official MCP SDK from every dependency section | import を lint で禁止し、使われない依存は fallow が見つける |
| drops them from the lockfile's root importer as well | `lockfile:check` が manifest と lockfile の一致を見る |
| leaves nothing of the Drizzle toolchain behind | 移行の時点の確認で、役目を終えた |
| ships the runtime Effect packages as dependencies and the test and diagnostic tools as devDependencies | fallow（`dev-dependencies-in-production` など）が覆う |
| pins vite-plus to 1.0 | 移行の時点の確認で、役目を終えた |
| runs the @effect/tsgo diagnostics inside check | check の中身の正本は `package.json` だけにする（AGENTS.md） |
| converts wire names by hand nowhere | 移行の時点の確認で、役目を終えた |

- 着手時に、上の表に無い `it` が残っていたら、それを移した先の issue がまだマージされていないということ。その場合は削除せず、BLOCKED として止める
- `test/check-gates.ts` は `test/platform-contracts.test.ts` も使っているので残す
- `effect-migration.test.ts` だけが使っていた依存（`yaml` の import など）が使われなくなったら、fallow の指摘に従って片付ける

### 設計指針

- 捨てる検査を、スクリプトや lint に移し直さない

- [ ] `test/effect-migration.test.ts` が無い

author: damianvtran
body:
## Summary of Changes

A new user sets the global approval default to `auto` — from settings, from the prompt, or by asking the agent — and the conversation they are in keeps prompting. The one path they want is the one that did not follow the file.

This change fixes propagation and puts an escape hatch in the prompt itself:

- **An explicit per-session choice is persisted with the conversation** (`approvals.json` beside the transcript) and outranks the global default **in both directions**. Resume reopens in it.
- **A session with no explicit choice follows `tool_approval_mode` live** through the existing `ConfigWatcher` (no second watcher): `ask -> auto` where the write is operator-authorised, and `auto -> ask` immediately, including mid-turn.
- **A mode change never answers a parked prompt.** It affects the next gate decision. The card on screen stays answerable and says what changed.
- **The approval card now carries both destinations** — "Set auto for this session" and "Set auto for all sessions" — plus the effective mode and its provenance (session override vs global default), with an inline confirmation in a reserved slot.
- `/approvals default ask|auto` is honoured from control connections (phone, attached pane) as an **authority-increasing** transition. The runtime writes the default through the settings facade in the gate-owning process, so every inheriting session there follows, and clears only the **issuing** conversation's record so "this conversation follows it" is true.
- Mobile: the gate sheet gains "run without asking in all sessions"; the pending approval card gains both handles.
- Desktop: the approval card gains both handles; "all sessions" also sets this conversation to auto, so the label is not broader than the effect.

### The precedence model (check this first)

1. An explicit per-session choice outranks the global default in **both** directions. A global `ask` does **not** re-arm a conversation that chose `auto`; it emits a warning notice naming the override and `/approvals ask` as the way to adopt the file. The mirror (`ask` over a global `auto`) keeps the existing keep notice.
2. A global change reaches every session **without** an explicit choice: running (watcher), idle and stored (at mount/resume).
3. The override is visible where the user asks: the card's effective-mode line, `/approvals`, and the conflict notice.

This deliberately revises the old "tightening is unconditional" invariant. An explicit conversation choice is the same human's narrower, newer instruction; the file is a default for the next conversation. Silently re-arming a conversation the user deliberately set to auto is the surprise this change exists to remove. A global `ask` still re-arms every session that did not choose.

### Mid-turn semantics

- Applying `auto` affects the **next** gate. It never retroactively approves an action already surfaced.
- A prompt on screen is **not** discarded, denied or unmounted. Its future stays unresolved; it gets a note ("Auto is set for the next approval. This action still needs your answer.") and is answered normally.
- Applying `ask` re-arms the next decision synchronously at delivery, including mid-turn. Parked prompts remain answerable; already-admitted actions are not cancelled.
- `y`/`n`/`A` still answer the card. `A` ("allow all") still answers this card **and** sets the session mode, because that is what the key has always meant.

## Related Issue(s)

- Related: #1282 (a running agent must not weaken its own gate), #1310 (same-uid subject must not self-authorise). Both boundaries are preserved and re-tested.
- #1310's `_adopt_remedy` text is unchanged; the new handles route through the same authority seam its refusals name.

## Impact

- **Breaking/behavioural:** a global `ask` no longer re-arms a conversation that explicitly chose `auto` (it now reports the override). `/approvals default <mode>` now takes effect on live inheriting sessions when issued from a control connection, and clears the issuing conversation's record.
- **Security:** no weakening. author: jonathandc64
body:
`RSX_VP_BUFFERS=0` makes the D3D12 backend skip its four per-frame vertex-program buffers, for a process that runs no game.

**Why.** The backend makes these buffers at start, 1.2 GB of upload memory at the defaults:
- the vertex buffer, 768 MB;
- the per-draw vertex constants, 264 MB;
- the per-draw fragment constants, 80 MB;
- the vertex fetch ring, 128 MB.

Demon's Souls' setup screens run in a process that never starts a game, and they compile the game beside them. That compile is held back by free memory (DemonsSoulsRecomp docs/53 section 16), so the 1.2 GB is better left to it.

**What changes**
- `init_d3d12`: with `RSX_VP_BUFFERS=0` it prints `[VPVB] no vertex-program buffers (RSX_VP_BUFFERS=0)` and skips the four.
- The default is 1, so nothing changes without the knob.
- Only a frame with guest draws uses these buffers: the per-draw paths, which already return early without them, and `render_frame`'s vertex-program pass. A process that draws only its overlay never reaches them.
- That pass now also checks for the vertex buffer and the vertex constants. So a game started with the knob, or one whose allocation failed, skips the pass instead of faulting at its first clear. The check runs once a frame.

**Tested** with a local Demon's Souls host built on this branch:
- **The setup screens alone** (a process that runs no game), sampled at 15 s: 397 MB private instead of 1,638 MB (1,241 MB less), and a working set of 234 MB instead of 1,373. The screen renders as before.
- **A whole real setup** with that host, against the same setup with a host that makes the buffers: compile 450 s -> 371 s, whole setup 524 s -> 443 s, 4.12 compiles at once on average instead of 3.36 (the table is in JonathanDC64/DemonsSoulsRecomp#159).
- **A game started with the knob by hand**, to check the new guard: it booted into the level and ran 65 s (1,906 flips) with no fault, drawing none of its geometry (the frames are black), as expected.
- Without the knob nothing changes: the default is 1, and the guard reads two pointers once a frame.
- `trail check`: no conflicts. It merges cleanly onto master and with #107.

The DemonsSoulsRecomp side sets the knob only in its setup-only process (JonathanDC64/DemonsSoulsRecomp#159). Its Play starts the game in a new process with the environment the setup process started with, so the knob never reaches a game.

`docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md` is not regenerated: on master it is out of date by about 130 knobs, and regenerating it adds about 1,700 unrelated lines.

## What changed  Adds exact session-scoped instance references, truthful inventory coverage, stable ranked discovery pagination, bounded source search and recovery, selected-property inspection, compile-only validation, and structured MCP outputs/errors. Preserves upstream cancellation/watchdog ownership and PR #16's separation of persistent facts from setup procedures.  ## Validation  - `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passed. - `bun run check` passed: TypeScript, Biome, actual `agent.lua` compilation, and 57 tests (including 20 tests executing the real Lua implementation in Luau WASM). - All three bridge/MCP transports passed controlled integration tests. - Ten isolated smoke checks passed in the connected Roblox client using real temporary Instances and the executor compiler. Fixture inventory/source getters were deterministic; temporary Instances were destroyed and the existing live agent remained connected.  ## Measured benchmarks  All six prescribed offline workflows succeeded with correct targets/evidence:  | Task | Calls | Evals | Retries | Returned bytes | Recorded ms | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Generic script / source lines | 2 | 0 | 0 | 984 | 6.822 | | Duplicate exact target | 4 | 0 | 0 | 1,680 | 4.154 | | Unparented script | 3 | 0 | 0 | 1,064 | 3.590 | | Unavailable evidence | 4 | 0 | 0 | 1,263 | 2.707 | | Compile, execute, assert | 2 | 1 | 0 | 70 | 1.657 | | Repair runtime failure | 3 | 2 | 1 | 416 | 3.303 |  These are prescribed handler workflows, not model-agent performance measurements. Actual SDK MCP samples measured 333 source bytes -> 666 text-plus-structured bytes (775 whole CallToolResult bytes), and 412 nested-eval bytes -> 824 text-plus-structured bytes (964 whole result bytes). Returning both representations duplicates content in these samples. Tokens were unavailable; no improvement claim is made. Timings vary with host load.  ## Remaining live-validation gaps  The new production agent has not yet been exercised end-to-end across real executor WebSocket/HTTP/file fallback, real inventory/decompiler capability variations, or multiple executors. The isolated smoke test does not establish completeness of production inventory or correctness of decompilation. No autonomous same-model before/after benchmark or model-token measurement has run. `docs/benchmark.md` contains the exact six prompts, metrics, fixture requirements, and comparison procedure.  ## Contracts and migration  Protocol 0.2 requires matching host/agent versions and session IDs. References expire and must never become permanent generated-script locators. Coverage distinguishes unavailable, failed, empty, and partial results. Compilation establishes syntax only; execution completion does not verify asynchronous callbacks. Cancellation is best effort, never rollback. Limits and final result contracts are in `docs/runtime-contracts.md`.  
## Post-merge local deployment verification

Merged as `353eb47` and updated both local checkouts plus the executor workspace's `agent.lua`. Preserved the deployment checkout's pre-existing shared-bridge work; retained a named backup stash. The deployed checkout passed 59 tests, including its two additional shared-bridge tests.

Compile-only validation, real running-script discovery with references/coverage, and an asserted execution returning `[42, nil, 3]` all passed.

Remaining gaps are now real-executor HTTP/file fallback, cross-executor variation and real decompiler/inventory completeness, plus the same-model autonomous before/after benchmark and token measurements. The production WebSocket connection is now verified; it is no longer an unrun deployment gap.

author: jackw6809
body:
@KakarottoCake

## What changes

`GC_FLAG_DISC_TEST` and `GC_FLAG_PAD_TRACE_PENDING` were both `8192u`, so a gameplay-trace test run stopped the disc motor at pad reads 1500 and 2200, and the heartbeat clearing the pending bit switched off an enabled disc test.

- `GC_FLAG_PAD_TRACE_PENDING` is now `32768u` (0x8000, a free bit). It is runtime-internal: only `gc_rt.c` sets and clears it, and the loader (`gcnative.cpp`) never touches it, so nothing else had to change.
- `gc_rt.h` now checks at compile time that all `GC_FLAG_*` values are distinct (their OR equals their sum) and that each is a single bit. C++ uses `static_assert`; the runtime's C99 build (`-Wpedantic`) uses a negative-size array typedef, since it rejects `_Static_assert`.
- Players were never affected; this only touches test runs.

Closes #250

## Testing

- [x] Host build and tests: 66 suites pass, `rvz` fails on macOS as always
- [x] Wii build (`make -f Makefile.wii`): builds the GC blob and plugins; only the usual pugixml and `video.cpp` warnings
- [x] The check fires: with the two flags on the same bit again, both the C99 and C++ builds fail
- [ ] `tools/gc_io_emutest.py`: not run here (needs the `unicorn` module, which is not installed on this machine). It only hardcodes `GC_FLAG_SD_SLOW` (0x20000), which did not move
- Dolphin: not needed, this only affects test runs
- A real Wii: not needed

## Self-review

- The new bit 0x8000 was unused by every other `GC_FLAG_*`; I listed all of them and searched the loader, runtime, tools and tests for hardcoded values.
- The flags word is only read and written by name, so the moved value changes no layout or loader/blob agreement.
- The check lists every flag by hand, so a new flag has to be added to it; forgetting leaves it unchecked but does not break anything.
