author: kpndevrootentri
body:
## 1. Redirect loop on tenant URLs ending in `/` (ff29987)

**Symptom:** Django pages loop with "too many redirects" (`https://django-expense-tracker.app.en3.wtf/accounts/login/?next=%2F`), and `fetch('/calculate/')` on test-calc fails with `TypeError: Failed to fetch`.

**Cause:**
```
GET /accounts/login/  → 308 → /accounts/login    (Next.js strips the trailing slash)
GET /accounts/login   → 301 → /accounts/login/   (Django APPEND_SLASH adds it back)
```
The proxy route also lost the slash: catch-all `path` params never carry it.

**Fix:**
- `next.config.js`: `skipTrailingSlashRedirect: true`, so tenant paths reach the proxy intact.
- `src/proxy.ts`: platform pages still 308 to the no-slash form, as before. Built from a plain `URL`, because `NextURL` re-appends the slash and would loop.
- Proxy route: re-appends the slash from `request.nextUrl.pathname` when building the upstream URL.
- Test: `POST /calculate/?a=1` reaches the container as `/calculate/?a=1`.

Also affects WordPress (`/wp-admin/`, permalinks) and FastAPI trailing-slash routes.

## 2. Django SQLite wiped on every redeploy (0d072ab)

A stock `startproject` writes `BASE_DIR/db.sqlite3` = `/app/db.sqlite3`, which is in the image, not on the `/data` volume. At start the container now:
- moves a committed `db.sqlite3` onto `/data` once, if `/data` has none yet;
- symlinks `/app/db.sqlite3 → /data/db.sqlite3`;
- runs `migrate` (from #15), then `runserver`.

Projects that already use `/data` (test-calc) or another database are unaffected. Only the default file name is handled.

## Testing
- `npm run type-check`; jest: 24 suites, 279 tests pass.
- Minimal Next 16 app with the same rewrite and route setup: tenant `/calculate/` → upstream `/calculate/`; platform `/dashboard/` and `/login/?from=x` → 308 to the no-slash URL.
- Real rendered Django template in local Docker. Each case was run on first deploy, after a container restart, and after a redeploy (new container, same volume):
  - stock `startproject`: migrations applied; data written after start survived;
  - committed `db.sqlite3`: seeded once, then kept;
  - `DATABASES = {}`: `migrate` fails, server still serves;
  - test-calc: `GET /` 200, `POST /calculate/` 200, row saved.
- Not tested against the production host.

## Deploy
- Web app: `cp -a .next .next.prev`, then `npm run build` and restart the web app. The build window affects all tenant sites.
- Worker: `pm2 restart dropdeploy-worker`.
- Django projects need a redeploy to pick up the new start command. Existing `/app/db.sqlite3` data in a running container is **not** carried over: it was going to be lost on the next redeploy anyway.

body:
## 概要

住民税エンジン `calculateJumin` に、障害者・未成年者・寡婦・ひとり親の非課税（前年の合計所得金額 135 万円以下なら均等割・所得割とも課さない）を入れます。

- 根拠: 地方税法 第24条の5第1項第2号（道府県民税）・第295条第1項第2号（市町村民税）
- 令和8年度税制改正の法律要綱（総務省 https://www.soumu.go.jp/main_content/001060865.pdf ）の第1の1 に本条の改正はありません（要綱の範囲で確認。改正法本文は未照合）。このため令和9年度も 135 万円のまま扱います

## 直る例

ひとり親・扶養 1 人・給与 185 万円（合計所得 120 万円）

| | 修正前 | 修正後 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 所得割 | 44,500 円 | 0 円 |
| 均等割 | 5,000 円 | 0 円 |

扶養 1 人の非課税限度（101 万円）は超えますが、135 万円以下なので非課税です。

## 変更点

- `js/core/jumin.js`
  - 入力に `selfDisabled` / `minor` / `widow` / `singleParent`（いずれも本人の区分）を追加
  - `singleParentDeduction` が 0 より大きいときも寡婦・ひとり親とみなす。既存の呼び出しを変えずに直すため
  - 本人の障害者は `disabilityDeduction`（扶養親族の分を含みうる）からは判定せず、フラグで受ける
  - 戻り値に `specialNonTaxable` を追加
- `templates/jumin-income.html`: 本人の障害者チェックを `selfDisabled` で渡す
- テスト
  - `scripts/test-jumin.cjs`:
    - 境目（135 万円ちょうど／1 円超）
    - 区分別（ひとり親・寡婦・本人の障害者・未成年者。控除額からの判定とフラグからの判定の両方）
    - 扶養親族の障害者控除だけでは対象外になること
    - 令和9年度
  - `scripts/test-jumin-income-dom.cjs`: ページ経由で、ひとり親・寡婦・本人の障害者がそれぞれ 0 円になること、135 万円を超えると課税されること
  - 追加したテストは修正前のコードで失敗することを確かめた（単体 46 件・DOM 3 件）
- 再生成: エンジンの `?v=` が変わるため、生成ページ 1,897 件を同梱
  - 内訳: 家計簿 1,730、保育料 56、住民税 54＋54、配当・自営・育休 各 1
  - deploy.sh と deploy-seido.sh が実行する生成スクリプトをすべて通し、`?v=` とテンプレートの変更以外に差分が出ないことを確認した

## テスト

`npm test` を構成する 24 本、`test:integrity`、`test:provenance`、保育料（wiring / selftest）、奨学金、bridge のテストは、すべて終了コード 0 でした。

- 挙動が変わるのは、`singleParentDeduction` か新しいフラグを渡す呼び出しだけ。現状は住民税の詳しい計算ページ（jumin-income）だけが該当する

- 家計簿・保育料・育休・自営のページは、これらの控除・区分を `calculateJumin` に渡していないため、本 PR では変わらない。別の PR で対応する

body:
Typing in the search bar made the whole bar move and its rows blink:

- The bar centred itself on its own height, so every row that arrived or left moved the field.
- `TabStore.suggest` emptied history and engine completions on each keystroke, so the list collapsed to its defaults (typed row, assistant, tabs) and refilled ~75 ms later — twice with engine suggestions on, since history and the engine answer separately.
- Rows were identified by content, and most suggestion rows change content every keystroke, so each refresh faded rows out and in under the `rows.count` animation.
- At one or two characters, resetting the list scrolled the first row to the scroll view's edge, hiding the gap under the field whenever the results could scroll.

Changes:

- The bar's top edge sits at a fixed fraction of the window (default a quarter down, about where a full list used to centre). It is clamped against the tallest list, so a short window moves it once, not per keystroke. The sidebar address editor is unchanged.
- `TabStore` publishes `suggestionsPending` until both halves of a query are in. `suggestions` is still always the current query's (the existing "rows must disappear immediately" test is untouched); the bar keeps showing the previous rows, and the previous engine completions under new history, until this query's arrive, then replaces them even with nothing.
- Rows are identified by slot, so a keystroke rewrites each slot in place; only slots added or removed at the bottom animate.
- Reset scrolls to the scroll view's top edge instead of the first row.
- Search Settings gains "Results shown" (6–12, default 8 — never fewer than the resting bar's tabs plus report row), "Bar position" (Top–Middle) and "Animate results". The animation switch gates the bar's existing `motion()` helper alongside Reduce Motion and Battery Saver, and its footnote says those also turn it off.
- `docs/BROWSING.md` gains a "The search bar" section covering the fixed position and the three settings.

author: hoferan
body:
The `venue-photos` bucket is public and had a 5 MB limit but no list of allowed content types. The upload form's `accept="image/*"` only filters the file picker, so an approved editor could put `text/html` or `image/svg+xml` into the bucket through the Storage API and have it served from the project's domain.

Migration 0014 sets `allowed_mime_types` to `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, `image/gif` and `image/avif`.

- JPEG is what `compressImageIfNeeded` writes. A photo of 5 MB or less goes up unchanged with the browser's type, which is why the other four are allowed: every current browser can display them.
- HEIC and HEIF are left out. Only Safari displays them, and an iPhone hands `accept="image/*"` a JPEG anyway.
- SVG is left out because it can carry script.
- Storage checks the declared type and serves the file under it, so nothing stored as an image is run as a page. Files already in the bucket are not touched.

`integration/storage.test.ts` has a new block where an emmental editor uploads each allowed type, and gets refused (415, "mime type … is not supported") for `text/html`, `image/svg+xml`, `application/octet-stream` and `image/heic`. The four refusals failed before the migration.

Not in this PR: `PhotoGalleryEditor` still uses `accept="image/*"`, so someone can pick an SVG or HEIC and get a generic upload error. Narrowing `accept` and showing a clear message for a 415 belongs with the editor work.

Checked locally against the Compose stack: `npm run lint`, `npm run test` (913 passed), `npm run test:integration` (123 passed).

body:
Closes #6

## Summary
- Edge discovery and bootstrap GETs go through Moodle's `\curl` wrapper, so the site proxy and the URL block list apply. `curl_init` and `curl_multi` are gone from the plugin. Up to four `/ping` calls run one after another.
- The picked edge is the only cached value. It is kept for one hour (`overlay_edge` TTL 3600, plus `cached_at` in the value). Plugin version is `2026102300` so Moodle reloads that cache definition.
- If `POST /v1/get-token` fails in curl (timeout, DNS, connect, TLS), the plugin asks `GET /ping`. Body `pong` means the edge is alive and the cache stays. No `pong` drops the cache, runs bootstrap again, and retries the token once. A token error from a live edge does not drop the cache.
- Refactor: rework the PHP overlay API to match the JS SDK session.

## Also added
- The room key now covers the presence packet `public.participant.<id>.state`, not only video, audio, and chat. That packet carries the display name, the role, and the camera and microphone flags. `start_room.js` hangs the same AES-256-GCM key on the `public.participant.` prefix. People in the room still see who is there. The overlay sees ciphertext. The packet still has no Moodle user id. The chat name was already inside `private.<role>.<id>.chat`.

## Test plan
- [x] Upgrade the plugin from the site notifications page so the cache TTL changes from 10 minutes to 1 hour.
- [x] Open a room and confirm an access token is issued.
- [x] Open the room again inside the hour and confirm bootstrap is not repeated.
- [ ] Point the cached edge at a host that does not answer `/ping` and confirm the next token request bootstraps again.
- [ ] Keep `/ping` returning `pong` while `get-token` fails at the transport layer and confirm the cached edge is kept.
- [ ] Break the main token and confirm the cached edge is kept.
- [x] Join two browsers in one room and confirm each still shows the other person's name, role, camera, and microphone.

author: baggepinnen
body:
ICA fitting does not expose convergence diagnostics or control its random initialization, and whitening can divide by numerically negligible covariance eigenvalues. This change adds optional diagnostics, numerical-rank checks, and component reconstruction. DUET gains controls for low-power bins, soft assignments, and distinct histogram peaks.

- Add `ICAInfo` through `return_info=true`, explicit RNG selection, and configurable nonconvergence handling. Default fits return the existing `ICA` model and retain the existing nonconvergence logging policy.
- Add covariance eigenvalue thresholds through `rank_rtol` and `rank_atol`; reject component counts exceeding the numerical rank and report that rank in fit diagnostics. The default relative threshold is `sqrt(eps(eltype(X)))`.
- Add `mixingmatrix`, `unmixingmatrix`, and reconstruction from selected source components, with optional mean restoration and documented behavior for reduced component counts.
- Add relative per-microphone power thresholds, normalized soft masks with configurable temperature, minimum histogram-peak spacing and relative height, and warnings when fewer peaks are available than requested. Retain hard masks by default and report retained bins through `H.reliable_bins`.
- Document the options and limitations. Add tests for reproducibility, nonconvergence policies, redundant and poorly conditioned channels, full and partial reconstruction, controlled source recovery, signal rescaling, mask normalization, large delays, and insufficient peaks.

Validation: `Pkg.test()` passes all 287 checks on Julia 1.13.1, including 174 new checks. `git diff --check` passes.

author: olayanju-1234
body:
Third PR of the correctness release. liftoff's webhook activity had to *return* "not delivered" for a 4xx instead of throwing, because any thrown error would be retried six times. Now an activity can say a failure is final.

## What
- **Worker flag**: `non_retryable` on activity completion (gRPC `CompleteTaskRequest`, HTTP). The step fails on that attempt whatever the policy allows. Go `worker.NonRetryable(err)`, TS `throw new NonRetryableError(msg)` (or any error with `nonRetryable: true`), Python `raise NonRetryableError(msg)`, Java `throw new Workflowd.NonRetryableException(msg)`.
- **Error types**: `error_type` on completion and `StepFailed`. SDKs fill it from the error class name (TS `err.name`, Python, Java); Go uses `worker.Typed(type, err)`. The engine types its own failures: `LeaseExpired`, `StartToCloseTimeout`, `ScheduleToCloseTimeout`.
- **Policy list**: `RetryPolicy.non_retryable_error_types` in every SDK. One decision point (`retryAfter`) reads the type and flag from history, so recovery decides the same after a crash (tested).
- **Workflow code sees both**: Go `*workflow.ActivityError{Type, NonRetryable}`, TS/Python/Java `ActivityFailure.type` / `nonRetryable`. Error text unchanged.
- **Older engines**: new SDKs send `error_type` on most failures; an older engine answers `400 unknown field`, so the SDKs resend without the new fields instead of losing the result. The e2e harness emulates that engine for one step to prove it.
- testsuite applies the same rules. ADR-0010, docs, CHANGELOG.

## Tests
Engine (flagged 404, policy-listed type, engine-generated StartToCloseTimeout type, recovery doesn't retry a non-retryable tail), HTTP, Go worker over gRPC, testsuite, TS + Python e2e with the older-engine fallback. Mutations: 11/11 killed (engine, Go worker, testsuite, TS and Python fallback + flag).

author: chinssiang
body:
## What

Brings the components in line with the v2 design canvas. The tokens already landed on `main` in 619370f; this is the shape, type and component work that uses them. It matches vomatt-ios PR #11.

**Shape and type**
- Cards and panels (`PollCard`, `Card`, the About panel, side cards, settings panels) round to 16px. Ballot rows, list rows and fields (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, OTP) round to 12px. Buttons round to 10px through `--radius`, set once in `Button`.
- `display-heading` and `item-title` move to weight 500, and so does the creator's poll-title preview.

**Volt discipline**
- Already held: the only full-size ink-on-Volt is `Button variant="create"`. The unread dot and count, the voter's own row and "your vote" pill, and the Seal's check keep Volt. Two stale "Apricot" comments now say Volt.

**Tide, the promise**
- New `TidePanel`, `TideRules` and `TideRule` in `components/ui/`.
- Used for "How vomatt counts" in the sidebar, the About panel's rules (lock, person, eye), and the creator's rules summary.
- The voting-window bar now uses `Progress variant="tide"`.

**The Seal**
- Replaces the "Vote cast." toast. It is a Tide surface with a 72px Tide ring and an inner dashed ring around a Volt check. It shows "Sealed. Thank you.", the `poll.sealed` sentence, the visibility sentence, and "{count} voted, you included".
- It shows in full once per cast, then folds to a compact row (36px mark plus the two sentences) on later visits.
- It opens with the optimistic ballot, closes again if the cast fails, and goes away on withdraw.
- A polite live region announces it once the cast is saved.

**Home rail**
- From `xl` up, a 280px rail sits beside the 640px feed. "Results are in" lists ended polls the viewer voted in, with unread dots. "Closing soon" lists open polls ending within 24h. Guests also get the login prompt there.
- Below `xl` the rail follows the feed. The left `AppSidebar` stays.

**Dark mode**
- `ThemeProvider` is mounted in the root layout, so `.dark` follows `prefers-color-scheme`. The toaster follows it too.

**Strings** (en and zh): `poll.sealedTitle`, `poll.sealedTurnout`, `pollDetail.ruleSealed`, `pollDetail.ruleOneVote`, `navigation.howCountsTitle`, `navigation.howCountsBody`, `homePage.resultsIn`, `homePage.closingSoon`. No key was removed or renamed. `poll.voteCast` and `pollDetail.sealedExplainer` are no longer used on the web but stay, since vomatt-ios copies these files and still reads `sealedExplainer`. iOS can switch from `ios.sealedTitle`/`ios.sealedTurnout` to the new `poll.*` keys.

`DESIGN.md` now matches: the dark-mode sentence, the Tide uses, title weights, the radius rule, the home rail, and new building-block rows.

## Why

The question stays the hero, and trust is shown rather than claimed. The Seal thanks the voter and says exactly what happens to the ballot, where a bare toast said only "Vote cast." Tide gives the rules one consistent look. Status still always has a text label, and nothing shows per-option counts while a poll is open. Turnout is the only number shown.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 749 passed. The toast test now asserts the Seal. New tests cover the folded row, withdraw, a failed cast, the About rules and window bar, and `PollSideCard`.
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `npm run lint`: 0 errors. The 6 warnings were already on `main`.
- Checked in a browser in light and dark mode at 1440px, and at 375px for the stacked rail with no horizontal scroll.
- Not checked in a browser: the Seal after a real cast, since the local env points at the production API, and the rail cards with data. Both are covered by unit tests.

body:
Part of #3868

- Items 1 and 2: `ping`/`longdesc`/`data` removed in the chat sanitiser hook (test widens the allow-list via `sanitizeWithConfig`, so reverting the hook call fails it). `form`, `input`, `textarea`, `select`, `option`, `optgroup`, `button` forbidden. GFM task-list checkboxes render as text `[x]` / `[ ]`; a test mounts the real chat-markdown component, so removing the wiring fails it.
- Item 3: the mermaid/preview SVG was not sufficiently sanitised. `sanitizeSvg` now rebuilds `<style>` from an allow-list (`svg-css-sanitize.ts`):
  - The text is parsed with the browser CSS parser (`CSSStyleSheet.replaceSync`); without one the `<style>` is dropped (fail closed).
  - Kept: top-level style rules only, whose selectors are `#<root svg id>` followed by descendant/child combinators and tag, class, attribute (`=`, `$=`, `^=`, `*=`) and `:hover`/`:first-child`/`:last-child`/`:nth-child()` selectors; declarations re-serialised from the parsed rule.
  - Dropped: every at-rule (`@media`, `@keyframes`, `@scope`, `@container`, `@import`, `@font-face`, `@property`, `@page`, `@starting-style`), nested rules, sibling/`:has`/`:not`/`:is`/`:where`/`:root` selectors, `position`, `inset*`, `top/right/bottom/left`, `z-index`, `pointer-events`, any value with `var()`, `image-set`, `image()`, `src()`, backslashes, comments, braces, `<`, or a `url()` that is not a bare `#fragment`.
  - Attributes: a `style` attribute goes through the same declaration filter; any other attribute with a backslash, comment or non-fragment `url()` is removed; href on non-anchor elements must be a fragment or a data image.
  - Root-level rules: a rule whose selector has no descendant combinator (`#id{}`, `#id:hover{}`) additionally loses `transform`/`translate`/`scale`/`rotate`/`offset*`, `margin*`, `float`, `overflow*`, `width`, `height`, `min-width`, `min-height`, `max-height`, `clip*`, `opacity`, `mix-blend-mode`, `filter`, `backdrop-filter`, `display`, `contain*`, `isolation`, `will-change`, `perspective*` (`max-width` is kept: it only shrinks). The outermost svg gets inline `overflow:hidden !important; contain:paint !important; isolation:isolate !important`, which beats any author rule. `!important` on descendant rules is kept, since mermaid's gantt text colours depend on it.
  - Also dropped: `attr()` values and `animation*`/`transition*` properties. A themeCSS payload (`&{transform:scale(40);overflow:visible;margin-top:-999px}`) run through the real renderMermaid is tested: root computed overflow hidden, transform none, nothing paints outside the box.
  - Cost: mermaid's edge animation `@keyframes` (two per diagram) and its `:root` font-variable rule are lost; sequence diagrams also lose `.actorPopupMenu` (positioning only).
- Tests (real browser tier): hostile payloads (brace in string/url, all at-rule kinds, CSS nesting, sibling/:has selectors, escaped url in attributes, var position), the no-CSS-parser case, and real mermaid flowchart, sequence, class, state, gantt, pie, er, mindmap and gitGraph keeping text/shape/marker counts and scoped rules.

author: metatrot
body:
The fleet now launches only from the worker AMI it was told to use, and only once that AMI is available. If the AMI is missing or its snapshot is still pending, the launch stops with a message naming the AMI and its state, instead of silently booting stock Ubuntu and installing everything at boot.

<details><summary>What changes</summary>

- `get_worker_ami_id` resolves the AMI (an id, or the SSM parameter naming one), checks it with `DescribeImages`, and raises unless its state is `available`. No stock-Ubuntu lookup.
- `_launch_with_fallback` loses the "snapshot pending → stock Ubuntu" branch. The spot → on-demand fallback stays: spot is opt-in, the machine is the same, and the switch is printed.
- `bootstrap.sh` loses the from-scratch install of Docker, the AWS CLI and uv, which only a stock-Ubuntu boot reached; it now requires Docker to be running.
- Docs: the "falls back to stock Ubuntu" sentences are removed.

Also deletes the inline daemon.json pool merge in bootstrap, which only a stock-Ubuntu boot needed, and instead fails if the baked daemon.json lacks the pool.
- `scripts/build_worker_ami.sh` exits before writing SSM or deregistering the old AMI if the new image never becomes available, since a pending AMI in SSM would now stop every launch.
</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

The fallback saved the wait after publishing a new AMI, at the cost of runs on an environment nobody specified, so results could come from two different machine setups without anyone noticing. It also forced the Docker address-pool handling in bootstrap that #2602 and #2616 discuss.
</details>

<details><summary>Validation</summary>

Live on the EC2 fleet: a run given a malformed AMI id stopped at launch with "Worker AMI … not found" before any instance, queue or SSM write was left behind; the same trivial run with the SSM AMI booted from it, passed the address-pool check and completed (one c7i.4xlarge, about six minutes). The earlier mocked AWS tests are removed, since CONTRIBUTING.md forbids mocking. `make check` passes.
</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Fleet launches now hard-depend on a valid, available worker AMI in SSM; AMI build/publish mistakes or stale SSM values block runs until fixed, but avoids silent mixed worker environments.
> 
> **Overview**
> EC2 fleet workers now **only** boot from the pre-baked worker AMI in SSM (or an explicit AMI id). The controller **stops before `RunInstances`** if the AMI is missing, invalid, or not yet `available`, instead of falling back to stock Ubuntu and installing Docker/uv at boot.
> 
> **`get_worker_ami_id`** resolves the AMI from SSM or a direct id, runs `DescribeImages`, and raises with a clear message when the image is absent or pending. **`_launch_with_fallback`** keeps spot → on-demand only; the pending-snapshot → stock Ubuntu path is removed.
> 
> **Worker `bootstrap.sh`** no longer installs Docker, the AWS CLI, or uv from scratch or merges `daemon.json` at runtime—it **requires** a running Docker daemon and the baked `10.224.0.0/11` address pool, failing fast otherwise.
> 
> **`build_worker_ami.sh`** verifies the new image is `available` before updating SSM or deregistering the previous AMI, so a pending AMI cannot block all launches. Docs drop the old “~4 minute stock Ubuntu” worker boot narrative.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 14dc580e9f7779b5eca6a316cefaaeb8155e754c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

author: djamart
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"djamart"} -->
_Requested by **Diogo Martins** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BYD8T37xZZGHjGkSi3SJXb?thread=cmsg_01BYD8T37xZZGHjGkSi3SJXbLzo9ZuQynSTPa93t2fWr8E)_

## What changed

A single icon button at the right of the header shows the current theme (sun, moon or monitor) and opens a menu with Light, Dark and System. On wide screens the menu opens to the right of the button so it never covers the page text; on narrow screens it opens below. System is the default and follows the OS colour scheme, including when it changes while the page is open. Light and Dark override it and are remembered (localStorage) across pages and visits, applied by a tiny inline script in `<head>` before the first paint, so there is no flash of the other theme. Without JavaScript the button stays hidden and the system preference applies, as before.

The light theme now uses the same cinnabar accent as the dark theme (headings, underlines, focus rings): 3.06:1 on papaya whip, AA for large text and non-text UI, enforced by `contrast.test.ts`. Raspberry red stays in the CV PDF and the favicon.

- `src/styles/tokens.ts`: cinnabar accent in both themes; `themeCss()` honours `data-theme` on `<html>` (`:root[data-theme='dark']`, and the OS dark scheme unless `data-theme='light'`), and sets `color-scheme` per theme.
- `src/utils/theme.ts`: the choices, parsing of the stored value and the menu's keyboard focus logic, unit tested.
- `src/components/ThemeIcon.astro`: the three icons, shared by the button and the menu.
- Accessibility: WAI-ARIA menu button pattern. The button ("Theme", `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`) opens a menu of `menuitemradio`s with `aria-checked`; Arrow keys, Home/End, Enter/Space choose, Escape or a click elsewhere closes, focus returns to the button. Strings live in `src/i18n/ui.ts`.

## How it was tested

author: hongjicai
body:
## Why

A CVM running several service types currently runs one broker, event and ingress container set per provider (`ZG_CONTROLLER_INSTANCES`). The compose's service list then grows with every type. pcverify's per-service baseline (`brokercompose.json`) needs a separate recorded deployment for every combination, so the fleet's compliance check doesn't scale.

With this change one broker process and one event process serve every provider on the machine. The compose keeps the same services however many providers it serves, and per-machine values live only in fixed-name environment variables. One recorded deployment can then cover every machine with the same engine setup.

## What

**`CONFIG_DIR` (broker and event).** Every `<name>.yaml` in that directory is an extra provider instance beside the `CONFIG_FILE` one. Each has its own wallet and on-chain service, database, controller, workers and metrics. They share the process, the TEE signer and quote, and the port.
- **Routing.** A request reaches an instance by the host of its `service.servingUrl`. Anything unmatched (health checks, Prometheus, IPs) goes to the primary.
- **Misrouting.** A request that reaches the wrong instance is refused, not mis-billed: the session token names its provider.
- **Checks before start.** All configs are loaded and checked before any instance starts:
  - distinct `servingUrl` hosts with no path;
  - distinct wallets;
  - distinct databases, compared by server and database name;
  - the primary's chain, serving contract and nvGPU setting;
  - at most one instance with LoRA enabled.
- **Attested overrides.**
  - `DATABASE_DSN` decides every instance's database **server**, so unsealed bodies stay in the in-CVM MySQL. With extra instances it is **required**, on the broker and the event service alike, so the two can never open different databases for one instance.
  - Only the database name is per instance: the one its own `database.dsn` names, else `<primary>_<name>`. The broker creates and migrates it; the event service waits for it.
  - `TARGET_URL` stays the primary's. An extra instance's upstreams come from its config, measured by the upstream-set record like every `modelPricing[].targetUrl` already is.
- **Metrics.** One `/metrics` on the primary's engine, mounted when any instance enables monitoring. It serves every instance's series.

**Per-instance state.**
- Metrics are a per-instance `monitor.Metrics`. Series names and labels are unchanged, so dashboards keyed on `server` / `provider_address` keep working.
- `proxy.New` no longer takes a monitor flag: TrackMetrics is installed exactly when the instance has metrics.
- The model-mismatch limiter moved from a process global onto `Ctrl`.

**Controller.** With `CONFIG_DIR` in its own env, `GET|PUT /v1/config/core?instance=<name>` reads and replaces `<name>.yaml`. Each change is recorded as `zg-instance-config-update` and restarts the primary broker and event.
- **Validation.** The whole set is validated under the change lock, with the broker's own loader and directory listing. It uses the `DATABASE_DSN` the broker container actually runs with, read over the docker socket.
- **Refusals.** A controller with `CONFIG_DIR` refuses a change when the broker has none. A primary change is validated against the instances too.
- **Single instance.** A controller without `CONFIG_DIR` does nothing new.
- **No creating or removing.** The API never creates or removes an instance.
- **Exclusive.** Refused together with `ZG_CONTROLLER_INSTANCES`.

**`zg-upstream-set` covers every in-process provider** (`doc/rtmr3-records.md` §4.3). Member lines may end with `provider=<0x + 40 lowercase hex>`. A set tags every member or none, and names are unique per provider.
- **Hash compatibility.** A set without providers, which is every deployment today, hashes exactly as before, so no signer rotates. This is pinned by `TestUpstreamSetHashWithoutProvidersIsUnchanged`.
- **When it is recorded.** Boot, a primary change and an instance change all record the union. A failed write re-records the set from disk.

**Docs.** `doc/controller-design.md` §3.3a describes the feature and the exact compose changes:
- `DOMAINS` on the ingress (dstack-ingress 2.2 already supports it);
- the instance-writing loop in `broker-config-init`;
- `CONFIG_DIR` on broker, event and controller;
- the broker's `DATABASE_DSN` literal on the event service.

The compose template itself is not in this repo.

## Single-instance deployments

With `CONFIG_DIR` unset (or the directory empty), behaviour is unchanged:
- routing, config loading and env precedence;
- RTMR3 records and key derivation;
- metrics output;
- shutdown order.

Startup order moved only in that the TEE quote is now taken before the DB connects.

## Rollout

1. Merge and release the reader first: 0gfoundation/0g-pc-e2ee#167. An older reader refuses a `provider=`-tagged record and reads the set as unknown.
2. Release this broker (target v0.5.5).
3. Migrate `ZG_CONTROLLER_INSTANCES` machines, then re-record their deployments in `brokercompose.json` with `pcverify -blocks`.
4. **Shared signer.** With `recordUpstreamSet` on, any instance's upstream change rotates the signer that all instances share. Every provider address then needs its signer acknowledged again on chain.

## Testing

- **Unit tests.** `go test ./inference/... ./controller/... ./common/...` pass.
- **Integration tests.** `go test -tags integration ./inference/... ./controller/... ./common/...` pass against MySQL 8.0 testcontainers, including the new `EnsureDatabase` test.
- **Lint.** `golangci-lint --new-from-rev` reports 0 issues.
- **New tests** cover:
  - two `Metrics` instances on one registry;
  - `/metrics` mounting;
  - the host router;
  - instance loading and every refusal;
  - controller in-process changes;
  - set validation and `CONFIG_DIR` disagreement;
  - provider-tagged grammar, render and hash;
  - the multi-provider record and its restore after a failed write.
- **Review fixes.** An independent review found seven issues, fixed in `e9c8654`. A second pass found six more, fixed in `c47aa8b`: unscrapeable metrics with the primary unmonitored, broker and event able to open different databases, and the event process creating empty databases, plus three cleanups. Each has a regression test. The shared-database and set-restore tests fail without their fix.
- **Not yet done:** no live two-instance run on a CVM. Still to check on a testnet machine:
  - router and compute-status reading each instance's model list through its own domain;
  - `pcverify -provider` matching two addresses to one recorded deployment.

This pull request introduces a comprehensive set of mandatory engineering standards and quality gates for the Kha Hoàng Minh project, focused on eliminating low-quality AI-generated output, enforcing strict frontend architecture, optimizing asset handling, and establishing a robust pre-delivery checklist. The changes add detailed documentation and configuration files that define the required practices for UI design, code organization, performance, and code hygiene.

The most important changes are:

**1. Anti-AI Slop & Senior Craftsmanship Rules**
- Introduces `.agents/rules/anti-ai-slop.md`, a detailed policy banning generic AI-generated design and code patterns ("AI Slop"), mandating authentic industrial aesthetics, proper UX, meaningful copy, atomic architecture, and strict localization.

**2. Frontend Architecture & Code Organization**
- Adds `.agents/rules/architecture.md`, formalizing a 5-tier atomic design system, enforcing thin route controllers, barrel imports, and centralized localization/data management for all frontend code.

**3. Asset Engineering & Performance Standards**
- Provides `.agents/rules/performance-assets.md`, establishing rules for optical logo normalization, Next.js image optimization (with explicit sizing and alt text), hardware-accelerated animations, and motion accessibility.

**4. Pre-Delivery Quality Checklist**
- Implements `.agents/rules/quality-checklist.md`, an 8-point verification gate covering UI surface hierarchy, dark mode contrast, asset handling, atomic structure, localization, and production build integrity, plus a zero-regression protocol for interactive features.

**5. Environment File Protection**
- Adds `.agents/hooks.json` to enable a pre-tool-use hook that blocks unsafe access or modification of environment files using a Node.js script, protecting sensitive configuration.

- **Galerie** : toucher une story avec photo ouvre directement le choix de photo du système.
- **Aperçu plein écran** (`components/PhotoStoryComposer.tsx`) :
  - un sélecteur passe de La séance au Relevé ;
  - le bloc de notes se déplace et se pince comme un sticker ; il s'aimante sur l'axe du milieu, et un double toucher le recentre ;
  - pendant le geste, on voit les zones qu'Instagram masque (250 px en haut, 220 px en bas) ;
  - la photo se cadre au doigt ;
  - on choisit entre « Couleurs du film » (virage pris sur les teintes de l'affiche, avec grain et vignettage) et « Photo brute » ;
  - le voile sous les textes suit la luminosité mesurée de la photo.
- **Partage** : une seule image JPEG 1080 × 1920, déjà assemblée, passe par le même circuit que les stories existantes (feuille de partage, sinon téléchargement). Le menu « … » propose aussi le sticker seul, en PNG transparent (pour une vidéo), recentrer le bloc et changer de photo.
- **Vie privée** : la photo est décodée et dessinée sur l'appareil, elle n'est jamais envoyée.

## Fichiers

- `utils/photoStory.ts` : géométrie et règles, sans import (placement, bornage, aimant, voile, cadrage, découpe de l'avis).
- `utils/photoStoryRender.ts` : dessin sur canvas, étalonnage, sticker seul.
- `ShareStoryButtonSimple.tsx` : nouvelle feuille, choix de la photo, et partage factorisé dans `deliverImage`.
- Textes FR/EN, `public/story-thumbs/`, `changelog.json` (nouvelle icône `photo` dans l'écran de mise à jour).

## Vérifications

- `tsc --noEmit` passe, et la suite de tests aussi : 281 tests, dont 10 nouveaux dans `tests/photoStory.test.mjs`.
- `vite build` passe.
- Recette dans Chrome en 390 × 844 avec Playwright sur le banc local : feuille, choix de photo, aperçu du Relevé, déplacement avec les repères, couleurs du film, Séance, export JPEG et sticker PNG.

À vérifier sur téléphone après la mise en prod :
- pincement à deux doigts (testé seulement à la souris) ;
- partage vers Instagram depuis la PWA iPhone et Android ;
- photo HEIC sur iPhone.

_Requested by **victor** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01CSEuL4WMFUhq8kBvNeWH8M?thread=cmsg_01CSEuL4WMFUhq8kBvNeWH8M829xAPTXEzKf9muMFWCNHG)_

## 这个 PR 做了什么

S11 W1 的 GO5c：入口 agent 可以替它代表的人提议一个目标，由那个人在控制台确认。

**之前：** 目标只能由内核代码直接建（`createGoalRun`），没有任何能力能提议目标。确认卡片只看到计划本身的提示（「没有平台能做的检查」），看不到请求人现在能不能真的启动这些步骤：一个步骤要用请求人没权限的门，确认后目标会跑到那一步才暂停（`authority_lost`）。陈述和计划里写了凭据，或者从读面抄回来的 `[redacted]`，`revise_goal` 照收计划。

**之后：**
- 新能力 `propose_goal`（handle 通道，`mode: propose`，`minRole: member`）：陈述、计划 v1、预算，可选 `idempotencyKey`。请求人就是调用者：Handle 上是 `obo`，人的通道上是登录的人。目标停在 `proposed`，什么都不执行，等请求人在控制台 `confirm_goal`。
- 入口 agent 在 Handle 上能读自己代表的人的目标（`get_goal`、`list_goals`、`get_goal_revision`、`list_goal_unresolved_actions`），只读请求人是 obo 本人的，owner 的 Handle 也一样。
- 确认卡片说清楚哪一步请求人现在启动不了、为什么。
- 带凭据或 `[redacted]` 的陈述、计划、修订理由都被拒，什么都不写，错误里指出具体位置。
- 目标只能替人提议：服务账号和 agent 主体发起的 `propose_goal` 一律 403。每个请求人同时等待确认的目标最多 5 个（可调），超出 409。
- 在控制台编辑器里修订时，没动过的调用（一步的 Worker 和输入、一条 reconcile 动作或检查、一条验收检查）里读出时被遮蔽的值、不可见字符被写成 `\u{…}` 的值保留存储里的原文，只检查新写的值；改过的调用里留下的 `[redacted]` 要重新填写。

### 能力与上限

- `propose_goal` 经 `propose_` 前缀进入口上限（member 的入口 Handle 就有）；四个目标读能力显式加进入口上限（`ENTRY_CEILING_EXTRA_CAPABILITY_NAMES`）。目标的各项操作（确认、暂停、修订……）仍只在人的通道。
- Worker 上限显式排除 `propose_goal`（`WORKER_CEILING_EXCLUDED_PROPOSE_NAMES`）：步骤里的 Worker 不能自己再开目标，否则会在推进器之外起一队 Worker，绕开目标的预算和依赖（和步骤 Handle 不带 `invoke_worker`、除非计划写了 `nested` 是同一个理由）。WorkerDefinition 声明了也拿不到（`computeChildHandleScope` 按 Worker 上限过滤）。
- Handle 上读目标只看 `requester = obo` 的（协调线程定的）：看全工作区、对别人的目标 hold / 取消只走人的通道（控制台）。owner 的 Handle 读成员的目标返回 404，`list_goals` 里也没有。
- **只替人提议**（评审 #493 第 1 条，协调线程定）：目标必须有一个能在控制台确认的人类请求人。注册表新增 `actsForPerson` 标记，`propose_goal` 带上它：
  - 人的通道：调用者不是人类主体（服务账号的 key）时，`authorizeCapabilityCall` 返回 403；
  - Handle 通道：分发时查 obo 的主体类型，不是 `human` 就 403（服务账号的 Handle、agent 主体）；
  - `issue_service_handle` 不再把它签进服务 Handle（和角色不允许的能力一样静默去掉），CLI 的 `issue-service-handle` 直接拒绝，控制台签服务 Handle 的能力列表里也不再列出；
  - `actsForPerson` 不能和 `scope: platform` 同用（注册表一致性检查）。
- **每个请求人的待确认上限**（评审 #493 第 5 条，协调线程定）：一个请求人名下同时处于 `proposed` 的目标最多 `GOAL_MAX_PROPOSED_PER_REQUESTER` 个（默认 5，正整数，内核启动时校验，写错就起不来）。超出时 409 `proposed_goal_limit`，`details.limit` / `details.proposed`，什么都不写；确认、驳回一个就空出一个位置。按请求人加事务级咨询锁，幂等回放在计数之前，所以重发照常拿回原目标。
- 入口 agent 在一轮对话里提议，这一轮记为目标的来源（`originated_in_turn_id`，和 `invoke_worker` 记 Task 的来源一样，用 `findAttributableTurn` 找 obo 正在跑的一轮）。人的通道上不记。

### 重发返回原来的目标（R-54，迁移 goal 0008）

`goal_runs` 加 `idempotency_key`（可空，不回填），键的两种形式和 `request_action` / `invoke_worker` 一样：
- 传了 `idempotencyKey`：存成 `explicit:<obo>:<sid>:<key>`（`scopeExplicitIdempotencyKey`）。同一个键返回它第一次建的目标，不管目标现在是什么状态、这次传的内容是什么（`changed: false`）。
- 没传：存成 `auto:<sid 或请求人>:<陈述、计划、预算的哈希>`。只在那个目标还是 `proposed` 时去重；确认、驳回或结束以后，同样的提议再来就是新目标。人的通道没有 sid，按人去重，所以控制台里连点两下是一个目标。
- 两个部分唯一索引兜底并发：同一个键并发插入只有一行，另一个调用在保存点里撞上唯一约束后回放赢家（和 `requestAction` 一样）。

### 不收的内容（错误格式和控制台的计划编辑器对齐）

- 陈述：空白（网关 400 `invalid_params`）；超过 2000 字符；带疑似凭据（400 `credentials_in_text`，`details.field: "statement"`）；带 `[redacted]`（400 `redacted_text_submitted`，`details.field: "statement"`）。
- 计划（`propose_goal` 和 `revise_goal` 一样）：带疑似凭据（400 `credentials_in_text`）或 `[redacted]`（400 `redacted_text_submitted`）。`details.field` 是第一个出问题的位置，`details.suspectedSecretPaths` / `details.paths` 列出全部位置（最多 20 个），格式是 `plan.` 加点分路径，数组下标从 0 开始，可以深到叶子：`plan.steps.0.input.password`、`plan.steps.1.input.targets.1.header`、`plan.acceptance.0.prompt`。判定规则和读出时遮蔽的规则相同（参数上按字段名，其余按文本）。
- `revise_goal` 的理由带 `[redacted]` 也拒（`details.field: "reason"`）。
- 一个 schema 字面量写在密钥名字段下（如 `input.schema.apiKey.default`）只算一次（评审 #493 第 2 条：以前参数规则和文本规则各算一次）。
- 计划检查（400 `invalid_params`，`details.problems`）：每条步骤级问题以 `step "<key>": ` 开头（重复的 key、依赖自己、依赖不存在的步骤、依赖成环、引用的 WorkerDefinition 不存在 / 不是 worker / 没发布）；目标级验收检查以 `acceptance[<i>] "<key>": ` 开头；只有「计划太大」不属于任何部分。
- 内容检查在幂等回放之前：带凭据的重发不会因为键匹配就拿回目标。
- 计划只能引用已发布的 `WorkerDefinition@version`（GO1 的 `validatePlan`，不变）；Procedure 作为计划模板在 GO5d。
- 预算由提议方定，确认时改不了（`confirm_goal` 只收 `goalRunId` 和 `revision`）；要改预算就重新提议。

这套格式按协调线程转来的控制台约定写，已和控制台线程对过；能力描述里也写明了（契约快照里能看到）。网关自己的参数校验失败（比如计划形状不对）仍是不带 `details` 的 `invalid_params`。

### 修订时没改的值保留原文（协调线程定，对齐 #501 在 #702 的意见）

控制台的计划编辑器从读出的计划预填，读出的是显示形式：疑似凭据换成 `[redacted]`，看不见的字符写成字面的 `\u{XXXX}`。用户没动的值原样提交时，不能被当成改动，也不能被拒收。`reviewRevisedPlan`（`plan.ts`）以「整次调用」为单位处理（#493 第二、三轮增量复审）：
1. 步骤按 key、计划级验收检查按 key，对齐到 `basedOnRevision` 那一版（`revise_goal` 只收等于当前版本的 `basedOnRevision`）。
2. 对齐的条目里，每一次调用整体比较：按读出原样提交，就换回存储的那次调用；任何地方改过（值、目标、门、操作），里面的值一律按提交的算，留下的 `[redacted]` 在它的位置拒收。调用是：
   - 步骤的 Worker 连同它的 `input`：换了 Worker，`input` 就不换回，否则存储的密码会交给新 Worker；
   - reconcile 的一条 `action`、一条 `check`，各自整个对象（含 `gatekeeperId`、`operation`），按位置对齐，而且只在这一步的 reconcile 条数和读出一样时才对齐，删掉或加一条，后面的都不换回；
   - 一条验收检查（计划级和步骤内的都按 key 对齐），整个检查对象。
   读出把每个被遮蔽的值都显示成同一个 `[redacted]`，所以单独按位置换回一个值，它就会跟着被删掉或对调的行走，或者被发往另一个 host、门或 Worker。调用之外的字段（`maxAttempts`、`dependsOn`、`nested`）不参与判断：「只改 `maxAttempts`、调用都原样」照样换回。别的 key 下放同样的显示形式不会换回原文。
3. 先换回，再查凭据和 `[redacted]`：只查这个人新写的值，位置仍按提交的计划算。原样提交的调用里，显示时被改过的值不进检查；显示时原样的值照常检查（它保持计划结构，检查在里面只可能找到检查上线前就存着的 `[redacted]`）。
4. 显示形式用 `get_goal` 读修订时的同一个函数 `planAsRead`（`views.ts` 和 `toWirePlanRevision` 都只用它，原来 `toWirePlanRevision` 里单独套的 `shownFreeTextIn` 已合进去）。
5. 换回后的计划再去 `validatePlan`，`samePlanEntry` 也拿它和以前的版本比，所以没动的步骤不会被替换、在跑的任务不会被终止。

前瞻（#493）：现在只有请求人能修订。以后如果修订也可以由别人发起（W2 的 planner、管理员 agent），这条换回规则要重新评估，因为那时「把存储的值挪到新上下文」就是一条外泄通道。

`update_operation_description` 按同一规则：提交的描述等于当前描述的显示形式时直接返回，不写、不记审计（结果里是显示形式）。

### 确认卡片：请求人现在能不能启动这些步骤（提示，不拒收）

`planAuthorityHints`（新 `application/goal/precheck.ts`）对每一步跑一遍推进器启动步骤时的同一个判断 `resolveStepAuthority`。这个函数是从 `createStepAttemptTask` 里提出来的，推进器和确认卡片共用：
- `requester_cannot_start_workers`：请求人的角色不能启动 Worker，或者已被停用。整个计划只给这一条。
- `step_gate_not_held`（带 `stepKey`、`gatekeeperIds`）：这一步的 Worker 声明了请求人现在操作不了的门。
- `step_capability_not_held`（带 `stepKey`、`capabilityNames`）：Worker 声明了请求人自己没有的执行类能力，`capabilityNames` 列出缺的全部能力（UX P2-2；推进器的 `authority_lost` 也带上这份列表）。
- `step_definition_excluded`（带 `stepKey`）：请求人的智能体设置排除了这个 Worker。

是提示不是拒收：权限是世界的状态，不是计划的毛病，owner 可以在走到那一步之前把门授给请求人。所以不存进修订，每次读都现算：`propose_goal` 和 `revise_goal` 的结果，以及还在 `proposed` 的目标的提议（`get_goal`、`get_goal_revision`）。确认时不再检查，走到那一步才暂停（推进器原有的判断，没变）。用同一个 Worker 版本的步骤只查一次。`revise_goal` 的结果只对还会开始的步骤算（已结束的保留步骤不会再启动）。

## 控制台在 GO6 怎么显示

这个 PR 已经改了控制台：
- **目标详情的步骤卡片**（UX P2-1）：请求人权限相关的提示放在卡片顶部，每条一个警告条；提示点名的步骤行上加标记「请求人无权限」或「智能体设置已排除」。「只凭请求人确认」这条和验收有关，留在验收卡片。
- **提示文字**（UX P2-2、P3-1、P3-2）：门写成「门「prod-cert-gate」、「99999999」」（没有名字时用短 id）；缺的能力用控制台的中文名，比如「步骤「apply」的 Worker 需要执行权限「发起动作请求」，请求人现在没有：这一步不会开始，目标会停在这里等人处理。可以请工作区所有者在「成员与授权」给请求人开通，或者驳回，让助手换个做法。」每条都写下一步怎么办。
- **确认卡片**（GO6 操作栏的「确认并开始」）：影响列表在步骤数和预算下面列出全部提示，每条前面加「注意：」（UX P3-3）。
- **错误**：`proposed_goal_limit` 显示为「等待确认的目标太多」，下一步「先确认或驳回一个等待确认的目标，再提议新的。」
- **签服务 Handle**（成员页）：能力列表不再列出 `propose_goal`。
- **能力标签**：`propose_goal` 显示为「提议目标」。
- **自助签 Handle**（账户页，给 Claude Code / MCP 用）：能力选择里多了「提议目标」和四个目标读能力，和内核的入口上限一致。
- 修订编辑器（GO6 后续）收到 `credentials_in_text` / `redacted_text_submitted` 时，按 `details.field` 和路径列表定位到字段，提示重新填写（换了 Worker、改了 reconcile 条数或门时，原来遮蔽的值都要重填）；`invalid_params` 按 `details.problems` 的 `step "<key>"` 前缀挂到对应步骤上。

入口 agent 真正能在对话里调用 `propose_goal`，要等 GO5e 把它注册成入口工具（`ENTRY_TOOL_CAPABILITY_NAMES`）、加入口 prompt 和 fake-llm 旅程。

## 主机窗口

### 新环境变量（可选）

`GOAL_MAX_PROPOSED_PER_REQUESTER`：每个请求人同时等待确认的目标上限，默认 5，正整数。不设就是 5；写错（0、负数、小数、非数字）内核启动失败并说明原因。

### 迁移 goal 0008

- 只加一个可空列和两个部分唯一索引（`goal_runs`），不回填，`idempotency_key is null` 的行两个索引都不收。
- 窗口前只读检查：`select count(*) from goal_runs;`（建索引的行数，预期很小）。
- 可逆性：上一版不知道这一列，插入时它是 NULL，两个索引都不管，回滚再升级不受影响。`goal_runs_status_guard` 不允许改这一列（它不在可改列里），这一列写入后就不变。

## 检查清单

- [x] **契约快照**：`pnpm contract:snapshot` 已更新（新能力 `propose_goal`，带 `actsForPerson`；`PlanHint` 多了四个 code 和可选的 `stepKey` / `gatekeeperIds` / `capabilityNames`；`revise_goal`、`propose_goal`、`update_operation_description` 的描述写明错误格式和「没改的值保留原文」）。`pnpm contract:check` 通过。
- [ ] **主机验收**：有迁移（goal 0008）和一个可选环境变量，release.md 需要条目（见上）。
- [x] **文档**：STATUS、dev

## 요약
AI·ML(`ai`) 트랙 11유닛 `u11-rag-agents`(RAG와 에이전트)와 12유닛 `u12-eval-ops`(평가와 운영)의 문제 파일을 작성했다. curriculum.json은 건드리지 않았다.

- 18레슨 × 10문제 = 180문제, 레슨마다 single 6 · ox 2(O 1·X 1) · fill 2(005·006)
- qslug: `rag-*`(u11), `evalops-*`(u12)
- 코드 문제 4개(python): 청크 나누기 오버랩 빈칸·청크 수, 정확 일치 채점 결과, JSON 형식 검증 통과 수 — 모두 실행해 정답 확인
- 계산 문제(토큰 비용 300원, TTFT 0.8초, 생성 4초, 오류율 2%, A/B 비율) 스크립트로 확인

## 점검
- `pnpm content:validate` 통과, `pnpm --filter @cs-daily/api test` 111개 통과
- 스크립트 전수 점검: 유형·위치, OX 균형, 문제 50자·보기 15자·해설 20~120자, fill 평문 정답, 힌트 노출, 정답 index 분포(0:34 · 1:35 · 2:39), 전 트랙 id 중복, 벤더 이름, 비유어, 기존 문장과 유사도 0.8 이상 0건, 코드 12줄·48자

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`LocalDisk.delete()` unlinks a file and its sidecar but keeps the folder it was in. A later `put()`, `copy()` or `move()` onto that folder's name then fails with `StorageKeyConflictError`, although `exists()` and `list()` show no key there. `InMemoryDisk` and `S3Disk` accept the same steps. `move()` leaves the source's folder behind the same way.

Issue Number: #33

## What is the new behavior?

Thanks to @johnnyhuirilef for the report, the repro and both ideas for the fix. This PR combines them:

- **Prune on delete and move (idea 1).** After a delete or move, each folder it left empty is removed, deepest first, up to the root (never the root itself, never `.nest-storage`). It uses non-recursive `rmdir` and stops at the first folder that still holds something or can't be removed. This keeps the tree from filling with empty folders that `list()` would still walk.
- **Write-side fallback (idea 2).** When the final rename hits a folder at the key, the write tries `rmdir` on it. If the folder was empty, the rename is retried; if not, it is still a `StorageKeyConflictError`. This covers roots that already hold empty folders from earlier versions, a crash between unlink and rmdir, or another tool.
- **Race handling.** If a concurrent delete prunes a write's folder after `ensureParent()`, the rename fails with `ENOENT`. The write then creates the folder again and retries, up to 3 attempts. If a file was put at that folder's name in between, the write gets `StorageKeyConflictError`, so the documented rule that `a` and `a/b` can't both exist still holds.

Sidecars are flat files under `.nest-storage/meta/`, so they leave no folders behind. `exists()` and `list()` are unchanged.

Tests: one test in the shared disk suite runs on every disk (it failed only on `LocalDisk` before). LocalDisk-only tests cover pruning, an empty folder left by another tool, a folder that still holds something (a conflict), and symbolic links. Two deterministic race tests stub `rename`.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?
- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

- Behaviour change: any folder under the root that a delete or move leaves empty is removed, including folders created by hand (for example a pre-made `uploads/`). The next write that needs it creates it again.
- The write-side fallback removes one level only. An already-present chain of empty folders such as `a/b/` still blocks `put('a')` until a delete through the disk prunes it.
- Windows: `EPERM` (rename onto a folder) and `EPERM`/`EBUSY` (rmdir) are handled, but untested, since CI runs on Linux only.

- GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw: RCE in the Image Optimization API via SVG. This repo sets `images.dangerouslyAllowSVG: true`.
- GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4: RCE in the Image Optimization API via AVIF
- GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36: RCE on Windows-hosted servers
- GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw: authorization bypass in middleware

There are also many high and medium issues: Server Components/Server Actions DoS, SSRF, cache poisoning, and others. See `gh api "/advisories?ecosystem=npm&affects=next@14.2.5&per_page=100"`. `next@16.4.2` has **0** advisories.

## What changed
- `next` 14.2.5 → 16.4.2, `eslint-config-next` 14.2.5 → 16.4.2
- `react` / `react-dom` 18.3.1 → 19.3.1, `@types/react` 18.3.3 → 19.3.0
- `react-leaflet` ^4.2.1 → ^5.0.0 (the React 19 peer). It is not imported in `src/` right now.
- `eslint` 8 → 9. `next lint` was removed in Next 16, so `lint` now runs `eslint .` with a flat `eslint.config.mjs` (`eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals`). `.eslintrc.json` is deleted.
- `tsconfig.json` / `next-env.d.ts`: the mandatory changes `next build` applies (`moduleResolution: bundler`, `jsx: react-jsx`, route type imports)

author: robmina
body:
`Reconstruction.Output` (and so `DetailedOutput` and every reco/recoMC output module built from it) and
`Reconstruction.RegrowOutput` get `compressionLevel : 505` (ROOT convention algorithm*100+level: ZSTD, level 5).
No Production config set a compression level before, so all reco outputs used art's default, zlib level 7.

**Why.** In the October 2026 reco profile, writing the output is 12-15 % of on-spill MC reco instructions and about
65 % of KPP data reco, most of it in zlib.

**Choice of setting.** Four settings compared with the reco profiling harness (Offline main, same events, all arms of
a workload on one host):

| workload | setting | CPU | output size | full read-back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| on-spill CE+1BB, 500 ev | zlib 1 (101) | -7.0 % | +2.9 % | -7 % |
| | LZ4 4 (404) | -8.6 % | +8.1 % | -33 % |
| | **ZSTD 5 (505)** | **-4.6 %** | **-2.7 %** | **-12 %** |
| KPP data run 124155, 2000 ev | zlib 1 (101) | -35.5 % | +8.3 % | 0 % |
| | LZ4 4 (404) | -36.3 % | +19.1 % | -23 % |
| | **ZSTD 5 (505)** | **-18.5 %** | **-5.7 %** | **-19 %** |

ZSTD 5 is the only setting that improves CPU, file size and read time together. zlib 1 and LZ4 save more CPU but make
files 3-19 % larger; that trade-off is for Production and computing to decide, so this PR does not take it.

**Test of this PR** through the real JobConfigs: this branch on the nightly build (Offline `78ea1fd5a`), the
PR (ZSTD 5) against the same configuration with `compressionLevel : 7` (the current default), same events, both arms
on one host:

| workload | events | CPU (zlib 7 -> ZSTD 5) | output size | full read-back (every branch, every entry) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recoMC/OnSpill.fcl`, CE+1BB MDC2025au | 500 | 63.1 -> 60.6 s (**-3.9 %**) | 146.1 -> 142.2 MB (**-2.7 %**) | 2.86 -> 2.48 s (**-13 %**) |
| `reco/Extracted.fcl` (KPP daqana3 data reco), run 124155 | 2,000 | 26.8 -> 21.0 s (**-21.6 %**) | 145.0 -> 136.7 MB (**-5.7 %**) | 5.53 -> 4.66 s (**-16 %**) |

One run per arm; expect a few percent of run-to-run noise on the on-spill CPU.

**The change is lossless.** EventNtuples made from the two arms' outputs are bit-identical (every leaf, rtol 0): 481
leaves over 500 events on-spill, 152 leaves over 2,000 events for KPP data.

**Reading the files.** Reading ZSTD needs ROOT >= 6.20.
- art and EventNtuple read the ZSTD outputs (they made the ntuples above).
- uproot in the Mu2e `ana` environment (python-zstandard 0.25) decompresses every basket of every branch of the ZSTD
  `.art` files without error: 11,589 baskets on-spill, 9,920 for KPP.
- EventNtuple `.root` files are written by TFileService and are not affected by this PR.

**Configs checked.** Every reco and recoMC JobConfig with a RootOutput resolves with `compressionLevel: 505` on all its
output modules: OnSpill, OffSpill, Extracted, NoField, NoFieldRun1B, OnSpillRetrigger, OffSpillRetrigger, regrowLH,
regrowKL, RefRegrow.

author: alecandido
body:
Closes #40. The diagnosis is in the [issue comment](https://github.com/qiboteam/qibocal-mcp-servers/issues/40); cancellation (#42) and MCP Tasks (#43) are left for later.

## Behaviour

- `execute_protocol` starts a background run, with its `run_id` assigned before it acquires. It then waits for the run up to `wait` seconds, 45 by default, which is below common client request timeouts.
  - A fast run returns its result as before, in a single call.
  - A longer run returns `{run_id, status, elapsed_s, executions, estimated_s, …}`, and the new **`get_run(run_id, wait)`** waits again.
  - A request that times out or is cancelled never stops the run.
- One acquisition runs at a time. During a run, notes, notes reading, state reads and context answer, while another acquisition, an update, an edit or a session switch is refused, with a message pointing to `get_run`.
- **Progress:** each run counts Qibolab's platform executions and sums the duration estimates Qibolab logs for them (`Pulse execution time: …`). A protocol may execute many times, so this is an "estimate so far", not a total. It also goes out as MCP progress notifications to clients that ask for them.

## Commits

1. **Runtime: background runs on a dedicated hardware thread.**
   - Qibolab installs signal handlers in `Platform.__post_init__`, which is why the platform is still created on the main thread.
   - Connection, acquisitions and disconnection move to one hardware thread, so the event loop stays free. The instruments are now connected at the first acquisition, not at startup.
   - New modules: `runs.py`, the run registry with bounded waits, shared with the gateway; and `progress.py`, which captures the estimates.
   - The frontend forwards `wait`, `get_run` and progress.
2. **Gateway: only acquisitions use SLURM.**
   - Updates, edits, sessions, notes, state reads and context are software only. With lazy connection they now run in a local worker on the access node, so they never wait for an allocation.
   - Acquisitions are background `srun` jobs that release the gateway's lock while they run.
   - Worker stderr is read line by line: marked progress lines update the run, which shows `queued` until the job starts.
   - A run still in progress when the gateway exits is stopped.
3. **Policy and docs.**
   - The policy now says: report a queued or running status with its estimate, wait with `get_run`, never resubmit.
   - The architecture, cluster, safety and reference pages describe the new behaviour; `get_run` and `wait` are documented.

## Verification

- `poe lint`, `poe test` (159 tests) and `poe docs` pass.
- New tests use a protocol that blocks until released, with a logged estimate, in direct mode. They check the running status and estimate, that notes and reads answer during the run, that state changes and acquisitions are refused, that `get_run` returns the images and reminder, and that updating afterwards works.
- A fake SLURM job that stays queued, then reports progress, then is released checks that its note ran locally, without `srun`.
- A shared test helper now serves the fake workers through real pipes. Existing assertions changed only where the behaviour did: only acquisitions call `srun` and connect.
- Checked by hand that the gateway's pipe handling works with a real subprocess.

Not yet tried on hardware.

## Behaviour changes to note

- Instrument connection errors now appear at the first acquisition rather than at startup.
- On SLURM, context, updates and notes create the platform on the access node, without connecting, using the same environment as the jobs.

Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Remotive, Kmong and Soomgo have recorded public HTTP executions; the results preserve source IDs, pay/package terms and bounded pagination. Job snapshots compare matching scopes and never treat a missing listing as proof of closure.

Reed and Upwork provide documented, caller-credential read clients with fixture coverage; live API access remains unverified. TokyoDev supports exact company/role identities and offline parsing of saved HTML, with current HTTP 403 kept explicit. No application, quote, order or message submission is included.

- Local root regression, focused integration checks, 17 existing client packs, doctor, consolidation audit and MyRealTrip pack compatibility.
- 16 actual native/common CLI executions, 18 capability receipts and independent job-ID readbacks. Kmong search/detail/reviews and two-page Soomgo collection were replayed.

author: strudeldoodles
body:
## A SuperLSS model saved on one machine loads on another

### What was wrong

`SuperLSS.from_bytes()` refused valid models saved on a different machine, or on the same machine with a different BLAS kernel or NumPy dispatch. Two checks compared recomputed floating-point values bit for bit.

1. **The likelihood plan identifier hashed a derived carrier.** For `GammaLS`, `LogNormalLS`, `GeneralizedGammaLSS`, `TwoPieceLogNormalLSS`, `TwoPieceNormalLSS`, `GaussianLS` with non-unit prior weights and `NegativeBinomialLS`, the identifier included a digest of the parameter-independent carrier. That carrier is `-log y`, `0.5 log w` or `-log(count!)`, times the row multiplier. Every load rebinds the plan and compares the identifier exactly, and so does the corrected-covariance replay. NumPy's AVX-512 `log` and the C library's `log` disagree by one ulp on about 0.1% of inputs, and neither is correctly rounded everywhere. So a model saved on an AVX-512 machine was refused on one without AVX-512, and the other way round. At 5,000 rows every affected family was refused in both directions.
2. **The manifest bound tolerances derived from a LAPACK norm.** A penalty face recomputes `rank_resolution`, `null_residual_bound` and `orthogonality_bound` at load, and the manifest compared them exactly. The first two scale with `np.linalg.norm(C, 2)` of its stored constraint matrix. The third is a function of the face's shape, so it never varied, but it was compared with them. Changing only the OpenBLAS kernel (`OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell`) moved the norm by an ulp. Any family's `fit_reml` that reached an exact penalty face was then refused with "manifest does not match fitted model payload".
3. Two smaller bitwise BLAS comparisons ran at load. Endpoint revalidation required the stored endpoint to equal a fresh BLAS replay of a face projection, and face-geometry matching compared two `N Nᵀ` products bit for bit.

v0.40.0 has the first two. SuperGLM had no such refusal.

### What users get

- A SuperLSS model loads, predicts and refits on any machine, whichever CPU, NumPy SIMD dispatch, C maths library or OpenBLAS kernel saved it.
- Every model saved by v0.40.0 or earlier, and by the builds that wrote schema 11, still loads. Old identifiers are accepted under the rule below. A model saved by this build is schema 12, which an older build refuses at its version gate instead of reporting a manifest mismatch.
- A model whose stored state does not match its rows is still refused. That covers a changed response, changed weights, another family or row law, or a carrier formula that moved by more than rounding.
- The extra load cost is O(n): about 1.6 ms per million rows for the carrier check.

### What changes

**Likelihood identity** (`distributional/likelihood_identity.py`, new):

- The built-in identifiers now hash only inputs stored exactly. These are the family and row-law tags, the weight digest and, for every family except `GaussianLS`, the response digest (and the count digest for NB). `GaussianLS`'s plan stores no response, so its identifier binds the weights only, as its `/v1` identifier did. Their tag moves from `/v1` to `/v2`. Any platform reproduces them bit for bit, so the loader still compares them exactly. `TweedieLSS` and `GeneralizedParetoLSS` keep `/v1`: their carriers are exactly zero.
- Each plan with a transcendental carrier gets a `carrier_rounding()` method. The loader and the corrected-covariance replay share one helper, `rebound_plan_mismatch()`. It checks the rebound carrier's sum against the fit's stored `parameter_independent_carrier` within the bound below, for `/v2` identifiers too, so a carrier formula change is still caught. Each plan names the `/v1` tag in a plain `legacy_identifier_tag` attribute. A family that never wrote one leaves it out or sets it to `None`. The fit refuses a plan whose legacy tag is the tag of its own identifiers, reading only the two strings, so it builds no carrier. The loader repeats the check.
- A stored `/v1` identifier hashed the carrier, so no other platform can recompute it, and it is never recomputed. It is accepted when its family tag matches the rebound plan's and the carrier sum passes the bound. The weights are still checked exactly against the stored weight root digest. The response is tied to the fit only through the carrier sum. That sum does not change when response rows are reordered, and it does not involve the response for `GaussianLS` with prior weights or for `TwoPieceNormalLSS`. The artifact's response digest binds the stored response to the manifest, not to the fit. Refitting records a `/v2` identifier, which binds the weights exactly and, for every family except `GaussianLS`, the response exactly too.
- Plans without `carrier_rounding()` keep exact identifier equality. That covers Tweedie, GPD and third-party families.
- The in-process consumers do not need the carrier in the identifier. The chunk-reuse certificate hashes the carrier array itself. The likelihood cache snapshots `carrier_digest`, which stays on the plans. The observed-endpoint reuse at `solver.py` only matches results produced in the same fit session. There is no cross-session warm start in `SuperLSS`. Refitting a loaded model under a different `log` is covered by a test.

**Manifest:** the manifest no longer records the three derived face tolerances. The loader drops them from older manifests before comparing. The face's stored arrays (constraint matrix, null basis, constraint basis) are still bound by their digests, and the tolerance certificates in `penalty_face.py` still run.

**Endpoint revalidation:** a stored endpoint must be within twice the projection's replay bound of a fresh replay, instead of equal to it bit for bit. **Face geometry:** two faces match when their stored null bases are equal. Otherwise their `N Nᵀ` products must agree elementwise within `2 gamma_{2r+4} (|N_L||N_L|ᵀ + |N_R||N_R|ᵀ)` at load, and within half that when a fit builds its result. The difference leaves the load room for another machine's rounding of both products.

**Schema:** the envelope major moves from 11 to 12, and 11 stays readable. Schema 12 changes the manifest against 11 in two ways: a new fit of a built-in family with a transcendental carrier records a `/v2` likelihood identifier, and a coefficient face records none of the three derived tolerances. Builds that wrote schema 11 compare the manifest exactly, so they must refuse a schema-12 artifact at their version gate rather than report it as tampered. This build reads schema 11 as it reads 8 to 10: `/v1` identifiers pass under the carrier-sum rule, and the derived face keys are dropped before the comparison. A schema-12 manifest never records them, so the reader does not drop them there, and one that does record them is refused. A model loaded from schema 11 keeps its `/v1` identifier when saved again, and is written as 12.0.0. `serialization_schema.py`, the `serialization.py` module docstring and the how-to guide record the rule.

### Why the bound is what it is

Write `u = 2^-53` and `gamma_k = k u / (1 - k u)` (Higham, *Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms*, 2nd ed., 2002, §§2.2, 3.1). A carrier row is `c_i = -m_i (F_i + h)`, where:

- `F_i` is one transcendental evaluation of exact inputs, either `log` or `gammaln`;
- `m_i` is an exact stored multiplier;
- `h` is a library constant such as `0.5 log 2π`, which itself comes from `log`.

Suppose each platform's `F_i` and `h` lie within `kappa u` of the exact value. Then two platforms' rows differ by at most `gamma_{2 kappa + 8} a_i`, where `a_i = |c_i| + beta |m_i|`. The `2 kappa` covers the two evaluations, 4 covers the sum and product roundings on each platform, and 4 covers converting to the live row magnitude plus the second-order terms. `beta` is `2|h|` for a constant term, 1 for `gammaln` (absolute error below magnitude one) and 0 otherwise.

Any order of `n - 1` additions sums the rows with error at most `gamma_{n-1} Σ|c_i|`

body:
Plan task **ST2** of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-23-ssh-trust.md` (SDD §26, decided by the owner 2026-10-23, D8): the conversion hosts' keys and the pin.

## What changes
- **SDD (own commit):** ST2's items become binding in §4.2, §4.3, §10 and §12, and §26 points to them. The §26.11 ST2 row is marked binding.
  - §4.2: `ConversionHostConfig.ssh_host_keys` and `Provider.conversion_host_pin` / `HostKeyPin {server_id, keys, source, pinned_at}`, which is server-owned.
  - §4.3: `conversion_host.key_pinned` and its data (no key comment, no console line).
  - §10: the "Host key pins" paragraph (the check's pinning, the console parser, the known_hosts writer), and `console_log(server_id, None)`, which reads the whole console unlogged.
  - §12: POST ignores the pin, PATCH refuses it, and both validate declared keys. The check row names the pinning.
- **§26.4 (separate SDD commit):** a replaced conversion host is *not* pinned again from its new console. The old sentence disagreed with LAB-SSH08, the plan's ST2 row ("reported, not used"), ST5's "conversion host replaced" refusal, CONV_HOST_KEY_UNKNOWN and §26.8's way out. The host stays refused until the operator declares its keys, or deletes it and a pre-staging creates and pins it again.
- **Control plane (B):**
  - `seamless_migrate.security.host_keys`: key validation (422 names the line number and the reason, never the line), the console parser (the keys block alone; two disagreeing blocks or none pin nothing; fingerprints-only consoles pin only keys read from the host whose fingerprint was printed), and the hashed known_hosts writer (`|1|salt|hash`, declared keys over the pin, never another server's pin).
  - The provider check pins a host without a pin from its whole console, once, and writes the pin and `conversion_host.key_pinned` in one transaction. A pin of another server is kept and reported in `status_message`.
  - The OpenStack whole-console read is a raw `os-getConsoleOutput` sent with `log=False`, so keystoneauth never logs the guest's text (§13.4).
- **Dashboard (C):** the provider type gains `ssh_host_keys` and `conversion_host_pin`, and `conversion_host.key_pinned` is among `PERSISTED_EVENT_KINDS`, filed under Providers and Security. ST7 adds the UI.

## Tests
All named plan tests failed first, then passed.
- `test_host_keys.py`: 8 passed. The hashed entries are checked with `ssh-keygen -F`.
- `test_provider_management.py`: 81 passed.
- `test_providers.py`: 183 passed, 1 skipped (pyVim).
- `test_events.py`: 23 passed, 3 skipped. This includes `test_event_kinds_match_sdd_4_3_and_the_dashboard`.
- The SDD readers in `test_api_core`, `test_config`, `test_preflight`, `test_platforms` and `test_seamless_doctor` are green after the rebase on f7c72c48.
- Dashboard: `eventCategories.test.ts` 58 passed, `Events.test.tsx` 26 passed, `npm run typecheck` clean.
- 12 hand-made mutants (parser, writer, check, validation) were all killed.
- `gitleaks dir` and `gitleaks git`: no leaks.

## Notes for later tasks
- **ST7:** the provider dialog rebuilds `conversion_host` on edit, so it must carry `ssh_host_keys`, or an edit would reset declared keys. The provider page should show a pin of another server as unused while declared keys win.
- **ST5:** `live.ts` refreshes providers on `provider.checked`. Pins the executor records will need their own refresh on `conversion_host.key_pinned`.
- **ST8:** the QASuite NFR-06 row gains the tests above, plus `test_openstack_reads_a_whole_console_without_logging_it`.

Block 6 of `the-audit-before-0-20-0`.

- The Nx generator schemas refuse an option they do not know, so a mistyped flag fails instead of being ignored.
- The Nx route keeps a package version the consumer already recorded, also an older one.

- `--shortcut` and `--menu` are written into generated code as escaped string literals.
- Composing into `providers` finds the end of the array itself by bracket depth, past nested arrays, strings and comments; an existing registration or `unless` marker is matched as a whole name, not as part of a longer one.
- `init` quotes every argument it hands to the Windows command shell, and refuses a quote, percent sign or line break there.
- `init` replaces an Angular application file only while it is still what `ng new` wrote, and otherwise stops before installing anything and names the file. It writes into the build project's own root rather than the workspace root.

body:
## Contexte

Le build de production après la fusion de #35 (`dpl_HejZurLzP…`) a échoué : crédit API Anthropic épuisé pendant la traduction des pages détaillées (`credit balance is too low`). La production est restée sur le déploiement précédent. La consommation était aussi bien plus forte que prévu.

Causes probables (coût réel non mesuré, pas d'accès à la console Anthropic) :
- **effort `high`** : la réflexion est facturée comme du texte produit (20 $/M jetons sur Opus 5.5) et dominait le coût ;
- **tout retraduit par environnement** : le build de production ne récupère pas le cache disque des previews, et les clés de cache changeaient avec le modèle et `PROMPT_VERSION` ;
- **un nouvel essai renvoyait tout le lot** quand un seul texte était rejeté.

## Changements

- **Mémoire de traduction dans Vercel Blob** (`src/lib/i18n/memory.ts`, fichiers immuables `i18n/translations/<empreinte>.json`) : clé = texte français + langue (+ `MEMORY_VERSION`), sans le modèle. Partagée par la production, les previews et les régénérations ISR : seuls les textes jamais traduits partent à l'API. Lecture en cache 5 min.
- **Effort `low`** au lieu de `high` (`src/lib/i18n/translate.ts`).
- **Nouvel essai limité aux textes rejetés** ; un texte refusé 3 fois est absent du résultat (affiché en français), n'est pas enregistré dans la mémoire et sera redemandé plus tard.
- **Slugs** : un slug non traduit n'est plus figé en français (`src/lib/i18n/slugs.ts`).
- Décision du 22/10 dans `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` mis à jour.

## Vérifications

- lint, typecheck, 753 tests, couverture, build (`TRANSLATION_MODE=identity`) : verts
- mutants : « langues » 29/29, « slugs » 9/9, mémoire 3/3 tués (nouvelles entrées pour la mémoire, l'effort, la relance ciblée et les slugs non traduits)
- `BLOB_STORE_ID` présent en Production et Preview sur Vercel

**Non vérifié** (bloqué depuis l'environnement cloud) : le vrai store Blob et les vrais appels API. À voir sur la preview / le premier build de production.

## À noter

- Le premier build après la fusion retraduit tout une fois (mémoire vide), puis presque plus rien : recharger le crédit Anthropic avant de fusionner.
- Si le crédit s'épuise pendant un build, il échoue encore (la production garde la version précédente) : c'est voulu.

- **Formats** and **PlayerNames**: how numbers and times are written, name matching.

The code is moved as it was, in the same order, so nothing should change on screen. MainForm went from about 7,700 to 5,900 lines; what is left is mostly the window itself (and the Trip Planner and the status line, which are next, stage 2c).

**64 new tests** (96 in all, every one passing) for these classes, most of them on a played session loaded the way the window loads it: names, joining and leaving the party, who has a mission, Gone, payouts and values, lost cargo ending a run, where a worker is, the leaderboards, the snapshots and transfers.

author: blackmkount
body:
Pediste: *"el personaje y los espacios deben verse como un juego caro... puedes cambiar el estilo gráfico... Te doy total libertad, sorpréndeme"*. Este PR cambia todo el arte del juego.

## Qué cambió

**Un estilo nuevo: "Mundo Impreso".** El pixel art se reemplaza por un diorama 3D suave y cálido del cuarto de un joven maker en una ciudad de valle latinoamericana inventada. Se presenta como una maqueta impresa capa a capa. La interfaz azul y cian se queda igual.

- **El mundo en alta resolución:** se dibuja al ancho de tu pantalla, con bordes suavizados y sombras suaves.
- **El cuarto:**
  - Ventana de verdad, con marco de aluminio, rejas, cortina mostaza y la vista del barrio: tanque de agua, varillas "para el segundo piso", ropa tendida y buganvilla.
  - El sol de la mañana entra a rayas por las rejas.
  - Piso de baldosa cálida, paredes verde salvia y crema, y una base que se ve impresa capa a capa.
- **La decoración:**
  - cama con cobija de tigre, tapete tejido y puf;
  - librero con plantas, guitarra y pósters inventados sin marcas;
  - guirnalda de focos, corcho con fotos, reloj, repisa de las primeras impresiones y basurero de impresiones fallidas.

  Todo va en zonas libres y no quita lugares para muebles.
- **La impresora del piso**, sobre su baldosa y con el cable al enchufe:
  - la pieza crece de a 1 cm, con una capa caliente naranja que se ve con cualquier zoom;
  - al terminar suelta destellos;
  - si falla, aparece un nido de "espagueti" del color del filamento.
- **Las siete impresoras** se distinguen por su forma, y en todas se ve crecer la pieza y el fallo.
- **El escritorio:** monitor de tubo beige, lámpara, cajonera y una caja de cartón como silla.
- **El rincón de despacho:** un guacal de madera.
- **Los muebles nuevos:** la estantería metálica ahora es más alta y las impresoras ya no la atraviesan.
- **El personaje:**
  - Mide 1,40 m, con cara pintada, ojos grandes con brillo, pelo de una pieza, buzo gris carbón con capucha mostaza, jeans y zapatillas blancas.
  - Trota doblando rodillas y codos, parpadea y se gira hacia ti cuando está quieto.
  - Celebra al cobrar, se agarra la cabeza cuando falla una impresión y saluda si lo tocas.
  - El retrato de arriba cambia de cara con lo que pasa.
- **Día y noche con el reloj del juego:** mañana, mediodía, tarde dorada y una noche lo-fi con lámpara, monitor, tira LED y luces del barrio. De noche cada impresora muestra su estado con su propia luz.
- **La firma "capa a capa":** lo que se agrega al cuarto aparece imprimiéndose, sólido abajo y con las capas que faltan en cian arriba. Queda listo para cuando llegue el comando de compra de la tienda.
- **Calidad gráfica en Ajustes:** Automática, Alta o Baja. En Automática el juego baja la calidad solo si tu teléfono va lento.
- **Panel de rendimiento:** se abre agregando `#debug` al final del enlace web. Muestra los cuadros por segundo, permite ver la noche o el taller lleno sin tocar tu partida, y tiene un botón "Salir de la prueba".
- **Las vistas 3D de la tienda y los retratos** se ven nítidas, con luz de estudio.

## Por qué así

- Se probaron **cuatro estilos dentro de copias del juego real**: diorama acogedor, mundo impreso con día y noche, pixel art pulido y miniatura de juguete. Cuatro jueces los compararon por capturas: un director de arte, un jugador, un técnico de rendimiento y un diseñador. Ganó "Mundo Impreso", con lo mejor de los otros injertado.
- Se construyó en 16 pasos, cada uno revisado por dos verificadores (código y capturas) y corregido antes del siguiente. Al final hubo una revisión de todo con 8 enfoques: 33 problemas confirmados, todos arreglados.
- **Es más liviano que antes:** el cuarto inicial pasa de 334 a 38 llamadas de dibujo, y el taller lleno de 1.042 a unas 133. Una prueba automática vigila que no suba.
- Todo el arte se arma por código: no hay recursos de terceros ni marcas reales.

## Decisiones que tomé con tu libertad total

Todas están anotadas en el GDD, versión 2.4, sección 16. Si alguna no te gusta, dímelo y la cambio:
- **D1:** se deja el pixel art.
- **D3:** el personaje se rediseña y el buzo es gris carbón con acento mostaza; el negro puro se perdía de noche.
- **D2:** no se agregan luces extra del motor. Las lámparas se calculan en el sombreador, así que la regla de "una sola luz" se cumple.
- **D5 y D6:** la estantería es más alta y se agrega la decoración del dormitorio.
- **D7:** opción "Calidad gráfica" en Ajustes.
- **D8:** se adelanta de la Fase 2 el día y la noche y las reacciones del personaje. Es solo visual: el juego no cambia.

## Cómo probarlo

Cuando fusiones, abre https://blackmkount.github.io/game/ en tu teléfono (si ves la versión anterior, recarga). Si ya tenías partida, sigue igual.

1. **Al empezar (08:00):** el sol entra con las rayas de la reja y cruza la impresora del piso. Nada se ve "pixelado". El personaje se ve bien: cara, ojos con brillo y capucha mostaza.
2. **Acepta un pedido e imprime:** mira la pieza crecer con su capa naranja, también con el zoom lejos. Al terminar salen destellos verdes. Al despachar junto al rincón, el personaje levanta el puño.
3. **Toca al personaje:** te saluda.
4. **De noche:** espera a las 20:15 del juego o usa `#debug` → "Noche". Se prenden las lámparas, la guirnalda y las luces del barrio, y el piso no se ve negro con el brillo del teléfono bajo.
5. **El taller lleno:** `#debug` → "Taller lleno", de día y de noche. Las siete impresoras se distinguen. Después toca "Salir de la prueba" y vuelves a tu partida.
6. **La Tienda:** las vistas 3D se ven nítidas.
7. **Ajustes → Calidad gráfica:** prueba Alta y Baja. En Baja no hay sombras del sol, pero se ve parecido.
8. **Lo más importante: mide.** Abre el enlace con `#debug` al final y dime cuántos cuadros por segundo marca en el cuarto inicial y en el taller lleno, de día y de noche, en Alta y en Baja. Nunca se midió en un teléfono de verdad, solo en mi computador sin tarjeta de video. Con esos números ajusto la calidad automática.

**Verificado por Claude:**
- `check.sh` y `run_tests.sh` pasan con 776 pruebas (antes 505). Ninguna prueba vieja se debilitó, y las que se adaptaron están anotadas en `docs/DECISIONES.md`.
- `screenshots.sh` saca 50 capturas, y las revisé.
- Exporté la versión web y la jugué en un navegador que simula un Pixel 7: cero errores, los mismos colores que las capturas, y el primer pedido se juega con toques.

## Qué queda pendiente

- **Medir en tu teléfono** (punto 8). Con eso se decide el umbral de la calidad automática y si las mallas se arman durante una pantalla de carga.
- Si pones una estantería en el lugar 5, tapa al personaje en su lugar de inicio. Que lo que tapa se vuelva transparente está planeado en la tarea 3 de la Fase 2.
- Detalles del personaje para más adelante: el hombro con el brazo arriba, el pulgar y los mechoncitos de la coronilla vistos de espaldas.
- **Propuesta para `CLAUDE.md`:** sumar las opciones nuevas de las capturas y la regla de luces "un sol con sombra y el resto en el sombreador". No lo cambié porque necesita tu visto bueno; el detalle está en `docs/PROGRESO.md`.
- Siguiente tarea sugerida: la Fase 1, tarea 3 (navegación nueva y HUD despejado).
