## Результат (первый этап Search Planner)

- **Реальный Python-код** `intelligence/search_planner/`: `input_loader`, `contracts`, `context_builder`, public imports.
- **Только immutable hierarchical approved RTB**: единственный параметризованный read-only PostgreSQL lookup связывает published deep tree, Builder publication, run status, deep status, оба Human Review, одобренные факты и snapshot анкеты по одному project/run.
- **HypothesisContext v1**: все 11 RTB node fields у направления, опциональной ветки и гипотезы; ancestry path, fact lineage с текстами, allowlisted project context (не копирует приватные лишние поля), ≤5 siblings, явный language/mode policy. У детей напрямую от направления `branch=null`.
- **Защитные ограничения**: отсутствие approved publication, другой project, draft или один Review, неопознанный факт, сломанный parent/path, отсутствие гипотезы у root, некорректный language policy → fail closed. Contexts не мутируют вход.
- **Тесты**: отдельный offline unittest + cross-check committed HypothesisContext JSON Schema при наличии `jsonschema`; добавлена реальная PostgreSQL проверка после 2 Human Review в уже существующий тест RTB (только `CM_TEST_PG_DSN`).
- **Документация**: отдельная инструкция, README, индекс.
- **Никаких LLM, Apify, Bright Data, DTK, миграций БД, платных вызовов или новой UI**.

## Как проверять
```sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_search_planner_foundation.py' -v
# Only disposable DB with CM_TEST_PG_DSN:
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_taxonomy_deep_db.py' -v
```
Тест подключения к PostgreSQL невозможно считать пройденным без отдельного CI с disposable DB.

**Stacked on PR #14**, поскольку JSON Schema HypothesisContext создана там. Target branch — `docs/ai-query-generator-architecture-v1`; после merge #14 PR надо ретаргетировать на `main`. Не сливать этот PR в main до #14.

Generator runtime + PostgreSQL attempt ledger/authorization (второй этап), затем OpenRouter и ThinkQE/MuGI/Jina.

author: martinpovolny
body:
## Summary

Extend the two existing OCP tag-mapping plan guardrails to the OCP-on-AWS project daily-summary UPDATE. The pre-ANALYZE flag refreshes only existing monthly leaves before a bill-scoped UPDATE. The materialized-candidates flag fences the candidate CTE so PostgreSQL computes it once. Each flag remains independent; the legacy SQL is retained when the materialization flag is off.

The bounded ANALYZE implementation is shared with the existing OCP accessor without changing its behavior. If optional ANALYZE fails, the UPDATE still runs.

## Why

A production auto-EXPLAIN captured an OCP-on-AWS tag-mapping UPDATE that ran for approximately 42 hours. Its plan repeatedly scanned the same day on the inner side of a nested loop. This patch targets that failure mode. It is a preventive plan guardrail, not a measured production speedup.

## Validation

- `AWSReportDBAccessorTest.test_ocp_on_aws_tag_mapping_guardrail_flags`: all four flag combinations and a single materialized CTE in PostgreSQL `EXPLAIN`.
- `AWSReportDBAccessorTest.test_ocp_on_aws_tag_mapping_analyze_failure_keeps_update`: two-month traversal and UPDATE after an ANALYZE error.
- `AWSReportDBAccessorTest.test_ocp_on_aws_materialization_preserves_mapped_tags`: actual JSONB output parity between legacy and materialized SQL.
- `AWSReportDBAccessorTest.test_populate_ocp_on_aws_tag_information` and six existing OCP tag-mapping guardrail tests passed.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`, Red Hat gitleaks, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Rollout

Both existing flags are enabled in Stage. The AWS extension will be exercised when this image reaches Stage and an OCP-on-AWS tag-mapping task runs. Production code and flag state are unchanged by this PR; compare writer plans and task durations before production targeting.

author: yonatan895
body:
## Escaped defect
e2e step `Application pod egress is blocked (agent pod, real sockets)` leaked one of three public connects intermittently (about 1 run in 3 lately): run 39936150839 (8.8.8.8:443 connected), job 120379823050 in run 39942787786 (9.9.9.9:443 connected), and dispatch run 39945681590 on this branch (kind-lifecycle, 8.8.8.8:443 connected, 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 refused).

## Refuted hypothesis
First version of this PR assumed the Kind node's masquerade briefly lapsed so a pod-sourced SYN missed the `-s 172.18/16` DOCKER-USER rule, and added a bridge-interface rule (`-i br ! -o br`) plus the pod CIDR as a source. Run 39945681590 refutes it: every node had `kind-masq-agent` in nat POSTROUTING, and the final counters showed the leaked SYN hit none of the three node rules (source 172.18/16: 14 hits; pod CIDR 10.244/16: 0; bridge interface: 0). It never traversed host FORWARD, so no host iptables rule can close it. Those rules are dropped in this version (egress_gate.sh is unchanged from main).

## Change
- e2e.yml (boundary step, after `egress_gate.sh install`): apply NetworkPolicy `rehearsal-default-deny-egress` to the lane namespace. Egress allowed: kube-dns (kube-system, k8s-app=kube-dns) port 53 UDP/TCP; pods of the same namespace (stand-in gateway, mock vLLM, Qdrant, agent, ingest, corpus-gen); the Kind network IPv4 CIDR on 6443 (API server, needed by the existing in-cluster control probe). The existing pod probes are kept. Counters/state diagnostics from the first version are kept (node nat POSTROUTING recorded in diagnostics/egress-gate-nodes-nat.txt). No job or step renamed.
- CI-only manifest: the product chart has only ingress policies (networkPolicy.enabled) and no egress option, so nothing is added to the chart. The chart-lifecycle lane's own namespace ($NS-chart) is not covered; no pod probe runs there.
- tests/test_egress_gate.py: workflow tests for the policy (Egress, default-deny selector, exact allowed destinations, applied after install, probes still after the boundary). docs/deploy.md updated.

## Enforcement verified
The pinned node image (kindest/node@sha256:a1ed56cf...) ships kindnetd v20260820-69b56db7 with networkpolicies RBAC. I created a one-node cluster on it with kind v0.33.0 locally: before the policy a pod reached 8.8.8.8:443 (3/3); after a default-deny egress policy allowing kube-dns and same-namespace pods, 8.8.8.8:443 and 1.1.1.1:443 were closed (3/3 each), a Service in the namespace stayed reachable (3/3) and in-cluster DNS resolved. Cluster deleted afterwards.

## Verification (tested SHA 16daf8e16067c29b139acd46b005efcdba2a013a)
- mfr-pytest tests/test_egress_gate.py tests/test_ci_gateway.py: 92 passed, exit 0
- qa:context: exit 0
- e2e dispatches on this SHA: runs 39948502619 and 39948516477 (results to be added; pod-probe results across all lanes). One clean run is not proof at this flake rate.
- Node probe: with the policy, pod connects no longer reach the host DOCKER-USER rule, so `require-hits nodes` failed in runs 39948502619/39948516477. Added step "Prove node egress is blocked (Kind node network namespace, real sockets)": `docker exec <node> curl` to 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8/9.9.9.9:443 (node image has no python) must fail; node namespaces are outside NetworkPolicy, so this exercises the host rule.
- e2e dispatch on af3c8ed (all 12 Kind lanes, pod probe, node probe and require-hits nodes success in each): 39956696267 success, 39956713828 success. A further dispatch on the merged head a06ef26: 39959484587 success (12 Kind lanes).
- First PR CI on af3c8ed failed broadly ("CI evidence unavailable: invalid identity"): the checkout parents did not match the event base because main moved (#930 etc.) during the run; fixed by merging origin/main (a06ef26). ruff check on the CI paths passes.
- Not run: shellcheck (not installed; egress_gate.sh unchanged).

author: patinaproject-goodyear[bot]
body:
`claude-session` prints one JSON line to report each worker run, and the `blocker-order` hook reads that line to block or order the card. Until now each side kept its own copy of the keys, so a key that one side renamed broke the other with no test failure. This pull request moves the format into one module that both sides use.

## What changes

- `plugins/blocker-order/result_line.py` defines the reports as dataclasses: `Waiting`, `Done` (a needs-input run is a `Done` whose `result` starts with `Needs input:`), `Failed`, and `Refused`, which has an optional `transient` flag. Every key comes from a dataclass field. A `Session` or `Outcome` adds its own fields as keys, and a field that holds its default writes no key. `line` writes a report. `last` reads the last JSON line of a process output as the one variant whose keys match it exactly. `waiting_on` and `needs_input` return what the hook acts on.
- `claude-session` builds `Session` and `Outcome` values instead of the old inline dict, and prints every report through `result_line.line`. It imports the module from the worker home's copy of the plugin, the same way it imports `linear.py`. A home without the plugin gets a plain refusal, and in that home no hook reads the line.
- The `waiting_on` and `needs_input` functions of the `blocker-order` hook now read through `result_line.last`. They accept the same lines as before.
- An implementation run still writes no `activity` key, and a triage run still writes `activity`, even as `null`, because `Done.activity` defaults to the `UNSET` marker.
- `check-install` loads the installed plugin as a package, so the plugin's relative import works when `check_hermes_tools` reads its tool lists.

The JSON line keeps its keys, including the `activity: null` key on a triage run and no `activity` key on an implementation run, so `SOUL.md` needs no change.

## Proof

`ResultLineTest` writes each report variant and reads it back. The `claude-session` tests run the real script for a done run, a needs-input run, a triage run, a failed run with and without output, a refusal, a transient refusal, and a waiting card. For each one they check that the printed line decodes to the expected variant and encodes back to the same JSON.

```text
$ python3 -m unittest -v tests.test_blocker_order.ResultLineTest
test_every_report_reads_back_as_written ... ok
```

## Summary

The setup checker gains one non-blocking row, **macOS window tiling**, which Sam decided on for drag insertion on 20 October 2026.

```diff
 SetupChecker.evaluate
   accessibility
   separateSpaces
   competingManagers
   stageManager
+  macOSTiling        # names each tiling option that is on
   fourFingerGesture
   threeFingerGesture
```

```text
tilingStatus(edge, menuBar, optionDrag)
  any option on      -> Problem: "Turn off <options that are on> in System Settings > Desktop & Dock > Windows."
  any option unread  -> Not checked, with manual steps
  otherwise          -> Passed
```

`SetupProbe` reads `EnableTilingByEdgeDrag`, `EnableTopTilingByEdgeDrag`, and `EnableTilingOptionAccelerator` from `com.apple.WindowManager`.
macOS stores these values only after the user changes them, so the probe treats an absent value as on, which is the macOS default.
`decisions/release-scope.md`, `decisions/setup.md`, check AP-6, and `PROGRESS.md` now list the check.

## Evidence

- **Before:** On `main`, the Setup page has no tiling row, and `decisions/release-scope.md` does not list the check.
  **After:** The built app on Sam's Mac shows **macOS window tiling: Passed** with all three options off.
  After `defaults write` turned on edge and Option-drag tiling and Check Again ran, the row read: "Turn off Drag windows to screen edges to tile and Hold ⌥ key while dragging windows to tile in System Settings > Desktop & Dock > Windows."
  All three options were set back to off afterwards.
- New tests: `reportsEachMacOSTilingOptionThatIsOn` and `aTilingOptionThatIsOnOutranksOneThatCannotBeRead`.
  `neverReportsAnUnreadableSettingAsPassed` now covers the tiling row.
- `make check` passes: docs, harness, compatibility, strict Swift and engine lint, the signed build, 144 Swift tests, the engine tests, the selftests, and DMG packaging.

A related engine defect turned up during the same run and is not fixed here.
With macOS tiling on, a tiled window that macOS filled or tiled returned to its column origin and width within 0.4 seconds, but kept the macOS height of 1410 points instead of 1394.

Proved by running the built app on Sam's Mac with the tiling options off and on, plus `make check`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

The check only reads preferences and never blocks management.

**Blast Radius:** setup.

A Mac with the macOS defaults now sees a Problem row on the Setup page.
With several problems, the Setup page scrolls inside the fixed 560 by 500 Settings window.

## Related issues

Part of #43

## Release

The setup checker reports macOS window tiling options that conflict with dragging windows in Miri.

author: justin13888
body:
## Summary
A source the viewer picks on the detail screen, before playback starts, is now pinned the same way a pick made inside the player already was (#292). Sustained rebuffering no longer downgrades it. Before this, the player had no way to tell a hand-picked file from the default the quality policy chose.

- `beam-android/core/model/.../PlaybackRequest.kt`: new `isSourcePicked: Boolean = false`.
- `beam-android/app/.../navigation/Destinations.kt`: new `Player.isSourcePicked: Boolean = false`, so the flag survives on the back stack.
- `beam-android/feature/detail/.../DetailScreen.kt`: `onPlay` gains a fourth parameter, `isSourcePicked`. `SourcePicker.onPick` passes `true`. The play button and the episode rows pass `false`.
- `beam-android/app/.../ui/BeamApp.kt`: the `MediaDetail` entry copies the flag into `Player`, and the `Player` entry copies it into `PlaybackRequest`. Home resume and Downloads build `Player` without it, so it stays `false` there.
- `beam-android/feature/player/.../PlayerViewModel.kt`: `start` seeds `isSourcePinned` from `request.isSourcePicked`. It only ever adds a pin, never removes one (see Decisions).
- `beam-android/feature/player/src/test/.../PlayerTest.kt`: two new cases. A request marked as picked is never downgraded: no downgrade request, no switch, no notice. Starting again does not drop a pin set in the player.
- `PlayerRoute.kt` (in the manifest) needed no change: it already passes the whole `PlaybackRequest` to `start`.

## Validation
- `mise run android:test`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- `cd beam-android && ./gradlew :feature:player:testDebugUnitTest --tests '*PlayerTest*'`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, after the second test was added
- `mise run android:lint` (ktlint + `lintDebug`): BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- `ktlint --relative '**/*.kt' '!**/build/**'` (after `mise run android:lint:fix`): clean
- The pre-push hook ran `mise run android:screenshot`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- Rust, TypeScript and docs gates: not run locally, because no file in their scope changed. CI covers them.

## Coverage gaps
- No test drives the path from `DetailScreen` to `BeamApp` (picker tap, `Player.isSourcePicked`, `PlaybackRequest`). That path is only parameter passing, and the compiler checks every call site of the changed `onPlay` signature. The behaviour it feeds into, the player honouring the flag, is tested in `PlayerTest`.

## Risks and rollout
- `Player` is a `@Serializable` nav destination. The new field has a default, so a saved back stack from an older build still decodes.

## Issue
Closes #291

## Decisions taken
Issue 291 - Android: carry a detail-screen source pick into the player as a pin

1. **Name of the flag.** Chosen: `isSourcePicked` on `PlaybackRequest`, `Player` and the `onPlay` lambda. It sits beside the player's existing `isSourcePinned`: picked is what the viewer did, pinned is what the player does about it. Rejected: `isExplicitPick`, which does not say what was picked. To reverse, rename the field at the six sites in this diff.
2. **How `start` seeds the pin.** Chosen: `isSourcePinned = isSourcePinned || request.isSourcePicked`, so it can add a pin but never clear one. `PlayerRoute` calls `start` from `LaunchedEffect(request.fileId)`, which runs again when the route is rebuilt, for example after a rotation. A plain assignment would then drop a pin the viewer set in the player. `playNext` still clears the pin when moving to another title. Rejected: plain assignment, for that reason. To reverse, assign `request.isSourcePicked` directly and delete the test `starting again does not drop a pin set in the player`.
3. **Signature shape.** Chosen: add a fourth positional parameter to `onPlay`. The manifest named the `onPlay` signature as the seam. Rejected: a separate `onPlaySource` callback, which would add a second play path through `DetailRoute` and `BeamApp`. To reverse, split the picker's call into its own callback.

This is the second real test of `verdict.yml`, after #78. The permission check now passes, but the workflow refused #73's verdict comment again: comment 6363676004, job 120386036060.

```
verdict comment 6363676004 is refused: invalid verdict: trailing characters at line 2 column 1
```

Cause: the agent proxy appends `\n\n---\n_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_` to every comment a session posts. `comment_json` expected the closing ```` ``` ```` at the very end of the body, so the footer became part of the JSON.

## Change

`comment_json` now takes the ```` ```json ```` block after the marker, up to its closing fence, and ignores anything after it. A comment without a fence still parses the rest of the body as before. This doesn't loosen any check: the comment still has to be unedited (the footer is added when the comment is created, so `created_at == updated_at` still holds), and the author still needs write permission.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check` and clippy (`-D warnings`) are clean.
- `cargo test --locked`: 317 passed.
- New tests: a unit round trip with the footer, and `verdict_apply_ignores_a_footer_after_the_json_block`. The cli test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- This is normal risk (src, tests and CHANGELOG only). No PROGRESS line, to avoid conflicts with #73.

author: peasee
body:
## 📝 Summary

A cold-tier promotion currently holds the table write lock while it encodes and uploads cold files. On an append-only capture, this change releases the lock during that work, then carries any appended warm files into the new snapshot before publishing. Deletes, replacements, schema changes, and physical file removal invalidate the capture and make the next attempt use the locked path. A catalog commit whose response is ambiguous is read back before any prospective files are removed; an unresolved outcome fences the provider until reload.

On 2026-10-23, an actual `spiced` retention interleaving removed four files from a protected snapshot while an off-lock upload was held. Commit `0544282cae1c29a05ad5822d6c95a83b77f07208` returned 16,384 rows after the delete but 32,768 after promotion and restart: 16,384 deleted IDs were reintroduced. The same script and proxy hashes against this PR's `3ce11b56362b434a3f2bd16a2bf05e0b99975131` returned exactly the 16,384 survivors after promotion and restart. The engine log shows the stale off-lock attempt discarded, then a locked retry committed. Artifacts: `/home/owner/coldperf/promotion-review/retention-20261023T092532Z` and `/home/owner/coldperf/promotion-review/retention-20261023T104050Z`; invocation and binary hashes are in each `manifest.json`.

Write performance was measured on the same machine and object-store proxy with the stored trunk binary `09c9fcc9f214708c9ebd275f7e719a13033a602a` versus this PR's CI binary (build [39932041749](https://github.com/spiceai/spiceai/actions/runs/39932041749), SHA-256 `da2c2cb826fcf60524b15fc50dbb9ef969fd1244616c727141d4fde2625029c6`). An A/B/B/A run used 1,280 writes per arm, 8,192 rows per write, and one cold promotion overlapping at least 16 actual in-flight writes per arm. All 10,551,296 input rows and all columns matched the oracle after writes and restart in every arm. Nearest-rank P99 scheduled-to-ack was 2,711.0 ms pooled on trunk versus 47.5 ms on this branch (−98.25%, 2,560 samples per side); the 2,663.5 ms improvement exceeds the 1,094.2 ms A/A spread, and both candidate arms beat both trunk arms. Service-time P99 also improved. Run: `python3 -u /home/owner/coldperf/promotion-review/promotion_abba.py --candidate /home/owner/coldperf/bin/3ce11b5636 --sha 3ce11b56362b434a3f2bd16a2bf05e0b99975131 --build-run 39932041749 --candidate-sha256 da2c2cb826fcf60524b15fc50dbb9ef969fd1244616c727141d4fde2625029c6`. Artifacts and per-write records: `/home/owner/coldperf/promotion-review/abba-3ce11b5636-20261023T104148Z`.

A separate cold-read A/B/B/A reused the unchanged 20-million-row, 14-file cold fixture with 1,000 timed queries per shape per arm. All 12,000 SQL outputs matched exact retained row objects. P99 in ms (trunk → branch): PK point 95.9 → 94.9; one-minute range 84.1 → 83.9; full-table aggregate 125.6 → 127.3, within its 2.0 ms A/A spread. Each arm made exactly 35,245 S3 requests across the 1,000 aggregate queries; the different P99 request count is a one-sample percentile-boundary effect, not an increase in total object requests. Artifact: `/home/owner/coldperf/results/promotion-cold-read-3ce11b5636-20261023T110107Z`, including every query latency/output, plans, manifests, and raw S3 logs.

## 🔗 Related

Related to #12849. This removes the upload-length writer pause for append-only eligible captures; tables with pending deletion state continue on the locked path.

## 🚨 Breaking Changes

None.

## 📚 Docs

Updated `docs/cayenne/cayenne.md` for capture reconciliation, retention invalidation, and ambiguous commit recovery.

## 👀 Notes for Reviewers

The A/B binary was built from `3ce11b56362b434a3f2bd16a2bf05e0b99975131`. Current PR head `910a53bd1677f12da9981d21689233677ca0716a` adds only a variable rename and groups unchanged private commit inputs after the first remote sign-off reported two Clippy diagnostics. The bounded follow-up command `timeout 60 /home/owner/coldperf/cargo-locked.sh check -p cayenne --tests` exited 0 on 2026-10-23 (`Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 31.33s`; full output: `/home/owner/coldperf/promotion-review/cargo-check-signoff-followup.log`). Remote sign-off rerun: [39948909621](https://github.com/spiceai/spiceai/actions/runs/39948909621). Please review the structural-version check under the listing fence and the catalog readback before cleanup; both protect against data loss rather than only the write-latency path.

author: akashdeshmukh-git
body:
`pcre2_next_match()` unconditionally dereferenced its pointer arguments (`match_data->start_offset`, `match_data->ovector`) without validating that `match_data`, `pstart_offset`, or `poptions` were non-NULL. Additionally, the internal `do_bumpalong()` helper dereferenced `match_data->code` to query newline and UTF options without verifying that `match_data->code` is non-NULL.

This change:
1. Adds `PCRE2_ASSERT()` preconditions and returns `FALSE` early if `match_data`, `pstart_offset`, or `poptions` is NULL.
2. Guards `match_data->code` and `match_data->subject` in `do_bumpalong()` when inspecting newline conventions and advancing across code units.
3. Extends `unittest()` in `src/pcre2test_inc.h` with test coverage verifying that NULL arguments safely return `FALSE`.
4. Documents the NULL pointer return behaviour in `doc/pcre2api.adoc` and `doc/pcre2_next_match.adoc`.

body:
Measures the prompt cache per main session and per subagent, and what each subagent's start costs against the always loaded rules, so the decision on trimming the lessons core or running fewer panel agents rests on a number. Nothing is trimmed here; that call is Dan's.

## What changed

- `tools/cache-usage.py` (not installed, so it adds no per prompt cost). Over a window (`--days`, default 7) it reads only the usage fields of each assistant message in `~/.claude/projects` and reports per transcript and per kind: requests, input, cache reads, cache writes (split into the five minute and one hour lifetimes), hit rate (cache read over all input). For each subagent it also gives the first request's cache write, which is its startup cost, set against the rules measured now: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` plus every `@` import, in characters, with tokens estimated as characters / 4 and labelled so. Main sessions are also split by entrypoint, so interactive sessions show apart from headless `claude -p` runs.
- A transcript with no usage field is listed as UNMEASURED, never counted as zero. A missing root or a window with no requests exits 1. Malformed lines and requests with no timestamp are counted, never dropped silently.
- `tools/test-cache-usage.sh`, with fixtures written by hand: invented content, usage fields only. They cover a split message counted once, a synthetic message, a malformed line, a message with no usage, an unmeasured transcript, out of window requests, two subagents (one with no meta file), a missing import and an offsetless timestamp.

## The open question, measured

- `/usage` in 2.1.309 has cache totals but no hit rate. The non interactive form (`claude -p "/usage"`, hooks off) prints no cache line at all. The binary's strings show the interactive stats tab renders `Cache read N · Cache write N` totals and a per model `Cache: N read · N write`. Neither has a hit rate or a split between main sessions and subagents.
- Transcripts record `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m/1h_input_tokens` on every request. A subagent is `<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` with `isSidechain: true` and `agentId`, and a main session is `<session>.jsonl` with `isSidechain: false`.

The 7 day numbers for the personal MacBook are posted on #1503.

## Decisions taken without Dan (sleep mode, recommended option)

- The token count of the rules is an estimate (characters / 4). Calling a tokenizer would need an API key and a network call for a number that is only a yardstick.
- Memory indexes and project CLAUDE.md files are left out of the rules size, because they vary by project. The comment says so.

## Tests

- Seen failing first: 19 of 24 checks red with the tool absent. The later checks for the entrypoint split and first read were seen red (3 failing) before they were implemented. The offsetless timestamp case was reproduced as a crash (`TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`, 3 failing) before the fix.
- `bash tools/test-cache-usage.sh`: 28 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite `bash payload/hooks/run-all-tests.sh` before the timestamp fix: ALL 191 SUITES PASSED.

Closes #1503

author: zm2231
body:
Every iOS test run installs the same app on the simulator, so a second run that starts on a simulator kills the first one's test runner before it connects ("test runner hung before establishing connection", "crashed with signal kill before establishing connection").

`scripts/ios-simulator.sh [iphone|ipad] run <command> [args...]` boots that simulator, then runs the command under `lockf` on `/tmp/agenthail-simulator-<udid>.lock`, held until the command exits. The path is fixed so every session on the machine contends for the same lock; a second caller waits. The command's arguments and exit status pass through unchanged, and `AGENTHAIL_SIMULATOR_UDID` is set for it.

The existing forms are unchanged: no second argument prints the UDID, `--boot` boots and prints it, and CI's caller is untouched.

Verified: two concurrent `run` invocations on one simulator serialize (the second starts when the first exits), including with different `TMPDIR`; `run sh -c 'exit 7'` exits 7; unknown arguments print usage.

author: jung-thomas
body:
Closes #2886.

## What

Adds **Step 0.5** (`guardCleanBuildInputs`) to `scripts/deploy-mta.cjs`: for **all envs**, **before** `build:all`/`mbt build`, the deploy now `die(1)`s if any **tracked** file under `hugo/assets` or `hugo/layouts` has uncommitted changes — naming the files.

## Why

The 2026-10-21 PROD-down: a deploy ran `build:all` in a checkout with an **uncommitted** edit to `hugo/assets/css/sap-fundamental.css`, so Hugo fingerprinted the dirty CSS (`9dbb07c7…`) while the CI content pipeline (clean `origin/main`) baked HTML referencing the committed hash (`7f01bb5…`). The fingerprints never matched → **404 on every tutorial** on `/tutorials/` and `/tutorials-qa/` (shared approuter).

`guardPrimaryTreeBranch` (Step 0) missed it: a dirty working tree keeps the **same HEAD SHA**, so both the PROD (branch) and DEV/QA (`HEAD===origin` SHA) paths passed with a dirty `hugo/assets/**` file.

## How

- Pure parser `dirtyBuildInputs(porcelain)` (exported) over `git status --porcelain -- hugo/assets hugo/layouts`:
  - flags tracked modifications in either column (`M`/`A`/`D`/`R`/`C`, index or worktree)
  - **ignores `??` untracked** — so `build:all`-generated `hugo/data/*.json` never false-positives (scope also deliberately excludes `hugo/data`)
  - rename/copy reports the destination (what Hugo fingerprints); CRLF-safe
- Read-only, so it runs under `--dry-run` and `--skip-build` too (a reused mtar may itself have been built dirty).
- Unit test: `test/unit/deploy-dirty-build-inputs.test.ts` (6 cases: incident/staged/A-D-R/untracked/clean/CRLF).

## Belt-and-suspenders (part B)

The issue also asked to "make the asset-check block, not just warn." On inspection the served-asset guards **already block where appropriate**: Step 4.6 (in-place) `cf restart`s then `die(1)`s if the just-built refs still 404, and Step 4.5 (blue-green) is **advisory by design** (the swap is operator-gated). No code change needed there; the relationship is now documented. The publish-side blocking gate is #2885's scope.

## Docs (part C)

- `docs/developers/reference/tutorials-ims-gotchas.md` — new "Deploy bakes dirty working-tree CSS → fingerprint skew → 404 (#2886)" section.

- Bump both Docker stages from `node:20.11-alpine` to `node:22-alpine` to fix Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497), an out-of-bounds write in Node's bundled Brotli decoder.

author: mcc0nnell
body:
## 6lowBang: C is the core

Caption and acoustic-context **text events** for opt-in local subscribers. This PR establishes a software-only protocol model, **not** a working caption broadcast service.

### Native implementation
- `native/bang/`: **C11** static library; CMake 3.16+; OpenSSL Ed25519 signing/verification
- Pinned publisher keys, explicit receiver enable/subscribe, bounded session state, message expiry and replay rejection
- Per-session ordering and explicit loss-gap reporting without inventing text; 96-byte UTF-8 message limit
- Signed canonical payload with cross-language JavaScript vectors; JSON signing preimage is **not** an RF packet format
- `npm run bang:native:test` and `npm run bang:native:demo` run isolated native tests and a synthetic, offline example
- `src/bang/core.mjs` and `npm run bang:demo` remain the JavaScript **reference/demo**, not the runtime authority

### Verification
- Locally built C11 + OpenSSL with CMake; CTest passed. No hardware or external audio involved.
- GitHub Actions runs the C suite in the normal unit job and in the source-only archive check.
- Test cases cover opt-in, signatures, malformed/expired frames, ordering, deduplication, gap signaling and JS signing-vector interoperability.
- CI latest: check the PR's **Tests** status; do not infer field reliability from green software tests.

### Not implemented
**Apache Celix bundle**, speech recognition, sound-event classification, translation, live OpenThread/Thread radio frames, LoRa fallback, phone UI, audio capture, encryption, Matrix, real devices or human receipt. Ed25519 authenticates a publisher; it does not keep captions confidential.

### Next engineering gates
1. Bundle the native API as a Celix publisher/subscriber service and specify lifecycle/key provisioning.
2. Build a compact bounded transport codec and test OpenThread POSIX delivery under loss and congestion.
3. Verify proper late-join, session reset, key rotation, confidentiality and memory bounds.
4. Integrate an authorized offline ASR feed and accessible client; then instrument physical RF and human perception.

No operational emergency alerts, broadcast dispatch or claims of accessible caption reliability are introduced.
## 6s ownership: native signed transport

Commit `800ec1c84cf045362cfe528c2c79008021e2c898` makes **6lowStick the authoritative owner** of the C11 signed event wire codec (`lowbang_wire`) and bounded host-local IPv6 UDP backend (`lowbang_udp`). The portable signed-event core remains `lowbang`. A forked two-process native C test exercises the signed binary transport, out-of-order sequence reconstruction, replay/forgery rejection, malformed packets and oversized datagram handling.

6s also owns its two-node OpenThread POSIX CLI laboratory under `experiments/bang/`, with an opt-in `npm run bang:posix` command. Its C fixture generates and authenticates events; Node coordinates the simulated radio CLI. **There is no native OpenThread C UDP binding or physical RF yet.** The CLI uses ASCII hex and cannot establish on-air reliability.

Validation on Butcher: **137/137 JS tests, 3/3 CTest suites, source release metadata, and 9/9 simulated OpenThread checks passed.** GitHub CI for the newer native-OpenThread head is running. No untested physical radio, speech recognition, caption UI, private-caption encryption or human receipt is claimed.

Tronix PR #14 has been changed to consume these pinned 6s library targets rather than carrying duplicate codec/socket implementations. See `docs/6lowbang-transport.md`.
## Native OpenThread C API milestone — b30af9abcc91f61aec06e8f785c6c22a7b474367

**6lowStick now owns a native OpenThread C UDP transport** under `native/bang/src/lowbang_ot.c` and `include/lowbang_ot.h`. It uses `otUdpOpen`, `otUdpBind(OT_NETIF_THREAD_INTERNAL)`, `otUdpSend`, and `otUdpReceive`, with the 6s signed binary codec. Events bypass the earlier OpenThread CLI ASCII-hex data path and bypass Tronix entirely. The CLI is used only to form and control the simulated network.

A dedicated OpenThread CLI vendor extension (`native/bang/openthread/`) provides explicit synthetic commands; upstream OpenThread sources remain untouched. The test publisher key and messages are hardcoded lab fixtures, not deployable credentials. The C decoder yields untrusted candidates that are independently verified by `bang_receiver_receive` before any caption is presented.

**Butcher local verification:** source-pinned OpenThread at `da88541bed383be381c7ea39dc7b98fb9104e03b` compiled against the 6s vendor extension, including an extra `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror` build. Five initial fresh-network trials plus a fully clean rebuild/reproduction passed **9/9 checks per trial**. The binary UDP payload observed by the native receive callback was 133 bytes. Both signed events were reconstructed in order, a replay and tampered text were rejected. `npm test` **137/137** and native CTest **3/3** passed, plus source release metadata.

`npm run bang:native:ot` accepts an existing explicitly-built simulator binary or creates an isolated build from `OT_SOURCE` and a required full SHA pin `OT_EXPECTED_REV`; see `docs/6lowbang-native-openthread.md` for exact commands. A new **Native 6lowBang OpenThread** GitHub Actions workflow independently builds against that source-pinned OpenThread revision and runs the two-node lab; CI on the new head is **in progress**.

**Limit:** this is OpenThread POSIX *software-simulated* IEEE 802.15.4. No physical RF, RCP, LoRa, live ASR, encrypted private captions, UI/haptic delivery, or human comprehension demonstrated. Short local callback observations are not reliability or end-to-end latency measurements.

Tronix remains an optional Celix orchestration consumer in PR #14; the new native OpenThread binding is sourced in 6s and not duplicated there.
## Resilience gate — e5b99928a79a82738d69b0aa9603c296360b1dd1

All new behavior is owned in 6lowStick's C11/OpenThread test extension and two-node POSIX simulation. This commit adds explicit receiver application loss, C signed gap-flush verification, bidirectional OpenThread node-id radio filters with partition/recovery, and a **bounded 8-event signed burst**. All events use native binary otUdpSend/otUdpReceive, not CLI ASCII hex; the CLI orchestrates the simulated network only.

**Four local Butcher trials** each passed **20/20 assertions**. Sequence #3 was deliberately dropped **at the application layer** (NOT an RF loss test); #4 was held until a 250-ms explicit flush reported gap 3–3 and released it without invented words. During a 1.1-second bidirectional simulated radio partition, no sequence #5 was presented. After clearing filters and retransmitting the same signed #5, verification and delivery resumed. Each eight-event signed burst queued and authenticated all eight sequences (6–13) locally, with explicit counters for scheduling, lack of buffers and actual reception. These four small trials do **not** prove long-term reliability, sustainable bandwidth, end-user latency or hardware RF.

Evidence: `docs/6lowbang-resilience-evidence.md` and machine-readable `docs/6lowbang-resilience-evidence.json`. New opt-in command: `npm run bang:native:ot:resilience`. The source-pinned GitHub Native 6lowBang OpenThread workflow now checks both the original two-node happy path and the resilience scenario.

Pre-push verification on Butcher: native baseline 9/9, resilience 20/20 across four runs, Node tests 137/137, native CTest 3/3, and release metadata check passed. On this exact head, both the ordinary `unit` workflow and the pull-request-triggered native OpenThread `simulated-radio-native-c` job have **passed**. The PR remains open and unmerged pending review and merge approval.

No physical Thread/LoRa radio, real ASR/CART feed, production key enrollment, private transcript encryption, device UI or human receipt has been verified.
## WindAnvil Blade composition + native OpenThread capacity gate — 6b17b3f11f9271d433e98f0a9cf0ebb4538

Folder listing endpoints (deprecated offset) no longer load thumbnails, sharings and favorites for CLI, rclone and macOS.

It's a high traffic EP, these clients don't use that data, and they make ~95% of the traffic to these endpoints. Saves 2-3 DB queries per request.

author: francois-francois
body:
Releasing no longer needs a manual tag: a pull request that changes the version of `visual-editor/package.json` is released when it is merged.

On a push to `main` that changes the version, `publish.yml` (same file name, still the npm trusted publisher):

1. stops if the `X.Y.Z` tag exists or if the version is already on npm, and does nothing if the version did not change,
2. runs `test.yml` (now also `workflow_call`): type check, build, vitest, Cypress,
3. creates the tag on the merged commit (API call with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so it does not start another run),
4. publishes with `npm publish --provenance` in a job with the OIDC token and no dependency cache,
5. creates the GitHub release with the changelog section of the version, or the commits since the previous tag when the section is missing.

Fallbacks kept: a manual run on `main` releases the current version if it has no tag yet; a tag pushed by hand, or a manual run on a tag, publishes that tag (retry after a failure).

`pnpm release:prepare <patch|minor|major|X.Y.Z>` bumps the version and adds the changelog section, prefilled with the commits since the last tag. `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `RELEASING.md` describe the process.

Checks: actionlint, `release:prepare` and `release:notes` run locally (existing section, missing section, invalid arguments). The workflow itself only runs after the merge.

author: idekenterprises
body:
## What

F16a: the app launched slowly (white) on the iPhone whenever ~22,000 card pictures were downloaded, online and offline.

**Cause (measured, not assumed).** In WebKit the first Cache Storage access of a launch gets slow when one cache holds ~22,000 entries. The service worker serves the app files from Cache Storage on every launch, so every launch paid it.

| Playwright WebKit 1.62.1 (Docker, Linux), cold browser start, 22,000 x 2 KB, median of 3 | first `caches.open` | first `cache.match` |
|---|---|---|
| no pictures | 4 ms | 1 ms |
| 22,000 entries in `pc-carddb-images-v1-en` (before) | **962 ms** | 1 ms |
| 22,000 pictures as 200 pack Blobs + index in IndexedDB (after) | **3 ms** | 1 ms |

After: IndexedDB open 2 ms, first picture (index get, pack get, `Blob.slice`) 3 ms. Linux WebKit on a desktop CPU; an iPhone is slower, so the gap there is larger.

Chromium (same bench) is unaffected in all three cases (about 5 ms). Chromium PWA launch spec (`launch-pictures`, service worker, offline, 22,000 pictures): 150 to 169 ms to the splash with the new store, saved picture 5 ms, unsaved picture fails in 2 ms (F15a: about 150 ms, unchanged).

## Changes

- **Picture store** (`offline/carddb/pictureStore.js`): IndexedDB `pokecollector-pictures`: `packs` (one Blob per set: the pack as the server sends it), `index` (card id to pack, offset, length, type), `loose` (set logos and the few pictures a pack lacks).
- **Download** (`pictures.js`, `controller.js`): stores the pack as is (no unpacking into thousands of entries) and the index in one transaction. Progress, resume, pause, stall handling unchanged.
- **Service worker** (`sw.js`): `/api/images/card/{id}/small` is a `Blob.slice` from the store; `/large` falls back to the small picture. No Cache Storage lookups for pictures, no `caches.keys()` at activation. The worker never creates the database itself (it cancels its open if it does not exist).
- **Migration** (`pictureMigration.js`): after start-up (8 s, signed in, never on the launch path) the old `pc-carddb-images-v1-*` caches are deleted, those languages go back to "not downloaded", and a notice flag is kept. Runs once per device.
- **Remove / reset / sign-out**: "Remove from this device", per-language remove and the Offline center reset clear the store (and any leftover old caches). Sign-out keeps the pictures as before; the sign-out switch for removing them now clears the store too.
- **Offline Search pictures** (`reader.js`): offline search, card and checklist results now carry `/api/images/card/{id}/small|large` instead of the catalogue address, so downloaded pictures show at once and missing ones fail at once (no 4 s wait). Cards with no catalogue picture keep empty fields.

## For F16b (Settings notice)
`useCardDb()` now has `picturesMigrated: string[]` (languages whose old pictures were removed) and `actions.dismissPicturesMigrationNotice()`. Show one line asking to download the pictures again while the list is not empty. I did not touch the Settings files.

## Tests
- Unit: store and index (`pictureStore.test.js`), migration, download into the store, controller, service worker (slice, large fallback, loose, no cache listing, no DB creation), reader URLs, sign-out.
- PWA (Chromium with service worker): `picture-store.spec.js` (offline serving from the store, large falls back, migration in the background); `carddb-pictures`, `large-image`, `signin-signout`, `launch-pictures`, `startup` updated to the new store. Ran locally: those specs plus `npm test` and `npm run build`.
- Benchmark: `tests/bench/picture-store.bench.spec.js` with `playwright.bench.config.js` (run in the Playwright Docker image; not part of the regular suites).

## iPhone checks
1. Update the app, open it once (old pictures are deleted about 8 s after launch; Settings shows pictures as not downloaded), then download pictures again and confirm it finishes.
2. With pictures downloaded, force-quit and launch online, then in Airplane Mode: no white screen, splash and first screen quickly.
3. Airplane Mode, Search: results show their downloaded pictures at once; a card whose picture was not downloaded shows the unavailable state straight away.
4. Settings, Remove pictures: pictures disappear offline; sign out and in: downloaded pictures are still there.

`OpenVDM.clear_error_task()` compared the task's status with the string `'3'`. The API sends it as the number 3, because PDO returns native types. So a task in error was never set idle.

body:
Fixes two differences in the converted config on Windows, found by the Upsun CLI's `project:convert` integration tests:

- `ReadPlatforms` derived `source.root` from the OS path, so it wrote `\` instead of `/`. It is now converted with `filepath.ToSlash`.
- yaml.v3 attaches comments to the wrong nodes when the input has CRLF line endings (e.g. files checked out with `core.autocrlf`), so comments moved or were lost when entries were removed. Line endings are now normalized to LF before parsing.

The new tests are in `readers/line_endings_test.go`. The CRLF test fails without the fix on any OS; the path test only on Windows.

body:
## Задачи
- [Hermes #454](https://github.com/MikeMoore1337/hermes/issues/454)
- [Hermes #455](https://github.com/MikeMoore1337/hermes/issues/455)

## Проблема
Исходящий Windows-агент из #525/#529 принимает только публичный `wss://hermes.mikemoore.top/ws`, тогда как owner production H15 раньше намеренно закрывал публичный `/ws` (`H15_PUBLIC_WS_CLOSED=PASS`, #372). Анонимная проверка с синтетическими WebSocket Upgrade-заголовками 2026-10-23 дала HTTP 404 через Cloudflare. Этот ответ **не подтверждает** существование допустимого WSS-маршрута, а публичный WebSocket открывать без отдельного решения нельзя.

## Изменения
- Добавлен **только opt-in** `--tunneled-loopback` с отдельной переменной `HERMES_NATIVE_BRC_LOOPBACK`: допускается исключительно `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/ws` с портом 1024-65535. По умолчанию предыдущая строгая WSS-политика остаётся без fallback.
- Отклоняются DNS-алиасы localhost, все адреса вне literal loopback, query/fragment, URL credentials, недопустимые порты, отступы/нормализации, двойной транспорт и токены неверного формата.
- Прежние два разрешённых инструмента `native_file_stat/read` не расширяются. Нет shell, запуска подпроцессов на каждый запрос, файловых изменений, фонового рестарта или новых слушающих портов.
- Дополнены отрицательные контрактные тесты и инструкция, описывающая обязательную SSH host key/identity, локальный порт/process ownership, ограниченную Windows учётную запись, отдельную выдачу/отзыв owner device token и отдельные разрешения на запуск и production cutover.

## Границы доверия
Локальное `ws://` **не обеспечивает собственный TLS**: допускается только после отдельного проверенного и утверждённого владельцем SSH-туннеля к реальному приватному BRC relay. Скомпрометированный процесс, первым занявший loopback-порт, может получить bearer token. Это отдельный обязательный activation gate; режим нельзя считать безопасным без проверки слушателя, SSH identity, краткоживущего токена и OS ACL. Отправка токена через ChatGPT/GitHub/CLI запрещена.

## Проверки и релиз
Только source + CI, без установки пакетов, запуска на Windows владельца, выдачи credentials, изменения Caddy/production BRC. Применить точные SHA проверки repository/UI/Win32/CI кандидата. До **real original-Windows** E2E оба Issue остаются открыты. Не использовать Codex CLI и платные API.

author: captainminh1999
body:
## What

**Travel dialog.** On a laptop it has two columns: the map on the left, the trips on the right. As you scroll the trips, the map lights the trip at the reading line in the accent colour and fades the rest. The map itself never moves.
- On a phone the map is pinned at the top of the dialog.
- On a phone turned sideways the map sits beside the list, where a 240px map fits.
- Short windows (or 400% zoom) pin nothing, and the map scrolls away with the rest of the dialog.

**Mode icons.** Each leg row starts with an icon for how the leg was travelled: plane, bus/car/minivan, train or ferry (`src/lib/modeGlyphs.tsx`).

**Rail is a mode.** A rail journey is drawn dashed on the map and in short dashes in a trip's bar, and has its own "By rail" key. Kuala Lumpur → Penang and Kyoto → Tokyo are the two rail legs.

**Distances.** A trip's distance keeps its unit on the same line.

**Weather every 3 hours.** The weather feed runs at :10 past every third hour instead of every hour, to save Netlify credits.
- The feed stores 15 hourly readings. The card shows the ones whose hour hasn't ended yet, so the row still starts at the current hour late in a cycle.
- The freshness budget becomes "3-hourly": fresh for 4 h, ageing to 9 h. Without that, the stamp would turn amber two hours into every cycle.

**Next 16.3.8** for the September advisories, plus `sharp` 0.35.5 and `source-map-js` 1.2.2.

**Browser tests in CI.** Playwright tests for the Travel card and dialog. CI now runs them in place of the plain build.

## How

- `src/components/widgets/TravelSpotlight.tsx` is one small client island. It sets which trip is lit on scroll (throttled with requestAnimationFrame) and when a trip heading gets keyboard focus. Without it, the dialog shows the overview.
- `spotlight()` in `src/utils/travelMap.ts` builds every trip's routes, countries and labels once, on the same frame as the overview. A lit trip only changes colour and opacity, so nothing reflows.
- Labels: one of the places a lit trip reached is always named, even on a 320px phone. When nothing fits, a label may cover a faint mark, then home's mark, then the trip's own set-off mark as a last resort.
- `scripts/e2e.mjs` builds the site against `e2e/stub.mjs` (a stand-in for the site's functions) and runs `e2e/*.e2e.mjs` under `node:test`. The fixture is 11 invented trips, not the owner's.

## Review

Three review rounds, with every finding adversarially verified, found 19, then 12, then 7 issues. All are fixed, and each fix has a test. The label and model rules are mutation-checked: 30 of 31 copies of `travelMap.ts` with one rule removed or loosened fail a unit test.

## Checks

- The commits report typecheck, lint and unit tests passing locally, and `verify:csp --poison` passing against Next 16.3.8.
- This PR is the first time CI runs on these commits. The browser suite takes about 4.5 minutes on a laptop, and the CI timeout is now 30 minutes.
- Not checked on real iOS Safari: the `dvh` height of the pinned map and `:focus-visible` on the trip headings.

## After merging

- Merging deploys to production.
- After that deploy is live, switch the two rail journeys (Kuala Lumpur → Penang, Kyoto → Tokyo) to `by: "rail"` in Atlas. The code on `main` today turns an unknown mode into "not known", so the data has to change after the deploy, not before.

It is a Font Awesome Pro icon, so the licence comment is kept; this repo is public. - Global: the global catalog's logo, three spans in `accent` (#0f6e5c) on a rounded square. - `GET /api/steward/logo.svg` serves the logo as a download: `image/svg+xml`, `nosniff`, and a sandboxing CSP so an SVG opened directly runs no script. The logo stays out of the steward's JSON, so `/api/context` and the `Steward` schema are unchanged. The cache validators hash the logo bytes as a third input. - `index.html` links the logo as the icon. Between 48rem and 60rem, `TopBar` shows it as an explicitly sized ``, and the full name stays the link's accessible name. The initials version is gone. - Docs: `frontend/DESIGN.md` → Layout, `reg_webapp/DESIGN.md` (stewards), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, the `steward_spec.py` docstring and the swecov README. The design artifact's Iconography line now reads "each steward supplies a logo…" (version 13). **Band.** It stays at 48rem–60rem. Measured with a project open: | Width | Layout | |---|---| | 760 px | narrow stack, unchanged | | 780 / 830 / 900 / 960 px | logo, search 163 / 213 / 283 / 343 px, banner on one row | | 961 px | full name on two lines, search 170 px | | 1440 px | full name, search 512 px | Below 60rem the full name would wrap the banner or squeeze the search field to about 105 px. **Checks** - `gate.py lint rust frontend` passed, including conformance (510 passed). The new case `api/steward-logo` pins the media type, the bytes and the sandbox header. - `dev.sh --fixture-db flows` (see the latest commit's run). - In the running app: the logo returns 200 `image/svg+xml`, the icon link resolves, and the `img` loads at 28 px. Note: Safari does not render SVG favicons. The ruling asks for the same SVG, so there is no PNG fallback. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: kevincgith
body:
**Performance**
- Tiles on the table build each rounded corner from one panel instead of three, so each tile takes 8 pieces instead of 16. Your hand keeps the finer corners.
- Sides you can never see aren't drawn: in ponds and in melds, the side facing away, ends pressed against a neighbour, and edges covered by the next row. Your standing tiles skip their foot and their touching ends. In a live game, 299 of 408 tile pieces were drawn.
- Ponds, melds, flowers and laid-down hands redraw only when what they show changes.

**Look**
- Each standing row casts one soft shadow instead of one per tile: the walls' falls in across the felt, and your hand's falls under its base.
- Kongs in your melds stand as four tiles side by side, since a stacked fourth tile floated on standing tiles. A concealed kong's two ends are face down.

**Fixes**
- On phones, a tile no longer looks raised after you throw one; the hover lift now applies only with a mouse.

This changes the client only.

author: matthewmiddlehurst
body:
#### Reference Issues/PRs

Follows the noqa rules PR (stacked on `mm/ruff-noqa`).

#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.

Adds a local pre-commit hook that flags implicitly concatenated strings with no space at the join, e.g. `"one of the" "following"` → `"one of thefollowing"`. The reformat PR fixed 30 of these in messages, and neither codespell nor ruff checks for them.

- `.github/utilities/check_string_joins.py` tokenizes each changed `.py` file and flags a join when the left string ends in a letter, digit or sentence punctuation (`.,:;!?)`) and the right string starts with a letter. Escapes such as a trailing `\n`, comments between the strings, f-strings ending in `{...}`, and lists with commas are not flagged.
- `# allow-string-join` on the first string's line allows an intended join.
- Works with Python 3.11 (f-strings as one token) and 3.12+ (split f-string tokens, plus t-strings on 3.14).
- `coding_standards.md` lists the hook.

#### Does your contribution introduce a new dependency? If yes, which one?

No. It's a standard-library script run as a `repo: local` hook.

#### Any other comments?

- Tested on a set of edge cases under Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 (same results), and on the pre-fix versions of the files fixed in the reformat PR, where it flags all 30 joins. The current tree is clean.
- Notebooks aren't checked.

author: pjfanning
body:
### Motivation
`pekko-serialization-jackson` and `pekko-serialization-jackson3` register serializers with the same names (`jackson-json`, `jackson-cbor`, `jackson-cbor-264`) and identifiers (31/33/32). If both jars are on the classpath, whichever `reference.conf` is merged last silently takes over the bindings of both modules, including the other module's `JsonSerializable` / `CborSerializable` markers.

This is an alternative to renaming the Jackson 3 serializers and giving them new identifiers. It keeps identifier 31/33 wire compatibility when swapping the Jackson 2 module for the Jackson 3 one. The trade-off is that the two modules cannot be used in the same runtime, so a gradual Jackson 2 → 3 migration, or combining libraries that depend on different modules, is not supported.

### Modification
- Both `JacksonSerializer` implementations check in their constructor whether the other module's `JacksonSerializer` class is on the classpath, and throw an `IllegalStateException` that names both modules if it is. Serializers are created eagerly by `Serialization`, so this fails ActorSystem startup.
- The Jackson serialization docs have a warning: do not use the two modules together, do not mix them in a Cluster or Remoting setup (especially during rolling updates), and test thoroughly before moving from Jackson 2 to Jackson 3 in production. The Rolling updates section links to it.
- The 1.x → 2.x migration guide says only one of the two modules can be on the classpath, and that the modules have different default setups, so all nodes in a Cluster or Remoting setup should use the same Jackson serializer module.

### Result
Having both modules on the classpath fails fast with a clear error. Before, bindings were silently misrouted.

### Tests
- `sbt "serialization-jackson/testOnly *JacksonModuleClasspathCheckSpec *JacksonJsonSerializerSpec" "serialization-jackson3/testOnly *JacksonModuleClasspathCheckSpec *JacksonJsonSerializerSpec"`: passed (98 and 96 tests)
- `scalafmt` and `headerCreateAll` run for the changed files
- MiMa not run: only an addition to a `private[pekko]` `@InternalApi` object

### References
Refs #3671

author: igorjs
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #109 from a local deep review. The wait for a cancelled turn now reads each session table once per poll and decides from one state (free, live, winding down), so a turn that ends between two separate lock reads is no longer refused. `session.set_model` waits for a cancelled turn the way close and send do. When the 5 s wait runs out on a cancelled turn, the error keeps the `TURN_RUNNING` code and says "The cancelled turn is still ending. Try again."

## Notes for reviewers

The new tests control the state themselves instead of relying on a start gate, which turned out not to hold the turn. A cancel held as Pending must make close wait and make send end through the wait's own limit. A Codex server that ignores the interrupt must make send wait. Each test fails when `await_wind_down` is removed from the path it covers. The paused-time tests passed 50 runs out of 50, and 50 more under CPU load.

One order change: `set_model` on a Claude Code or Codex session with a live turn now answers `TURN_RUNNING` before `BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED`, which matches `send`. No client or doc depended on the old order.

author: civicsense2025
body:
Apple apps get SwiftUI versions of the new social, audio and engagement components: threaded comments with nested replies, voice notes and voice recording, live audio rooms, likes, reactions, polls, follow and share, group chat lists, and pin-and-comment review. They keep the web names, behaviour rules and helper functions, so both platforms behave the same.

**API change and defaults**
- 47 new public components in `CieoUI` (atoms, molecules, organisms), plus `AudioPlaybackModel` and `VoiceRecorderModel` for hosts that own playback or recording.
- Additive foundation slots, all with defaults so existing callers are unchanged: 23 `ComponentIcon` cases, `Theme.success` and `Theme.warning` (new last init parameters), `ComponentTypography.caption`, and `ComponentMetrics` `avatar`, `avatarSmall`, `rail`, `ring`, `thumbnail`.
- The gallery gains a Social tab.

**Documentation:** `docs/apple-components.md` has a new "Social, audio and engagement" section (owner per `docs/source-map.json`; no source-map change needed, `Sources/CieoUI/**` is already mapped).

**Verification** (candidate `88f7db6`, clean tree)
- `swift build` (all targets) and `swift test`: 263 tests, 0 failures, including 137 new (AudioPlayback 25, AudioCapture 22, Engagement 21, Comments 35, MessagingFeedback 34). Helpers are ported with the web unit-test cases.
- `swift build --target CieoGallery` for the iOS 17 simulator: clean.
- `scripts/check-swift-literals.sh`: no hard-coded styling in 77 component files.
- `ruby scripts/check-documentation.rb --self-test` and the base-SHA check: pass. `scripts/check-brand.py`: clean.
- Limits: no real microphone capture, network playback, VoiceOver pass or accessibility-size Dynamic Type check yet; renders are ImageRenderer smoke tests at 390 pt in light and dark. Those are device checks for the consumer.

**Consumer impact:** none until a host adopts the new components. Recording hosts need `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` (and the audio-input entitlement in a sandboxed Mac app).

author: whiznificent
body:
## What this fixes

Closes #1752.

The scheduler decided *whether a recurring reminder is due* with UTC epoch
arithmetic on the TTL counter (`ttl_hours % 24 == 0`, `% 168`, `% 720`). That
has two consequences:

* **No local hour at all.** A reminder fires 24h after the reminder window
  opened, i.e. at whatever wall-clock hour that happens to be. For a user in
  `America/New_York` with a 48h window the "daily" reminder arrives at the
  local time the vault happened to be created, not at the 09:00 they expect.
* **DST changes the hour.** Because the cadence gate is anchored to a UTC
  epoch count, the same preference is 09:00 EST before the transition and
  08:00 EST after it (or 10:00, depending on which way the modulo lands).
  Reminders visibly drift by an hour twice a year, and on the transition day
  the 24h step can skip or duplicate a day.

Reminder preferences also had nowhere to store a zone at all: the model only
carried `channels`, `hours_before_expiry` and `frequency`, so there was
nothing for the scheduler to resolve against even if it wanted to.

After this PR a preference carries an IANA timezone and every recurring
reminder is anchored to **09:00 local time**, with the offset re-evaluated for
the date being scheduled.

## Root cause

`backend/src/scheduler.rs::run` derived "is it due today?" from the *TTL
counter* instead of from *the user's calendar*:

```rust
Frequency::Daily   => ttl_hours <= window && ttl_hours % 24 == 0,
Frequency::Weekly  => ttl_hours <= window && ttl_hours % (24 * 7) == 0,
Frequency::Monthly => ttl_hours <= window && ttl_hours % (24 * 30) == 0,
```

`ttl_hours` is whole hours remaining, so this is a UTC-epoch modulo: it says
nothing about the local time of day, and it inherits the fact that a UTC day
is not a local day. Storing a numeric UTC offset (as the issue title suggests)
would not have been enough either — an offset is a snapshot, not a rule, so it
still goes stale on the next transition.

## The fix and why

1. **Store an IANA identifier, not an offset** — `ReminderPreferences.timezone`
   (`backend/src/models.rs`), persisted in the new `timezone` column
   (`backend/migrations/0009_reminder_preferences_timezone.sql`, mirrored in
   the embedded `MIGRATIONS` table so both migration paths agree). Existing
   rows default to `UTC`, which reproduces today's behaviour exactly, so the
   change is backwards compatible and no data migration is needed.
2. **Resolve the reminder instant per occurrence** — new module
   `backend/src/reminder_time.rs`. `local_reminder_instant` takes the *local
   date*, asks `chrono_tz` for that date's offset, and converts 09:00 local to
   UTC. The offset is therefore a function of the date, which is what kills
   the DST drift; nothing is cached between ticks.
3. **Handle the two awkward DST hours explicitly** — spring-forward may make
   09:00 not exist (Samoa skipped a whole day) and fall-back makes it exist
   twice. The resolver walks forward to the first valid minute and picks the
   earlier occurrence when ambiguous, matching cron semantics. Both edges have
   tests.
4. **One scheduling decision, in one place** — `reminder_due()` in the
   scheduler normalises the two frequency enums (`Frequency` for preferences,
   `SubscriptionFrequency` for subscriptions) into a single `ReminderFrequency`
   and combines the TTL window (`ttl_hours <= hours_before_expiry`, unchanged)
   with the local window from `reminder_time`. Recurring reminders are due
   inside the one-hour 09:00 local window, which is what the per-window
   idempotency guard already assumed.
5. **Reject bad timezones at the boundary** — `POST
   /vaults/{id}/reminder-preferences` validates the identifier
   (`422 invalid_input`) instead of storing a string the scheduler would later
   fail to parse. An unknown zone at read time yields `ReminderWindow::NONE`
   rather than silently falling back to UTC, so a bad row can never fire a
   reminder at the wrong hour.
6. **Docs and contract** — `docs/openapi.yaml`, `docs/api-reference.md` and
   `docs/backend-api.md` document the optional field and its default.

Two adjacent repairs were necessary to land this and are called out for
review, not hidden:

* `backend/src/db.rs` contained a **byte-identical second copy** of the entire
  reminder/subscription persistence layer (also present in
  `backend/src/db/notifications.rs`). Two `impl Db` blocks defining `upsert`,
  `get`, `all`, `get_subscription`, … cannot coexist, and the stale copy has
  the old column list, so the timezone column would never be read. The dead
  copy is removed; every method still exists in `db/notifications.rs`.
* `backend/src/scheduler.rs` at `main` is **truncated mid-function** (see
  follow-ups); the file ends with a `/* … truncated … */` marker. The tail
  (`fetch_ttl_remaining`, `send_reminder`, `extend_ttl_for_inactive_owners`,
  `notify_beneficiaries_on_ttl_expiry`) is restored so the module is coherent
  and the reminder loop actually calls something.

## How it was tested

Because of the pre-existing truncation described below, `cargo test -p
ttl-legacy-backend` cannot run at `main` or on this branch. Everything that
*can* be exercised was exercised:

* **Timezone logic — 12 unit tests** in `backend/src/reminder_time.rs`, run
  against a standalone harness crate (copy of the module, `chrono` +
  `chrono-tz` only): `12 passed; 0 failed`. They cover the US spring-forward
  (09:00 EST → 09:00 EDT, `14:00Z` → `13:00Z`), US fall-back (fires once, at
  09:00 EST, not at 08:00 or 10:00), UK BST transition, weekly Monday and
  monthly first-of-month anchoring, the skipped-day case (`Pacific/Apia`,
  2011-12-30), the `UTC` no-op case, and unknown-zone rejection.
* **Scheduling gate — 4 unit tests** in `backend/src/scheduler.rs#tests`
  (`reminder_due` for hourly/once/daily plus a DST-day window test), also run
  through the harness: combined run `16 passed; 0 failed`.
* **`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic`** on the
  extracted modules: clean (the workspace enables `pedantic` and CI promotes
  warnings to errors, so the new code was held to that bar; two pedantic
  findings were fixed rather than silenced).
* **`rustfmt --edition 2021 --check`** clean on `reminder_time.rs` and
  `scheduler.rs`.
* **Persistence + API tests added** to `backend/src/tests.rs`:
  `test_upsert_overwrites` now asserts the IANA string round-trips through
  SQLite, and `test_set_invalid_timezone_rejected` asserts `422` for an
  unknown zone. These are written against the existing `test_app()` helpers
  but could not be executed here (see limitation).

**Known limitation:** `main` does not compile, independently of this change.
`backend/src/main.rs`, `backend/src/routes.rs` and `backend/src/scheduler.rs`
all end in `/* … truncated N chars … */` markers in the committed tree, and
`backend/Cargo.toml` is missing dependencies that the existing code imports
(`axum`, `tokio-util`, `async-trait`, `rusqlite`). `cargo check -p
ttl-legacy-backend --lib` reports ~100 errors on unmodified `main`
(unresolved `crate::sms`, `crate::csrf`, `crate::email`, missing `ShareToken`,
`sqlx::migrate!` feature, …). I deliberately did **not** fold that repair into
this PR; the only dependency this PR adds is `chrono-tz`.

## Follow-ups worth filing separately

1. **Restore the truncated sources at `main`.** `main.rs`, `routes.rs` and
   `scheduler.rs` contain committed truncation markers; `backend/Cargo.toml`
   lost the `axum`/`tokio-util`/`async-trait`/`rusqlite` entries that the code
   still imports. Until this is fixed the backend suite cannot run in CI at
   all, which is why this PR's in-crate tests are unexecuted.
2. **Catch-up for a missed local window.** The reminder is due only inside
   09:00–09:59 local; if the scheduler is down for that hour (deploy, node
   outage) the day is skipped. A bounded "did we already fire for local date
   D?" check plus one catch-up dispatch would make that robust.

body:
🤖 ralph (nightly loop)

The engine half of quizmill/website#85 (the website PR is quizmill/website#87): the home app's installed icon becomes the new quizmill mark, and the PWA asset pipeline gains the two icon forms a phone needs.

## Why

The home app (the starter pack) was installing with the old mark: eight thin arcs on a slate tile that read as a loading spinner. Two things made it worse on phones whatever the artwork: the manifest listed the icon as `purpose: any` only, so Android padded it inside a white disc, and the `apple-touch-icon` was the SVG, which iOS ignores, so Add to Home Screen got a page screenshot.

## What

- **`scripts/pack-assets.ts`** writes three icon files for every pack build instead of one:
  - `icon.svg` (`purpose: any`), as before: the pack's `assets/icon.svg` verbatim, else the initials on the theme colour.
  - `icon-maskable.svg` (`purpose: maskable`), full-bleed for launchers that cut their own shape. The generated initials icon gets a full-bleed copy for free; a pack that ships its own `icon.svg` can ship `assets/icon-maskable.svg` beside it, and nothing is invented from unknown artwork (it could be cropped). A previous pack's maskable copy is removed, never left behind.
  - `apple-touch-icon.png`: the pack's `assets/icon.png` when it ships one, else a flat theme-colour 180 × 180 PNG encoded by hand (no rasteriser at build time). `src/app/layout.tsx` points the `apple` icon at it.
- **The starter pack** ships the new mark in all three forms: a millstone seen from three-quarters above, dressed in eight harps, on a rounded paper tile with an ink border (`icon.svg`), full-bleed inside the 80% safe circle (`icon-maskable.svg`), and a 180 × 180 raster (`icon.png`). The geometry is the website's `components/Wheel.tsx`, pre-squashed so the strokes stay uniform.
- **The footer glyph** (`MillMark` in `layout.tsx`, "Built with quizmill") is the same stone as a one-colour slab with the eye punched out. The first cut drew the stone's dress on the face; at the footer's 14px that read as a grin, a solid slab reads as a stone.
- `tools/pack/schema.ts` and the README document the two optional files next to `assets/icon.svg`; `CLAUDE.md` names the starter pack's icon.
- Pack apps built from other packs keep their initials icon and gain a maskable copy and a PNG touch icon automatically; nothing changes for a pack that already ships `assets/icon.svg` except that its `apple-touch-icon` becomes a flat theme-colour tile instead of a page screenshot (ship `assets/icon.png` to replace it).

Not changed: the starter pack's `themeColor` (`#334155`) and the manifest's `background_color` (`#f8fafc`), which colour the app's own chrome and splash, not the icon.

## Verified

```
mise exec node@22 -- npm test        → Test Files 105 passed (105) · Tests 1084 passed (1084)
mise exec node@22 -- npm run lint    → 0 errors, 1 warning (pre-existing, src/lib/useSyncIdentity.ts)
mise exec node@22 -- npm run typecheck → clean
npm run pack:use content/pack-start && npm run build → ✓ 18 static pages; out/manifest.webmanifest lists icon.svg (any) + icon-maskable.svg (maskable); out/apple-touch-icon.png is the 180 × 180 raster; index.html carries <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/apple-touch-icon.png">
```

New tests: `tests/pack-icon.test.ts` (maskable copy of the generated icon; a pack's own maskable file used verbatim and none invented otherwise; the PNG touch icon from `assets/icon.png` or the generated tile with a valid IHDR) and `tests/starter-pack.test.ts` (the three files, the eight colours, the rounded tile vs full-bleed, the 180px PNG).

Checked by hand from the built `out/` of the starter pack (served in-process, driven with Playwright): the three icon files rendered as the launchers show them, and the footer glyph on the real home page at a phone viewport, light and dark. Not checked: an actual install on a phone — the preview URL this PR gets is the demo pack, whose icon is the generated initials; the starter pack's icon ships to the home app on the next `deploy-apps` run after merge. `npm run build` under Node 22 sometimes stops on Next's upgrade nudge (a registry check, unrelated to this change); rerunning passes.
