author: bytenik
body:
Changeset files generated by the JavaScript tooling quote package names, such as `"@scope/package": patch`. The parser currently keeps those delimiters in `PackageName`, so consumers cannot match these entries to the package's unquoted name.

Strip one matching pair of single or double quotes when parsing package names. Quoted and unquoted entries then contribute to the same release. Consume front-matter lines independently of the number of unique package names so duplicate normalized keys preserve the summary and retain last-entry-wins behavior.

This changes the parsed names exposed by the public API. A major changeset documents the compatibility change, and the format documentation describes quoted names.

Follows the parser-level fix suggested in https://github.com/knope-dev/knope/pull/2051#issuecomment-6348096081.

Validation:

- All 12 tests pass with `cargo test --locked`.
- The quoted-name and normalized-duplicate regressions fail against the original parser.
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo +nightly fmt --check`, and `git diff --check` pass.

The raster's scratch layout was written out three times: `r3d_pipeline_carve()`, `raster_scratch_bytes()`, and `raster_upscale()`, which worked out the upscale-map pointer again. `r3d_pipeline.h` also included `render/raster.h`, the only include in `render/` that points up a layer. The layout is now stated once, in the raster. | Before | After | |---|---| | `r3d_pipeline_carve()`, `r3d_pipeline_culled_bytes()`, `r3d_pipeline_buffers_t`, `R3D_PIPELINE_CACHE_WAY` and `raster_lens()` in `r3d_pipeline.h` | `raster_carve()`, `raster_culled_bytes()`, `raster_buffers_t`, `RASTER_CACHE_WAY` and `raster_lens()` in the new `render/raster_internal.h` | | `raster_scratch_bytes()` adds up every part a second time | carves with integer offsets and returns where `draw` starts plus `sizeof(draw_work_t)` | | `raster_upscale()` finds the maps after the last attachment | uses `raster_carve().upscale` | | `r3d_pipeline.h` includes `render/raster.h` | includes only `render/raster_split.h`, for `RASTER_SPLIT_PERMILLE` | ```mermaid flowchart LR Bytes["raster_scratch_bytes"] -->|carve| Internal Draw["raster_draw, census"] -->|carve| Internal Up["raster_upscale"] -->|carve| Internal Internal["raster_internal.h

The verifier now checks the raw payload CBOR, and the test helpers in `protocol/common` and `protocol/localmessagenotification` sign the same bytes dmq-node signs. author: alexjba
body:
Part of https://github.com/status-im/status-app/issues/21528 and https://github.com/status-im/status-app/issues/22659.

### What does the PR do

When Android puts the app in the background, it hides the app's window. Qt doesn't treat that window as hidden, only obscured. The render thread stops, but Qt keeps the whole scene graph, the QRhi/EGL context and the Mali driver's pools alive for as long as the app stays in the background.

The new `Status::BackgroundGraphicsRelease` in StatusQ listens for `Qt::ApplicationSuspended`. For every `QQuickWindow` that is no longer exposed, it temporarily turns off persistent graphics and the persistent scene graph, then calls `releaseResources()`. With those flags off, the threaded render loop invalidates the scene graph, destroys the QRhi and exits the render thread. On resume, Qt's own expose rebuilds everything through the normal startup path. The window is never hidden, so the platform window and its Android surface lifecycle are left alone. It is installed from Nim on Android only. Each suspend logs one info line (`status.backgroundGraphicsRelease`): windows released (QRhi freed), windows kept because no GPU resources were freed (e.g. already released by an earlier suspend, or not using the threaded render loop), windows skipped because they are still exposed, and the elapsed ms.

### Why not `hide()`/`show()`

The earlier experiment hid the window on suspend and showed it again on resume. It freed the memory, but after a resume the app hung (`dumpsys meminfo` timed out). The hang was caused by the experiment's timing code, not by hide/show:

- Each queued `frameSwapped` call deleted the same `QElapsedTimer`. Six calls arrived, so the timer was freed several times, and some of those frees hit memory that already belonged to other allocations.
- That corrupted the jemalloc heap. A binder thread later took a SIGSEGV. ART's crash handler then tried to unwind, which allocates memory, and it spins forever in `je_extent_avail_remove` (simpleperf stack, 100% CPU). The process neither dies nor responds.
- I reproduced the hang on the device with the experiment's code. The same non-persistent hide/show without that timing code ran clean.

Calling `releaseResources()` on an already-obscured window needs no change to the window's visibility, so it is the smaller mechanism. Calling it while the window is still exposed only drops caches (−4MB, as measured before), so the release waits for the suspend.

### Measurements

Redmi A5 (Android 15, Mali, GLES, threaded render loop), PR build at 442e4ce021 with this change on top. A runtime switch picks between release and off in the same APK. Three background/foreground cycles of 40s each, plus two of 5.5 min.

| | off (today) | release |
|---|---|---|
| Native heap allocated, in background | ~182 MB | ~130 MB (**−52 MB**) |
| EGL mtrack, in background | 9.2 MB | **0** |
| Total PSS, in background | ~320 MB | ~285–292 MB (**−30 to −35 MB**) |
| Native heap allocated, 15s after resume | ~182 MB | ~157 MB (the scene graph rebuilds smaller) |
| Activity START → first content frame | 91–144 ms | 238–439 ms (median ~270 ms, **+~170 ms**) |
| `releaseResources()` while suspended | — | 29–83 ms |

- `dumpsys meminfo` responded after every resume. There was no crash or restart over 5.5 min in the background.
- Resume screenshots match the off build: no artifacts, and no grey rectangle.
- Input works after resume. An open popup with a focused text field survives a release cycle, and typing continues.

### Tests

`TestBackgroundGraphicsRelease` (StatusQ C++, threaded render loop) checks that:
- an unexposed window's scene graph is invalidated on suspend and its QRhi is destroyed (`window.rhi()` becomes null). Without the `persistentGraphics=false` toggle the scene graph is still invalidated but the QRhi survives; the QRhi check fails in that case (verified by removing the toggle);
- the suspend log line reports released, kept and skipped windows; a second suspend in a row reports the window as kept, not released;
- an exposed window keeps its scene graph;
- other application states keep it;
- the persistence flags are restored for every true/false combination (fails if they are always restored to true);
- showing the window again rebuilds the scene graph;
- the object follows `QGuiApplication::applicationStateChanged`.

It skips on the software scene graph, for example `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`. **CI runs StatusQ tests only on Linux with `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`, where every case skips in `initTestCase`, so CI gives this change zero coverage.** The tests only exercise anything on a machine with a GPU: 9/9 pass on macOS (Metal).

### Side effects

- `QQuickWindow::releaseResources()` also purges the `QQuickPixmap` cache and the GUI-thread shader cache (`qquickwindow.cpp` ~1305-1307), not just the scene graph. Part of the −52 MB may therefore be the pixmap cache: off-screen images are re-decoded (or re-fetched) after resume.
- `QSGRhiSupport::destroyRhi` writes the automatic pipeline cache on every suspend (`finalizePipelineCache`, `qsgrhisupport.cpp` ~1303). That is part of the 29–83 ms, and likely helps cold start.
- `QSG_RENDER_LOOP=basic` (for example via `status-env.txt`) silently disables the release: the GUI-thread render loop's `releaseResources()` only drops caches.

### Interaction with Vulkan (#22928)

Resume after a release recreates the QRhi. On Vulkan, `QRhiVulkan::create` → `supportsPresent(window)` → `QAndroidPlatformVulkanWindow::vkSurface()`, which returns the existing (null) surface while the application state is still `Suspended` (`qandroidplatformvulkanwindow.cpp` ~85-89). If the QRhi is recreated before the state leaves `Suspended`, the window could stay blank. Pending a combined device run of both PRs (≈20 background/foreground cycles, including fast lock/unlock), plus checks with a video playing and with the QR scanner open while backgrounded.

### Risks

- Resume is about 170 ms slower before the first frame, because the GL context, textures and glyph caches are rebuilt every time the app comes back.
- Every item has to handle `sceneGraphInvalidated`. StatusQ has no custom scene graph nodes or textures. The Qt Multimedia `VideoOutput` used by the QR scanner handles invalidation itself. Backgrounding with the scanner open was not tested: the measured base predates the scanner change.
- `releaseResources()` runs while Qt is stopping the event dispatchers for suspension. On the device it always finished before the app was suspended. If it ever lands after the dispatchers stop, the release would just complete on resume.
- Android only. iOS is not changed.

PR6 of the student hub plan: the Jobs half of Collaborate, plus Teams and share agreements. It follows "Addendum: Collaborate", "Collaborate decisions (Aref, 2026-10-23)" and "Collaborate v2". Base is `feature/student-hub`. Ideas, comments and funding come next in PR5, which is stacked on this branch.

## What changed
- **Migration `0006_collaborate.sql`.** Adds these tables: `project_team`, `jobs` (claim, delivery, review and payment fields inline), `job_criteria`, `job_events`, `share_agreements`, `share_agreement_lines`, `share_agreement_acceptances`, and the `job_state` view.
  - CHECKs enforce three rules: exactly one poster (a member, or the Instructor through `poster_is_instructor`), money or share present, and shares for members only.
  - Triggers keep jobs and job events. Events cannot be updated or deleted. Agreements must start pending, can only move through allowed transitions, and activate only when lines total exactly 100% and, for proposals, everyone listed has accepted, along with every approved holder whose line the version drops or lowers. Lines and acceptances are frozen.
  - Partial unique indexes allow one pending and one active agreement per product. Deleting a product cascades its agreements and sets `jobs.project_id` to NULL.
- **Derived state with no cron.** `job_state` computes `effective_state` and `lapse` (claimant left, claim expired after twice the window, auto-accepted after 7 silent days, poster left). It works in read-only mode. A lapse is written as a system event by the next mutation on that job.
- **Domain ops (`lib/d1/collaborate.ts`).** Each op is one `db.batch`. The first statement is a decision `SELECT`, every write is guarded on it, and a final check reports `stale` if a guard flipped mid-batch.
  - Job ops: post, edit, cancel, claim (at most 2 active claims), abandon, release (after the window), deliver, accept, request changes (2 rounds), reject once (the second reject opens a dispute), mark paid, confirm receipt, report not received, dispute. Instructor ops: hide, restore, resolve.
  - Team ops: invite, accept or decline, leave, remove.
  - Agreement ops: propose and respond.
  - Reads `collab_board`, `collab_job` and `collab_team` are added to `readOnlyOperations`.
- **Worker.** `POST /collaborate/action` (`worker/collaborate-action.ts`): same-origin form posts, 400 when `tier`, `state` or `effective_state` (or another server-owned field) is posted, `confirm=yes` required for destructive steps, 303 back with `?message=`, and 503 in read-only mode. Page data comes from `worker/page-collab.ts` through a one-line hook in `worker/page.ts`.
- **UI** (`frontend/pages/collaborate.tsx`, `frontend/pages/job.tsx`, `frontend/job-form.tsx`, `frontend/project-team.tsx`, `frontend/collab-ui.tsx`, `frontend/collaborate.css`):
  - Jobs board with Money, Share, "Funded by <instructor nickname>" and skill filters. The nickname comes from the community row.
  - My jobs: posted, claimed, history, and jobs completed. The Instructor sees disputes to settle.
  - Post and edit form with a live tier preview.
  - Job page:
    - the five-step comb and hexagon pay badges in mono
    - criteria and timing, with every date shown in Tehran time
    - a card with exactly one honey button for the viewer's next step
    - the delivery and payment record
    - the full audit trail for the poster, the claimant and the Instructor.
  - Team & shares on the product page, after the roadmap: a roster, invites, the agreement bar and table with the note that it is the team's own record and not a legal contract, the pending version with answers, a proposal editor with equal split and a total check, and the version history.
  - Teams tab: invitations, agreement versions waiting for your answer, and your teams.
  - Every money surface says Vibies records money and never moves it.
- **Review fixes (Fable, approve with changes).**
  - **No dispute dead end.** `job_resolve` no longer refuses a share the poster cannot cover. With accepted or paid, the share settles as the smaller of the poster's active line and `share_percent * tier / 100`, and 0 when the product was deleted. The money half always settles. The resolve event records `share` and `shortfall`, and the history reads "The poster's line covered 20% of the share, 30% short". `job_accept` keeps its guard, and its failure copy now tells the poster to open a dispute for both `insufficient_share` and `project_missing`.
  - **Granted shares stay.** `job_resolve` refuses open and cancelled once `share_granted` is set. The resolve form shows only accepted and paid in that case, with "A granted share stays in the agreement. Choose accepted or paid."
  - **Hidden jobs.** The poster, the claimant and the Instructor keep acting on a hidden job. Hiding only removes it from the board and from everyone else, and a claim by anyone else still gets `hidden_job`.
  - **Holder consent.** A proposal that drops or lowers the line of an approved holder in the current active version waits for that holder's acceptance. Revoked holders do not block. The schema trigger, the activation guard, `agreement_respond` and both reads include those holders. `team_remove` leaves shares as they are; a change only comes through an accepted version. The Teams tab and the product page show "Version N changes your share from X% to Y%" to affected holders.
  - **Minimum share is 2%** in the form, the parser, the op and the 0006 CHECK, so the 50% tier never rounds to 0.
  - **Settled by the Instructor.** A paid resolution leaves `receipt_at` empty. The claimant sees "Settled by the Instructor" and can still confirm or report it did not arrive.
  - `job_reject` clears `delivered_at`. `job_release` also works in Changes requested once 3 days have passed since the change request.
- **Tests.**
  - `tests/d1-collaborate.test.ts`: 14 tests on node:sqlite covering the lifecycle, tiers, rounds, derived state, shares N+1, triggers and visibility, plus the review fixes: the deleted-product and two 60% job reproductions, a granted share refusing open and cancelled, `job_not_received`, hidden-job parties, reject and release from changes, the 2% minimum, `job_edit` after an expired claim, and holder consent with a removed and a revoked holder.
  - `worker/collaborate.test.mjs`: Miniflare boundary tests covering roles, forbidden fields, https delivery, expiry and auto-accept, shares, a dispute resolved over HTTP with the shortfall, hidden jobs, read-only 503s (the hide check now uses the Instructor session), and origin and form rules.
  - A collaborate schema test in `tests/d1-schema.test.mjs`, and read-only coverage in `tests/read-only.test.ts`.
  - `worker/boundary.test.mjs` now applies every migration in order instead of a fixed list of three.

author: andreasbis
body:
## Motivation

Loading `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local` (about 95 GiB in 21 safetensors shards, about 23k tensors per shard) took about 13 minutes. Other checkpoints of similar total size load in under 100 seconds on the same machine, and the same checkpoint loads in 61 seconds with NVIDIA's vLLM image.

The default loader (`enable_multithread_load` is on unless set otherwise) is `buffered_multi_thread_safetensors_weights_iterator`. Each worker thread creates every tensor view of a shard with `{k: f.get_tensor(k) for k in f.keys()}` before any tensor is copied to the GPU. On a cold page cache this reads the shard through one 4 KiB page fault at a time.

Measured on one shard (4771 MiB, 22908 tensors, cold page cache, copying to the GPU), reproducing the loader's two access patterns with safetensors `safe_open` and `get_tensor`:

| pattern | time | rate | page faults |
|---|---|---|---|
| create all views, then copy each | 31.1 s | 153 MiB/s | 1,107,812 |
| create a view and copy it, one tensor at a time | 3.2 s | 1495 MiB/s | 3 |

Both read the same 4771 MiB from disk, and a second run reproduced the numbers within 1%.

## Modifications

`buffered_multi_thread_safetensors_weights_iterator` now calls the existing `_prefetch_checkpoint_file` on a shard in its worker thread before opening it. The file is read sequentially in 16 MB blocks into the page cache, so the views that follow fault in from memory. The `disable_mmap` branch is unchanged.

A unit test checks that each shard is read before it is opened.

## Results

Checkpoint: 21 safetensors shards, about 95 GiB, `--tp 1`, on a 990 EVO Plus 2TB NVMe SSD. Times are "Load weight begin" to "Load weight end" in the server log.

| | Multi-thread loading, 21 shards | Target model | MTP draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| Without this PR | 8:58 (25.6 s per shard) | 587.7 s | 20.0 s |
| With this PR | 2:03 (5.9 s per shard) | 134 s | 6 s |

The "before" figure is from an earlier run on the same machine, not from a back-to-back comparison.

Hardware: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), driver 615.78.08, torch 2.14.1+cu130, safetensors 0.8.0.

## Not measured

- Other checkpoints. This was only measured on the checkpoint above. A checkpoint already in the page cache pays one extra sequential read pass, and I did not time that.
- Hosts where RAM is smaller than a shard times the number of workers.
- The remaining gap to vLLM (2:03 against 61 s).

I have not established why creating every view first causes 4 KiB faults in `safetensors` / torch. The test above shows the effect and that reading sequentially first removes it.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit test added (`test_prefetch_checkpoints.py`), the file's 22 tests pass
- [ ] Other models timed before and after

author: weijunswj
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"weijunswj"} -->
_Requested by **That Vibecoding Guy**_

Before: the generated status table sat above the title on #421 and on every child page, used nine columns, mixed finished work with active rows, and treated COMPLETED and RETIRED as classes. The hand-kept "Programme index" stayed as a second table. Comments were not linked from the pages, nothing ran unless someone typed the command, and a branch read right after a state write could return the old file (`STATE_READBACK_MISMATCH` on the first #421 apply).

After: #421 opens with its title and CURRENT, then one **Programme Graph** where the Programme index was, with the owner's columns `Task | Child # | PR # | Class | Status | Lane | Task Description`. Rows sort CORE, HARDENING, LATER, then COMPLETED with the most recent last; sub-tasks sort like any row. Each task page shows its title, direction note, then its status box, and every catalogued page ends with a clickable list of every comment on it. The page updates itself on a merge to main and on any issue or comment change, once the owner adds the key. State writes read back from the commit they created.

This implements the owner's answers of 23 Oct (the Programme page build spec); the spec's assumptions are listed for the owner's confirmation in the project thread.

How:
- **Placement:** a new optional binding field `projection` (`replace_section` "Programme index", `after_section` "CURRENT"). A block above its place or a named section still on the page moves once; then the pass settles.
- **Graph:** Class is CORE/HARDENING/LATER (OPTIONAL shows as LATER). Status is QUEUED/IN PROGRESS/COMPLETED (retired shows as COMPLETED with "Retired:" in its description; a planned task with an open PR is IN PROGRESS). Lane is the current gate. The catalogue gains `name` and `description`; child state gains `completed_at`, filled once from the issue close time or set by the controller. Native sub-issues follow the graph order.
- **Comment trace:** a generated `TRACE` block closes each catalogued body: `- <date> · <record> · [<summary>](#issuecomment-<id>)` with `SUPERSEDES=` and "superseded by", under the rule that the body comes first and the latest comment wins. When the body would overflow, the whole list moves into one new index comment (posted under an intent and read back) and the body keeps its link, repeating as comments grow. The audit also fails on unmarked superseded records; `--repair --ledger` adds topic tags.
- **Report-only findings:** `TRACE_STALE`, `TRACE_UNLINKED`, `TRACE_SUPERSEDED_UNMARKED`, and `PR_UNTRACKED` for an open PR that says `Refs #n` for a task whose state records no PR.
- **Triggers:** `.github/workflows/programme-reconcile.yml` runs on push to main, on issue and comment changes by the owner or a collaborator (never pull request comments), and by hand. It runs one at a time, waits 45 seconds after edits, scopes a task event to that task, and skips issues that aren't catalogued. It writes as the controller's operator using the `TOOLKIT_PROGRAMME_WRITER` variable and the `TOOLKIT_PROGRAMME_TOKEN` secret, and does nothing until both exist. Its own edits lead to a run that finds nothing to change, so it can't loop.
- **Read-back:** the store reads each write back at the PUT's `commit.sha`, takes the next sha from `content.sha`, and uses its own written version when a later branch read still shows the replaced one.

Lane PR into `batch/lanes` (#550). No version number (the batch takes one). Refs #421, #423.

## Waiting on the owner (nothing live until then)

- The scope summary: recording real task state, the first apply on #421 (53 planned changes, 0 holds in a read-only dry run), and the label cleanup.
- Creating the `TOOLKIT_PROGRAMME_TOKEN` secret and the `TOOLKIT_PROGRAMME_WRITER` variable.

## Safety

- The pass still never closes, deletes or merges. Its only new GitHub write is posting an index comment for an overflowing trace, under an intent, read back, and never posted twice.
- `replace_section` removes the named hand-kept section in the same body write that places the graph, as the owner decided for #421.
- The workflow has `contents: read`; all writes use the owner-created secret. Without it the workflow reads and writes nothing.
- No labels are set or removed.

## Validation

- Programme state, reconcile, authority and decision-trace audit tests: 68 passed, 0 failed (after merging the latest `batch/lanes`).
- `run-tests.cjs --changed --base origin/batch/lanes`: 35 files, 446 tests, 445 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped.
- New tests cover the seven columns and sort, completion times, the comment trace, overflow into one index comment and back, an interrupted index-comment move (no second post), lagging branch reads, and untracked PRs.
- `validate-toolkit`, `audit-published-surfaces --check` and the whitespace check pass.
- Read-only dry run against live #421: 53 planned changes (42 page bodies, 7 completion times, 4 sub-issue moves), 0 holds; `PR_UNTRACKED` for #423 (#552) and #538 (#541).

**Offline autosave**
- The game saved every 2 s whenever anything changed, which stopped play for about 0.1 s each time. That came to 97 hitches a minute at top speed in the alone run, and a big town takes about 0.4 s per save.

author: rubentxu
body:
## La mentira

El producto publicaba un trozo de la identidad de una cosa como si fuera su
nombre.

Para un símbolo pasaba por casualidad: el nombre está en el medio de la
identidad, y un `split(':').nth(1)` acierta. Para una declaración que un
lector de infraestructura nombra —un recurso de Terraform, un play de
Ansible— el trozo que sobrevivía era el **fichero** donde la cosa vive.

El producto llegaba a publicar esto:

```
"main.tf" es el símbolo del que más depende el proyecto (score: 0.649).
```

## Dónde caía

Seis sitios tocaban la identidad a mano, y cada uno contestaba una cosa
distinta:

| Sitio | Qué hacía | Qué contestaba |
|---|---|---|
| Rutas calientes publicadas (MCP) | `split(':').nth(1)` | el fichero, para una declaración |
| Preguntas sugeridas | `split(':').nth(1)` | el fichero, para una declaración |
| Vista de continuidad | segundo segmento desde la derecha | el fichero, para una declaración |
| Proyección genérica | descartaba el hecho | el fichero desaparecía del grafo |
| Proyección genérica | `(fichero vacío, la identidad entera, línea 1)` | posición inventada |
| Índice de nombres | `if let Some(...)` | la declaración no entraba, y con ella sus relaciones |

## Qué cambia

- El dominio declara la gramática de la identidad y la lee en **un solo
  sitio**: un símbolo, una declaración de Terraform y una declaración de
  Ansible. Una identidad que el producto escribe se lee y dice su nombre y su
  fichero; la que no encaja se dice que no encaja. No se inventa un fichero
  ni una línea.
- Los publicadores toman el nombre del símbolo que lo lleva, en vez de
  trocear su identidad.

**La identidad no cambia de bytes.** El recurso sigue siendo
`tf:main.tf:aws_s3_bucket.app_bucket`; lo que cambia es que ahora hay un sitio
donde se lee, y que quien la lee ya no responde con el fichero.

## La evidencia

Tres contratos nuevos, todos verdes:

- `the_identity_the_product_writes_is_the_one_it_reads.rs` — la propiedad:
  toda identidad que el producto escribe la entiende el lector. Las
  identidades **no están escritas a mano**: las producen los lectores del
  producto sobre un corpus, así que la propiedad no puede pasar sobre una
  forma que el producto dejó de escribir.
- `the_product_publishes_the_name_a_symbol_carries.rs` — lo que el producto
  publica.
- `the_fact_path_does_not_invent_the_place_of_a_declaration.rs` — el camino de
  hechos: una declaración conserva su nombre y su llamada resuelve.

**El discriminante se midió en las dos direcciones.** Revirtiendo el lector
—que se queda con la gramática del símbolo solo— los contratos de identidad
y de hechos se pusieron rojos, con el mensaje que dice qué falta:

```
the product writes the identity "tf:main.tf:aws_s3_bucket.app_bucket" and
the reader does not read it back
```

Revirtiendo los publicadores —vuelven a trocear la identidad— los contratos
de nombres publicados se pusieron rojos, y el producto vuelve a decir en voz
alta la mentira:

```
the published hot paths must name the thing, got ["main.tf"]
```

Con cada mutación revertida, los contratos volvieron a verde.

## Un número que no era cierto

La auditoría atribuía al producto «siete gramáticas de identidad». Medido: siete
sólo cuadra si además se cuentan los destinos de relación, que no son
identidades de nada. Las identidades que el grafo nombra son **cinco**: el
símbolo, la declaración de Terraform, la declaración de Ansible, el documento
y el issue. Las tres primeras las nombra el camino del producto; las dos
últimas, la capa multimodal.

## La medida

Producción: **+241 / -83** (neto +158, de los cuales 154 son el módulo nuevo
con sus pruebas; el resto del cambio de producción es +87/-83). Contratos:
**+348**. Corpus: **+19**.

author: lu-zero
body:
## What

CPU decode with attention sinks went through `sinks_attn_cpu`: transpose the whole KV cache, then two batched matmuls with a single query row. At 90 tokens of cache that is 2.9 ms for QK and 1.6 ms for AV per layer, against 0.13 ms for the softmax. The cost grows with the cache, so it decides whether a long context is usable on CPU at all.

The single-query kernel already streams K and V once and takes windows, causal masks, and softcap. The sink is one extra denominator term with no value, so it now joins the running max and sum. CPU decode (`q_len == 1`) dispatches there. Prefill stays on the tensor path. A non-finite sink is ignored, so a model with no sinks is bit-identical (`test_flash_attn_cpu_single_q_sinks_off_is_bit_identical`).

## Measured

Flint, 49 layers, one step, attention phase. Node 2, 16 threads, schedutil. `attn_proj` is the load proxy for the box.

| context | before | after | `attn_proj` before / after |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~45 tokens | 39-79 ms | 3.2 ms | 45-50 / 42 ms |
| ~90 tokens | 235 ms | 3.6 ms | 100 / 42 ms |
| ~200 tokens | not run | 4.5 ms | - / 42 ms |

The after numbers are at equal or longer context and still an order of magnitude below the shortest before number.

body:
Three local, credential-free providers so the clock, battery and system-monitor widgets can get real data.

- `system.time` {hm, hms, date, tz}, `system.temp` {celsius} and `battery.status` {percent, state, timeLeft}, with the field names and JSON types of the web catalog and the widgets' sample data. A real daemon in a throwaway dir returned real values on this machine.

FIFOs, `/dev/zero` symlinks, directories and oversized files return an error promptly instead of hanging a worker (tests with a 2 s timeout; removing each guard fails a test).
- `owd` refuses to start on a path-like `TZ` (exit 2, the value is never printed).
- Battery discovery finds any supply of type Battery; time zone tests cover Kathmandu, New York spring-forward and overlap, and a leap day.
- New dependency `jiff` 0.2.38, pinned exactly (DEP-TIME): local time zones without libc `localtime_r`. `cargo audit` and `cargo deny` are clean.

An independent review found the unbounded-read problem and the `TZ` stall; both are fixed here.

**Not verified:** battery states other than Full on a real machine (fixtures only); the 1.88 minimum Rust version on an actual 1.88 toolchain.

author: ryansawyer6003
body:
## Why

Queues on AppSocket, LPD, `http://` or Raw don't describe the printer, so Windows shows every printer as color with no two-sided option. Discovery (the `snmp` backend) offered every printer as `socket://`, because with no `DeviceURI` rule it only probes 9100 and 515. Tested on the reference server: with an IPP-only `DeviceURI` rule, discovery offers `ipp://<address>/ipp/print`.

## Changes

- **Dockerfile:** keep only the `ipp`, `ipps` and `snmp` backends. `cupsd` checks for `<ServerBin>/backend/<scheme>` when a queue is added or changed and refuses it with "Bad device-uri scheme" if the backend is missing. So non-IPP queues can't be created from the web interface or `lpadmin`, and the web interface doesn't offer them. The build fails if any other backend is left, so a package update can't quietly add one back.
- **`snmp.conf.template`** (new), rendered at every start like `cupsd.conf`:
  - `DeviceURI "." ipp://%s/ipp/print`: discovery offers only the IPP address, because a `DeviceURI` match replaces the 9100/515 probes.
  - `Address @IF(<printer interface>)`: discovery broadcasts only on the interface that holds `PRINTER_IP`, instead of the stock `@LOCAL`, which also broadcast SNMP on the client-facing network. It falls back to `@LOCAL` with a warning.
- **entrypoint:** at every start, warns about any existing queue on a scheme the image no longer supports, since it can't print.
- **Smoke test:** checks that exactly `ipp ipps snmp` are installed, that `socket://` is refused and `ipp://` accepted, and that `snmp.conf` has the IPP-only rule and an `@IF(...)` address (CI now passes `PRINTER_IP`).
- **Docs:**
  - IPP only, so the 9100/driver fallback is removed.
  - Discovery is still not recommended: the address is hidden until an entry is selected, and trixie has the Add Printer bug.
  - README Known limitations adds the Add Printer use-after-free (CUPS 2.4.10, fixed upstream in 2.4.12) and corrects the model-name note to cover Debian 12 and 13.

## Not tested here

No Docker daemon was available where this was written, so CI's image build and smoke test are the first real run. Tested locally:
- the backend cleanup loop under `dash`, against a copy of the reference server's backend directory;
- the `printers.conf` scan and the interface lookup, against sample input;
- the `snmp.conf` render;
- `shellcheck -S warning`.

## Heads-up: release base image

The Dockerfile is `FROM debian:trixie-slim`, so the next `vX.Y.Z` release cut from `main` publishes **prod on trixie**. Keeping prod on bookworm while `dev` stays on trixie needs a channel-specific base, for example a build argument the publish workflow sets per channel. That isn't in this PR.

Opening a changed-test-scope task on the node canvas grew its frame and moved the rest of the canvas over 420ms at the old zoom. The camera then waited for the move to end (about 540ms) and jumped to the new zoom in a single frame. Every open and close was two motions with a snap at the end.

author: cebertowicz
body:
Owner thread: Turn & Delivery
Owner thread ID: af204877

## Problem

When the backend restarts while a delegated worker's Turn is running (an app update, for example), boot recovery ends that Turn with `backend restarted while Turn was running`, but the worker's owner is never told. Recovery calls `finish_turn` directly, so it skips the canonical turn-end hook that every live terminal runs: `record_turn_end_logged` -> `on_thread_turn_complete`, which sends the owner's `child_turn_errored` wake (`notify_turn_error`), updates the worker's plan liveness, and drives the woken threads.

## Change

- `recover_threads` also returns `ended_turns`, the `(thread_id, turn_id)` of each Turn whose `finish_turn` settlement was applied (new `StartupRecovery.ended_turns`, default empty).
- The restart error string is one constant (`RESTART_TURN_ERROR`) shared by recovery and the drive phase.
- `drive_startup_continuity` records each ended Turn through `record_turn_end_logged(outcome="error", error=RESTART_TURN_ERROR, turn_id=...)`, then drives that thread's settlement, as one recovered item, so a failing item still cannot cancel its siblings.
- No matching or classification logic is added: the hook reads the same delegation links it already reads for live terminals.

## Ordering

The hook runs before the thread's `drive_terminal_settlement`, as the live error path (`step_handler._handle_error`) records the turn end before its terminal is driven. The hook reads only committed database state, which `finish_turn` already wrote in the recovery transaction (including any successor claim), so driving first would add nothing and would make the owner's wake wait on a successor Turn's admission.

## Tests

- New `test_restart_recovery_owner_wake.py` runs `reconcile_startup_continuity` and `drive_startup_continuity` on a real database:
  - a restart-ended delegated worker's parent gets the `child_turn_errored` wake and is driven, and a later pass records nothing again;
  - an undelegated recovered Turn updates its liveness and creates no parent wake;
  - a Turn from the current boot epoch is untouched and records nothing.
- Existing tests that hand `drive_startup_continuity` a stand-in recovery object now carry `ended_turns=()`.

Fixes #1377

author: scratchsmith-ci[bot]
body:
Merging this PR tags and publishes **v1.8.0**.

Generated by knope from the `.changeset/*.md` fragments; don't hand-edit.

---

## Features

### `unpack` reports the setuid and setgid bits it clears ([#353](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/353))

For each path in the final image that had a setuid or setgid bit, `unpack` prints a warning line on standard error. The new `stripped_setid` field of `--format json` lists the same paths.

## Fixes

### `index` warns when the registry names another digest ([#369](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/369))

When the registry's answer names a digest other than the index just pushed, `index --sign` refuses to sign, but `index` without `--sign` said nothing. It now reports a warning, as `pack --push` does: a `warning:` line in the text output, and a new `warnings` array in `--format json`. The push and the exit code are unchanged.

### `install.sh` says why a download failed ([#365](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/365))

With wget, `install.sh` hid the reason a download failed, so a missing release, a proxy and a dead network looked the same. It now prints wget's last error lines when a fetch fails, and stays quiet when it works. The cosign signature bundle download no longer hides its error with either tool, so a refusal over a missing bundle shows why the fetch failed.

### `unpack` reads an OCI archive whose entries start with `./` ([#356](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/356))

`tar -cf img.tar .` inside an OCI layout directory stores `./index.json` and `./blobs/sha256/…`. `unpack` failed on such an archive with "archive has no index.json". It now reads those entries as the same files.

## Security

### `unpack` and `diff` bound the memory they use on a hostile archive ([#344](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/344))

`unpack` read each entry of the outer OCI archive into memory. A small GNU sparse entry could expand to gigabytes of zeros and go around the decompression limit. Scratchsmith now skips entries it does not use, refuses a sparse entry that it must read, and reads no more than the archive's own size. `diff` now hashes files as a stream instead of loading each whole file.

### `graph`, `pack`, `index` and `diff` escape the rest of their untrusted text ([#359](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/359))

Some output still printed text from a binary, an image or a registry without escaping it: the names, paths and interpreter in `graph` text output, the loader line and the size table in the `pack` text report, the duplicate-platform and multi-arch errors from `index`, and file-walk errors from `diff`. A line break or a terminal escape sequence in that text could forge output lines. Scratchsmith now escapes it. JSON output and exit codes do not change.

### `diff`, `index` and the musl check escape control characters ([#340](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/340))

A file name in an image, a platform string from a registry, or a string in a musl binary can hold a newline or a terminal escape sequence. `diff` and `index` text output and the musl error printed that text raw, so it could forge report lines or drive the terminal. Scratchsmith now escapes those characters. JSON output and exit codes do not change.

### `unpack` escapes archive text in its error messages ([#345](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/345))

`unpack` put text from the archive into its error messages raw: media types, digests, blob names, entry paths and the tar error. A hostile archive could then forge lines or send terminal escape sequences to standard error. Scratchsmith now escapes that text and caps each string at 8 KiB. Exit codes do not change.

### `install.sh` stops when cosign is installed and the signature bundle is missing ([#348](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/348))

With cosign installed, `install.sh` warned and installed anyway when it could not fetch `checksums.txt.sigstore.json`. An attacker who swaps the tarball and the checksums can also withhold the bundle. The script now stops the install in that case. Set `INSECURE_ALLOW_MISSING_SIGNATURE=1` to install with the SHA-256 check only.

### `pack` and `graph` stop reading a device after 256 MiB ([#339](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/339))

A `DT_NEEDED` entry can name a device such as `/dev/zero`, and the resolver read it until the host ran out of memory. Scratchsmith now stops after 256 MiB of a character or block device and exits `1` with an error that names the file.

### `pack` and `graph` refuse a library or a loader that cannot load ([#360](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/360))

A `DT_NEEDED` entry or a program interpreter (`PT_INTERP`) can name any host file that is an ELF, such as a core dump, and scratchsmith copied that file into the image. Scratchsmith now refuses a library that is not a shared object (`ET_DYN`), and an interpreter that is not `ET_DYN` or `ET_EXEC`, and exits `1`. A PIE executable is `ET_DYN`, so this check does not refuse one.

### `pack` and `graph` no longer hang on a FIFO ([#361](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/361))

A `DT_NEEDED` entry can name a FIFO, and the read of it waited forever for a writer, or read a writer's endless stream. Scratchsmith now refuses a library that is not a regular file before it opens it, and exits `1`. A FIFO that you name with `--include` no longer hangs `graph` after its read, stops at 256 MiB like a device, and `pack` refuses it at once, because it cannot be staged.

### `pack` and `graph` refuse a non-ELF file named by the binary ([#338](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/338))

A `DT_NEEDED` entry or a program interpreter (`PT_INTERP`) can name any host file, such as `~/.docker/config.json`, and scratchsmith copied that file into the image. Scratchsmith now refuses a library that is not an ELF, and an interpreter that is not a regular ELF file, and exits `1`. A data file that you name with `--include` stages as before.

### `--sign` signs the manifest digest that scratchsmith pushed ([#346](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/346))

`pack --push --sign` and `index --sign` signed the digest that the registry named in its `Location` header. A hostile or broken registry could name a different image, and scratchsmith then signed and attested that image. Scratchsmith now hashes the exact manifest bytes it uploads, signs that digest, and exits `1` when the registry names a different one. A push without `--sign` behaves as before.

### `pack` keeps soname symlinks inside the image root ([#342](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/342))

A `DT_NEEDED` name such as `../../../tmp/libx.so` comes from the packed binary, and scratchsmith created its soname symlink at that path joined under the staging directory. The link could land outside that directory. Scratchsmith now walks the name inside the image, where `..` at the root stays at the root. A link already in a reused `--output` directory is read the same way, so an absolute link value names a path in the image, not on the host.

### `pack --no-build` keeps every write inside a reused output directory ([#352](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/352))

A reused `--output` directory can hold a link with an absolute target, such as `lib -> /usr/lib`. Scratchsmith joined each staged path under the directory and let the host follow that link, so a library copy, a `--strip`, or a generated file such as `/etc/passwd` could land on the host's own files. Scratchsmith now reads every link in the directory the way the image will, so each write stays inside the directory.

### `pack` keeps the staged loader inside the image root ([#341](https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/pull/341))

The program interpreter path comes from the packed binary, and scratchsmith joined it under the staging directory as text. A path such as `/../../tmp/x` put the loader copy outsid

author: abe-borg
body:
## Problem

[Abe-Borg/spec-surgeon#95](https://github.com/Abe-Borg/spec-surgeon/pull/95) made the to-do list the place documents wait. Documents get there by the red X on a preview, the user asking the assistant (`set_aside`), the plan refusing them, their copy not being made, and what recovery has not fixed.

That PR merged with the engine only. The window showed neither why each document waits nor a Put back button. The help, the docs and the trust surfaces described none of it, and CLAUDE.md treats those surfaces as a contract that changes in the same change.

## Resulting behaviour

- **The window**
  - Both to-do cards, in the chat and under the copies, show each document's reason.
  - The card under the copies has **Put back** beside each document (`POST /api/put-back`).
  - That card stays in view during a pass. Its subtitle says a document put back joins the others when the pass ends.
  - In Safe mode the chat card keeps master's "Go to Default mode" button, with the reasons shown too.
- **Help.** "When a file is left untouched" now says where documents go and how they come back: set aside for later, refused at plan time, failed at delivery, Set the rest aside, and Put back.
- **Trust surfaces**
  - The request card says Claude can set documents aside at your word, and nothing in them changes. It also says each request carries the names on the list and why each waits.
  - The preview, outcome-plan and Create cards say refused and failed files go on the list, and that a refused Create moves nothing.
  - The Start over / New conversation card now also covers the to-do list: Work on them, Put back, and Set the rest aside.
  - The dossier's "what the AI may touch" table lists set aside.
  - Ledger: A26 (Put back), A27 (Set the rest aside), B18 (the automatic moves to the list) and claims T54–T55. Also updated: the chat's tool list, what a request carries, and what the saved conversation keeps.
- **Docs**
  - `README.md` gets a to-do list paragraph.
  - `docs/CONVERSATIONAL_DESKTOP.md` covers the ways onto the list, Put back and recovery.
  - `docs/WEB_API.md` covers `todo[].why` / `reason`, the put-back route and the chip.
  - `CLAUDE.md`, plus S5's item and status row in the plan.
- **Mock server and flows:** reasons on the cards, and Put back.

## Merge with master

Master brought in Safe mode, the numbering engine and later-step refusals. Conflicts were resolved by keeping both sides:

- **IDs.** Master took A23–A25 and T52–T53 for Safe mode, so this PR's entries are now A26, A27, T54 and T55.
- **Card count.** Master's Safe-mode card took the dossier to 25 cards, above the test's limit of 24. The to-do list therefore joins the Start over / New conversation card again (they were one card before this PR). That card now also names a Safe-mode button among the ways onto the list.
- **Built page.** `web/static` was rebuilt from the merged sources.

## Validation

- **Frontend unit tests:** 132 pass. The to-do chat item carries reasons, and an older view's entries still normalize.
- **Browser flows:** `tools/flows.mjs` in Chromium against the rebuilt page, 106 pass. They cover:
  - the reason on both cards;
  - a Put back per document;
  - Put back emptying the list;
  - master's Safe-mode flow.
- **Put-back route:** `tests/test_set_aside_bin.py` covers it; a path that isn't on the list is refused with 400.
- **Trust facts:** `tests/test_trust_facts.py` passes, and the copy types no number of its own.
- **Full Python suite:** 5,333 passed, 4 skipped.

Release acceptance (leave unchecked until evidence exists):

- [ ] Replay both saved 2026-10-18 recipes against the private 12-spec corpus; attach output counts and verification results.
- [ ] Run the installed Windows candidate with Word; verify 12 delivered files, readable preview/records and no crash log.
- [ ] Run one live request in the installed release candidate's window; attach its run folder's `DIAGNOSTICS.md` and `logs/` (no documents) to the release and record the candidate commit, model, elapsed time and cost.

- `/admin/users/<id>`: profile, role, ban state, maintained addons, submissions and their moderation log. Ban, unban and set-role now record events through a Better Auth after-hook.
- List rows link to the pages. The dashboard's "Manage in admin" opens the addon page.

## Scope
- Rejected first listings have no addon row, so their history shows on the author's user page.
- This PR also removes comments that only restated the code across the stack so far, and shares the search length limits as constants.

## Blast Radius
Adds an after-hook on three Better Auth admin endpoints. It logs and continues on failure, so a ban never fails because of the record.

## Verification
- `tests/admin-views.test.ts`: a changes-requested then approved listing shows two decisions; ban, unban and set-role over HTTP record events with the actor.
- Driven live with `verify-web` as moderator and admin: delist, relist, request changes, ban and transfer all show in the log.

body:
## What this adds

- Real Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at `/mcp` with bearer-key authentication, per-key scopes and CORS support for external MCP clients.
- MCP tools to discover the workflow, diagnose saved scenes, queue browser script runs (preview by default), request real viewport renders and retrieve job results including screenshot images.
- An authenticated, persisted execution queue. AI code is not executed on the server: the signed-in Studio browser tab runs it via the existing Forge sandbox, returns logs/errors/validation and captures its actual WebGL canvas.
- Preview vs apply flow: applying requires `scene:execute` + `scene:write`, a matching project revision and server-side scene validation.
- MCP key management routes, new `scene:execute` scope, endpoint UI, job migration and tests.

## Important operational requirement

For `run_script` and `render_project`, the matching saved project must be open in Studio in a signed-in browser tab. The MCP AI client orchestrates the job and polls for its result. Forge does not require or store a provider API key.

## Verification

Awaiting branch CI: build, typecheck, MCP/job regression tests and lint.

author: y-shimomura-gop
body:
## 目的

全面作り直しスタックの PR06。ベースは `chore/2026-10-23/golden-align-jobs`。

塗布系のジョブと装置 route が実機へ送る G-code の列を golden に固定する。ジョブは実 JobManager と実アプリで走らせ、終了時の駐機まで記録する。

## 変更

- f6dbb25 `fix(api)`: `POST /emergency-stop` の route は `Klipper.emergency_stop` を unbound で渡していた
  - そのため FakeKlipper の実装（M112 の記録）が使われず、基底の Moonraker 実装が呼ばれていた
  - 接続のメソッドを呼ぶ lambda に替えた
  - `firmware_restart` は基底でも `self.send_gcode` を動的ディスパッチで呼ぶので、元のまま残した
- 27af5aa SceneCamera: 同じ XY で引き戻してから押し出すと、差し引き 0 になって塗布痕が写らなかった
  - 送った順に足し、引き戻しはその XY に出ている量までしか減らさないようにした
- c09db84 golden 本体
  - `test_paste_jobs.py`
    - paste_solder を led_blinker で 5 分岐 × 回転 0 / 5° 採る。分岐は「初回パージが写る」「写らずクリーニングして成功」「やり直しても失敗」「運転時補正あり」「ノズル未教示でこすらずにやり直す」
    - 詰まりは CloggedKlipper で作る
    - height_plane、toolhead_offset（測った値が設定と 1 画素以内）、loading（押出・吸引・回転と引き戻し・jog・指定 X）も採る
  - `test_routes.py`: マシン操作の REST（全 7 action）、ノズルキャップとクリーニング位置の記録、クリーニングのテスト、緊急停止、ファームウェア再起動（UpdateSandbox の中だけ）、ジョブ終了時の駐機
  - `scenarios.py` に塗布系のシナリオを足した
  - `conftest.py`: `test_align_jobs.py` から共通部分を寄せ、`mount_klipper` を分けた。通知音を記録する `audio_player` fixture を足した
  - `machine.toml`: `[paste_dispenser.pad_align]` を他の paste_dispenser の表の隣へ移した
- ノズル未教示の分岐は、`[paste_dispenser.nozzle_clean]` を座標なし・動作値（`passes = 3`）だけの節に置き換えて作る
  - 設定ページから動作値だけ保存したときの、現場で起きる未教示の形（blueprint D7）を再現している。PR11 で座標の無い節の扱いが壊れたら検出できる
- ローディングの入力待ちは、`progress_stage == LOADING_STAGE`（src の定数を import）と、FakeAudioPlayer に入力待ち音 `"prompt"` が記録されたことの両方で待つ。ログ文言は複写しない

## 振る舞いの保存

- 既存の golden（`procedures/`、PR05 の `jobs/`）は書き換えずに全部通った
- `tests/golden` を更新なしで 2 回続けて流し、2 回とも同じ結果。新しい golden も決定的に再現した
- `make test-no-hardware` は全体で 3629 passed
- src の変更 2 点の影響
  - `system.py`: 本番の Klipper では同じメソッドが呼ばれる。既存の `tests/web/api/routers/test_system.py` も通る
  - `fake.py`: 影響はテストと api-fake 用の fake だけ。押し出してから戻す通常の塗布の描き方は変わらない（既存の SceneCamera テストも通る）
- golden は現状の送信列をそのまま記録した。loading の jog Z が絶対値の `G1 Z10.0` になる、といった現状の挙動もそのまま固定してある

## 仕様からの逸脱

仕様は「src は変えない」だが、次の 2 点で src を変えた。どちらも本番の動きは変わらない。

1. `src/web/api/routers/system.py`（`fix(api)`）
   - route が `Klipper.emergency_stop` をクラスから取り出して渡していたため、FakeKlipper の上書きが効かず、基底の Moonraker 実装が `AttributeError`（`_client` が無い）で落ちる
   - これでは緊急停止の golden を採れないので `lambda klipper: klipper.emergency_stop()` に替えた
   - src の Klipper の派生は FakeKlipper だけで、本番で送るものは同じ
2. `src/pcbasm/hal/fake.py` の SceneCamera
   - XY ごとに MOVE を単純に足していたため、toolhead_offset の最後の点が写らず、計測点不足で失敗していた
   - 送った順に `max(0, 累計 + MOVE)` で足すよう直した。`tests/pcbasm/hal/test_fake.py` に仕様テストを 1 本足した（旧実装では落ちる）
   - PR05 の golden は押し出しを含まないので変わらない

仕様の読み替え:

- 運転時補正の「なし」は purge_shows の分岐で兼ねた
- ノズルキャップ / クリーニング位置の記録は何も送らない。空の golden ファイルは作らず、`sent == ()` と machine.toml に書いた値を assert で確かめる
- toolhead_offset は、led_blinker だと銅箔の形を円と取り違えるので、未塗布の銅板（実運用と同じ）で採った
  - 測った toolhead は設定値から約半画素（約 0.017 mm）ずれる。許容は 1 画素にした
- `tests/golden/machine.toml` の表の並びを変えた
  - `[paste_dispenser.pad_align]` が `[probe]` の後ろにあると、`ConfigStore.write_machine_settings` で paste_dispenser.* を書くときに `assert isinstance(child, Table)` で落ちる（tomlkit が OutOfOrderTableProxy を返す）
  - 001 の live の並びにそろえて避けた

## 申し送り（この PR では直していない）

- **write_machine_settings の AssertionError**: paste_dispenser の表が離れて並ぶ machine.toml だと、設定ページやジョブからの書き込みが落ちる
  - リポジトリのテンプレート 2 つ、`data/testing`、001 の live は表が続けて並んでいるので、今は起きない
  - 002 の live machine.toml の並びは未確認。PR17 の前に確認したい
- **toolhead_offset の約半画素の偏り**: 原因が SceneCamera の画素中心の取り方か、円検出（src）か未切り分け。検出側が原因なら実機の toolhead 測定にも同じ偏りが乗る
- **緊急停止の golden**: `M112` と `timeout=10.0` は FakeKlipper での記録の形にすぎない。本番は Moonraker の HTTP `/printer/emergency_stop` に送る
- nit: `test_paste_jobs.py` の `run` fixture の型（`Callable[..., None]`）が緩い。`clogged: float` は inf を渡すための型で、回数としては読みにくい

## 実機で確認すべき点

テストと fake の追加が中心で、実機確認は基本的に不要。ただし `system.py` の変更は本番の route に入るので、merge 前に 001 で 1 回ずつ確かめてほしい。

- [ ] 緊急停止ボタン（`POST /api/emergency-stop`）で Klipper が緊急停止し、実行中のジョブが aborted になる
- [ ] ファームウェア再起動（`POST /api/firmware-restart`）で Klipper が再起動し、続いて pcbasm-api / pcbasm-ui が再起動する

## 検証

- `make format`: すべて Passed（変更は git add してから実行）
- `make type`: pyright 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `uv run pytest tests/golden -m "not hardware"`: 84 passed
- `make test-no-hardware`: 3629 passed, 189 deselected
- `make test-e2e`: テンプレートと JS を変えていないので未実行

author: psalajova
body:
Dex issues `gsm-cli` ID tokens valid for 24 hours, so the Rover group memberships the proxy authorizes with could be up to a day old. The proxy now accepts a token only within one hour of its issuance time (`iat`), allows one minute of clock skew because Dex and the proxy run on different clusters, and rejects tokens without `iat`.

This matches the secret-manager CLI in openshift/ci-tools-standalone#55, which re-logs in when a cached token is 57 minutes old, so normal CLI use never hits the limit.

After the image is promoted, the running proxy pods pick it up only on restart (`oc -n ci rollout restart deployment/gsm-proxy` on core-ci); the Deployment has no image trigger.

Tested: `go test -race ./pkg/gsm-proxy ./cmd/gsm-proxy`; the new table cases fail if either the age limit or the clock-skew allowance is removed.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

`gsm-proxy` now rejects Dex ID tokens without an `iat` claim, issued at least one hour ago, or issued more than one minute in the future. The proxy still checks the token signature, issuer, audience, expiration, and identity claims. This limits how long the proxy trusts group membership in a signed token, even if the token has not expired.

The production guidance warns operators that re-login does not guarantee fresh upstream group membership. It recommends verifying upstream freshness behavior and an emergency revocation mechanism before relying on the token-age limit for membership revocation.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: cruzdanilo
body:
adds a 9th web leg, `e2e (eth, brave, 500x994)`, on brave's built-in wallet, with no shim and a new wallet every run. it covers the no-`wallet_sendCalls` fallback (sponsored user op signed with `personal_sign`), the eip-6963 brave connector and the browser wallet sign-up sheet. metamask also creates a new wallet now, so no web leg uses the deterministic seed.

## commits

- **follow browser ui popups on web**: `windows.patch` turns on chromedriver's `windowTypes: ["browser_ui"]` and follows a browser ui target while its document is visible. brave's approval panel is such a target, and brave keeps it after approval with its document hidden, which now counts as closed. hidden browser ui (chrome's omnibox popups) is never followed. no brave-specific code, fit for upstream.
- **create a new metamask wallet**: create instead of import, so `EXPO_PUBLIC_E2E_MNEMONIC` leaves the web e2e job.
- **move the eth send to its own leg**: portfolio's eth mint and send move to `subflows/eth.yaml` (moved, not copied; `local.yaml` chains it before portfolio, so native runs the same steps). portfolio now opens the send screen first from the asset screen, so it takes the advanced intro's "Turn it on", which no leg covered, instead of repeating "Not now".
- **sign up with brave's wallet**: `subflows/brave.yaml` creates the wallet in `chrome://wallet`; `signIn.yaml` signs up through "Sign up with browser wallet" and the panel; `sign.yaml` approves; `send.yaml` gets the sign hook.
- **run the eth web e2e on brave**: brave 1.98.60 from its release zip, headed under `xvfb-run` (headless brave rejects every wallet request with 4001). chrome rows stay headless. codecov waits for 12 uploads.

body:
## What and why

This is the screen for the rest of Octavia's I3 (Intake Forms, review of Oct 20, items 17 and 20). After Publish, the form gives "a shareable URL usable behind a website button and website embed code, each with Copy". It follows Rasel's decision of Oct 22: only a service's main form has a link, and the link is its Begin Online page. **Stacked on #1039** (API), which is stacked on #1038 (contract). Their diffs show here until they merge.

**Form Link** (`intake-forms/_components/form-link-dialog.tsx`): a dialog titled with the form's name, holding R56's shared `PublicLinkSection` (#1020). It shows the link and the embed code, each with Copy. A notice appears when the link takes no submissions (draft, inactive, archived or hidden). It opens from three places:
- **After Publish** in the builder, when the form is a main form.
- **The builder's More menu** ("Form Link"), to open it again.
- **The main form's card menu** in Form Templates. Other forms have no Form Link item.

What the dialog says in each case:
- **A form that is not a main form:** if the API answers 404, the dialog says "Only each service's main form has a public link: its Begin Online page. Send this form to a client instead."
- **API unreachable:** the frame keeps its place, with the reason and Try Again.

**Two builder fixes Publish needed.** Without them, the dialog after Publish could not open on LVP's real forms:
1. **Editing a published form now stays on that form.** The builder used to save it as a separate copy, and the API makes a copy with `service_default` off when the service already has a default. So the result was never the main form, and the library filled with copies.
   - The API already saves the changes as the form's next draft version (R37; `intake-workspace-actions.e2e.test.ts:702`). The builder now uses that.
   - The published version stays live, sent forms keep theirs, and the main form keeps its link.
   - An archived form still saves to a copy.
   - The status line already promised this ("Published as a new version. Forms already sent keep the earlier one.").
   - The title stays "Edit Form Template" over a new draft version.
2. **Publish takes a saved form's grids, repeating groups and State lists as they are.** #1031's check mirrored the API, but the builder shows a grid or group as a section break and a State list as a dropdown with no choices. So the check refused every built-in form, three sections at a time on LVP's Annual Tax.
   - The draft now marks those loaded fields `stored`. Breaks and dropdowns added in the builder are still checked.
   - The API keeps those fields by key (`form-builder.ts`).
   - On the real local API, LVP's Annual Tax intake published as version 2, and its Begin Online page serves its 72 fields with the 4 grids, 2 groups and 2 State lists.

**The mock** (`mocks/intake-forms.ts`) now does the same:
- Saving a published form makes its next draft version, and the list still shows it Published.
- Each service's first template is its main form.
- Business Development is off Begin Online, so the mock can show a HIDDEN link.

**What the embed code needs to work on a firm's website** (from #1038, in `docs/work/R60-intake.md`, Needs):
- **R1:** frame headers. The portal sends `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`.
- **R15 or Rasel:** the draft cookie is `SameSite=Strict`.
- **R17:** no page reads `?embed=1`.

The link works today.

## Screenshots

Real local API, LVP's Owner, 1440 px, with one at 375 px. No mockup has this element; the sheets say so in the design cell.

![I3 Form Link after Publish: result, API unreachable, 375 px](https://github.com/RaselMridha792/firmivra/blob/f9e3c30f49ec8df7b91024f5cb2d4167df77b468/apps/web/e2e/screenshots/r60-intake-link/r60-form-link-builder.jpg?raw=true)

![I3 Form Link on the main form's card, and none on another form](https://github.com/RaselMridha792/firmivra/blob/f9e3c30f49ec8df7b91024f5cb2d4167df77b468/apps/web/e2e/screenshots/r60-intake-link/r60-form-link-card.jpg?raw=true)

## Design match

- [x] Every part of the design was cropped and enlarged, and its elements listed and counted (rule 1). There is no mockup for this element: Octavia's items 17 and 20 list it as a URL and an embed code, each with Copy. Both are built.
- [x] Every element is built; no widget was dropped (rule 2)
- [x] Where there is no data, the widget shows its frame with a quiet empty state (rule 2): loading, not a main form, and API unreachable each keep the block's frame
- [x] The page was checked in three states (with data, empty, API unreachable) and every widget's frame shows in each (rule 2)
- [x] Icons are solid Phosphor icons (rule 3): `LinkSimple` (fill) on the menu items, the rest from R56's block
- [x] Colours and sizes come from `packages/ui` tokens (rule 4): the kit's `Modal` and R56's block, with no new styles
- [x] The page was rendered at 1440 px and compared region by region (rule 5)
- [x] The screenshots sit next to the design (rule 6): above
- [x] Components come from `docs/ui-kit.md` (`Modal`, `Button`, `PublicLinkBlock` through `PublicLinkSection`)

**Differences:** the dialog has no mockup. Its title is the form's name, so the block's own "Form Link" heading is not repeated.

## How to test

```bash
pnpm --filter @firmivra/web exec vitest run "src/app/firm/(workspace)/intake-forms/builder/_components/builder-draft.test.ts"   # 3 of 3
cd apps/web && pnpm exec playwright test -c playwright.mock.config.ts r60-intake-link tumit-intake-builder tumit-intake-templates   # 14 of 14
```

By hand (local, LVP's Owner):
1. Open Intake Forms > Form Templates and choose Form Link in the Annual Tax intake card's menu. The link and embed code show, and Copy works.
2. Open the form in the builder and click Publish Form. The status says "Published as a new version", the address keeps the same id, and Form Link opens.

- [x] Tests added or updated:
  - `r60-intake-link.spec.ts`: Publish, Copy, the More menu, the card menu, HIDDEN and not a main form.
  - `tumit-intake-builder.spec.ts`: a published form's draft stays on the form.

- [x] Tenant-scoped: web only. The API (#1039) reads in the firm's scope.
- [x] Audit log entry for any action on client data: unchanged. The API audits saves and publishes; reading a link changes nothing.
- [x] No changes to `packages/db/prisma`, `infra/` or `.github/workflows/`
- [x] No secrets and no real client data
- [x] Checks run locally, after merging `main`: web `tsc` 0 errors; ESLint and Prettier on the changed files; the specs above. The other intake mock specs pass, except `r17-intake.spec.ts:8`: the portal's intake page expects 6 cards and gets 7. This branch changes neither that page nor its mock (noted in `R60-intake.md`).
- [x] One ticket or one page in this PR (I3)

author: petterannerwall
body:
Closes IRM-58

## Summary

Ponytail now runs at full strength in every session, routines and cloud sessions included. Impeccable comes in full: the skill, its four agents and its design detector. This is your decision of 2026-10-23. Cloud sessions only get what the repository ships, so everything is vendored and pinned like the other skills.

```text
.claude/
├── skills/ponytail, ponytail-audit, ponytail-debt, ponytail-help, ponytail-gain   # DietrichGebert/ponytail@09c434a (5.3.2)
├── hooks/
│   ├── ponytail-*                  # ponytail's hook scripts and statusline, pinned
│   ├── package.json                # {"type":"commonjs"}: the root package.json is ESM, ponytail uses require
│   ├── impeccable-scope.sh         # DESIGN.md and the craft floor set design completeness; ponytail governs code structure
│   └── impeccable-engine.sh        # runs impeccable's engine only at pinned checksums
├── agents/impeccable-*.md          # pbakaus/impeccable@5cb95ee, upstream's own .claude/agents
├── settings.json                   # the hooks below
└── skills.lock.json                # pins all of the above, plus impeccable's engine sha256 per platform
```

| Event | Hook |
|---|---|
| SessionStart | ponytail's rules; impeccable's detector, which also installs the pinned engine and exports `IMPECCABLE_BIN` |
| UserPromptSubmit | ponytail's level tracking; the impeccable scope for a typed `/impeccable` |
| SubagentStart | ponytail's rules for every subagent except impeccable's (`^(?!impeccable-)`) |
| PostToolUse | impeccable's detector after Edit, Write and MultiEdit; the impeccable scope when the Skill tool runs impeccable |
| Stop | impeccable's detector deep pass |

**Supporting changes:**
- `skills.sh` can pin a file pattern in a folder, not only a skill folder. It also fails when impeccable's `VERSION` and the pinned engine's version differ.
- `docs/guardrails.md` 2.5 and section 3 record the decision. That reverses "no skill installs hooks", and the record includes the costs the old repository's audit found.

## Evidence

- **Hook tests:** `.claude/hooks/test.sh` checks that:
  - a session starts with ponytail's rules, and a subagent gets them;
  - an impeccable agent doesn't get them;
  - an impeccable task and a typed `/impeccable` get the scope, and another skill doesn't;
  - an engine off its pin is refused and not installed, and the agent's calls then get a failing engine.
- **Pin check:** changing `.claude/hooks/ponytail-map.js` made `skills.sh check` fail on `ponytail-hooks`. The skeptic lens also saw it fail on an added, deleted, edited or symlinked pinned file.
- **Real engine:** a real run installed the darwin-arm64 engine at its pin, and `engine-probe` answered `impeccable-engine 0.1.16`. That held with a cache path containing a space too.
- **Checks:** `make check` passes.

**Skeptic pass, two rounds:**
- **Round one, P0 (security):** impeccable's launcher downloads its engine from upstream release `engine-v0.1.16`, which is not immutable, and checks it only against that release's own sidecar. The engine would then run in every routine, with the session's tokens. Fixed: `impeccable-engine.sh` pins the engine's sha256 per platform, and the launcher may never download one itself.
- **Round one, P2 and P3:** the statusline scripts were missing from the pin, and the detector skipped MultiEdit. Both are fixed.
- **Round two, P2 and P3:** after a failed download, the agent's calls could fall back to unchecked caches, and the export wasn't quoted. Both are fixed.
- **Left for you:** the impeccable plugin synced from claude.ai still runs its own unpinned launcher in hooks on your machine. Removing the plugin copies, as you planned, clears it.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** sessions

Every session in the repository runs these hooks once this merges, routines included. A broken hook shows up as a hook error at session start, and reverting the PR removes it.

## First principles

1. **Why did the problem happen?** The plan copied skills but no hooks. That kept ponytail and impeccable's detector out of cloud sessions and routines, which only get what the repository ships.
2. **What could be removed or simplified instead?** Nothing here is new code apart from two short hooks: the scope message, and the pinned-engine wrapper the security finding called for. Everything else is upstream's, pinned.
3. **What alternative was considered, and why was it rejected?** Vendoring impeccable's engine binaries. That's about 75 MB for four platforms in git history. Pinning their checksums gives the same guarantee.

## Not live yet

- **To confirm in the first cloud session after merge:** that `node` is on the path for ponytail's hooks, and that the engine downloads from GitHub.
- **Remove the duplicate ponytail and impeccable plugins** from Claude, so each hook runs once.

author: maxeliseyev
body:
Third step of device cross-signing (TODO 76). The core is merged (construct-core #70, 0.58.0). The protos are in construct-protos #26, and this PR vendors them.

## What
- **Migration 074:** `devices.device_certificate`, which is NULL or exactly 5382 bytes.
- **`DeviceService.PublishDeviceCertificate`:** the calling device vouches for another active device of its own account.
  - The ownership check is inside the `UPDATE`, so it cannot be raced.
  - The certificate must name the caller as its signer.
  - The signature is not verified here; peers verify it.
- **key-service** serves the certificate in `DevicePreKeyBundle.device_certificate`.
- **Flow A proof of keys:** `ConfirmDeviceLink` keeps which device used the token and its `link_key_proof` in Redis for 15 minutes, the token's lifetime. `GetDeviceLinkResult` returns this only to the account that issued the token. Any other token reads as EXPIRED, so tokens cannot be probed.
- **Cargo.lock:** the same commit as #92 (ctutils, tokio). Without it the pre-push `cargo audit` stops the push. The content is identical, so the two PRs merge in either order.

## Three questions
1. **What the server learns:** nothing new. A certificate is public data about keys the server already serves. `link_key_proof` is an HMAC under the secret from the old device's QR, which the server never sees.
2. **What a party can withhold or substitute:** the server can withhold or alter a certificate or a proof. Peers then see an unsigned device, or the old device refuses to sign. Either way it is the safe side. The server cannot forge either. One account cannot write a certificate into another account's devices.
3. **Trust boundary:** trust in the device set moves from the server to the account's devices.

## Tests
- `set_device_certificate`, run against local Postgres with all migrations applied. The test is `#[ignore]` like its neighbours. 5 SQL mutations, each killed: the account subquery, `<> $1`, the signer's `is_active`, the subject's `is_active` and the length.
- The signer check: 3 mutations killed.
- The Redis link-result encoding.
- fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo audit` are clean.

author: dexterhere
body:
`ow install <id>`, `ow list`, `ow remove <id>` for spec widgets (JSON only, nothing from a widget is executed), and a payload-free `grants.reload` admin op. Design: `docs/INSTALL_DESIGN.md`.

- The registry index comes from the website; the three widget files come from GitHub at the exact pinned commit, through `ow-egress` only (no git, no shell). Strict JSON, id equality, the schema and layout rules re-implemented in Rust, a spec widget must declare no network, files or spawn, and providers must match the catalog snapshot in the binary. `planned` needs `--allow-planned`; `removed` is always refused.
- Consent: a plain-language access summary, then the person types `yes` on a terminal. The terminal input queue is flushed first, so pasted text cannot answer for you. `--yes` needs `--accept-access <hash>` over registry, repo, commit, file bytes and grants, and is refused with a non-default registry.
- Install is staged and swapped, rolled back if the grants write fails; grants are edited in place with comments kept and `grants.toml` stays 0600. Hand-written grants for the same id are announced before they are replaced or removed.
- New dependency `sha2` 0.11.1.

An independent review found a type-ahead consent bypass and a `--yes` one-liner bypass among others; all are fixed with tests that fail when the fix is removed.

**Residual risks:** trust in the website's index and in GitHub; no signatures and no per-file hashes in the index yet (web change listed in HANDOFF); same-uid processes can edit installed files; the grant key is a self-claimed widget id (D-1). Nothing renders a spec widget yet.
**Differences from the website:** emoji in names are refused by `ow`; combining marks are checked by Unicode block; depth limit 40 vs 12.

body:
## What this adds

**Physical inventory variance investigation** (`analyses/count_variance`)
- It follows the 30 June 2026 Variance Investigation Report (the narrative and its Detailed Variance Report) and the Variance Management SOP:
  - stock variance = minus the amount on the inventory difference account;
  - positive and negative variances are never offset against each other;
  - each line is Justified (in any capitals) or Not Justified;
  - inventory variance = Σ|Not Justified variance| ÷ final closing stock, and accuracy = 100% − variance, with a 0.5% tolerance (a parameter).
- Inputs:
  1. The G/L variance lines with ACTION, REASON and Final Validation Status (new dataset `gl_variance_lines`).
  2. Optional: the final closing stock per item and WBS (`final_closing_by_wbs`). This accepts this app's "Closing by ID and WBS" sheet or the count findings workbook's "Item Detail by WBS".
  3. Optional: an RBC report data sheet, for the split by programme (`rbc_material_categories`).
- Outputs:
  - the narrative's tables: headline (Table 1), justification by plant (Table 2), root causes (Table 3), required actions (Table 4), accuracy by stock category and programme (Table 5), accuracy by plant (Table 6);
  - the lines with an amount moved to retained earnings;
  - the detailed variance report;
  - a dashboard with filters and search; Excel, Word and PowerPoint reports.
- **Checked locally on Ferdinand's real files** (outside git): Tables 1, 2, 5 and 6 and the retained-earnings finding are reproduced to the franc. For example: 5,297 lines, 5,153 Justified, absolute variance 5,743,645,228, inventory value 82,384,817,907, accuracy 99.96%; every programme's figure matches, and NYARUGURU shows 3.64%.
- Tables 3 and 4 need a root cause and a required action per line, which are not in the G/L file. They fill in when the file has those columns (question Q8).

**RBC accountability**

**Engine**
- An absent optional column now keeps its type. Before, a file without an optional number column made a run fail; the variance browser test exposed this.

- The closing-stock workbook's "Final Closing Stock" and "Closing by ID and WBS" sheets have no formula total row, so they can be uploaded again as inputs. A test reads one back through the parser.

## Tests

- Q7: whether an RBC item new on RMS-PRG-FND-CP may take its programme name from other-WBS lines.
