## C98 — Structured export, no redundant exporter or state provider

**Stack:** PR #787 reading preview → PR #789 text-only export → **this incremental PR**. Product SHA `7120c2f31f204a48143c8fa24232badba50f1af0`, with a single C97 parent `c9b967889d60c198e58bed3f5109ecb5499099db`.

**Evidence-backed gap:** the approved local TXT download is linearized for accessible reading and cannot faithfully preserve typed block structure, decorative-image flags or custom block types. Add a separate, explicitly triggered **JSON draft download** containing `{format, version, title, content}`, with the unmodified existing `PageContent` object and every authored accessibility field.

- Reuses existing filename sanitization, PageEditor state and CSS; no new provider, storage schema, server-side data access, API requests or public sharing.
- Maintains image/video/audio references as JSON strings and accessibility metadata, **not binary attachments**. Import, remote backup, automated upload and sharing are NOT implemented.
- Makes privacy limits explicit: locally downloaded file can contain private authored material and resource references.
- No automatic save; existing authenticated save flow is unchanged. No forced conversion of block types or restrictions on learner subjects.
- New targeted tests: lossless structured block round-trip, decorative and unknown blocks, filename sanitization, browser API denial and unsaved draft independence. Earlier C96/C97 PASS reused.
- Dedicated testing workflow goes on a separate diagnostic-only branch; evidence is required before PASS status.

**DRAFT/NO-GO.** No merge, deploy, Render, GHCR, hosted database, RLS, secrets, main, Flonts, canonical artwork or infrastructure modifications; preserve #536/#594/#595, C03/ORG02, independent QA/accessibility and release review.

Permite que os usuários baixem o rascunho da página atual como um arquivo JSON estruturado, sem salvá-lo nem compartilhá-lo pelo servidor.

author: cryptojones
body:
Selecting a function in the workbench always asked the kuna CLI for its decompilation and for both directions of its cross references — even when the cache had already answered. Every answer is a process run against the binary, so every click paid for three of them and repeated what was already known.

### What is asked now

- The **decompilation** is asked for only when the function is not in the cache.
- The **cross references** are asked for one direction at a time: `--from` only when that direction is not cached, `--to` only when it is not. An answer of *no* references at all counts as an answer — the CLI was asked, and it said nothing.

A function that has been looked at once is not run against the binary again on the next click.

### The reload path

A reload empties the cache, so the workbench asks again when the export has been written since or the binary behind it has changed. The reload keeps the cache the answers live in and empties it itself, rather than relying on a fresh provider to bring a fresh cache — so emptying it is the reload's own doing, and the test can hold it to that.

The cache is kept only when the same export is being reloaded. Another export is another binary, and its answers are none of this one's.

### Also: a note on the binary beside the export

`KunaCli::for_export` falls back to `root.join(export.name)` when the export's README names a binary that is no longer there. That only finds the binary when the export was named after it; an export named for something else — a version, a target — has to keep the binary where its README says it is. The doc comment now says so.

### Checks

- `cargo test --workspace` — green (10 ag-cli, 12 ag-corpus, 40 ag-ui — three new; `crates/ag-engine` untouched)
- `cargo clippy -p ag-ui --all-targets` — clean
- rustfmt clean on every touched file (`ui/src/app.rs`, `ui/src/data/kuna.rs`, `ui/src/data/kuna_json.rs`)

### How much it was costing

The three questions are three process runs against the binary. On the 17 KB sample ELF used for the kuna JSON surfaces (`scratchpad/kuna-export-sample`, kuna v1.980) they take 0.10 s, 0.09 s and 0.06 s — about a quarter of a second per click, and it grows with the binary: kuna loads and analyses the whole target each time.

author: daveybehavey
body:
## Why

Fleet report #114 flagged a Google review-policy risk on the live `/review` page, verified from source on `main`: the review ask was conditioned on a good experience while problems were routed to a private text first. That is the review-gating shape Google's Maps user-content policy prohibits (soliciting only positive reviews / diverting negative ones privately before they can review), and the page also suggested what reviewers should mention.

A follow-up grep found the **same defect pattern** in a second file: `docs/review-request-template.md` — the SMS templates actually sent to customers, which are arguably the higher-risk surface (the fixed `/review` page is the handoff link inside them). Scope was extended onto this branch so one gate covers both files.

Copy-only fix, two files: `src/pages/review.astro` and `docs/review-request-template.md`. No link, analytics attribute, structured-data, QR, or option-card changes; no operational guidance in the docs file changed — only customer-facing template language plus removal of the suggested-content section.

## Before / after — `/review` page (`src/pages/review.astro`)

| Spot | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meta description | "If you had a good experience with Maestros Services, you can leave a quick review or send us a text if something needs attention." | "Share your experience with Maestros Services in a quick Google review. Honest feedback, good or bad, helps local homeowners know what to expect." |
| H1 | "If we did a good job, a quick review helps a lot." | "A quick review helps a lot." |
| Subline | "Short, honest feedback helps local homeowners know what to expect and helps a small, owner-operated business keep growing." | "Short, honest feedback, good or bad, helps local homeowners know what to expect and helps a small, owner-operated business keep growing." |
| Secondary button | "Need help first?" | "Need help with something?" |
| Side card | Kicker "What to mention" + suggested-content list (service helped with / your area / what stood out: communication, timing, cleanup, final result) | Kicker "Good to know" + two factual notes: reviews are public on Google and help other homeowners know what to expect; every review is read and honest feedback, good or bad, shows what to keep doing and what to do better. No suggested review content. |
| Help box in card | "If something needs attention — Please text or call (250) 858-1781 first so we can understand what happened and help sort it out as quickly as possible." | "Need help with your service? — If something about your recent service needs attention, text or call (250) 858-1781 and we will work with you to sort it out as quickly as possible." |

The contact path now stands as a separate, equally visible option for service help. There is no "first"/sequencing language anywhere on the page, and the Google review button is presented unconditionally.

## Before / after — SMS templates (`docs/review-request-template.md`)

| Spot | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same-day template (ask) | "If you were happy with the work, would you mind leaving us a quick Google review? It really helps local homeowners find us." | "Would you mind leaving us a quick Google review? It really helps local homeowners find us." |
| Same-day template (needs-attention line) | "If anything needs attention first, just reply here and I will take a look." | "And if anything needs attention, just reply here and I will take a look." |
| Direct-link template | "Mentioning the service and your area helps a lot. Thanks again." | "Thanks again." |
| Issue Recovery template | "If anything did not feel right or needs attention, please reply here **before leaving a review**. I want to understand what happened and make it right where possible." | "If anything did not feel right or needs attention, please reply here and let me know. I want to understand what happened and make it right where possible." |
| "What To Ask Them To Mention" section | Present (work done / area / what they liked: communication, reliability, cleanup, timing, result) | Deleted entirely |

The Issue Recovery line was the most explicit gating in the repo — a direct ask to contact privately *before* reviewing. It is now a standalone service check-in with no reference to reviewing at all; wanting to make it right is kept, tying it to the review is gone. The 2–3-day follow-up template was already neutral and is byte-identical.

## Validation

- Page fix (`9df0491`): `npm test` — all 11 chained suites pass; no test pinned the old page wording, so no pin updates. `npm run build` — green, 378 pages; built `dist/review/index.html` contains the new headline, button label, and card heading.
- Templates fix (`cdd7625`): `npm test` re-run — exit 0, all suites pass; no test pinned the old template strings either, so no pin updates. `npm run build` re-run — green, 378 pages.

author: sku0x20
body:
Since #50 the plugin's `jar` task reads `gitSha`, which ran `git rev-parse --short HEAD` unless `-PgitSha` was set. A build without git (for example an image build that doesn't pass `-PgitSha`), outside a repository, or before the first commit failed.

`gitSha` now comes from a `ValueSource` that returns `unknown` in those cases, matching the Dockerfile's `GIT_SHA` default. `providers.exec` can't do this: a missing binary throws before `isIgnoreExitValue` applies.

Checked by hand, reading `Implementation-Version` from the jar:
- In this repo: `65c9f60`, HEAD.
- Outside a repository: `unknown`.
- In a repository with no commits: `unknown`.
- With `git` replaced by a missing binary: `unknown`.
- After a new commit with the configuration cache reused: the new SHA.

author: johnlizarazo
body:
Closes #7

Con este PR, `core-bancario` publica las **6 herramientas de la constitución**.

## Qué entrega

- **`bloquear_tarjeta`** (regla 3): bloquea de inmediato una tarjeta del cliente, identificada por `cliente_id` y `ultimos4`, con el motivo.
  - No tiene parámetro ni paso de aprobación: el bloqueo ocurre en el mismo llamado.
  - Repetir un bloqueo, o bloquear la 9012 que ya venía bloqueada en los datos, responde éxito con `ya_estaba_bloqueada: true`.
  - Si la tarjeta es de otra persona o el cliente no existe, responde el mismo `NO_ENCONTRADO` que `consultar_transacciones`.
  - Una tarjeta bloqueada se puede seguir consultando y disputando.
- **`escalar_a_analista`**: valida el resumen según la causa, que es una lista cerrada (`persona_solicitada`, `umbral`, `fuera_de_politica`, `intentos_agotados`, `otra`).
  - Siempre son obligatorias la causa, las acciones realizadas y la acción recomendada. Si faltan varias, un solo error las nombra todas.
  - El cliente es obligatorio salvo con `persona_solicitada` (regla 4). Las transacciones son obligatorias con `umbral` y `fuera_de_politica`.
  - El core **guarda para el analista** el resumen completo: cliente con nombre, transacciones con fecha, monto, comercio y caso de disputa tomados de sus datos (regla 2), y total.
  - Al agente **solo le responde** `escalamiento_id`, `causa`, `estado` y `cantidad_transacciones`. Como escalar no exige identidad verificada, la respuesta no debe servir para consultar productos (ajuste C1 del análisis).
- **Estado de la tarjeta:** el valor de los datos es el inicial; los bloqueos de la sesión viven en memoria del core, igual que los intentos y las disputas.
- **Tipo `ListaTexto`** para las listas: el esquema publica `array` de `string`, y la herramienta acepta una lista o un texto con una lista JSON. Cualquier otra forma responde con el contrato.
- **Ajustes heredados del #6:**
  - Una fecha vacía y una de solo espacios se tratan igual, como fecha omitida.
  - El número de caso sale de un contador propio.
  - `Politica.limite_dias` define el límite de días una sola vez.
- La rule de MCP documenta `ListaTexto` y que una herramienta exenta de identidad no devuelve datos de productos.

## Cómo se verificó

- `uv run pytest`: 322 tests en verde (antes eran 264); `ruff check` sin problemas.
- En una sesión nueva de Claude Code se probaron los 8 pasos de `quickstart.md §2` contra `core-bancario`: bloqueo, bloqueo repetido, tarjeta bloqueada en los datos, tarjeta ajena, escalamiento por umbral sin datos de productos en la respuesta, persona solicitada sin cliente, campo faltante y umbral sin transacciones. Todos dieron el resultado esperado, y la lista enviada desde Claude Code fue aceptada.
- `bloquear_pii.py --diff` sobre el diff de la rama: sin hallazgos.

## Revisiones

**Código (`revisor-codigo`): APROBADO**, con 6 no bloqueantes:
1. Queda una comparación `pais == "CO"`, que solo elige el texto "nacionales" o "en el exterior"; el límite ya sale de `limite_dias`.
2. `plan.md` menciona cambios en `errores.py` que no hubo.
3. No quedó anotado en el repositorio cómo envía Claude Code la lista.
4. El commit de T014 tiene otro mensaje e incluye además la regla sobre herramientas exentas.
5. `ruff format` partió el conjunto `CAUSAS_SIN_CLIENTE` en tres líneas.
6. No hay un test para `persona_solicitada` con transacciones y sin cliente.

**Cumplimiento (`revisar-cumplimiento`): APROBADO.**
- **NO APLICA**: los hooks de identidad y umbral (#9), el hook `Stop` y el reconocimiento del pedido de persona (#10 y #13).
- **Lo que esta rama sí aplica, del lado del servidor**: las reglas 2, 3 y 5. Las tres cumplen.
- **No bloqueantes**:
  - `escalar_a_analista` responde distinto si una transacción no existe o si es de otro cliente, lo que permite saber si un identificador existe, aunque sin datos. Sugiere usar un solo error para los dos casos.
  - El hook del #9 debe cubrir `bloquear_tarjeta` y comparar al cliente verificado con el titular de la tarjeta.

## Límites conocidos

- Los bloqueos y escalamientos de la sesión viven en memoria y se pierden al reiniciar el core.
- La identidad antes de bloquear la garantiza el hook del #9, y la obligación de escalar, el hook `Stop` del #10.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Problem Sentry [SDK-PYTHON-12Q](https://blaxel.sentry.io/issues/7809397325/) — `McpError: Session terminated`. A persistent MCP session (`PersistentMcpClient`) is sticky to one backend via the streamable-HTTP `mcp-session-id`. When that backend is recycled, scaled down, or hibernated — or a follow-up request is routed to a replica that no longer knows the session — the request gets HTTP 404, which the MCP SDK surfaces as `McpError("Session terminated")`. `call_tool()` already caught this and returned an `isError` result, but **`list_tools()`** (and `initialize()`'s first request) let it escape **unhandled**. It propagated through `connect()` → `BlTools.initialize()` and was picked up by the SDK's own unhandled-exception Sentry hooks (frame `tools/__init__.py:list_tools`), producing the reported issue. ## Root cause (validated) Reproduced end-to-end against a real streamable-HTTP MCP server with a 404-injecting proxy that mimics a server-side session drop. Confirmed via the SDK's own capture predicate that the `McpError` raised through `list_tools()` has `_is_from_sdk=True` and `WOULD_CAPTURE=True`, matching the Sentry fingerprint exactly. `call_tool()` on the same condition was caught (no capture), consistent with only `list_tools` appearing in Sentry. ## Fix Detect the terminated-session error, discard the dead session, and **transparently reconnect-and-retry once** for `initialize` + `list_tools` + `call_tool` (shared `_run_with_session_retry` helper). A single reconnect heals the common transient recycle; a genuinely unavailable server still surfaces the error after one retry rather than being masked or looping. The exit-stack teardown is factored into a shared `_drop_session_stacks` reused by `_close` and the new `_discard_session`, preserving the existing safe stack-swap behavior. ## Validation - Reproduction harness: `list_tools` and `call_tool` now reconnect and succeed on a dropped session; a permanently-down server still raises; **0** Sentry captures across all scenarios (previously the `list_tools` path was captured). - New unit tests in `tests/core/test_tools.py`: reconnect-and-heal for `list_tools` and `call_tool`, bounded (single) retry on a permanently-terminated session, and that non-terminated errors are not retried. - `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` pass; existing tool tests pass (12/12). ## Remaining risk Low. Change is scoped to `PersistentMcpClient`. A truly unavailable server still raises after one retry (real failures are not hidden). The pre-existing cross-task exit-stack teardown noise (close timer running in a different task) is unchanged and does not reach Sentry; it can be addressed separately. Fixes Sentry SDK-PYTHON-12Q.

author: almarionai
body:
## Description

`cowork run` parsed `--provider` and `--model` but never passed them to the task, so every run used the global default model. The only way to switch was `cowork providers configure`, which changes the global default: runs could not use different models at the same time, and a run could silently use the wrong model.

`cowork run --provider <type> --model <id>` now pins that run's task to the model with the same `modelPinned` mechanism the conversation model picker uses (#555). The global default stays unchanged.

```bash
cowork run "draft the board deck" --provider openrouter --model moonshotai/kimi-k3
cowork run "draft the board deck" --model gpt-6-sol         # current provider
cowork run "draft the board deck" --provider ollama         # that provider's saved model
```

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Test update

## Category

- [x] LLM Providers
- [x] Other (CLI)

## Changes Made

- New `src/cli/run-model-pin.ts`: builds the pin and checks it before the task exists. An unknown provider, a provider that is not configured, a provider with no saved model, or a pin `resolveTaskModelSelection` would not honor stops the run with exit 1. Without this check the executor would quietly fall back to the global model.
- `direct-run.ts`: adds `providerType`, `modelKey` and `modelPinned: true` to the task's `agentConfig`, and prints the resolved model (`Model for this run: <provider>/<model>`, or a `task_model` event with `--json`). The provider-name helpers (`normalizeProviderType`, `resolveSupportedProviderType`) moved into the new module so `main.ts` can use them too; behavior is unchanged.
- `main.ts`: `buildDirectTaskArgs` forwards `--provider`/`--model` to the local runner, which covers `--detach` too. `--remote` runs send the pin as `agentConfig`, which the control plane already validates with `AgentConfigSchema`. On `--remote`, `--model` is required, because the remote node's saved model can't be read locally. Help text updated.
- `tests/cli-direct-run-settings.test.ts` extracts CLI functions from `direct-run.ts` by name; it now binds the two moved helpers from `run-model-pin.ts`.
- Docs: "Choosing the model for one run" in `docs/cli.md`, plus a CHANGELOG entry.

## Security Considerations

- [x] This change has been reviewed for security implications (describe below)

No new IPC or tool surface. The pin goes through the existing `modelPinned` path. Remote runs send a field the control plane already accepts and validates (`AgentConfigSchema`: provider enum, model key up to 200 characters). Access profiles are unchanged.

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally on macOS
- [x] Tested with at least one LLM provider (OpenRouter and OpenAI-compatible routes, against loopback fakes)

Unit tests: `src/cli/__tests__/run-model-pin.test.ts` (new, 14 cases) and `src/cli/__tests__/main.test.ts` (local forwarding, remote `agentConfig`, and remote `--provider` without `--model` refused before connecting).

End to end with the built CLI (`node bin/cowork-cli.js`) on a throwaway profile (`COWORK_USER_DATA_DIR`, `COWORK_DISABLE_OS_KEYCHAIN=1`). Two fake OpenAI-compatible servers bound to `127.0.0.1:18431` (global default, `openai-compatible`/`global-a-model`) and `127.0.0.1:18432` (`openrouter`, saved model `saved-b-model`) logged the model of every request:

| Run | Model calls |
|---|---|
| `--provider openrouter --model pinned-b-model` | 4/4 to :18432 with `pinned-b-model` |
| no flags | 4/4 to :18431 with `global-a-model` |
| `--model pinned-a-model` | 4/4 to :18431 with `pinned-a-model` |
| `--provider openrouter` | 4/4 to :18432 with `saved-b-model` |
| `--provider groq --model x` | exit 1, "not configured", no requests |
| two pinned runs at once on the same profile | each run's calls went only to its own model |

`cowork providers list` showed `Current: openai-compatible (global-a-model)` after all runs.

Gate: `build:electron`, `build:daemon`, `build:cli`, `type-check`, `lint`, `fmt:check` and `npm run test` pass.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code

- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

author: itstimwhite
body:
<!-- customer-changelog/v1 {"releaseWorthy":false} -->

### Problem

Product Screenshots run [40011855089](https://github.com/JovieInc/Jovie/actions/runs/40011855089) on main `7e88ce8` (#22831) failed `Capture hud-isolated screen proof` — `tests/product-screenshots/hud-isolated-screen-proof.spec.ts:118`, attempt 1 + retry: axe `label-content-name-mismatch` (serious) on **11 Ovie launcher buttons** (`data-testid=ovie-launcher-*`, e.g. `button[aria-label="Symphony, Unavailable"]` — Symphony, GBrain, Hermes, GitHub PRs, Gmail, Linear, Mercury, Production, Status, Vercel). The same step passed on `cc4532a` (run [40011129819](https://github.com/JovieInc/Jovie/actions/runs/40011129819)).

### Root cause

`compare cc4532a...7e88ce8` contains exactly one commit: #22831 (`.public-container` — one public width for header/hero/footer, `--ds-public-gutter`, header padding-inline changes). The launcher rail component is byte-identical across green and red. Per axe 4.14's `label-content-name-mismatch` implementation (`labelContentNameMismatchEvaluate`): visible text is gathered pixel-aware (`ignoreIconLigature`, `pixelThreshold 0.1`) and `if (!visibleText) return true` — heavily clipped text is excluded as an icon ligature. #22831's header/gutter changes altered the /hud page chrome and the launcher buttons' clipping so the previously sub-threshold label text now renders visibly; the buttons then fell under the visible-text vs accessible-name comparison, and the overriding `aria-label` phrasing failed it. The template: `aria-label={`${label}, ${status}`}` over content that already visibly renders both.

### What changed

- `apps/web/components/features/admin/hud/OvieLauncherRail.tsx` — drop the overriding `aria-label` on the LaunchControl button template (the ONE template behind all 11 violations). The accessible name now comes from the visible content ("Symphony Unavailable") — it contains the visible text **by construction**, which passes the axe check under every clipping state of those spans (both visible: identical text; label clipped below the ligature threshold: visible text is a subset of the name; both clipped: empty visible text). This matches the compact rail variant in the same file, which already names its buttons from content, and the repo's established pattern for this rule (#22826, #22839/PlatformPill, #22361). `title` (the why-tooltip) is unchanged — it is not the accessible name when content exists.
- `OvieLauncherRail.test.tsx` — regression assertions: launcher buttons have no overriding `aria-label` and their accessible name is the visible `label + status` content.
- No axe rule suppression, no spec/assertion change, no feature flag, no route skip.

### Sweep

- The rail's other surfaces are clean: the All-tools drawer rows are non-interactive `<li>`s with visible text; the search input's `aria-label='Search All Tools'` is an input (no visible text content — the rule does not apply); the compact variant already names from content.
- `OvieMacHud.tsx` aria-labels checked (`Talk To Summer` link, `Week over week growth …`, `Shipping throughput …`) — none override visible text on interactive elements in the failing set.
- No open PR overlaps these two files (#22829's lane touches Storybook/global tokens; #22804/#22797 are product-page PRs with no HUD files).

### Assumptions / disclosures

- No Linear issue — dispatch-driven remediation (4th feature-page/chrome land red on this post-merge-only gate).
- gbrain unreachable in this runtime (noted per workflow).
- `workflow_dispatch` of screenshots.yml is not available to this app's GitHub surface (verified — no dispatch action); per the steer's fallback, PR CI is the pre-merge proof environment, and the post-merge main Product Screenshots run is the full-producer acceptance signal. The PR-lane A11y job's rendered gate is synthetic-shell based (does not exercise /hud), so the pre-merge live-axe proof for this exact DOM is the construction-level guarantee (name == visible text) plus the colocated accessible-name test; the definitive full-spec run happens on main right after merge and is posted back here.

### Verification

- `biome check` (2.5.14, repo config) on both touched files: clean.
- Full PR-lane pass/fail list on the head will be posted as a PR comment (Source Validation, Affected Unit Tests 1–4, Exact-head Coverage, A11y, Capture changed UI, PR Ready, …).
- Acceptance: the next Product Screenshots run on main after merge — `Capture hud-isolated screen proof` with zero axe violations, plus every other producer green.

### Dispatch

`check:Generate Screenshots: unhealthy` — iteration 4; run 40011855089 on `7e88ce8` (#22831), `Capture hud-isolated screen proof` axe label-content-name-mismatch on 11 Ovie launcher buttons.

author: iiloni
body:
## Change

On Android, a reminder's notification came back every time the app was opened, even after tapping **Done**.

The phone remembers when it last rang each reminder (`rung`/`walls` in `ReminderAlarms.schedule`), but it only kept that record for reminders still in its alarm list. A reminder leaves the list soon after it rings: the server moves it on, and the hourly background check brings that to the phone. When the app then opens, it hands the phone the reminders from its local database, which date from before the server moved this one on, until sync catches up. With no record of the ring, the phone treated the time as unrung (it rings anything under a day late) and posted the notification again.

The phone now keeps a ring record for the day in which a reminder can still ring late, whether or not that reminder is in the current list. ADR 0018 notes this.

## Validation

- New Robolectric `ReminderAlarmsTest` (SDK 24 and 36): a due reminder rings once; a reminder that left the list and comes back as the older copy does not ring again; a reminder set again for later is still scheduled. The stale-copy case fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `./gradlew :app:testDevDebugUnitTest`: all Android unit tests pass.
- `./scripts/dev.sh check`: passed.
- Not yet tried on a device.

## Review notes

**Done** still only dismisses the notification, as ADR 0018 specifies. This PR stops the repeat rings without changing what Done does.

author: bastotec
body:
## Intent

Fix a Deck secondmate that fails every launch with 'fm-deck-worker: session start did not publish a complete digest'. Measured cause: on a heavily loaded Mac (load average 180-300 on 8 cores) a large second-mate home's session start takes about 100-140s (lock stage ~16s, bootstrap ~53s, wake-queue ~25s), and bin/fm-session-start.sh hard-bounds itself at FM_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT (default 120s) and prints a STARTUP TRUNCATED banner. The Deck secondmate host (bin/fm-deck-worker.sh) refuses to start without a complete digest, so every relaunch failed the same way. No single stage is pathological; it is general slowness. Decision: the host, which nobody interactively waits on and which treats truncation as fatal, passes its own larger bound to session start: FM_DECK_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT, default 600s, with empty/nonnumeric/zero/padded-zero values falling back to the default so the bound is never disabled. The 120s default of fm-session-start.sh itself is deliberately unchanged for interactive callers, and bin/fm-deck-chat.sh (primary host) is deliberately left out of scope. A regression test in tests/fm-deck-harness.test.sh runs the real worker with a fixture session start that records the bound it received; it fails on the old worker (passes 120) and passes now.

## What Changed

- Give the Deck secondmate host a dedicated `FM_DECK_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT`, defaulting to 600 seconds, so slow startup has more time to publish a complete digest.
  Empty, nonnumeric, zero, and padded-zero overrides fall back to 600 seconds; the interactive 120-second default and primary Deck host remain unchanged.
- Add a regression fixture that runs the real worker and checks the timeout passed to session start for default, custom, and invalid overrides.
- Remove the verification documentation's outdated statement that no timeout limit is increased.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped to the secondmate host's startup budget, preserves the interactive default and primary host, and introduces no substantiated correctness or intent-conformance issues.

author: jimedusot-beep
body:
Sasori previously shared only SIG BLE controls; proprietary toys had no live family mapping and physical-effect results had no repeatable review workflow. This adds a selected original WowWee MiP protocol family behind Connect / Identify / Status / Find / Stop, remembered family-specific bindings, and a shared Identify → Status → bounded effect → clear check recipe.

MiP follows the pinned manufacturer transport/command tables: binary version/status queries, strict ASCII-hex replies, and only dim-blue/off chest LED frames. Web and Swift independently restrict commands; matching replies and queued writes never claim authentication or physical confirmation. There are no motor, sound, firmware, arbitrary-write or guessed Elmo commands.

Action trials record fresh connection IDs, timing, outcomes, cleanup and separate owner observations. Ten distinct local live checks with unchanged known model/firmware form a review target; failures/untested checks reset it, and imported/synthetic claims cannot qualify. Storage preserves IndexedDB v4 and existing preferences, validates batches atomically, and supports private export/import/removal.

Elmo remains blocked by missing evidence. A fresh public-artifact request returned HTTP 403; available file/context searches recovered no APK/managed assembly. The new private APK intake CLI hashes actual artifacts, optionally extracts the bounded managed assembly outside the repo, and lists G1–G8 without executing it, extracting credentials or claiming signature/publisher/method verification. Documentation links exact sources and next evidence requirements.

The simulator smoke check also requires readiness-marker and screenshot proof when simctl launch hangs; a timeout alone never passes.

- Local `npm run check`: 186 Node tests, 7 Python tests, lint/format/type checks and credential-pattern scan passed.

author: danielmarbach
body:
Stacked on #8008.

An `UnconditionalSuppressMessage` on a field doesn't cover the field initializer, because the initializer's IL ends up in the constructor. That happened in four places:

- `ExpressionBasedMessagePropertyAccessor`: the unsuppressed IL2026 made ILLink crash while reporting it (`MessageOrigin.ToString()`, "Sequence contains no elements"). That crash is why the trimmed variant of `TrimmedEndpoint` didn't compile sagas.
- `SagaMetadata` (two fields) and `MessageHandlerRegistry`: these are the IL2026 warnings every trimmed or AOT publish of the sample reports.

The suppressions now sit on an explicit constructor and on static methods that do the lookups. Caching and initialization order stay the same. `TrimmedEndpoint` compiles the saga into both variants now.

Without the accessor fix, the trimmed `TrimmedEndpointTests` fails with the ILLink crash. With it, both variants run the saga, and the trimmed publish only reports the unrelated IL2057. The Core tests and the saga acceptance tests pass.

The reflection lookups also suppress IL3050, because every caller is annotated with `RequiresDynamicCode`. Both variants now only report IL2057. The ILLink crash is dotnet/runtime#129562, fixed for .NET 11 by dotnet/runtime#129869.

author: victorlucss
body:
Switching Chats felt slow and sometimes showed "New chat" for a saved Chat (the recording Victor sent). Measured on a dev copy of the real `.milagre` state: every switch rebuilt the whole transcript, 90 to 460 ms on the main thread (markdown parse, React mount, and a framer-motion unmount that forced layout per pill), and the composer showed the new-chat header until the Chat's page came back from the host. On a busy Mac that read takes seconds, which is the video. Chats of other computers add a network hop to the same path.

This copies what makes [MonoCode](https://github.com/hardbeat920/monocode) fast at this, its `TranscriptPool`:

- **The last four transcripts stay mounted.** `TranscriptSlots` in ChatComposer renders each through a portal into a node of its own (`lib/transcript-slots.ts` keeps the LRU). The shown node sits in the host; parked ones leave the document with their DOM intact, so the find bar and DOM queries only ever meet the Chat on screen, and coming back is one insertion. The scroller is keyed by the slot, not the per-open counter, which remounted it anyway. Each parked message keeps its laid-out height, so a reopened Chat sits still at its bottom; a message never laid out makes the scroller measure once more. A draft's slot becomes its saved Chat's without a remount.
- **No "New chat" flash.** A saved Chat whose page is still loading keeps the conversation layout (empty) instead of the new-chat header, desktop and phone.
- **Hover prefetch.** A sidebar row reads its Chat's page after 90 ms under the pointer, so the click paints at once (local SQLite, or another computer's network).
- **Other computers' Chats paint from their offline copy** (`computers:recall`) while the computer's own answer is on its way.
- **Opt-in timing**: `localStorage.setItem("milagre.measureNavigation", "1")`, then `performance.getEntriesByName("milagre:chat-switch")`.

Dev copy, real chats (47 and 40 messages), main-thread long task per switch:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| first open of a Chat | 90 to 460 ms | 90 to 440 ms (unchanged: parse + mount) |
| coming back to a Chat | 90 to 460 ms | none |
| "New chat" shown while the page loads | yes | no |

- **One composer across Projects.** The composer was keyed by Project path, so every Project switch rebuilt it and its transcripts; now the parked transcripts outlive the switch.

Also exercised, on the production renderer, with two Projects on different Claude accounts and with a second dev copy paired as another computer (LAN route):

| switch | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| back to a Chat in the same Project | 90 to 460 ms | none |
| back to a Chat in another Project, other Claude account | 230 to 310 ms | 105 to 150 ms |
| back to a Chat on another computer | same path plus the network | 85 to 180 ms, transcript at once |

What is left on those paths is the App re-render itself (`adoptProject` under `flushSync`: sidebar, panels, context propagation into the transcripts); the first open of a Chat still parses and mounts it (90 to 440 ms for a 40-message Chat).

Not in this PR: the first-open cost (startTransition, lighter markdown); trimming the App re-render on a Project switch.

Screenshots from the real app: the "before" is a frame of Victor's recording; the "after" is the desktop dev app against a copy of his real Chats.

| before: a saved Chat shows "New chat" while its page loads | after: coming back to a Chat, instant, at its latest turn |

| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-ptf/milagre-ade/957fba07a96e9c7b6a71c59e696a4c61dc7fc111/tab-switch-pool/before-new-chat-flash.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-ptf/milagre-ade/957fba07a96e9c7b6a71c59e696a4c61dc7fc111/tab-switch-pool/after-revisit.png) |

| another computer's Chat (paired dev copy "B", production renderer) |

author: franciscbalint
body:
Rebuilt on top of `main` after PR #30 landed. That PR already brought the validate options, real-time AI scoring, the filters, the list evaluator and the first four S3 jobs — so this branch now adds **only what is still missing**, on main's structure, rather than a second copy of that work.

Ports the rest of `407f0a8` and `b0444f8` from the Python SDK. Everything is documented at https://www.zerobounce.net/docs/.

## Validate options

`ValidateOptions` gains `DomainInfo`, `GreylistProcessing` and `CallbackURL`. A nil pointer is not sent, and booleans go on the wire as the strings `"true"`/`"false"`.

`CallbackURL` is where the greylist retry posts its result, so it is rejected without `GreylistProcessing`, and when blank — before any request is sent.

`ValidateResponse` carries `DomainWebsiteExists`, `DomainRegistrantCompanyName` and `Message`. `Message` is the API's `Message` key, returned instead of a result while a greylist retry is still running.

## The rest of the documented bulk surface

- `EmailFinderS3File`, `DomainSearchS3File` — https://www.zerobounce.net/docs/api-integrations/amazon-s3-bulk-api
- `ValidateSFTPFile`, `ScoreSFTPFile`, `EmailFinderSFTPFile`, `DomainSearchSFTPFile`, `ExportSFTPFile` — https://www.zerobounce.net/docs/api-integrations/sftp_bulk_api

All six share `BulkFileJobOptions` and `bulkRootFileJob`, and go out through main's existing `postBulkRootForm` on the bulkapi root.

Two shapes differ from the rest and are easy to get wrong:
- `ValidateSFTPFile`'s `file_name` is **optional** — leaving `FileName` empty uses the input bucket from the account's settings. Every other job requires it.
- `ExportSFTPFile` sends `export_path`, not the `export_bucket` that `ExportS3File` sends.

The SFTP server, path and protocol are never sent by the SDK; they come from the account's ZeroBounce settings.

## Inbox Placement Tester

On `INBOX_PLACEMENT_URI`: the API key goes on the query string, bodies are camelCase JSON, and unset fields are left out. Spends the account's inbox-test credits.

## Base URLs

`LIST_EVALUATOR_URI` and `INBOX_PLACEMENT_URI` are new. They are separate base URLs rather than paths built from `BULK_URI`, and `SetURI` does not touch them. `GetListEvaluatorResult` now uses the first of those and URL-encodes the file id as a single path segment.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt` clean on the new files
- [x] `go test -short ./...` — **95 pass, up from 89 on main**; the same 3 live-API integration tests are skipped
- [x] Offline only: the new tests reuse main's `useFake` harness, which swaps `http.DefaultTransport` for a recorder. `useFake` now also restores the two new base URLs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

## RD-66: `ai_agent_mailbox` sub_status

Folded in from the former `feature/ai-agent-mailbox-substatus` branch, which has been deleted now that the commit lives here.

Adds the `ai_agent_mailbox` sub_status, which the API returns alongside both `valid` and `catch-all`. Tests cover both pairings, plus an unrecognised sub_status to pin that a value added to the API after this SDK ships degrades gracefully instead of failing the whole validate call.

No `sub_status_ai_agent_mailbox` usage counter was added: it is not documented.

author: m000gg
body:
📚 Overview
This PR introduces the `preferredLanguage` field to the user profile, laying the groundwork for localization and personalized communications. It covers the full lifecycle of the feature: database schema migration, entity and DTO updates, administrator registration controls, and user self-service profile management.

🛠 Key Changes
**Database & Entity Model**
*   Added a new Flyway migration script introducing the `preferred_language` column (with a safe default fallback) to the users table.
*   Updated the `User` JPA entity and corresponding DTOs (`UserRegistrationDto`, `UserProfileUpdateDto`, `UserResponseDto`) to include and handle `preferredLanguage`.

**Admin Registration Flow**
*   Updated administrator user creation forms and backend processing logic to allow admins to assign a preferred language when registering new accounts.

**User Profile Self-Service**
*   Updated the user profile service, controllers, and frontend templates to allow authenticated users to view and update their preferred language.
*   Added input validation to restrict values to supported language codes (e.g., `en`, `de`, `uk`, `ru`).

🚦 How to Verify
*   **Verify through tests**: Run `mvn clean verify` to ensure all unit and integration tests pass successfully and Flyway migrations apply cleanly against the database.
*   **Verify through application**: Log in as an admin to create a user with a specific preferred language, then log in as that user to view and modify the language setting from the profile page.

Out of Scope
*   A full-scale i18n translation overhaul of the entire dashboard user interface.
*   Automatic browser language detection and redirection.

🔗 Closes: #102

author: mightye
body:
## What

The pnpm and yarn-classic half of ferralon-ai/tracker#317 (PR1c). Until now a pnpm or yarn-classic lock went through `addUnplaced`: every pin became an unread, scripts-unknown entry, and the dependency lane withheld run-wide. This PR places those packages, reads their verified tarballs and resolves loads into them, the way #217 does for npm.

- **Semantic regions.** Neither lock records a physical layout the lane can trust. yarn classic hoists at install time, and pnpm's hoist and linker settings decide what its store exposes. So a pnpm or yarn-classic lock root becomes a *semantic region*, and a load inside it is answered from the lock's edges rather than a path walk:
  1. A declared load (the requirer's own lock edge, or a first-party importer's manifest entry) resolves to that edge's target. Every linker guarantees this.
  2. A load of a name the requirer's tarball bundles resolves to nothing; the bundled copy is unread and the package withholds run-wide.
  3. A package loading its own name resolves to itself.
  4. Any other (phantom) load may find one of the region's copies (whichever pnpm or yarn hoisted), or, when none is hoisted where its walk passes, climb out of the region to whatever Node's walk finds above it. Its candidates are the union of the two. One candidate resolves to it. Several resolve to none, and the load site's walk-miss limit targets every candidate (its name, plus each copy's package name, which covers an `npm:` alias). The walk above the region is closed-world only over directories a lock accounts for, so it needs one more precondition, below.
- **Workspace globs.** The lane reads only the two pattern shapes it can show select exactly what pnpm and yarn classic select: a literal relative path (`packages/a`), and a literal prefix with one trailing `/*` (`packages/*`). Every segment is plain (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `@` and `-`, not starting with `.`), so there is no leading `/` or `./` and no `.`, `..` or empty segment, and none is `node_modules` or `bower_components`. A selected directory is a member through a regular file named exactly `package.json`. Any other pattern withholds. So does a pattern path that exists only in another case or through a symlink, and, under a `/*`, a symlinked entry, a `node_modules` or `bower_components` entry (yarn classic selects members there, pnpm skips them), a dot-named directory holding a manifest, a member manifest in another case or next to a `package.yaml` or `package.json5`, or a member `yarn.json` in any case (yarn classic reads a member from either manifest).
  - Shapes withheld: any `!` pattern (pnpm excludes with it whatever its position, yarn classic ignores it), `**`, a `*` that isn't the whole last segment (`packages/a*`, `pack*/a`), `?`, brackets, braces, extglobs and backslashes. A `pnpm-workspace.yaml` that is blank or comment-only, or whose `packages` is null, withholds too: pnpm 8 and 9 take every package in the tree as a member for the first and fail on the second, while pnpm 10 and later take the root alone for both. A `yarn.json` at the root or in a member withholds, because yarn classic reads it as a manifest and the lane doesn't. Winning these back is a separate follow-up.
- **File-name case.** A build may run on a case-insensitive filesystem, where a package manager opening `binding.gyp` finds `Binding.gyp`. A tarball's or patch's `binding.gyp` and `package.json`, and the trigger files checked above a region and at a region root (install config files, `.npmrc`, `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `.yarnrc`, pnpmfiles, `package.yaml`, `package.json5`), match in any case. A `.npmrc`, `package.json` or rc file named in another case is not judged; it withholds.
- **Regions nest.** A load chooses the region whose root is the longest prefix of its directory. An npm region keeps #217's physical walk, and a member that two locks claim leaves the layout incomplete.
  - Discovery makes a region only where it finds a lock, so the walk above a semantic region below the build root is accepted only on positive grounds. Each directory above it, up to the build root, must either be one a lock installs for (a lock root, a semantic importer or an npm workspace), or be inert:
    - no `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `.yarnrc`, `.yarnrc.yml`, pnpmfile, lockfile, `binding.gyp`, `package.yaml`, `package.json5` or `node_modules` there. npm, pnpm and yarn classic run `node-gyp rebuild` at install for a directory with a `binding.gyp` and no install or preinstall script, and pnpm installs from `package.yaml` or `package.json5` when there is no `package.json`;
    - a `.npmrc` that is absent, or readable and setting only registry, scoped-registry, per-registry credential, TLS, proxy, retry, output and save keys. Hoist and linker settings, `pnpmfile`, `global-pnpmfile`, any unknown key and an unparseable file withhold. Only keys are compared, never values;
    - a `package.json` that is absent, or readable, parseable and made only of allowlisted keys: metadata (`name`, `version`, `private`, `description`, `license`, `author`, `contributors`, `repository`, `homepage`, `bugs`, `keywords`, `funding`, `files`, `publishConfig`), self-load keys (`type`, `main`, `module`, `types`, `typings`, `sideEffects`), tool selection (`engines`, `packageManager`), `config`, tool configuration that only the named tool reads (`prettier`, `browserslist`, `eslintConfig`, `eslintIgnore`, `stylelint`, `jest`, `babel`, `lint-staged`, `husky`, `commitlint`, `nyc`, `c8`, `ava`, `mocha`, `xo`, `postcss`, `remarkConfig`, `size-limit`, `release`, `renovate`), and `scripts` with no possible install hook. A script is a possible hook by class, not by list: any `pre*` or `post*` name, any manager-namespaced name containing `:` (such as `pnpm:devPreinstall`), and `install` and `dependencies`. `prebuild` and `postbuild` withhold as a precision cost.
    - `workspaces` and every dependency map, even an empty one, are not inert, because a workspace root hoists its members' dependencies into its own `node_modules` while declaring none.
  - Any other directory leaves the layout incomplete. The check runs for every pnpm or yarn classic region below the build root, including a repo's only region. Repos whose only lock is at the build root never run it.
  - Node's walk continues above the build root; the lane's scan stops there. That is sound when the build directory is the checkout root.
- **Synthetic paths.** Placed entries get module ids such as `<root>/node_modules/.pnpm/<key>/node_modules/<name>`. Nothing stats, reads or walks them; tarballs come from the store. So a directory of the same name that an earlier install left on disk is never consulted (`DecoyAtSyntheticPath`, which also has a chmod 000 variant).
- **pnpm.** `lockfileVersion` 5.4, 6.0 and 9.0 only. Anything else, a missing or duplicated version, or YAML outside the subset pnpm writes leaves the layout incomplete. The pnpm 10+ two-document lock is read when its environment document pins only the package manager. Peer variants of one tarball are separate entries. A `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with no keys or a null `packages` withholds, since pnpm 8 and 9 read it differently from 10 and later. Settings are read from the project `.npmrc`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and package.json `pnpm`, never from `$HOME/.npmrc` or a global rc.
  - Withholds: a pnpmfile (on disk or configured), non-empty `packageExtensions` or `configDependencies`, an unknown workspace or `pnpm` key, an unknown lock root key (which covers `pnpmfileChecksum` and `packageExtensionsChecksum`), `excludeLinksFromLockfile`, package.json `resolutions`, a `package.yaml` or `package.json5` at the region root or in a workspace member (the lane reads neither, and members are found by `package.json`), and any config file that exists but can't be read.
  - `overrides` are trusted only when the config map equals the lock's map key for key.
  - Linker and hoist settings are accepted unread; rule 4's union holds under eve

author: alpha912
body:
## Summary

SPECIFICATION.md §9.2 says node-to-node requests MUST send `X-Node-ID`, `X-Node-Signature` and `X-Timestamp`, and the reference backend enforces this (`apps/backend/src/routes/federate.ts`). But `protocol/openapi.json` declared none of these headers on `POST /api/v1/federate/announce` or `/federate/offer`, and listed only `202`. A client generated from the reference contract therefore always got an undocumented `401`.

- **`openapi.json`**
  - Adds three shared, required header parameters under `components.parameters` (`XNodeId`, `XNodeSignature`, `XTimestamp`, the last typed `date-time` with the ±5 minute rule). Both federate operations reference them.
  - Both operations now list `400` (invalid body, or a missing or malformed `X-Timestamp`) and `401` (missing node headers or credentials, or a stale timestamp), matching what the route returns.
  - Security is unchanged: the operations still inherit `BearerAuth`, which the backend accepts alongside `X-API-Key`.
- **SPECIFICATION.md §8.2**: the two federate request examples now show all three §9.2 headers; before, they showed only `X-Node-Signature`. No normative text changed.
  - Adding those lines shifted 10 pinned clauses, so `profiles/core-dp/requirements/spec-v0.2.0-normative-manifest.json` is re-pinned. Only `source_line` values change; ids and statement hashes are untouched.
- **New `apps/backend/tests/openapi.federate.test.ts`**: checks that every header the contract declares is actually enforced by the route, and that every rejection status the route returns is documented. All 4 cases fail against the old contract.
- The site mirror is re-synced, and the protocol `CHANGELOG.md` is updated.

Not in this PR: `@apidevtools/swagger-parser` rejects `servers[0].variables.node` on `main` as well ("unevaluated properties"). Without the `servers` block, both `main` and this branch validate. That pre-existing issue looks like a validator quirk with OpenAPI 3.1 server variables, and it isn't touched here.

## Tree(s) touched

- [x] `apps/backend` (test only)
- [x] `apps/site` (mirror re-sync only)

author: thelinuxkid
body:
## Problem
With fastify 5.12.6 (consumed via cruiselines, deployed 2026-10-23) every valid API key was rejected with 401 / code 1004, and Fastify's request logs contained the raw request including `rawHeaders` with the plaintext bearer token. Pinned back to 5.12.5 in enricai/cruiselines#56; this is the engine-side root cause.

## Root cause
`extendLogger` (src/lib/logging.ts) replaced `info/warn/error/debug` with own properties bound to the logger they were created for. Pino children inherit those properties, so every child log call went out through the parent logger and lost the child's bindings and serializers.

Fastify <= 5.12.5 masked this: it created request child loggers with `{ level: context.logLevel }`, and the empty-string default makes pino rebuild the child's own native log methods (verified: `child({}, { level: "" })` gets own methods, `child({}, {})` inherits the parent's). 5.12.6 only passes `level` when set (fastify#7058), so `request.log` now inherits the parent-bound wrappers. Instrumented on the old code: `request.log.info` is an own native method on 5.12.5 and the root logger's wrapper on 5.12.6. Consequences with 5.12.6:
1. Fastify's `incoming request` / `request completed` logs serialize the raw request (no `req`/`res` serializers), leaking `rawHeaders` with the Authorization token (redact only covers `headers.authorization`).
2. The `req.headers.authorization` redact path mutates the live request headers to `[REDACTED]`, so `extractBearer` returns null and auth answers 1004 for every key.
3. `request.log` lost its `reqId` and child bindings.

## Fix
- Wrappers bind to `this` (fallback: the logger they were built on, for detached calls); `errorWithStack` does the same.
- `buildLoggerOptions` is split out of `getLogger` (no behaviour change) so a test can use the real redaction wiring; `getLogger` is silent under NODE_ENV=test.

## Verification
- New `src/lib/logging-fastify.test.ts`: real Fastify app on the real logger options; asserts the header is intact, the token never appears in logs, the request log is compact, and `request.log` / `errorWithStack` keep `reqId` + child bindings.
- Passes on fastify 5.12.5 and 5.12.6. Negative control: the previous `logging.ts` on 5.12.6 fails all 3 (`seen: '[REDACTED]'`).
- logging, pii-redaction, auth and server suites: 50/50 on both fastify versions. typecheck, lint and build clean.
- Built server on 5.12.6 with a real bcrypt key: valid key 200, wrong key 401, 0 log lines containing the key, 0 containing `rawHeaders`.

## After merge
Cut an engine release and bump `@enricai/barnacle` in enricai/cruiselines; then fastify can be unpinned there (Dependabot's 5.12.6+ PRs will then run this test).

author: ericson-j-santos
body:
## Objetivo
Acrescentar uma inspeção Windows estritamente delimitada ao workflow manual do runner dedicado, para descobrir candidatos nativos sem instalar PostgreSQL nem iniciar WSL/serviços.

## Escopo
- Win32/registro somente leitura: versão Windows; registros WSL apenas do HKCU do runner, sem lançar distros; serviços PostgreSQL por prefixos conhecidos; versões de binários no layout Program Files/PostgreSQL 10–18; metadados reduzidos de volumes fixos; snapshot TCP transitório em memória, filtrado antes da saída para as portas 5432, 8000, 15432 e 18210, sem emitir IPs/PIDs nem resolver owners.
- Sem subprocesso no coletor, Docker, SQL, conexão ao banco, leitura de configurações/credenciais, endereços, comandos, usuários ou caminhos pessoais no recibo.
- Modo novo opt-in e somente manual, owner/attempt 1, main e SHA completo exatos, ambos os jobs CI nativos executados com sucesso, Session Launcher e Command Gateway Risk 1 preservados.
- Concorrência nativa isolada por run_id, validade de admissão 300 s e nenhum cancelamento no modo novo. Recibo allowlist local e em logs; sem upload de artifact no modo novo.
- Modo legado e seus controles continuam presentes.

## Validação
- 30 testes sintéticos do coletor e 17 testes de contrato do workflow, sem coleta real do host.
- CI #718 push do SHA exato 75b72fc968deed0866875215a2fb5734a2449fb9: success. Windows 1.043 passed/9 skips preexistentes; Linux 1.044 passed/8 skips preexistentes. Compile e controles Node também passaram.
- CI #719 da PR: success nos dois jobs, com os mesmos totais.
- Evidências: https://github.com/ericson-j-santos/desktop-pc24x7-runtime/actions/runs/40017844785 e https://github.com/ericson-j-santos/desktop-pc24x7-runtime/actions/runs/40017850719 .
- Revisão estática independente do delta final sem novos bloqueios. Corrigidos o grupo de concorrência, a declaração do snapshot TCP e a fixture Windows, sem afrouxar o guard de produção.
- Readback dos quatro arquivos confirmado no SHA final. Nenhuma inspeção física; chamadas Win32 reais ainda não homologadas.

## Gates e limites
NÃO INTEGRAR enquanto a governança de main estiver bloqueada: a leitura atual mostra ausência de proteção/ruleset efetivo; draft e checks não substituem enforcement. Exigir checks reais do SHA final e revisão do delta antes de integração. A execução física permanece separada e limitada à autorização específica.

Mesmo um inventário medido não qualifica banco, persistência, backup/restore, restart, systemd ou instalação. WSL de outros usuários e instalações customizadas continuam desconhecidos. DATABASE_URL não é configurada por esta PR.

The chosen official action.yml files declare node24: [checkout v7.0.1](https://github.com/actions/checkout/blob/v7.0.1/action.yml), [setup-go v7.0.0](https://github.com/actions/setup-go/blob/v7.0.0/action.yml), [setup-node v7.1.0](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/blob/v7.1.0/action.yml), [golangci-lint-action v9.3.0](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint-action/blob/v9.3.0/action.yml), [upload-artifact v7.0.2](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/v7.0.2/action.yml), [download-artifact v8.0.2](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/v8.0.2/action.yml). Combined workflow actionlint passed; hosted runs must still confirm that direct actions emit no Node 20 deprecation annotations. Benchmark-report composite pins remain unchanged as scoped by the plan.

This draft is isolated from `origin/master` (`6dd3b475a2becf7ad505840317bb87f40ff2f824`). Existing local evidence below comes from the combined release worktree and is not a claim that this isolated PR passed the full matrix. Standalone CI, review and the applicable release gates remain pending.

The initial 2.8.0 pin failed in hosted Lint v2 because its Go 1.25-built binary cannot analyze dependencies requiring Go 1.26. The [official support policy](https://golangci-lint.run/docs/welcome/faq/) requires a compatible compiler and analyzer release; [2.13 added Go 1.27 support](https://golangci-lint.run/docs/product/changelog/#v2130), and this update pins [2.15.0](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/releases/tag/v2.15.0) in both action invocations and the examples installation. The same released binary passed the root lint step on Go 1.27.3 in the W34 branch (job 120711135272); that is supporting evidence, not an isolated W40 pass. Actionlint passed after this change; the new hosted run must validate both modules and examples.

Follow-up local validation: official 2.15.0 darwin/arm64 release SHA256 `d1e409481a8ca846c4bc97e781eb5cb1bd5c23353a0b3977a1cbda1b1b6447d5` matched the published checksum; the executable reports it was built with Go 1.27.0. Root `config verify` passed. In the final combined integration worktree, `GOFLAGS=-p=1 GOMAXPROCS=2 golangci-lint run --timeout=15m ./...` from `v2` passed with `0 issues.` This validates the new analyzer against the affected module without changing v2 runtime source.

body:
Consumers of a non-empty `:outs` view can reuse a stale image when the generated artifact exists only inside Docker or is stale on the host: the output view contributes neither its producer's sources nor its dependency chain to the fingerprint.

Include the owning producer's recipe in the runtime fingerprint walk. Image scope follows that recipe instead of hashing host copies of generated artifacts; native scope continues to hash the declared output contents. Empty output views retain their existing behavior. The CUE manifests, dependency declarations, and Docker COPY interfaces are unchanged. Prepare runtime version `v1.2.3`.

Validation:

- The new check fails before the fix and passes afterward for native and image scopes, missing and stale artifacts, producer sources, command sources, and cross-project inputs. Unrelated edits leave the fingerprint stable.
- Fingerprint, cache, and ignore suites pass, as does the full CUE positive/negative suite.
- A separate check using existing generated-SQL fixture manifests reproduces the unchanged key with the previous runtime and observes the producer input changes with this fix, without adding a source dependency to the database image.

author: juanmicrosoft
body:
Fixes #1633
Fixes #1632
Fixes #1634

Part of #1592 (no silent wrong answers).

> **Review status: NOT-VERIFIED.** The Codex budget (3 rounds + 1 verification pass) ran out with 6 MAJOR findings open (listed under "Open findings"). Per the assignment, work stopped there. Every closed finding has a regression row; the open ones do not have fixes yet.

## What changed

### #1633: compound assignments read their target before the right-hand side
All assignment statements, compound assignments and `++`/`--` go through one lowering, `ConvertAssignmentStatement`. That covers expression statements, for headers, expression-bodied members, setters and expression lambdas.
- The target is split into the parts C# evaluates first (`DecomposeAssignmentTarget`): a receiver, or a receiver and its indexer arguments, with struct field paths peeled to the location that holds them.
- A part is bound to an untyped temp (`§B{_asgN} part`) when it would otherwise run twice (a compound read and store) or after statements the right-hand side hoists (`PartsToCapture`, `BindTargetParts`). Each temp goes right after that part's own hoists, so the parts keep their order.
- A compound read is bound ahead of the right-hand side's hoists. `x += F().N()` becomes `§B{_asg} x`, `§B{_chainF} §C{F}`, `§ASSIGN x (+ _asg …)`. Hoists that only create a lambda or a literal count as effect-free.
- `??=` stays `t = t ?? v` only for a variable or field target with nothing hoisted. Otherwise it becomes `if (!(t is object)) { hoisted; t = v; }`, with every non-fixed part bound first.
- These shapes stay C# under the new `compound-assignment-order` loss (NotSupported registry entry):
  - a value-type receiver that would need a temp;
  - a ref-returning property or indexer target;
  - an index with a user-defined or dynamic conversion;
  - a user-defined input conversion when the right-hand side hoists;
  - user-defined `++`/`--` and C# 14 instance compound operators;
  - dynamic compound assignments.

### #1632: hoisted statements land right before their own statement
- `ConvertBlock`'s per-statement logic moved, unchanged, into `ConvertStatementInto`.
- Unbraced if/else, loop, `using`, `lock` and `fixed` bodies (`ConvertEmbeddedStatement`) and switch sections (`ConvertStatementList`) now convert as statement lists of their own.
- Lock, checked and for headers now flush their hoists before the statement, not after it.
- The #1574 chained-assignment site check accepts these positions (`IsStatementListPosition`). `CH-unbraced-if`, `CH-switch-section` and `CH-loop-body` in `ConverterDefect1574Tests` now expect native.

### #1634: small integer types keep C#'s narrowing cast
`NarrowingCastType` adds the cast for every compound operator and for `++`/`--` (statement and postfix-value forms) on `byte`, `sbyte`, `short`, `ushort` and `char`: `b = (cast u8 (+ b 10))`, which emits `unchecked((byte)(…))`.
- The cast is emitted only when Roslyn reports an existing explicit numeric conversion.
- The cast follows the module overflow mode.
- `checked`/`unchecked` blocks and expressions stay C# (existing behavior), so overflow matches the original.
- A nullable small integer stays C# as the new `compound-assignment-narrowing` loss (Calor's cast would drop the `?`).

## Audit of the other hoisting sites
| Site | Finding | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Labeled statement | `L: y += 5;` dropped the statement (silent; corpus: FluentValidation `CollectionPropertyRule.cs` lost its dependent-rule loop after `AfterValidate:`) | fixed: label, then the statement and its hoists |
| `else if` condition | its hoists ran before the whole `if` chain (`else if (x++ > 0)` always incremented; `else if (o is int n)` cast unconditionally; corpus: MediatR `HandlersOrderer.cs` read an undeclared `_idx` temp) | fixed: `else { hoisted; if … }` |
| `if` condition | the update of a hoisted `x++` went into the then-body | fixed: only pattern bindings go into the body |
| `while` condition | hoists ran once, before the loop | fixed: `while (true) { hoisted; if (cond) {} else break; body }` |
| `do`-`while` condition, `catch` filter, switch-expression guard | hoists ran outside their condition | stay C# (`compound-assignment-order`) |
| Prefix and postfix increments | `Use(x, x++)` passed the incremented `x`; `a[I()]++` ran `I()` twice; `byte` `_pre + 1` failed CS0266 | `CheckPostfixHoist` escalates when an earlier operand reads the variable or may act or throw (`MayActOrThrow`), or when the operand's receiver or arguments have effects or are not fixed under a getter; the cast is added |
| Condition call staging (`HoistCallsFromCondition`) | `if (x < Bump())` ran `Bump()` before reading `x` | staged only when no earlier inline operand can change or act (`CallStagingKeepsOrder`) |
| Expression lambdas | `x => total += x` became `total = x`; their hoists ran outside the lambda | fixed |
| Accessor expression bodies | hoists were not flushed into the accessor | fixed |
| Simple element assignment (`§PUT`/`§SETIDX`) | receiver and key ran after right-hand-side or key hoists | the receiver is bound before key hoists, the key before right-hand-side hoists; an effectful key conversion escalates |
| `?.` statements, pattern variables, out-var lowering | rows `A-null-conditional-unbraced`, `A-pattern-variable-unbraced`, `P-out-var-unbraced` match the original | no change needed |
| Block lambdas and anonymous methods | `ConvertBlock` clears the enclosing statement's pending hoists. A fix exposed arguments being converted twice in `ConvertExpressionStatement`'s invocation path (duplicate `_lam` binds), so it was reverted. Any dropped hoist leaves an undeclared temp, which fails to compile (loud). | **not fixed**, listed here |

## Tests
`tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/InteropScope/ConverterCompoundAssignmentTests.cs` adds 937 tests:
- **185 C# rows × 5 surfaces:** library, CLI default, CLI passthrough, MCP default and MCP passthrough-on-error. Each row is converted, compiled, run with a 30 s hang guard, and compared with the original C#. Each row also states native or preserved. The rows cover:
  - every compound operator against hoisted right-hand sides, properties and indexer arguments;
  - receivers that change; struct receivers; lists, dictionaries and strings; `??=`;
  - unbraced if/else/loop/using/lock/foreach bodies and switch sections, plus the audit sites;
  - every compound operator plus `++`/`--` on `byte`/`sbyte`/`short`/`ushort`/`char`, each in `checked`, `unchecked` and checked-increment forms;
  - nullable byte, enums, properties and arrays;
  - negative controls;
  - every Codex reproducer.
- **7 shape tests** (12 cases): temp shape, single index evaluation, cast emission per type, unchanged controls, placement under an unbraced loop, loss reports and registry entries.

Fixture changes:
- The reporting tests' round-trip-failure stand-in was the trailing-label example, which this PR converts natively. The new stand-in is a private static property with accessor bodies, a separate pre-existing CS0273/CS0274 bug.
- The `W1-F6-rescue` fixture and transcript were regenerated with `CALOR_REGENERATE_W1_TRANSCRIPTS=1`.
- `website/content/cli/{convert,mcp}.mdx` and the interop guide were updated (8 native conversions in place of 3).

Manifest: `manifest_bump.py` +837, +45, +55, so `Calor.Compiler.Tests` goes 14033 → 14970.

Local runs at `4356e38af`, with HOME and CALOR_HOME isolated and submodules initialized:
- `Calor.Compiler.Tests`: 14,967 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed (total 14,970).
- `Calor.Conversion.Tests`: 475/475, so the D-S1.5 fixtures did not move.
- `Calor.Evaluation` scorecard: 22/22, so the scorecard did not move.

## Corpus
Only two corpus files convert differently from main. Both are silent-drop fixes from the audit: FluentValidation `Internal/CollectionPropertyRule.cs` and MediatR `Internal/HandlersOrderer.cs`.

**Ratchets.** Regenerated with `CALOR_UPDATE_BINDER_BASELINE`, `CALOR_REGENERATE_CALOR0270_LEDGER` and `CALOR_REGENERATE_CALOR

author: carlosbonetti
body:
## What this changes

**Python 3.14 is now the minimum.** `requires-python = ">=3.14"`. Pyright, ruff and black target 3.14, every workflow sets up 3.14, new scenario packages from the scaffold require 3.14, and the README and docs say 3.14. `uv.lock` is re-locked for `>=3.14`, which drops the 3.12/3.13 wheels and `zipfile-zstd`, a backport that only older Pythons needed.

**Black's py314 output.** In 14 files, `except (A, B):` becomes `except A, B:` (PEP 758). A diff check shows no other line changed.

**Dependency advisories.** `uv audit` and `npm audit` now report none.

| Package | Advisory | From → to | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| fastmcp-slim (via `pydantic-ai[mcp]`) | GHSA-vqqp-x5qm-5qp4, GHSA-7xgj-8392-5q4r | 4.0.10 → 4.1.3 | `uv lock --upgrade-package` |
| jupyter-server (notebooks group) | PYSEC-2026-4054 | 2.20.0 → 2.21.1 | same |
| setuptools (torch; the build backend) | GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w | 84.0.0 → 84.2.1 | same, and the `[build-system]` floor is now `>=84.1.0` |
| filelock (huggingface-hub, datasets, torch) | GHSA-v4x8-3wr5-3wq8, GHSA-9vhv-jxww-xfm5, GHSA-567q-5qvw-pf92 | 3.29.0 → 4.2.4 | same; a major, allowed by its parents (`filelock>=3.10.0`), and never imported by glossogen |
| zod (via eslint-plugin-react-hooks, dev) | GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 | 4.4.3 → 4.6.7 | `npm update zod` |

**Frontend overrides removed.**
- **`postcss: ^8.5.10`** dates from c7dbf6d73, when next pinned a vulnerable postcss. next 16.4.2 pins 8.5.23 itself. Its copy now moves only when next does: if an advisory hits 8.5.23 first, the override comes back.
- **`@types/react` / `@types/react-dom`** repeated the devDependency pins. Every dependent accepts 19.3.0, so `npm ls` shows the same deduped tree without them.

**Config drift.**
- **Dependabot's docker entry** only watched `/`, so `frontend/DockerfileFrontend` (`node:22-alpine`) never got a bump. It now covers `directories: ["/", "/frontend"]`.
- **The frontend CI step's name** now lists vitest, which `make check-frontend` runs.

## Why

The production image has run `python:3.14-slim` since Aug 10 (3b392e3f4), while CI tested 3.12 and the package declared 3.12. Now the declared, tested and deployed versions are one and the same. The advisories come from `uv audit` and `npm audit` on `main`. This is the first maintenance run of the code-health policy.

## Verification

All of these ran locally on Python 3.14.3:

- **pytest** (`-n auto --dist loadgroup`): 2002 passed, 2 skipped. That's the same count as `main` on 3.13.
- **Linters:** `make lint` and `make check-server` pass, and black's `--check` is clean after the reformat.
- **Python builds:** the notebooks (`--nbmake`, 4 passed), `mkdocs build --strict`, `make check-package` (792 expected wheel files) and `make gen-api-types` (no diff) all pass.
- **Frontend:** `npm ci` and `next build` pass, and `npm audit` reports 0.
- **Locks and workflows:** `uv lock --check` passes, `uv audit` finds no vulnerabilities, and actionlint passes on ci.yml.
- **Lock smoke test:** huggingface-hub's `WeakFileLock` and filelock's `FileLock` both acquire on 4.2.4.
- **Server:** `glossogen serve` on 3.14 against a copied veyru run starts clean, and the runs list and run detail API both return 200.
- **Review:** MOLEQUE-85 said ship on the advisory and lockfile changes.
- **End to end:** RABICO-31 ran `serve` and `next dev` on spare ports against copied runs. The pages return 200, the Tailwind CSS compiles, and the logs are clean. Both checks ran before the 3.14 switch.

Found along the way, not fixed here:
- container_yard_stacking runs from May return 500 on the run detail API. They lack `yard_slot_count`, `initial_row` and `batch`, which `ContainerYardCaseStarted` requires (`src/glossogen/scenarios/container_yard_stacking/events.py:45-56`).
- `huggingface_hub>=2.2.0` is a direct dependency that nothing in `src/` imports.
- verspec is archived (it comes in through mike, docs group).
- On macOS, `make test` shows 50 WeasyPrint collection errors, because SIP strips `DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH` from `make`'s shell. Running pytest directly with that variable set avoids them.

PRs #274–#276 touch some of the reformatted directories. If one conflicts on an `except` line, re-run `black .` after rebasing.

## Releasing

This is labelled **`release:minor`** (0.15.0): raising `requires-python` breaks installs on Python 3.12 and 3.13, which would be a major after 1.0. Switch to `release:major` if you want this to be 1.0.0, or to `norelease` to hold off on deploying.

## Checklist
- [x] `make lint` passes
- [x] `make gen-api-types` produces no diff (if a response model changed)
- [x] Docstrings on new modules and public functions
- [x] No dead code left behind

author: tauceti-ai-for-science
body:
This PR adds the function-field carrier for algebraic Belyi pairs, `TauCeti.IsAlgebraicBelyiPair k F`. It applies over a field `k` of characteristic zero to a function field `F` finite over `k(t)` through an `Algebra (RatFunc k) F` structure. The conditions are that the constant field of `F` is exactly `k` (`IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F`), and that every place of `F` over a place of `k(t)` other than `t = 0`, `t = 1`, `t = ∞` (`TauCeti.Place.zeroOneInfty`) has ramification index `1`. It proves the characterization by Stichtenoth-unramified places (`isAlgebraicBelyiPair_iff`), and that `k(t)` over itself is the trivial pair. It then proves that radical extensions `y ^ n = u` unramified outside `0`, `1`, `∞` are Belyi pairs (`IsAlgebraicBelyiPair.of_pow_eq`, `.of_pow_eq_of_gcd_ord_eq_one`). Specialised to the family `y ^ n = c t ^ a (t - 1) ^ b` with `n` coprime to one of `a`, `b`, `a + b`, this gives a Belyi pair (`.of_pow_eq_X_zpow_mul_X_sub_one_zpow`) of degree `n` (`finrank_eq_of_pow_eq_X_zpow_mul_X_sub_one_zpow`). The concrete witness is the power map, modelled as `AdjoinRoot (Y ^ n - t)` over `k(t)`. It is a Belyi pair of degree `n`, totally ramified over `0` and `∞` and unramified elsewhere (`isAlgebraicBelyiPair_adjoinRoot_X_pow_sub_C_X`, `finrank_adjoinRoot_X_pow_sub_C_X`, `isTotallyRamified_adjoinRoot_X_pow_sub_C_X`, `ramificationIdx_adjoinRoot_X_pow_sub_C_X_eq_one`).

Roadmap: BelyiMaps

Milestone: `BelyiMaps/README.md`, Layer 9.1 "The algebraic carrier", the **New object: `AlgebraicBelyiPair`**: "an algebraic Belyi pair is a function field `F/k` … with exact constants `IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F` — together with a finite `k`-embedding `k(t) ↪ F` such that every place of `F` over a place of `k(t)` other than the three marked places `t = 0`, `t = 1`, `t = ∞` has ramification index `1`", with the marked places being "the finite places of the monic irreducibles `t` and `t − 1`, and the infinite place". The definition carries `[CharZero k]` rather than a separability hypothesis, as 9.1 pins. It is a `Prop`-valued predicate on the given algebra structure, named `IsAlgebraicBelyiPair` after the `Is…` convention for predicates (compare `TauCeti.IsFunctionField`). From the 9.1 bullet list this PR covers the structure, separability (an instance in characteristic zero, so no declaration), the edge case `F = k(t)` and the power-map example with its local data at `0` and `∞` ("`{(n,1)}` at `0` and at `∞`"). The degree-2 pair of `4t(1 − t)` is the member `y ^ 2 = 1 − t` of the radical family, recorded in the module docstring. Layers 9.5 ("the pair `(M(X), ℂ(t) ↪ M(X))` is an algebraic Belyi pair over `ℂ`") and 9.7 ("For an algebraic Belyi pair `(F, ℂ(t) ↪ F)` over `ℂ`, construct an analytic pair") consume this carrier. It is independent of the analytic Riemann–Roch input that blocks 9.3's second half and 9.4. After this PR, 9.1 still needs the `localData` multiset with its weighted ramification partition, the residue-degree example at `t = 1` over `ℚ`, morphisms and base change, the comparison with AlgebraicCurves' curve model, and the branch-point `S₃`-action. As earlier Layer 7 to 9 PRs note, the README files Layer 9 under the planned successor `BelyiAlgebraicAndDescent`, which does not exist yet, so this PR cites BelyiMaps. No open PR touches this material (the one open BelyiMaps PR, TauCeti#20397, is the analytic degree theorem of 9.3).

The changes:
- `FieldTheory/FunctionField/Belyi/Basic.lean` (new): `Place.zeroOneInfty` with its membership lemmas, `IsAlgebraicBelyiPair`, `isAlgebraicBelyiPair_iff`, `isAlgebraicBelyiPair_ratFunc`.
- `FieldTheory/FunctionField/Belyi/Radical.lean` (new): the radical Belyi criteria, the vanishing of the radicand's order away from `0`, `1`, `∞`, and the power map. `isTotallyRamified_adjoinRoot_X_pow_sub_C_X` and `ramificationIdx_adjoinRoot_X_pow_sub_C_X_eq_one` only assume `n` invertible in `k`; characteristic zero stays on the Belyi-pair statement.
- `FieldTheory/FunctionField/Radical/Basic.lean` (new): the degree `n` of `y ^ n = c t ^ a (t - 1) ^ b` over `k(t)` (`finrank_eq_of_pow_eq_X_zpow_mul_X_sub_one_zpow`), independent of the Belyi layer.
- `FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/XPowSubCX.lean` (new): `irreducible_X_pow_sub_C_X`, the `Fact (Irreducible …)` and `FiniteDimensional` instances for `AdjoinRoot (Y ^ n - t)` under `[NeZero n]` (following Tau Ceti's `Module.Finite R (AdjoinRoot (cyclotomic n R))` instance), `finrank_adjoinRoot_X_pow_sub_C_X`, and `isSeparable_adjoinRoot_X_pow_sub_C_X` for `n` invertible in `k`.
- `FieldTheory/RatFunc/Basic.lean` (new): `TauCeti.RatFunc.X_sub_C_ne_zero` and `TauCeti.RatFunc.algebraMap_mul_X_zpow_mul_X_sub_one_zpow_ne_zero`, the nonvanishing of `X - a` and of the radicands in `k(X)`, independent of place theory.
- `FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/Order.lean`: `ord_X_eq_zero_of_ne` and `ord_X_sub_C_eq_zero_of_ne` (`X` is a unit at every place of `k(X)` other than `X = 0` and `∞`, and `X - a` at every place other than `X = a` and `∞`); and the order of `c X ^ a (X - 1) ^ b` at every place (`Place.ord_algebraMap_mul_X_zpow_mul_X_sub_one_zpow`) with its values `a`, `b`, `-(a + b)` at `0`, `1`, `∞`, and a place where this order is coprime to `n` (`Place.exists_gcd_ord_algebraMap_mul_X_zpow_mul_X_sub_one_zpow_eq_one`).

Reuse: I grepped the pinned Mathlib and `TauCeti/` for Belyi pairs on the function-field side, for sets of marked places of `k(t)`, for the orders of `X` and `X - a` away from their own places, and for the irreducibility of `Y ^ n - t`, and found none. The proofs rest on Tau Ceti's place theory: `Place.restrict`, `Place.ramificationIdx`, `Place.IsUnramified`, `restrict_surjective_of_finiteDimensional`, and the radical-extension results `Place.ramificationIdx_eq_of_pow_eq` and `Place.ramificationIdx_eq_one_of_pow_eq_of_dvd_ord` (Stichtenoth, Proposition 3.7.3). They also use `isIntegrallyClosedIn_of_pow_eq_of_gcd_ord_eq_one` (Corollary 3.7.4), `Valuation.X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_of_gcd_ord_eq_one` and `Valuation.finrank_eq_of_pow_eq_of_gcd_ord_eq_one`. No Mathlib PR material or external formalization is vendored. The references, Stichtenoth's *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes* and Girondo–González-Diez's *Introduction to Compact Riemann Surfaces and Dessins d'Enfants*, Chapter 3, are cited in the module docstrings.
